# RouteIQ - Project Handbook

RouteIQ is the daily dispatch planner of **NMWC** (National Mineral Water Co., Muscat, Oman). Every evening it turns tomorrow's sales orders into truck loading plans and delivery routes: which truck carries which orders, in how many loads, in which stop order and at what times.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Built for** | NMWC dispatchers (planners and supervisors) and the admins who keep the master data (customers, trucks, drivers, products, settings) |
| **Status on 25 Sep 2026** | **Live in production** on Railway since 24 Sep 2026 (PR #25). `main` is at `f2f4099` (PR #30) |
| **Repository** | `github.com/rahmanmansoori244-droid/routeiq` (**private**) |
| **Stack** | pnpm monorepo: `apps/web` (Next.js 14 App Router + Prisma 5 + PostgreSQL), `apps/solver` (Python FastAPI + Google OR-Tools routing and CP-SAT), `packages/shared-types`, `infra/osrm` (self-hosted OSRM road routing), `docs/` |

**How to use this handbook**

- **People:** [section 1](#1-where-everything-is) gives quick answers. [Section 3](#3-daily-dispatch-process-flow) walks through the daily workflow as the code runs it. [Section 5](#5-running-testing-deploying-operating) covers running, testing and deploying.
- **AI code reviewers:** start with [section 7.3](#73-guide-for-an-ai-code-reviewer). It covers where to start reading, how to run the tests, the invariants that must hold, the riskiest code, what is out of scope and what you must not do. [Section 7.4](#74-review-leads-found-while-writing-this-handbook) lists the leads already found. Check them; do not assume they are confirmed.
- **Citations.** Each statement names a repo-relative path, and where useful a function, so you can jump straight to it. The facts come from `main` at `f2f4099`, the git history, the merged pull requests and `docs/`. Facts marked **(per work log)** come from the operator's build notes and are not recorded in the repo.
- **What wins.** Where this handbook, older documents and the code disagree, **the code wins**, then `docs/`. `CLAUDE.md` (the May 2026 SaaS spec) and `OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md` are historical.
- **Conventions.** P1 is the highest priority and P5 the lowest. Times of day are minutes from local midnight in the tenant timezone (default `Asia/Muscat`), so 390 means 06:30. Money is OMR and distances are km. A "plan" is one `RunPlan` row: one depot, one delivery date, one version.
- **No secrets, no customer data.** This handbook names environment variables but never gives their values, and it contains no real customer data. Keep it that way when you edit it.
- **Stabilization release.** The security part (PR1) changed sign-in, sessions, roles, the driver app and several env vars. [`docs/SECURITY.md`](./SECURITY.md) describes the result and the owner runbook; the sections below are updated to match and mark the review items fixed. PR3 (plan lifecycle and concurrency) added database locks for every plan change, copy-forward re-plans that keep the previous plan when the optimization fails, the stale-day guard on the dispatch screen and the solve admission ([2.7](#27-background-job-model), [3.11](#311-step-9-late-orders-and-plan-versions), [3.14](#314-status-values-and-transitions)). PR4 (review F08, F04, L23) freezes the facts each plan was made with (stop, truck and settings snapshots: a later pin or hours correction is shown as "changed after planning", never applied silently) and adds the dispatch feasibility gate: the optimizer re-checks every timetable it returns, the web re-checks each truck-day, and a truck whose times break a rule cannot be locked, loaded or dispatched until it is re-planned ([3.8](#38-step-6-load-states), [3.10](#310-step-8-exports), [4.11](#411-post-solve-stage)).
- **Audit of 27 Sep 2026.** An external audit (findings F01-F26 and the earlier-open items E1-E5) was verified independently; the consolidated assessment and the owner's decisions are in `.dev/audit-2026-09-27/VERIFIED-ASSESSMENT.md` (local, `.dev/` is not in git). Fixed so far: **A2 "Dispatch screen: never save the wrong thing"** (F06, F07, F13, F16, F17) and **A3 "Intake and master data"** (F02-F05, F20, F24-F26, with the migration `20260930093000_master_data_no_orphans`), both merged in main (their [7.4](#74-review-leads-found-while-writing-this-handbook) blocks come before A1's); **A4 "Recovery, races, readiness"** (audit PR4; F09-F11, F15, F19, F21: a plan left "optimizing" and **Reset stuck plan**, races between password resets, between admins and between a plan read and "Use instead", the `/api/health` readiness gate, the OSRM health check), merged in main (its blocks come before A1's); and **A1 "Quick hardening"**: F01's first part (image endpoint off, no Server Actions enforced in CI), the public source maps, Node 22, and the E2 quick fix for uploads, with its review fixes (a crafted file of a few KB could still block the app for minutes; the upload caps bound one upload's work, but a file near them still blocks the app for 5-11 s until the worker of assessment PR 5). **A1 v2** closed the rest: a crafted old .xls could still make `XLSX.CFB.read` itself use memory that grows with the square of the file size (E2 for .xls), an "ID"-column CSV sent as Excel was wrongly refused, and decision 4's localhost binding was documented but `next dev` still listened on every interface. **A1 v3** closed four more ways a small upload under every cap could still block the app for minutes or run it out of memory (a long number format on many cells, `xl/metadata.xml`, a threaded-comment person list, self-closing typed cells) and a semicolon "ID" CSV still wrongly refused. **A1 v4** closed the files that made SheetJS read one part many times while the caps counted it once (two sheets naming one worksheet part: a 121 KB file took up to 108 s and 3.4 GB, or ran the app out of memory; a comments part or a drawing named again and again; an external link listed many times) and chart sheets, whose chart points SheetJS turns into cells past every cap. **A1 v5** made that replay number the sheets the workbook's relationships do not name as SheetJS does (from the text of `xl/worksheets/sheet.xml`, not its size): a part holding only a byte-order mark made it count the wrong sheet's parts, and a 3.5 KB file of repeated comments blocked the app for 10-22 s ([7.4](#74-review-leads-found-while-writing-this-handbook), A1's six blocks, after A4's; [`docs/SECURITY.md`](./SECURITY.md) section 9). And **A5 "Owner rules: correct locations, every order has a depot"** (the owner's standing rules of 27-28 Sep 2026, answering what A2 and A3 left open): a reading that is not exact is saved only as a pin placed by hand and checked again on the server, an import never stores such a pair as usable, a LOW location nobody confirmed is not planned, no load goes out with a stop at a point that is not usable or was replaced, and every order and order file has a depot (migration `20260930120000_orders_always_have_depot`); imported locations nobody confirmed (HIGH or MEDIUM) are still planned, with a note; a pair a dispatcher types or pastes counts one zero at the end like the import ("Same rule everywhere"); a pin corrected after planning does not block the load, the driver gets the new pin ("Allow, driver gets new pin") (owner, 28 Sep). Branch `audit-5-owner-rules`, with main `2a20cd7` (A4 and A1) merged in ([7.4](#74-review-leads-found-while-writing-this-handbook), A5's blocks). And **P5 "Uploads read in a separate process"** (assessment PR 5: E2 fully fixed, owner decision 16; called P5 because A5 is the owner-rules PR): every uploaded file (order file and late orders, customer import, baseline) is read in its own short-lived process with a heap cap and a time limit that really stop it, at most two at once, so reading a file within the 10 MB limit can no longer freeze or crash the web process (still open, see the P5 blocks: the upload request itself is read whole into the web process before the 10 MB check, and the order check of a very large file runs in it, about 2-3 s for 50,000 lines); a file over those limits is refused in plain words and nothing is saved (new optional variables `UPLOAD_WORKER_MAX_HEAP_MB`, `UPLOAD_PARSE_TIMEOUT_MS`, `UPLOAD_PARSE_CONCURRENCY`, [2.9](#29-environment-variables-by-service)); since its review the rows the parser sends back are at most 128 MB, each text sent once, and since its second review a CSV sent as text has A1's 200-column and 2,500,000-cell caps too, no longer row or more cells reach the web process, and the web process keeps the rows compact (about 20 MB for the widest legal file, under 1 MB for NMWC's), so a small file cannot fill the web process either; since its third review an order file of more than 32,767 different sales orders (legal: up to 50,000 rows) is checked and can be added, where it was refused with Prisma's own text, and any other failure while an order file is checked is answered in plain words (500 `CHECK_FAILED`). Branch `audit-p5-upload-worker`, on main `3451f4d`, merged in main as `d5b436f` (#47) ([7.4](#74-review-leads-found-while-writing-this-handbook), P5's blocks, after A5's). And **A6 "Solver and plan-output accuracy"** (assessment PR 6: F08, E4, E5, E3, F22, F23, E1; owner decisions 13, 14, 15 and 26): weights checked to 0.1 kg with no hidden margin (a load may weigh exactly the payload), a stop left out for its weight says so (only when a check proves no packing of the trucks carries it), only new overtime counts when choosing a truck, the load repack never gives up before its first answer, the loading sheet's kg equals the load's, an option that breaks the timing rules says so, cost per case is rounded once, and locked and dispatched loads keep the depot pin they were planned from. Branch `audit-p6-solver-accuracy`, on main `3451f4d`, with main `d5b436f` (P5) merged in; no migration ([7.4](#74-review-leads-found-while-writing-this-handbook), A6's block and its three review-fix blocks, after P5's, the last ones).
- **Outside benchmark of 8 Oct 2026.** An outside simulation and optimization benchmark at `5b2ee06` (report in [`docs/review-pack/benchmark-2026-10-08/`](./review-pack/benchmark-2026-10-08/); its evidence bundle with an independent checker on the archive branch `evidence/benchmark-2026-10-08`, not merged) found that a same-day re-plan could lose feasible work after exact timing (F02: P02's C3 unserved while a truck stood idle; F07: D5 kept 84 of 180 stops) and that a short time limit could leave only a plan that breaks the rules (F01: D3 at 60 s). Branch `fix-replan-recovery-and-fallback` fixes F01, F02 and F07: a wider fit pool, a fully timed incumbent and recovery of left-out stops in strict priority order, more of the request's time when P1-P3 work is still out, a constructive fallback, a checked partial plan instead of a VIOLATED-only answer, and the plan screen's warning when P1-P3 orders are left out while trucks are unused ([4.11](#411-post-solve-stage)). F03 (no split when one truck fits, even with a cheaper rental split) is owner policy ([6.2](#62-decisions)); F04 / F05 matter only with kg limits; F06 is wording; PyVRP's penalty scaling and preferred windows are the next fix ([7.1](#71-open-backlog-ranked)). No migration.

It is private: never copy it anywhere. `.env`, `.env.local` and `.env.*.local` hold real configuration values. Build output and dependencies (`node_modules/`, `.next/`, `apps/solver/.venv/`, `__pycache__/`) are also ignored |

### Is all of it on GitHub?

- **Yes: all of the code is on GitHub.** `origin` is `github.com/rahmanmansoori244-droid/routeiq` (private), and everything built so far is merged into **`main`**. Production deploys from `main`. When this handbook was written (25 Sep 2026), `main` was at PR #30 (`f2f4099`) plus this handbook (PR #31).
- **Other branches:** each feature was built on its own branch (for example `nmwc-dispatch-mvp`, `split-deliveries`, `driver-pack`, `optimizer-fewer-trucks`). Those branches are all merged, so treat `main` as the only source of truth. The Dependabot branches are open dependency-update PRs that have not been merged.
- **Tracked:** all source code, migrations, tests, CI, Dockerfiles and docs.
- **Not tracked on purpose:** see the last row of the table above. An online reviewer sees the complete code but no real data and no configuration values. Production values are Railway service variables.

## 2. Repository map & architecture

RouteIQ is a pnpm/Turborepo monorepo with three runtime pieces:

- a **Next.js 14 web app** (`apps/web`), which serves the UI and the REST API and runs the background optimization jobs;
- a **Python FastAPI optimizer** (`apps/solver`), built on Google OR-Tools;
- a **self-hosted OSRM road-routing server** (`infra/osrm`).

All data is stored in PostgreSQL through Prisma. Production runs on Railway ([5.6](#56-deployment-on-railway)).

### 2.1 Repository tree

```
routeiq/
├── apps/
│   ├── web/                    Next.js 14 app: UI pages, REST API, background optimize jobs (TypeScript)
│   └── solver/                 FastAPI optimizer service: OR-Tools dispatch planner + PyVRP second search (+ legacy PyVRP)
├── packages/
│   └── shared-types/           TypeScript wire types shared by web and solver contract
├── infra/
│   └── osrm/                   Docker image of the OSRM road-routing server (Oman + UAE map baked in)
├── docs/                       Current runbooks and design docs (Sep 2026) - these win over CLAUDE.md
├── .github/                    CI workflows, Dependabot config, PR template
├── CLAUDE.md                   HISTORICAL: original v1.3 multi-tenant SaaS build spec (May 2026)
├── OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md         HISTORICAL: May 2026 build/bug-hunt report from the PyVRP era
├── README.md                   Entry point; links to docs/
├── .env.example                Placeholders for the main web and solver variables (the full list is in section 2.9)
├── docker-compose.yml          Local dev only: Postgres 16 + PostGIS, and the solver container
├── package.json                Root scripts (turbo dev/build/lint/typecheck/test, db:*), engines Node 22.x (A1), pnpm>=9
├── .nvmrc, .node-version       Node 22 (A1): read by CI (setup-node), nvm/fnm and Railpack
├── pnpm-workspace.yaml         Workspaces: apps/*, packages/*
├── pnpm-lock.yaml              Locked JS dependency versions (lockfile v9)
├── turbo.json                  Turborepo task graph (build/dev/lint/typecheck/test; .env is a global input)
├── .npmrc, .prettierrc, .editorconfig, .gitignore
└── .dev/        (git-ignored)  Local only; not on GitHub; contains real data - do not copy
```

> **Historical documents.** `CLAUDE.md` is the May 2026 SaaS specification, and many code comments still cite "CLAUDE.md §N". `README.md` says that wherever `CLAUDE.md` disagrees with the `docs/` files or the code, **the docs and code win**. `OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md` describes the PyVRP build of 12 May 2026. The dispatch planner has since replaced that engine.

### 2.2 The web app

`apps/web` is a Next.js 14 App Router app.

```
apps/web/
├── middleware.ts           Edge middleware: unauthenticated /t/* and /admin -> /login (query string kept); signed-in users bounced off /login,/signup to /
├── instrumentation.ts      Startup hook: loads Sentry config per runtime; logs missing production settings; starts the in-process janitor (Node runtime only)
├── next.config.js          Security headers (HSTS, nosniff, DENY framing, baseline CSP), images.unoptimized (/_next/image off, A1),
│                           instrumentationHook, Sentry wrapper (browser source maps only with an upload, deleted after it, A1)
├── app/                    Pages (React Server Components) + *-client.tsx client components
├── app/api/                118 route files. Most return the { data, error } JSON envelope; the exceptions are
│                           /api/health (readiness) and /api/health/live, the NextAuth handlers, the Excel/PDF exports and
│                           the job-debug download (files), and /api/orders/sample (CSV)
├── lib/                    All server-side logic (tables below)
├── components/             App shell (sidebar, mobile-sidebar, topbar, user-menu, nav-link, page-shell; (16 Oct 2026) alert-bell, alerts-api; (20 Oct 2026) alert-review-dialog; (24 Oct 2026) change-password-dialog),
│                           maps (plan-map, pin-map, map-picker; (18 Oct 2026) truck-day-map: MapLibre + OSM), empty states, ui/ (shadcn/Radix primitives)
├── prisma/                 schema.prisma, migrations/, seed + fixture scripts, synth-data/
├── scripts/                (A1) remove-public-source-maps.mjs (last step of `pnpm build`); build-guards.ts + check-build-output.ts:
│                           CI check after the build (no Server Actions, no .map in .next/static; since P5 the upload parser,
│                           since review M3 the PDF renderer);
│                           (P5) build-upload-parser.mjs (a `pnpm build` step) and upload-parser-build.cjs: esbuild bundle of the
│                           upload parser into .next/upload-parser/parse.cjs; upload-parser-dev.cjs: the same, built on use, for dev and tests;
│                           (M3) build-pdf-renderer.mjs, pdf-renderer-build.cjs and pdf-renderer-dev.cjs: the same for the driver
│                           sheet renderer, .next/pdf-renderer/render.cjs
├── tests/                  Vitest: lib/ (pure unit), tenant-isolation.spec.ts (real DB), integration/ (HTTP; web + solver running)
├── types/modules.d.ts      Declares the mapbox-gl CSS module
├── sentry.{client,server,edge}.config.ts   Sentry init per runtime. Since the driver link (4 Oct 2026) all three, and
│                                           lib/observability.ts, use lib/observability-scrub.ts: no trace of /d/ or /api/d/,
│                                           /d/<token> rewritten to /d/[token], Authorization dropped, cookie and tokens redacted
│                                           (19 Oct 2026) the same for the salesman link: no trace of /s/ or /api/s/, /s/<token> -> /s/[token]
├── sentry.config.example.ts                Template/instructions
└── vitest.config.ts, tailwind.config.ts, postcss.config.js, components.json (shadcn), tsconfig.json, .eslintrc.json
```

**Pages (`app/**/page.tsx`, 36 in total).** Every tenant page goes through `app/t/[slug]/layout.tsx`, which runs `getCurrentTenant(slug)`. A slug that does not match the user's tenant returns 404.

| Route | Files | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | `app/page.tsx` | Sends the user to `/login`, `/admin` (SUPER_ADMIN) or `/t/<slug>`. A session the server no longer accepts goes through `/api/auth/end-session` first, so there is no redirect loop |

There are **no Server Actions**, and until the Next.js upgrade there must be none (owner decision 4 of the 27 Sep 2026 audit, A1): a unit test fails on any `'use server'` in the app's code and CI fails the build when `.next/server/server-reference-manifest.json` lists an action (`scripts/check-build-output.ts`). The unused `experimental.serverActions.bodySizeLimit` setting is gone from `next.config.js` (A1). Server Components read the database directly through `tenantDb`. Client components call `/api/*` with `fetch`; `api()` in `app/t/[slug]/dispatch/client-api.ts` unwraps the `{ data, error }` envelope.

**API route handlers (`app/api/**/route.ts`).** 93 of the 118 route files use `withTenantApi()` from `lib/api.ts`. In this table, "any" means any signed-in tenant role, VIEWER included. The full matrix is checked in: `apps/web/tests/lib/api-role-matrix.spec.ts` fails CI when a handler is added, removed or re-gated without updating it.

A1 review: `guardSpreadsheet` lets SheetJS read only an .xlsx, an old .xls or CSV text (it picks its reader from the first bytes), refuses more than 2,500,000 cells with a value, 10,000 comments or links over 200,000 cells before SheetJS reads the file, checks each zip part's two names, hides binary parts; `parseExcelSheets` reads without formulas and checks each sheet's range (200 columns, 2,500,000 cells over all sheets) before any sheet is turned into rows; since the P5 second review a CSV sent as text (Papa Parse) has the same two caps (`parseCsv`: its header before Papa makes a row object; `checkCsvCells`: each line's values, and all values with the header's, after the row limit; the two caps now live in the dependency-free `upload-limits.ts`). A1 v2: an old .xls that is a compound file has its structure checked in linear time first (`checkCompoundFile`), so `XLSX.CFB.read` cannot be made to use time and memory that grow with the square of the file size; a CSV whose first header is "ID" is read as CSV, not refused as SYLK. A1 v3: a file that begins with "ID" is judged by replaying SheetJS's SYLK reader over the whole file (`idFileReader`: refused when it reads as SYLK or the reader would do more than 100,000 steps before it gives up); a cell is counted as SheetJS makes one (a type or a value, also on a tag that closes itself); at most 1,000 metadata entries of each kind and 1,000 comment authors; SheetJS reads with `cellText: false` (no display text; since A5 was merged with A1, the customer import alone keeps a reference to the number format or, for CSV sent as Excel, the text of its lat / lng cells, and works out the decimals they show on the sheet it reads only, in the one column per name the rows keep, trying each format once per upload (at most 20, each at most 64 characters): `shownSources`, `ShownFormats`, A5 fourth review; a CSV sent as Excel whose first header is "ID" keeps its text too, unless SheetJS's SYLK reader would format a value in it first, `idFileFormatsCells`, A5 fifth review). A1 v4: `sheetReads` replays which parts SheetJS reads for each sheet (its relationships, comments, drawing of notes; external links as often as they are listed), a part read again counts again against every cap, two sheets that read one worksheet part are refused as damaged, a chart, dialog or macro sheet is refused, and `parseExcelSheets` checks that SheetJS reads the sheet list the guard replayed (`sameSheetList`). A1 v5: the replay takes SheetJS's "Numbers iOS" numbering (`xl/worksheets/sheet.xml`, `sheet1.xml`, ...) and its `xl/workbook.xml` fallback only when that part holds text as SheetJS reads it, as SheetJS does. `parseUpload` itself has no timeout: it is synchronous (the old 10 s timer could never fire). Since P5 only the upload parser process runs it for an upload (`upload-parse/`, next row); a file near the caps took the web process 5-11 s (A1's measure) and more on a busy PC. Since the CSV intake review fix (9 Oct 2026) `parseUpload` picks the reader by the file's content, never its type: CSV text always goes to Papa Parse, every value as written (`decodeCsvText`: byte-order marks, strict UTF-8, then a mostly-UTF-8 file still as UTF-8 (`utf8Counts`: more well-formed UTF-8 letters than places that are not UTF-8; each such place read as U+FFFD, with a warning naming how many), else Windows-1256 with a warning; every line break read as a line feed, so a bare LF in a file of CR LF lines ends its row; a quote never closed refused naming the line; U+0000 taken out; a web page or binary content refused), so SheetJS reads only .xlsx / .xls bytes for an upload; the A1 text above about CSV text read by SheetJS (the guard's text branch, `cellText` and `idFileFormatsCells` for a CSV sent as Excel) describes paths no upload reaches since then. **Database and scripts (`apps/web/prisma`).**

- `schema.prisma` has 48 models and 20 enums:
  - `Tenant`, `TenantConfig`, `User`;
  - `Depot`, `Truck`, `Driver`, `Region`, `Customer`, `CustomerTypeProfile`, `Product`;
  - `UploadBatch`, `Order`, `OrderLine`, `IntakeLineKey`;
  - `RunPlan` (one plan version per depot + date), `PlanLoad`, `ScenarioResult`, `RouteAssignment`, `RunJob`, `UnservedOrder`;
  - `ManualBaseline*`, `DriverShift`, `TruckLocation`, `DeliveryProof`, `AuditLog`, `PasswordResetToken`;
  - (helpers, 13 Oct 2026) `Helper` and `PlanLoadHelper` ([3.9](#39-step-7-a-driver-per-load)); `Truck.defaultHelperId`, `PlanLoad.helpersSetById` / `helpersSetAt`.
  - (driver leave, 6 Oct 2026) `DriverLeave` ([3.9](#39-step-7-a-driver-per-load));
  - (delivery outcome and the driver page, 4 Oct 2026) `DriverLink`, `StopVisit`, `StopEvent`, `DeliveryPhoto`, with the enums `StopEventKind`, `StopEventSource`, `DeliveryOutcome`, `NotDeliveredReason`, `PhotoPositionStatus` ([3.18](#318-delivery-outcomes-and-the-driver-page)). `StopEventKind.DEPOT_DEPART` (16 Oct 2026, migration `20261016180000_ops_alerts`): the driver's Leaving for next load, a load-level event (sequence and visit NULL) on the load the truck leaves with, at most one per load ([3.20](#320-operations-alerts)).
  - (the hire suggestion, 6 Oct 2026) `HireOption` (the trucks a depot can rent for a day) and `HireSuggestion` (one what-if per plan version and its suggestion); `Truck.onlyOnDate` and `Truck.hireOptionId` ([3.19](#319-the-hire-suggestion)).
  - (operations alerts, 16 Oct 2026) `OpsAlert` (one row per alert rule and physical subject: depot, date, truck, load, stop) and `OpsAlertDigest` (one row per alert e-mail, counts only); `TenantConfig.alerts*` (the master switch, off by default, and one threshold per rule). Rules and defaults: `lib/alerts/catalog.ts`; migration `20261016180000_ops_alerts`. Since 20 Oct 2026 an alert's cause & action is on its row (`OpsAlert.review*`, `detailsRemovedAt`; migration `20261020000000_alert_notes`): rows are deleted 90 days after their date as before; only with `ALERT_KEEP_FOR_ANALYSIS=1` (owner decision pending) are they kept as long as the analysis data, their text and free texts removed after 90 days.
  - (IVMS live link, Ayun GPS trackers, 16 Oct 2026; `lib/ivms/`) `TruckPosition` (latest live position, the map only), `TruckTrailPoint` (history pulled from Ayun, the only source of GPS times), `IvmsEvent` (depot and zone moves; a trail move with whether its time is exact, `observed`, since the GPS alerts review of 18 Oct 2026), `IvmsState` (calls per class per UTC day, lease, backoff) and `IvmsTruckDay` (history pulled so far, GPS suppressed); `Truck.ivmsImei`, `Depot.ivmsZoneName` (both hidden from every read by the Prisma global omit in `lib/db.ts`) and the `TenantConfig.ivms*` settings (OFF by default).
  - (the analysis dataset, owner request 19 Oct 2026; `lib/analysis/`) `FactTruckDay`, `FactVisit`, `FactLeg` and `FactDepotTurn`: facts per delivery date kept for later analysis, written only by the nightly job, never a raw position; `TenantConfig.analysisRetentionDays` (730 by default) ([3.22](#322-the-analysis-dataset-facts-kept-for-later-analysis)).
- The 50 migrations are listed in [5.5](#55-database-migrations). The dispatch data model is in [3.15](#315-data-model-used-by-the-dispatch-flow).
- Scripts:
  - `seed-nmwc-dispatch.ts` (`db:seed:dispatch`): demo tenant; `SEED_PASSWORD` sets the demo logins.
  - `nmwc-dispatch-data.ts`: pure generator of fictional demo data (seeded PRNG).
  - `nmwc-dispatch-fixtures.ts` (`fixtures:dispatch`): writes `tests/fixtures/nmwc/*`.
  - `seed-synth.ts`: loads the `synth-data/` CSVs. `check-priority-drops.ts`: diagnostic.
  - `check-saved-readings.ts` (audit PR A5 sixth review): read-only count, per company, of customers confirmed from a pasted reading whose saved text reads as not exact today; since the A5 seventh review only a text that reads back to the saved point is judged, and customers placed on the map or with typed numbers are listed apart; owner-run before the A5 deploy ([5.12](#512-how-to-verify-a-deploy) step 13).
  - `grant-platform-admin.ts <email> [--tenant <company slug> | --no-tenant] [--allow-self-signup] [--revoke]` (PR1): the only way to grant or revoke platform admin; owner-run ([`docs/SECURITY.md`](./SECURITY.md) section 3). Since the review of 9 Oct 2026 (web-auth-security-2) it prints the account and its company first, grants only when `--tenant` names the account's own company (without it, a dry run), and refuses a company made through public sign-up (its `SIGNUP` audit row) unless `--allow-self-signup` is passed; an unknown option is refused.
  - Deleted in PR1: `seed-nmwc.ts` (hard-coded demo password, review L9) and `smoke-driver-flow.ts` (left driver-app residue in the `nmwc` tenant).

Rule 22: a solve whose worker processes cannot start is 503 `WORKERS_UNAVAILABLE` ("The planner is busy or restarting - try again in a minute."), and `/ready` reports the failed start (`workers`, `ok: false`) |

Skipped (SKIPPED / `ALLOWED_TRUCKS`, `_limits_decide`) while a stop's `allowed_truck_ids` leaves out a truck that can still take a load (small truck only customers, 13 Oct 2026: PyVRP 0.14 has no allowed vehicles per client) - the default `SOLVER_PYVRP_ALLOWED=skip`; with `model` (or `thorough`, Thorough solves only; 16 Oct 2026) it runs and models the lists: each truck's vehicle type and routing profile carry the stops it may not carry, every arc into and out of them is `PV_MAX_VALUE` (2^44, PyVRP's own "no edge") and every drive into them `FORBID_S` (2 x the horizon) longer, so such a visit always has time warp and is never feasible; penalties raised and started low; `worst_case` counts the forbidden arcs apart; profiles over 64 MB skip as `ALLOWED_TRUCKS` (`LimitsTooLarge`); `plan_of` refuses a stop on a truck it may not use (`INVALID_PLAN`); a day where no list decides anything builds the same model as before -, and (SKIPPED / `FULL_TRUCK`, `_full_truck_day`) while a stop fills a truck alone under the one-customer rule (13 Oct 2026: its model keeps every load at bays x Pallet fill). The model (every price from the engine's functions), the CPU gate, the stopping rule, the mapping back with validation, and its own stage job. See `OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md` §12 |

Imports neither PyVRP nor numpy. The engine side is in `dispatch_solver.py` (`_recommended_best_of`): with K > 1 the main search runs exactly as with one, in the solve's own pool; the other K-1 run in their own pool (`_start_extra_workers`: optional, pipe flags, the out-of-memory killer's first victims), each from another stop order (`_variant_worker`), ranked on the engine's own goal for RECOMMENDED (`_rank_variant`); THOROUGH joins them after `SOLVER_BEST_OF_JOIN_SEC` (never into the reserve), QUICK waits `QUICK_WAIT_SEC`; the alternatives start from the best-ranked plan, and a failed main search is replaced by the best other one |

### 2.6 Runtime architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Clients
    B["Dispatcher / admin browser<br/>client components"]
    D["Driver phone PWA<br/>/driver - retired, 410"]
  end
  subgraph WEB["apps/web - Next.js 14, exactly ONE replica"]
    MW["middleware.ts<br/>edge: login redirect"]
    RSC["Server Components<br/>app/t/[slug]/**/page.tsx"]
    API["Route handlers<br/>app/api/**/route.ts<br/>withTenantApi"]
    SVC["Domain logic<br/>lib/dispatch/*, lib/exports/*"]
    JOB["In-process job runner<br/>lib/jobs/dispatch-job.ts<br/>globalThis inflight Map"]
    JAN["Janitor every 60 s<br/>lib/jobs/janitor-loop.ts"]
  end
  DB[("PostgreSQL<br/>via Prisma, tenantDb")]
  subgraph SOLVER["apps/solver - FastAPI, private network"]
    EP["main.py<br/>/optimize-dispatch<br/>/route-geometry<br/>/health"]
    WK["Spawned worker processes<br/>OR-Tools routing + CP-SAT repack"]
  end
  OSRM["OSRM - infra/osrm<br/>/table /route /nearest<br/>no auth, private only"]
  HAV["Haversine x multiplier<br/>fallback, labelled Estimated"]
  EXT["Resend email, Sentry,<br/>Mapbox - all optional"]

  B -- "page requests" --> MW --> RSC
  B -- "fetch /api/* JSON, polls every 2.5-3 s" --> API
  D -. "retired: 410 Gone" .-> API
  RSC -- "tenantDb reads" --> DB
  API --> SVC --> DB
  API -- "202 + RunJob row" --> JOB
  JOB -- "POST /optimize-dispatch, X-Solver-Token, up to 600 s (QUICK) or the cap + 2 min (THOROUGH)" --> EP
  API -- "POST /route-geometry 15 s, GET /health 4 s" --> EP
  EP --> WK
  EP -- "/table blocks 45x45, 30 s x 2 tries" --> OSRM
  EP -. "OSRM_URL unset or failing" .-> HAV
  JOB -- "persist scenarios, apply RECOMMENDED" --> DB
  JAN -- "fail jobs with no heartbeat for 5 min, close shifts over 18 h" --> DB
  API -.-> EXT
```

**Request paths.**

1. **Pages.** `middleware.ts` checks the NextAuth JWT (and its 12 h absolute lifetime) at the edge and only redirects unauthenticated users; the database re-check of the user happens in the Node runtime (`lib/session-principal.ts`). The tenant layout `app/t/[slug]/layout.tsx` calls `getCurrentTenant(slug)`. That loads the tenant by slug, checks it against the session, and returns `{ tenant, user, db: tenantDb(tenant.id) }`. Pages then read through `db` directly.
2. **API.** Handlers are wrapped in `withTenantApi(handler, { role, rateLimitKey })` (`lib/api.ts`). In order, the wrapper:
   1. calls `auth()`, which re-checks the user, tenant and password against the DB (30 s cache): no session → 401; no tenant on the session → 403;
   2. applies the optional rate limit, only when `rateLimitKey` is passed (no route passes it today; the limited routes call `rateLimit()` themselves);
   3. checks the role rank → 403;
   4. builds `ctx = { user, db: tenantDb(session.user.tenantId), ip }`;
   5. maps Zod errors to 400 and Prisma P2002 / P2025 / P2003 to 409 / 404 / 400.

   The tenant of an API call always comes from the **session**; no API URL contains a slug. Much of `lib/dispatch/*` and `lib/jobs/*` uses the unscoped `prisma` client and passes `tenantId` explicitly in each `where`.
3. **Web → solver.** `lib/solver-client.ts` reads `SOLVER_URL` and `SOLVER_TOKEN` through `solverEnv()` (`lib/solver-env.ts`: trimmed, no trailing slash; the readiness check of `/api/health` reads them the same way) and sends the header `X-Solver-Token: $SOLVER_TOKEN`.
   - `callDispatchSolver()` uses `postJsonLong()` (`node:http` / `node:https`), not `fetch`. Node's undici `fetch` gives up after 300 s without response headers, and the solver sends nothing until the plan is ready. It waits `solverWaitMs` (`lib/dispatch/search-mode.ts`): 600 s for QUICK (`DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 600_000`), the THOROUGH cap + 120 s for THOROUGH (1,320 s with the 20-min cap), on its own connection with TCP keepalive ([2.8](#28-timeouts-budgets-and-limits)).
   - An HTTP 404 from the solver is reported as "optimizer is being updated", because web and solver deploy independently. For other errors, FastAPI's `{ detail }` is passed through (for example 504 `SolveAborted`).
   - (Third review of audit PR4) No call follows a redirect: `node:http` never does, and the road-line call and the readiness check ask with `redirect: 'manual'`, so the token never goes to the address a redirect names. A redirect fails the optimize call with a message that names `SOLVER_URL`, and `/api/health` answers `degraded` `SOLVER_URL_REDIRECTS`. A token that is not plain ASCII is not sent at all ([2.9](#29-environment-variables-by-service)), and (fourth review) neither is anything to a `SOLVER_URL` no call can use, such as one without `http://`.
4. **Solver → roads.** `resolve_matrix()` (`apps/solver/providers.py`) takes the OSRM URL from the request's `config.osrm_url` (from `TenantConfig.osrmUrl`) first, then from the `OSRM_URL` env var. If OSRM is not configured or fails, the plan falls back to Haversine distances labelled Estimated; it is never blocked. The web decides the provider before calling (`routingProviderFor()` in `lib/dispatch/customer-attrs.ts`). Details are in [4.5](#45-distance-and-time-matrix).
5. **Inside the solver.** The endpoint is `async` (29 Sep 2026): it runs the solve in a worker thread (`anyio.to_thread.run_sync`) and watches its caller; when the caller closes the connection (the web restarted, or its wait ran out) the solve is cancelled within about a second and its slot frees. `_run_scenarios()` solves RECOMMENDED first, then the two alternatives warm-started from it. Each scenario runs in a `multiprocessing` "spawn" pool, because OR-Tools holds the GIL and would otherwise freeze `/health`. `_post_solve()` then runs the CP-SAT load repack. The whole request must finish within `SOLVER_BUDGET_SEC` (540 s) for QUICK, before the web's 600 s wait, and within the THOROUGH cap (1,200 s) for THOROUGH, before the web's 1,320 s wait ([4.9](#49-worker-pool-budget-and-deadlines)).

### 2.7 Background job model

Optimization is asynchronous: the API answers **202** and the client polls. The detailed steps are in [3.6](#36-step-4-optimize); failures and the janitor are in [5.9](#59-job-failures-and-the-janitor).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant UI as Dispatch screen
  participant RH as Route handler
  participant SO as startDispatchOptimize
  participant DB as Postgres
  participant JOB as dispatch-job in web process
  participant SV as Solver
  UI->>RH: POST /api/dispatch/plan or /api/runs/:id/optimize or /replan
  RH->>SO: tenantId, runId, user
  SO->>DB: refuse if superseded, legacy or already applied
  Note over SO,DB: a job already QUEUED or RUNNING, or in the in-flight map, is not refused - the call returns 202 with that job and starts nothing new
  SO->>SO: buildDispatchRequest in plan-service.ts, then solve admission (quota, slot or queue)
  SO->>DB: one transaction - intake lock, plan row lock, checks again, RunJob QUEUED, RunPlan OPTIMIZING, audit OPTIMIZE_STARTED
  SO->>JOB: scheduleDispatchOptimize registers the promise in the inflight map
  RH-->>UI: 202 with runJobId
  JOB->>JOB: wait for a solver slot when queued
  JOB->>DB: RunJob RUNNING 20 percent, heartbeatAt every 30 s from now until the job ends
  JOB->>SV: POST /optimize-dispatch, waits up to 600 s (QUICK) or the cap + 2 min (THOROUGH)
  SV-->>JOB: RECOMMENDED, MIN_TRUCKS, MIN_DISTANCE scenarios
  JOB->>DB: transaction - plan row lock, still OPTIMIZING with this job? save master weights, persistDispatchResult, applyScenario RECOMMENDED, RunJob SUCCEEDED, audit OPTIMIZE_SUCCEEDED
  loop every 2.5 to 3 s while OPTIMIZING (10 s once a THOROUGH search has run a minute)
    UI->>RH: GET /api/dispatch/day or /api/runs/:id/plan
  end
```

- **Search modes (owner request 29 Sep 2026: "make sure the solver is giving an optimal solution even if it runs for 20 mins"; decision "night plans long, day re-plans quick").** Every job searches QUICK or THOROUGH (`RunJob.searchMode`, `lib/dispatch/search-mode.ts`). QUICK is the automatic search time by day size, exactly as before. THOROUGH lets the whole optimization take up to `THOROUGH_MAX_SEC` (20 min) and stops the recommended plan's search early once it stops improving ([4.9](#49-worker-pool-budget-and-deadlines)). OPTIMIZE, Re-plan and the late order's "Re-plan now?" ask which one, with the expected time; the choice is pre-selected by the plan's day in the company timezone (the rule same-day planning uses): THOROUGH for a plan made before its delivery day (the evening plan for tomorrow), QUICK on the day itself, so trucks are not held. The screens work the default out from the clock when the button is pressed (`searchModeNow`, with the company `timezone` the day and plan data carry), not from when they were loaded: skeptic review of the long-search PR, a day or plan screen opened at 23:50 for tomorrow and still open at 07:30 (nothing reloads it while nothing runs) pre-selected Thorough on the delivery day, said "This plan is for a later day" and left out the "for today" warning (`searchModeDefault` on the data is what the server computed at read time; `search-mode-midnight.spec.ts`). An API call that names no mode (a script, an older screen) searches QUICK, exactly as before. The mode goes into the request (`config.search_mode`, THOROUGH's cap as `config.max_search_sec`), the job, the `OPTIMIZE_STARTED` audit row and, with how long it searched and why it stopped (the solver's search report), into the saved plan: the plan screen, the job message, the Excel SUMMARY and ASSUMPTIONS. Never "optimal": "searched 14 min; stopped when it stopped improving". The report is always the recommended plan's search; when the dispatcher applies an alternative ("Use instead"), the screen and the Excel say that option's own search instead - "The MIN TRUCKS option is in use. It searched for up to 1 min for its own goal (the fewest trucks), after the recommended plan's search (Thorough: 12 min of up to 20 min; stopped when it stopped improving)." - from the option's `time_limit_sec` (`searchOptionOf`; `PlanDetail.searchOption`, `summaryJson.solver.limitSec`), and the Excel leaves out the recommended plan's progress points (skeptic review: the recommended plan's "stopped when it stopped improving" was shown as the alternative's, which ran to its own limit with no early stop). The SUMMARY "Route search" note gives the option's optimizer time ("MIN_TRUCKS option · optimizer time 75 s": its search and the load re-check), no longer "searched 75 s".
- **A same-day plan is timed from when its search really starts; THOROUGH from the end of its search (review of the long-search PR; ISSUE 6 for QUICK).** Same-day plans start from now ([3.11](#311-step-9-late-orders-and-plan-versions), `plan-from.ts`): no new load leaves before now + the turnaround, and loading counts from now. A THOROUGH search runs up to its cap before the plan exists, and may first wait for a solver slot behind another THOROUGH (up to 20 minutes more), so "now" at the button press was wrong: measured, a same-day THOROUGH lost 7-18 of its 30 preparation minutes, and one queued behind a night plan planned departures before it was saved. So for THOROUGH the start times the new loads from now + the cap (`retimeSameDay` in `plan-service.ts`, with `searchLeadMin` = the cap in whole minutes), and the job times them again when it really gets its slot (`runJob`, which also stores the request it sends): `shift_start_min` = start + cap + turnaround, `loading_from_min` = start + cap. The plan warning, the "Planned from" / "Loading from" ASSUMPTIONS rows and `PlanSettings.searchLeadMin` say so ("now 09:00 + up to 20 min Thorough search + 30 min preparation"). The loads are timed conservatively when the search stops early. A plan for a later day changes only when its job starts on the delivery day itself (after midnight): loading then starts when its search starts (QUICK) or ends (THOROUGH). **QUICK too (ISSUE 6, 7 Oct 2026):** it was sent exactly as built, so a Quick search queued at 09:05 that started at 09:20 (behind other solves, the admission queue or the plan's previous job) still let a load leave at 09:05; PR8 and the long-search PR had re-timed THOROUGH only. Every job now times its request again when its search really starts (`retimeAtStart` in `runJob`: QUICK from that moment, THOROUGH from it + the cap), again before each call after the optimizer's "busy" answer (`PREEMPT_RETRY`), and stores what it sends; the start hands the job its clock (the press + the time since: the wall clock in production). The start's own times stay in the `OPTIMIZE_STARTED` audit row; `builtAt` (the plan inputs' `capturedAt`) never moves. The hire what-if does the same at its real start (`runHireJob`, `retimeRequestAt`, also after being queued again or a "busy" answer; stored with `HireBasis.timedAt`), and **Use this plan** keeps those times ([3.19](#319-the-hire-suggestion)). The confirmation says it on the delivery day: the plan cannot be used, and its loads cannot be locked or dispatched, before the search ends.
- **Two starts for one plan.** A start while a job runs for the version (another dispatcher, a stale screen) starts nothing and answers 202 with that job, its own `searchMode` and `alreadyRunning: true` - also when the other start wins inside the start transaction. The day screen's toast is built from the answer (`optimizeStartedText`): "An optimization (Quick) was already running for this plan, so your choice (Thorough) was not applied. When it ends, re-plan with Thorough if needed." Before, the toast said "Optimizing (Thorough)" for the other dispatcher's Quick job.
- **Heartbeat (long searches).** From the start transaction until the job ends, the process running the job writes `RunJob.heartbeatAt` every 30 s (`HEARTBEAT_MS`, `lib/jobs/dispatch-job.ts`), also while it waits for a solver slot. The plan screen calls a job lost only 2 minutes after its **last sign of life** (heartbeat, else start, else creation; `lastSignOfLife` in `lib/dispatch/stuck-plan.ts`), and the janitor fails it 5 minutes after its last heartbeat ([5.9](#59-job-failures-and-the-janitor)). So a THOROUGH search running for 20 minutes - in this process or, during a deploy, in the previous one - is never shown as lost or reaped, and a job whose process vanished (a crash, out of memory, a kill) is found within 2 minutes and failed within about 6. Jobs from before heartbeats keep the old rule (15 minutes after they started).
- **Shutdown (a deploy during a solve).** `instrumentation.ts` registers `installShutdownHandler()` (`lib/jobs/shutdown.ts`): on SIGTERM or SIGINT every job this process runs is failed at once with "The server was restarted (an update) during this optimization. Nothing was saved - optimize again." (`failJob`: job, plan and audit row in one transaction; a re-plan version keeps the previous plan it holds), so the plan can be optimized again right away. The connection to the solver closes with the process, and the solver cancels that solve and frees its slot ([4.9](#49-worker-pool-budget-and-deadlines)). Next.js 14 exits on SIGTERM by itself unless `NEXT_MANUAL_SIG_HANDLE` is set, so without it the failure writes race the exit: set `NEXT_MANUAL_SIG_HANDLE=1` on Railway ([5.6](#56-deployment-on-railway)) and this handler owns the exit (at most 8 s of writes, then exit 0). Either way the heartbeat covers a job whose writes did not land. The handler fails what `scheduleDispatchOptimize` registered (`activeDispatchJobs`, from the moment the job is scheduled: waiting for a solver slot or searching). Skeptic review of the long-search PR: the shutdown tests filled that list by hand, so a job that never registered passed them all; `long-search-jobs.spec.ts` now drives real jobs (searching, and waiting behind another THOROUGH) and `instrumentation.ts`'s `register()` itself with a SIGTERM (checked: a job that does not register fails them).
- **Use the best plan found so far.** During a THOROUGH search a dispatcher (PLANNER or above since the owner decision of 5 Oct 2026; it was SUPERVISOR) can end the search early (`POST /api/runs/:id/stop-search`, audited `SEARCH_STOPPED`, `lib/dispatch/stop-search.ts`, the button under *Searching for the best plan* on the plan screen). The web asks the solver (`POST /optimize-dispatch/stop`); the search ends at the next plan it finds (usually within a second), the alternatives are skipped and the loads are re-checked with QUICK's time, and the job saves that plan as usual (its search report says `STOPPED`). Nothing is cancelled: the plan stays OPTIMIZING until the job saves it.

- **One job per plan.** `trackInflight(runId, …)` in `lib/jobs/optimize-job.ts` keeps an in-memory `Map` on `globalThis.__routeiqInflight`, shared with the instrumentation bundle. A second start for the same run returns the active job. Since PR3 the database decides, not this map: the start transaction locks the plan row and answers 202 with the job that won a race. Since audit PR4 (F09) a 202 always names a job the database still has QUEUED or RUNNING: never an ended job, and never "the in-flight map has something" alone (a job whose promise is just finishing after its commit is over; the new start is chained after it).
- **Guarded finalization (PR3, review F07 / ADD-JOB-AUDIT).** The result is saved in one transaction that first locks the plan row and checks that the version is still `OPTIMIZING` with this job as `currentJobId` and the job still `RUNNING`. Otherwise the result is stale (the version was superseded, reaped, or another job took over): the job is marked FAILED "Stale result" and the plan is not touched. `OPTIMIZE_SUCCEEDED` is written in the same transaction, so a saved plan can never be marked FAILED by a later audit error.
- **On failure.** `failJob()` fails only a job that is still QUEUED or RUNNING, and moves the plan to FAILED only while it is `OPTIMIZING` with this job as current (never over READY or SUPERSEDED); it writes an `OPTIMIZE_FAILED` audit row. Since audit PR4 (F09) the job, the plan and the audit row are ONE transaction that first locks the plan row (the order every plan writer uses: plan, then job): if any write fails nothing changes, and the job, still in progress in the database with no live process (its heartbeat stops with its promise), is failed with its plan by the janitor 5 minutes after its last heartbeat. A stale result is recorded the same way (job and audit row together). A re-plan version holds a copy of the previous plan ([3.11](#311-step-9-late-orders-and-plan-versions)), so after a failure it is FAILED but still usable. When the solver finds no plan at all (RECOMMENDED `NO_SOLUTION`) for a version that already holds a plan, that is a failure too and the plan is kept.
- **Solve admission (PR3, review F16).** `lib/dispatch/solve-admission.ts`, shared by every solve entry through `startDispatchOptimize`:
  - **Quotas:** 15 optimization starts per user and 30 per company in any rolling hour (429 `SOLVE_QUOTA_USER` / `SOLVE_QUOTA_TENANT` with `Retry-After`; only starts that created a job count).
  - **Concurrency:** `SOLVER_MAX_CONCURRENT` (default 2) solves at once in total, and per company one less than that, at least 1 (so 1 per company with the default, 2 with `SOLVER_MAX_CONCURRENT=3`). One company can therefore never hold every slot; waiting solves start fewest-running first, then in the order they were queued (fair order, below).
  - **Queue:** a start beyond the caps is not refused. Its job is created and waits (QUEUED, "Waiting: N optimization(s) ahead") until a slot frees. A company may have at most 2 solves of each search mode waiting (2 QUICK and 2 THOROUGH); one more of that mode answers 429 `SOLVE_QUEUE_TENANT` with `Retry-After` (120 s QUICK; THOROUGH the cap in use, at most 600 s) to that company only, naming the mode ("... 2 Thorough optimization(s) waiting ... (a Thorough search takes up to 20 min), or choose Quick" - the time is `THOROUGH_MAX_SEC`, never a fixed 20 minutes). Review of the long-search PR: counted together, two waiting THOROUGH night plans (each up to 20 minutes) refused a same-day QUICK re-plan with "try again once one of them has started". The shared queue holds 10 (`maxQueue`): once it is full, a company that already has a solve of that mode waiting gets 503 `SOLVER_BUSY` until there is room, but **a company with nothing of that mode waiting is always queued**, so other companies filling the queue never lock it out. Only the absolute cap of 200 waiting (`queueHardCap`, process memory) answers 503 to every start that would wait.
  - **Fair order:** a freed slot goes to the waiting solve of the company with the fewest solves running; among those, first come first served by when the solve was queued, whether or not its company ever ran one; so first come first served within a company. A company at its own concurrency cap keeps waiting. The guarantee: a company with nothing running is never overtaken by a solve queued after its own, so it waits at most for solves that were queued before it. It is only that: once the company runs a solve, solves queued later by companies running fewer start first, and at its own cap (1 with the defaults) its next solve waits for its running one to end; a second start while one of its solves waits can get 503 when the shared queue is full (third review of PR3: the docs promised "the next free slot" and "never refused"). `position()` estimates the place with the same rule, assuming the running solves end in the order they started.
  - **Per search mode (29 Sep 2026).** Every ticket is QUICK or THOROUGH, and the company caps are counted per mode, so a QUICK solve never waits behind a THOROUGH one (up to 20 minutes), only behind other QUICK solves and the total. THOROUGH solves run at most `thoroughConcurrent` at once over all companies (default one less than the total, at least 1) and one per company. With the default `SOLVER_MAX_CONCURRENT=2`: a night plan searching thoroughly holds one slot, and a same-day re-plan of any plan starts at once in the other (it waits only while another QUICK solve holds it); a second THOROUGH waits for the first; a THOROUGH waiting for its turn never holds up a QUICK queued after it. This relaxes "one company can never hold every slot" in exactly one case (its THOROUGH + its QUICK): another company's solve then waits for that QUICK solve only, and the next free slot goes to the company running fewer. `position()` assumes QUICK solves end before THOROUGH ones. With `SOLVER_MAX_CONCURRENT=1` a THOROUGH holds the only slot: run at least 2, and 3 (with the solver's `MAX_CONCURRENT_DISPATCH=3`) once the solver's CPUs are known.
  - Review of PR3: with the first defaults (2 per company = every slot, one shared first-come queue) a sign-up company could take both slots and all 10 queue places, and NMWC's OPTIMIZE got 503 or waited about 45 minutes. Second review: five sign-up companies with 2 waiting each still filled the queue of 10, so NMWC, with nothing waiting, got 503 for as long as they kept it full; and a company that had never run a solve won every tie, so a stream of fresh sign-ups went ahead of NMWC's waiting solve.
  - The solver itself refuses more than `MAX_CONCURRENT_DISPATCH` concurrent solves with 503 "solver busy" (defence in depth during a deploy overlap); the job then fails with "busy, optimize again in a minute".
- **Planner unavailable (rule 22, owner decision, audit policy 22; 30 Sep 2026).** When the solver cannot start its worker processes it refuses within seconds with 503 and the code `WORKERS_UNAVAILABLE` ([4.9](#49-worker-pool-budget-and-deadlines)), instead of searching inside its API process and freezing the planner for the whole search (20 minutes and more for THOROUGH). `callDispatchSolver` turns that answer (and only that one: the slots-full 503 keeps "busy with other plans") into `SolverError` with `code: 'WORKERS_UNAVAILABLE'` and the dispatcher's message **"The planner is busy or restarting - try again in a minute. Nothing was changed."** (`lib/planner-unavailable.ts`). `failJob` ends the job FAILED with that message and moves the plan to FAILED as for any failure, so the previous plan stays in use: a failed re-plan version keeps its copy of it, locked and planned loads unchanged, and the screen says "Optimization failed - previous plan kept" ([3.11](#311-step-9-late-orders-and-plan-versions)); a first optimization saves nothing. The `OPTIMIZE_FAILED` audit row and `RunJob.errorJson` carry `code: 'WORKERS_UNAVAILABLE'` (to find every refusal), and the web log gets the administrator's line `ALERT WORKERS_UNAVAILABLE: the route optimizer's worker processes could not start or stopped working, so it refused plan <id> (job <id>) ...` next to the solver's own ERROR line (the same 503 comes when the recommended plan's own worker process stops and cannot be replaced, or its search cannot start; when another worker stops while the recommended search runs, the recommended plan is kept, only the other options are skipped, and no refusal happens, [4.9](#49-worker-pool-budget-and-deadlines)); these log lines, the audit row and `/api/health` are all there is: nothing in the repository notifies anyone, so an administrator sees them only through log alerts or monitoring set up outside it; `/api/health` answers `degraded` `SOLVER_WORKERS_FAILED` while the solver's `/ready` reports the failure - at least 5 minutes, even if a retry works meanwhile ([5.8](#58-health-endpoint)). The job's solver slot, its admission ticket and its in-flight entry are released as for any failure, so OPTIMIZE (a first plan) or RE-PLAN (a plan in use) works again at once; there is no automatic retry, the dispatcher presses the button again (`planner-unavailable.spec.ts`).
- **Planning rules, phase A (owner decisions 29 Sep 2026; branch `planning-rules-break`).** (1) **Unloading finished by closing.** The web always sent `config.window_rule: 'FINISH'` (since 13 Oct 2026 the company setting `TenantConfig.windowRule` decides, FINISH by default: [4.4](#44-how-the-web-shapes-the-request)) with the TRUE closing time (`hard_end_min`); only the solver subtracts the stop time, in one helper (`load_repack.latest_start_s`, `pref_end_bound_s`) that the route search (cumul range, soft upper bound at preferred end - stop time, clamped at 0), `_window_prefilter`, the repack (`facts().hi`), the LP timing, `timing_ok` and `_build_scenario` (`hard_window_ok`, `pref_ok`, the window and early costs) all call. A stop whose unloading is longer than its receiving hours is dropped before the route model as `HARD_WINDOW_INFEASIBLE` ("Unloading takes 90 min, but the receiving hours 06:00-07:00 are only 60 min long: it can never finish before closing."; an empty time range would fail the whole model). `feasibility.check_scenario` re-derives the rule (departure <= closing; `CHECK_VERSION` 2). Every scenario echoes `window_rule`; the web takes the rule a load was planned with ONLY from that echo (`rulesFrom(..., echo)` sets `PlanRules.windowRule`, hashed only when set), so the web gate checks each load under its own rule: a load planned before the rule, locked or not, is never blocked after the fact, and a plan asked with the rule but made by an older solver gets a note (`plannerRulesNote`). An absent field means the earlier START rule at both ends, so any mix of old and new web and solver during a deploy is safe (deploy the solver first). (2) **Split deliveries:** every visit gets the customer's full base stop time plus the per-case time of its own cases (`stopService`; the 5-minute minimum per part is gone); `PlanSettings.splitStopTime: 'FULL'` and `windowRule: 'FINISH'` record what was asked. (3) **Driver shift by the dispatcher:** `PATCH /api/tenant/config` accepts PLANNER and up, but a non-admin may change only `DISPATCHER_SETTINGS_FIELDS` (first departure, shift maximum - shown as Latest return too - overtime after and the break, and since the data collection rules of 1 Oct 2026 the loading gate and the days ahead of the data to collect; 403 `ADMIN_ONLY_SETTING` otherwise) and gets back only those fields; Settings shows a dispatcher only the Driver shift card and the Customer data before loading card. Audited as every settings save. No migration and no production data change: after deploy the dispatcher sets First departure 07:00 and Latest return 18:00 (11 h) on Settings; overtime stays as it is ([`DISPATCHER_GUIDE.md`](./DISPATCHER_GUIDE.md), Driver shift). (4) **Latest return is absolute** (review; owner: "18:00 is the latest return"): the web sends `config.latest_return_min` = the tenant's first departure + shift maximum (never the same-day "now + turnaround" start); `_truck_hours` caps every truck's latest return at it (so the route search, the repack and the LP all hold it), `check_scenario` flags a later return as `SHIFT_LIMIT`, and every scenario echoes it (`PlanRules.latestReturnMin`, hashed only when set), so the web gate blocks only loads planned with it. On Settings, changing First departure keeps the Latest return (the shift maximum follows).
- **Planning rules, phase B: the driver break (owner decisions 29-30 Sep 2026; branch `planning-rules-break`).** One break of `config.break_min` per truck-day (one driver per truck per day), STARTING in `[break_start_from_min, break_start_to_min]` (Settings: Driver break, Break may start from, Break must start by; the dispatcher may edit them; migration `20261002090000_planning_rules_break`, default 0 = off until set), on the road between two unloadings or at the depot (it may overlap a reload), never while unloading; inside the shift, paid, counting toward overtime. **Needed by times, never by load status** (`dispatch_solver._break_state`, `feasibility._check_break`, web `breakProblem`): first departure (frozen loads included) before the window start and last return after its end; idle time before a same-day plan does not count (`break_lo_s` includes `loading_from_min`), so after the window a truck back from locked morning loads takes no new load. States: DUE, NOT_NEEDED, IN_FROZEN_LOAD (a recorded `FrozenTrip.break_start_min`, or a depot gap between locked loads), NOT_POSSIBLE (locked loads through the window, a warning only). **Solver:** the route search stays break-free with a search-only margin (span or end cumul minus the break on DUE trucks; `_search_day_end`, the same for the second search, PyVRP, whose hard windows also end at the latest start under finish by closing); `load_repack.time_truck` places the break exactly - the break-free LP as a lower bound (taken when it already meets the rule), then one LP per position (none needed, DEPOT before a load, ROAD after stop i incl. the first leg and the way back, never between two parts of one customer) until one reaches the bound; ties: none, depot, road; the road break starts right after the previous unloading; `timing_ok` checks it (return = last departure + drive + break on the way back). The repack tries the break-free CP-SAT model first and uses the break-aware one (depot interval + road-break variants picked by leg coverage, capped) only when time_plan cannot place every break in the proposal; a proven-infeasible break-aware model is retried with the break as a penalty. `_build_scenario` emits `PlannedLoad.driver_break`, the arrival after a road break, the return with a break on the way back, `TruckDayCostOut.break_status`, the `break_rule` echo and the NOT_POSSIBLE warnings; a raw search plan is never EXACT under the break rule, so the safety net re-times it (also at 0 min loading per case). `check_scenario` BREAK. Settings that cannot work (from after to, a break as long as the shift) plan no break with a warning (no 422) and are refused on save (`breakSaveProblem`). **Web:** `PlanLoad.breakJson` (written by `applyScenario`, sent back as `FrozenTrip.break_*`, copied into every version), `PlanRules.break` ONLY from the echo (hashed only when set, with the load's break), the gate BREAK (a missing break BLOCKs a planned load and flags a locked one frozen; a load planned before the rule, or one on the road, only warns), outputs: the load row and a BREAK row on the plan screen, *unloading until* per stop, Excel (Unloading column start-until, BREAK rows, the load header, the manifest note, TRUCK DAYS note, ASSUMPTIONS rows worded by the echo), the driver sheet (header, break row, unload until) and WhatsApp (unload until, the break line). Benchmark: [`OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md`](./OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md) section 13.
- **The hire suggestion's what-if (6 Oct 2026, [3.19](#319-the-hire-suggestion)).** After a job saved a plan that leaves orders out for the fleet's capacity, loads per truck or time, and the depot has hire options, the job (once its solver slot is free) starts a what-if: its OWN job, a `HireSuggestion` row (QUEUED, RUNNING with a heartbeat every 30 s, SUCCEEDED / FAILED / CANCELLED), never a `RunJob` of the plan, so no plan check, stuck-plan rule or OPTIMIZE / RE-PLAN ever waits for it. It uses the same solve admission as a **background** ticket (`reserveBackground`): no hourly quota, at most one waiting per depot-day (its key, `hireCheckKey`) and at most 5 per company (`BACKGROUND_TENANT_WAITING`), a waiting one starts only after every dispatcher's solve that can start; for a dispatcher's solve a running background ticket counts toward the total only, never a company cap, so a what-if yields only when the optimizer is really full, and then only the fewest that make room (`preemptFor`: the smallest set, the requester's own company's first, then the checks never stopped before - a check queued again after a stop is not the first stopped again, third review of the hire branch - then the newest). The preempted what-if's optimizer call is cancelled (the solver checks its control in the road-matrix phase too, `providers.MatrixCancelled`, so its slot frees within about a second), and it goes back to the queue once (its new ticket held at once: a failed write then ends it FAILED and gives the ticket back). A job - a dispatcher's or a hire check's - that took that slot, or started within `PREEMPT_SETTLE_WINDOW_MS` (60 s) of a preemption or of a running check stopped by its own job (`release({ abandoned: true })`: a new optimization of its day; third review), (`SolveTicket.mayMeetBusy`) takes the optimizer's "busy" answer again every 1.5 s for up to 90 s (`PREEMPT_RETRY` in `solve-admission.ts`, `dispatch-job.ts` and `hire-whatif.ts`; `plan-lifecycle.spec.ts`, `hire-flow.spec.ts`). A new optimization of the day stops the day's checks (`cancelHireChecksOfDay`); a SIGTERM (a deploy) ends the checks this process runs at once, FAILED (`failHireChecksForShutdown`, from `jobs/shutdown.ts` with the optimizations); one lost with its process otherwise is failed after 2 minutes without a heartbeat (`failLostHireChecks`, on every read and by the janitor). System endings are audited with no request IP.
- **Why exactly one replica.** The in-flight map, the rate-limit buckets, the solve admission and the plan map's road-shape cache all live in process memory. `README.md` and the header of `lib/jobs/optimize-job.ts` therefore require **exactly one web replica**. Plan correctness no longer depends on it: every plan mutator takes database locks (PR3, [3.14](#314-status-values-and-transitions)), which also hold across a Railway deploy overlap.
- **Janitor.** `instrumentation.ts` → `startJanitor()` (unless `ROUTEIQ_DISABLE_JANITOR=1`) runs `reapStuckJobs()` and `reapStaleShifts()` 5 s after boot and then every 60 s, with the hire suggestion's `failLostHireChecks()` (a check lost with its process) and `retireOneDayTrucks()` (one-day hired trucks whose day is over are set `active = false`; [3.19](#319-the-hire-suggestion)). It fails jobs orphaned by a redeploy: every push to `main` redeploys web and kills in-flight solves. At most every 10 min the same loop also runs the delivery outcome's sweeps, which complete loads (`completeReturnedLoads`) and delete data (`runDeliveryJanitor`: photo bytes, positions, idle daily drivers; [3.18](#318-delivery-outcomes-and-the-driver-page), [`admin.md`](./admin.md)). Every 2 min at most it also runs the operations-alert sweep (16 Oct 2026, `runAlertSweep` in `lib/alerts/sweep.ts`) for the companies that switched alerts on, each followed by its e-mail digest (`sendAlertDigest` in `lib/alerts/notify.ts`, which sends only with Resend set up and recipients saved, outside the quiet hours), unless `ROUTEIQ_DISABLE_ALERTS=1`. The same sweep, with the digest, can be triggered through `/api/cron/janitor`. (The analysis dataset, 19 Oct 2026) At most every 10 min, in its own try and before the GPS retention, the nightly job builds the facts of the day before from 03:00 company time, refreshes and freezes older ones and purges those past `analysisRetentionDays` (`runAnalysisJob` in `lib/analysis/job.ts`, at most 20 s per run; [3.22](#322-the-analysis-dataset-facts-kept-for-later-analysis)). (IVMS live link, 16 Oct 2026) The GPS retention also runs here at most every 10 min, in its own try, and the IVMS poller has its own 15 s timer (`startIvmsTimer`, not started without the `AYUN_*` variables or with `ROUTEIQ_DISABLE_IVMS=1`; [3.21](#321-gps-live-link-ayun-times-live-map-tracker-mapping)). Audit PR4 (F09): each job is reaped in one transaction with its plan and audit row, and the sweep then repairs plans left OPTIMIZING behind an ended job ([5.9](#59-job-failures-and-the-janitor)).
- **Stuck plans (audit PR4, F09).** A version is OPTIMIZING exactly while its current job is QUEUED or RUNNING; every way a job ends moves the plan in the same transaction. A plan found OPTIMIZING behind an ended (or missing) job - left by the old two-write janitor - is put back to FAILED with an `OPTIMIZE_FAILED` row, reason `STUCK_PLAN`, by the janitor sweep (`repairStuckPlans`) and first thing by every OPTIMIZE and RE-PLAN request for it (`repairEndedJobPlan`), which then start real work. (The screens disable OPTIMIZE and Re-plan while a plan is OPTIMIZING, so the janitor or the dispatcher's **Reset stuck plan** does it, and the plan screen says so; review of audit PR4.) A job lost by a restart (QUEUED or RUNNING, not in this process, no sign of life for 2 minutes: no heartbeat, start or creation since) can be failed at once by a dispatcher (PLANNER or above since 5 Oct 2026) with **Reset stuck plan** (`POST /api/runs/:id/reset-stuck`, audited `PLAN_RESET`, `lib/dispatch/stuck-plan.ts`); the plan screen says which case it is (`PlanDetail.stuck`). `getPlanDetail` asks the in-flight map once, before its read's snapshot starts (second review of audit PR4): a job that saves its plan and leaves the map while the plan is being read is still OPTIMIZING / RUNNING in that snapshot, and asked at the end of the read it looked "lost" (the *server restarted* line and **Reset stuck plan** for one reload).

### 2.8 Timeouts, budgets and limits

| Hop / item | Value | Where |
|---|---|---|
| UI polling while optimizing | 3 s (day view), 2.5 s (plan view); 10 s once a THOROUGH search has run a minute (the progress line "… - 6 min so far" ticks on the screen every 5 s) | `dispatch-client.tsx`, `plan-view.tsx`, `searchPollMs` in `lib/dispatch/search-mode.ts` |
| Web → solver `/optimize-dispatch` | **600 s** QUICK; **THOROUGH: its cap + 120 s** (1,320 s with the 20-min cap). Raw `node:http` (undici `fetch` gives up after 300 s without headers), its own connection (`agent: false`: no agent idle timeout) with TCP keepalive every 30 s. A reset connection (the solver restarted), a refused one and the wait running out fail the job in plain words, retryable (`solverCallFailure`) | `solverWaitMs` in `lib/dispatch/search-mode.ts`; `postJsonLong()`, `SOLVER_KEEPALIVE_MS` in `lib/solver-client.ts` |
| **THOROUGH cap** (whole solver request) | **1,200 s** (`THOROUGH_MAX_SEC`, web and solver; the web sends it as `max_search_sec`, the solver's own value is the ceiling). RECOMMENDED searches until `thorough_tail_sec` before the cap (at least QUICK's time), and stops early once it has not improved for max(300 s, 0.5 × the time searched so far), never before QUICK's time; the alternatives (at least 60 s) and the load re-check (30 s per CP-SAT solve) fit in the tail - below a 20-min cap both shrink in proportion to at most 30% of it, never below QUICK's (`thorough_tail`); one deadline for everything | `thorough_cap_sec`, `rec_limit_sec`, `thorough_tail_sec`, `StallRule` in `dispatch_solver.py` ([4.9](#49-worker-pool-budget-and-deadlines)) |
| Web → solver `/route-geometry` / `/ready` (readiness, audit PR4) | 15 s / 4 s (for the whole answer, body included, since the third review of audit PR4) | `GEOMETRY_TIMEOUT_MS`; `READY_TIMEOUT_MS` in `lib/health.ts` |
| Web → solver `/optimize` (legacy, unreachable) | 240 s | `SOLVER_TIMEOUT_MS`, `callSolver()` |
| **Whole solver request** | **540 s** | `SOLVER_BUDGET_SEC` (env override), `dispatch_solver.py` |
| RECOMMENDED search limit (automatic) | 5 s up to 25 stops, 20 s up to 120, then straight lines to 50 s at 150 and 150 s at 200 stops (175 stops: 100 s), 150 s up to 350, 240 s above (PR7: before, 20 s up to 200 stops jumped to 150 s at 201; so 121-200-stop days now get more and no day size gets less, an owner decision after PR7's first schedule had given 201-299-stop days less). The web always sends `time_limit_sec: null`, so `TenantConfig.solverTimeLimitSeconds` has no effect. The Settings page states the same schedule from `searchTimeSec` in `packages/shared-types/src/planner-bounds.json` (PR7 review), which a pytest checks against `auto_time_limit` for every day size | `auto_time_limit()`, `TIME_LIMIT_POINTS`; web copy `SEARCH_TIME_SCHEDULE` / `autoTimeLimitSec` in `lib/planner-bounds.ts` |
| RECOMMENDED fitted to the budget | min(limit, remaining budget − 20 s) | `_run_scenarios()`, `REC_OVERHEAD_SEC = 20` |
| RECOMMENDED backstop | 2 × limit + 60 s, capped at the budget end; when exceeded, `SolveAborted` → HTTP 504 | `REC_GRACE_SEC = 60`, `_await_worker()` |
| Alternatives (MIN_TRUCKS, MIN_DISTANCE) | half the limit (at least 2 s) when warm-started, plus 20 s grace; skipped with a warning if less than 2 s of budget remains | `_run_scenarios()`, `SOLVER_ALT_GRACE_SEC` |
| CP-SAT repack | each solve min(15, max(3, limit / 2)) s; stage deadline rounds × (job budget + extension + 2 s for a late closing recovery, `CLOSING_LATE_SEC`) + 20 s, no later than budget end − 2 s | `REPACK_CAP_SEC`, `REPACK_MIN_SEC`, `STAGE_GRACE_SEC`, `_post_solve()` |
| Solver → OSRM | Whole matrix within `MATRIX_BUDGET_SEC` (min(90 s, 20% of the budget); then estimates, labelled). Per attempt connect 2 s, read min(30 s, time left); 2 attempts, 1 s backoff, no retry without time; `OSRM_TABLE_TILE` coordinates per call (default 90; production can use 1000), `OSRM_PARALLEL` calls at once (default 2); snap limit 5 km (PR5, review F19) | `providers.py` (`OSRM_TABLE_TILE`, `OSRM_PARALLEL`, `OSRM_MAX_SNAP_M`), `dispatch_solver.py` (`matrix_budget_sec`) |
| Stops per optimization | at most 600 (422; the web answers 422 `TOO_MANY_STOPS` first); above 350 the optimizer adds a "Large day" warning (the web adds none) | `MAX_STOPS` in `dispatch_models.py` and `MAX_DISPATCH_STOPS` in `lib/planner-bounds.ts` (the 422s); `LARGE_DAY_STOPS` in `dispatch_solver.py` (the warning; the web's copy in `lib/planner-bounds.ts` only words the Settings "Effective planner values" line) |
| Health probes | web → solver `/ready` 4 s for the whole answer (audit PR4; an unreachable solver is `degraded`, not a failure); solver → OSRM 2 s, cached 60 s; Docker OSRM `healthcheck.sh` 4 s | `lib/health.ts`, `routing_status()` in `main.py`, `infra/osrm/healthcheck.sh` |
| Saving the plan | transaction timeout 120 s, `maxWait` 15 s | `lib/jobs/dispatch-job.ts` |
| Screen actions waiting for a plan row (load change, Use instead, re-plan, new plan, optimize start) | row / day lock wait 5 s (`SET LOCAL lock_timeout`), then 409 "Plan is being saved - retry" (`PLAN_BUSY`); load changes run in a 30 s transaction | `lib/dispatch/plan-locks.ts` (PR3) |
| Solve admission | 15 starts per user and 30 per company per rolling hour; `SOLVER_MAX_CONCURRENT` (2) concurrent in total and one less per company (at least 1), counted per search mode; THOROUGH at most one less than the total over all companies (at least 1) and 1 per company; at most 2 waiting per company **and mode** (then 429 for that company, naming the mode; `Retry-After` 120 s QUICK, THOROUGH the cap up to 600 s); a shared queue of 10 that refuses (503) only a company that already has one of that mode waiting; 200 waiting at most (then 503) | `lib/dispatch/solve-admission.ts` (PR3; modes 29 Sep 2026) |
| Solver concurrent solves | `MAX_CONCURRENT_DISPATCH` (2); more answer 503 at once. A solve whose caller disconnects (the web restarted) is cancelled within about a second and frees its slot | `apps/solver/main.py` (PR3; cancel 29 Sep 2026) |
| Solver re-timing for moves by hand (`/retime-truck-days`, PR M1) | at most `RETIME_BUDGET_SEC` (10 s) per check, its road matrix within `RETIME_MATRIX_SEC` (6 s; then estimated distances, labelled), at most `RETIME_BEST_TRIES` (24) places timed for a best place; `RETIME_MAX_CONCURRENT` (4) checks at once, then 503 "Route checks busy" with Retry-After 5 s; at most 6 trucks and 120 stops per check (422; 80 before v2, 25 Oct 2026). A best place for several stops or a whole load (v2) times at most `RETIME_BEST_TRIES` layouts in all, whatever the number of stops. With "allow anyway" (`relax`) the strict phase uses at most half of the time left after the road matrix (`RELAX_SHARE`, a constant) and the relaxed phase the rest; out of time, the answer says so and offers nothing to allow. One small LP per truck and break position, in the API process; no dispatch slot, no worker process. The web waits 20 s for it (`callRetimeTruckDays`, `RETIME_TIMEOUT_MS` in `lib/solver-client.ts`); a save re-checks within 10 minutes of its check (`PREVIEW_MAX_AGE_MS`); Check is limited to 30 a minute per user (`LIMITS.planEditCheck`) | `apps/solver/retime.py`, `main.py`, `lib/dispatch/plan-edit.ts` |
| Solver worker start (rule 22) | the pool starts before the road matrix and must run its first task within `SOLVER_WORKER_START_SEC` (30 s; about 0.5 s when healthy); a pool that cannot start (an `OSError`: at once) or whose workers die while starting (after the 30 s) is 503 `WORKERS_UNAVAILABLE`, never a search in the API process | `_start_workers` in `dispatch_solver.py` |
| Job heartbeat | written every 30 s while a job waits or runs | `HEARTBEAT_MS` in `lib/jobs/dispatch-job.ts` |
| Stuck job / janitor interval | a job with a heartbeat: 5 min after its last one (`STALE_HEARTBEAT_MS`), however long it has been running; a job from before heartbeats: 15 min after it started (`STUCK_JOB_MS`) / 60 s; (audit PR4) a plan behind an ended job is repaired at the next sweep (a plan without any job after 1 min, `STUCK_PLAN_GRACE_MS`); a lost job - no sign of life for 2 min (`JOB_LOST_AFTER_MS`) - can be reset by a dispatcher | `optimize-job.ts`, `janitor-loop.ts`, `lib/dispatch/stuck-plan.ts` |
| Shutdown (SIGTERM / SIGINT) | the jobs of the stopping process are failed at once, at most 8 s of writes, then exit (with `NEXT_MANUAL_SIG_HANDLE=1`) | `SHUTDOWN_FAIL_MS` in `lib/jobs/shutdown.ts` |
| Plan detail / export read | one REPEATABLE READ transaction, `maxWait` 5 s, `timeout` 20 s; it takes no locks (audit PR4, F21) | `PLAN_DETAIL_TX` in `lib/dispatch/plan-detail.ts` |
| Stale driver shift | 18 h | `SHIFT_STALE_MS` in `shift-janitor.ts`; `driver-auth.ts` |
| Web session | 8 h idle, **12 h absolute** (PR1); user re-checked at most every 30 s | `lib/auth.ts`, `lib/session-principal.ts` |
| Upload parse (order file, customer import, baseline) | (P5) **In its own process, never on the web's event loop: killed after `UPLOAD_PARSE_TIMEOUT_MS` (15 s) or at a heap of `UPLOAD_WORKER_MAX_HEAP_MB` (512 MB), and the file refused (400); at most `UPLOAD_PARSE_CONCURRENCY` (2) at once, then a wait of up to 5 s (8 waiting at most), then 503 with Retry-After 5; the answer it sends back at most 128 MB (`MAX_RESULT_BYTES`, each text sent once; P5 review), a larger one refused (400) the same way as a file that needs too much memory, and so is one with a row of more than 200 cells or more than 2,500,000 cells, checked in the web process before a row is built (P5 second review)** (`lib/upload-parse`). Before P5: no timeout (synchronous on the event loop; the 10 s timer before A1 could never fire). Bounded by the caps as well: 10 MB, 50 MB unpacked, 1,000 parts, 10 sheets, 50,100 rows read per sheet, and since the A1 review 200 columns, 2,500,000 cells (since the P5 second review for a CSV sent as text too), links over 200,000 cells, 10,000 comments, .xlsx / .xls / CSV only; since A1 v3 1,000 metadata entries of each kind and 1,000 comment authors; since A1 v4 a part SheetJS reads again (for another sheet, another spelling of its name, an external link listed again) counts again against every cap, and chart sheets are refused. The caps bound the work, not the time: in the web process (A1) a file just under them blocked every user for 5-11 s and took about 1 GB (measured then: an .xlsx of 50,000 rows x 49 columns 9-10 s, the same as CSV sent as Excel 7-11 s, ten sheets of 50,000 rows 5-6 s; NMWC's shape at the row limit about 2.5 s); P5's before / after figures are in its 7.4 block | `lib/upload-parse/`, `lib/csv.ts`, `lib/workbook-guard.ts` |
