| Driver sheets (PDF) | (Review M3) **In their own process, never on the web's event loop: killed after `PDF_RENDER_TIMEOUT_MS` (120 s) or at a heap of `PDF_RENDER_MAX_HEAP_MB` (1024 MB), and the pack refused (500, "print one truck or one load at a time"); at most `PDF_RENDER_CONCURRENCY` (2) at once, then a wait of up to 60 s (8 waiting at most), then 503 with Retry-After 30.** Before: no limit, on the event loop (the review measured a 150-stop day at 8-13 s with the web frozen for 4-7 s in one go, a 300-stop day at 13-26 s with 6-10 s; measured since in the renderer: 300 stops 7-10 s and 460 MB, 408 stops 12 s and 560 MB, one load about 1 s and 130 MB, the web's longest stall about 20 ms) | `lib/pdf-render/` |
| Railway health checks | 300 s | Railway dashboard |

The chain **solver budget 540 s < web wait 600 s** (QUICK) and **THOROUGH cap 1,200 s < web wait 1,320 s** is deliberate: a request never outlives its caller. Orphaned jobs are found by their heartbeat (lost after 2 min, reaped after 5), not by how long they ran, so a 20-minute search needs no longer janitor threshold; and a caller that goes away cancels its solve on the solver. Measured wall times on the maintainer's machine for all three options (`docs/OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md` §8.3): about 31–57 s for the 60–150-stop days (the syn60 days took 31–32 s) and 252–253 s for 300 stops. These were measured before PR7. Since then **121–200-stop days get more** search time (150 stops 50 s instead of 20, 175 stops 100 s, 200 stops 150 s instead of 20), so expect roughly 1.5 × the extra seconds more wall time there (about +45 s at 150 stops; about +3 min at 200, so a 200-stop day now takes about the 4 min a 201-stop day already took). No day size gets less than before (owner decision, PR7 review): 201–350 stops keep 150 s (a 240-stop day like the re-test's S03 still about 229 s), and up to 120 and above 350 stops nothing changed.

### 2.9 Environment variables by service

Names and purpose only. This is the complete list; `.env.example` has placeholders for the main variables only (not `RESEND_FROM`, the `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` and other Sentry variables, `ROUTEIQ_DISABLE_JANITOR`, `SEED_PASSWORD`, the test and script variables, the solver tuning variables or the OSRM image variables). Production values live in Railway. Which local file each process reads is in [5.2](#52-local-development).

**Web (`apps/web`).**

| Variable | Required? | Purpose / read in |
|---|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL` | yes | Postgres connection (`prisma/schema.prisma` datasource) |
| `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` | yes | JWT signing secret. next-auth reads it implicitly; app code never references it |
| `NEXTAUTH_URL` / `AUTH_URL` | yes (prod) | Public base URL. Reset links use `AUTH_URL`, else `NEXTAUTH_URL`; production refuses to build one without either (`lib/password-reset.ts`) |
| `DRIVER_LINK_SECRET` | no | (4 Oct 2026) The secret driver links (QR) are derived from (`lib/driver-link/token.ts`); unset = `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`, else `AUTH_SECRET`; none of them = driver links off (503 `DRIVER_LINKS_OFF`). **Rotating it (or `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` without it) makes every driver link answer "replaced"** until the dispatcher reopens the Link dialog or prints the sheets again (a new link is made then). Driver links use `AUTH_URL` / `NEXTAUTH_URL` as their base, else the dispatcher's own host |
| `SALES_LINK_SECRET` | no | (19 Oct 2026) The secret salesman links are derived from (`lib/sales-link/token.ts`); unset = the driver link's secret (`DRIVER_LINK_SECRET`, `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`, `AUTH_SECRET`); none = salesman links off (503 `SALES_LINKS_OFF`). Rotating it makes every salesman link answer "replaced" until the office opens the Salesman link dialog again; setting it keeps driver links untouched |
| `SOLVER_URL` | yes | Solver base URL (`lib/solver-client.ts`, `lib/health.ts`, both through `lib/solver-env.ts`). Spaces around it and trailing slashes are ignored (`http://solver:8000/` works; review of audit PR4). Missing: `/api/health` answers 503 `SOLVER_URL_MISSING` and a production boot logs a `[config]` error (audit PR4). It must be a full address, `http://<solver private address>:<port>` (or `https://`), typed as plain text: without `http://` (for example Railway's private domain pasted alone, `solver.railway.internal:8000`), with `http//`, a hidden character or a space in it, a user name and password, or a `?` or `#`, no call can use it, so `/api/health` answers 503 `SOLVER_URL_INVALID`, a production boot logs a `[config]` error, and the optimize and road-line calls send nothing (`solverUrlUsable()`; fourth review of audit PR4) |
| `SOLVER_TOKEN` | yes | Shared secret sent as `X-Solver-Token`, without spaces or a line break around it (`lib/solver-env.ts`; review of audit PR4). Plain ASCII only (letters, digits, punctuation): a hidden zero-width space, curly quotes or a non-breaking space pasted with it cannot be sent the same way by every call (third review of audit PR4). Local dev only: also the fallback for `JANITOR_TOKEN`. Missing, not plain ASCII, or refused by the solver: `/api/health` answers 503 (`SOLVER_TOKEN_MISSING` / `SOLVER_TOKEN_INVALID` / `SOLVER_TOKEN_REJECTED`), checked with the solver's `GET /ready` (audit PR4); the first two also log a `[config]` error at a production boot |
| `JANITOR_TOKEN` | yes (prod) for the manual janitor route | Auth for `/api/cron/janitor` (`X-Janitor-Token` / Bearer). In production it is the only accepted token (PR1); unset = every call refused. The in-process janitor does not need it |
| `OSRM_URL` | not read by the web since PR5 | The legacy Map tab goes through the solver (review F22); every map and plan uses the **solver's** `OSRM_URL`. A value left on web does nothing |
| `MAPBOX_TOKEN`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_TOKEN` | optional | Token passed to the map pickers and map pages (map tiles only; no Mapbox routing since PR5) |
| `RESEND_API_KEY`, `RESEND_FROM` | yes (prod) for reset emails and alert e-mails | Password-reset email via Resend. Without the key, production sends nothing and logs only the user id (PR1); development logs the link. `/api/health` reports `email`. (16 Oct 2026) Operations alert e-mails need BOTH (a verified sender: there is no default for them), the company on `ALERT_EMAIL_TENANTS` and the company's recipients under Settings; without them alerts show in RouteIQ only ([3.20](#320-operations-alerts)) |
| `SUPER_ADMIN_EMAILS` | optional | Comma-separated list. Since PR1 it grants nothing on its own: SUPER_ADMIN is honoured only for a user who also has the role, granted by `prisma/grant-platform-admin.ts`. Sign-up never grants it |
| `SIGNUP_MODE` | optional | `closed` turns public sign-up off (404, notices); anything else = open (the default, owner decision) (`lib/signup-policy.ts`) |
| `TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS`, `CLIENT_IP_HEADER` | optional | Client IP for rate limits and audit rows: the X-Forwarded-For entry this many places from the right (default 1), or a single-value header the edge sets (`lib/client-ip.ts`). Confirm once against a LOGIN audit row. If the IP cannot be resolved (`0`, or a header the edge does not send) the log warns once, audit rows have no IP and sign-in uses per-account limits only |
| `SENTRY_DSN`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`, `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT`, `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` | optional | Error reporting (`sentry.*.config.ts`, needs the DSN) and source-map upload at build time (`next.config.js`). Browser source maps are made only when `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_ORG` and `SENTRY_PROJECT` are all set, and are deleted from the build after the upload (the last step of `pnpm build` removes any `.map` left under `.next/static`), so they are never served (A1) |
| `ROUTEIQ_DISABLE_JANITOR` | optional | `1` turns off the in-process janitor |
| `ROUTEIQ_DISABLE_ALERTS` | optional | (16 Oct 2026) `1` turns off the operations-alert sweep (no new alert, no alert e-mail) whatever the companies' settings; the rows already raised stay readable ([3.20](#320-operations-alerts)) |
| `ROUTEIQ_DISABLE_ANALYSIS` | optional | (The analysis dataset, 19 Oct 2026) `1` stops the nightly facts job (nothing built, refreshed or purged); the rows already kept stay readable in the Analysis data export ([3.22](#322-the-analysis-dataset-facts-kept-for-later-analysis)) |
| `ALERT_EMAIL_TENANTS` | optional | (16 Oct 2026) The companies (their slugs, separated by commas or spaces) that may send operations-alert e-mail at all. Unset: none - signup is open, so without it any company could send to any address through our sender. Also the **Send test email** button needs it ([3.20](#320-operations-alerts)) |
| `ALERT_KEEP_FOR_ANALYSIS` | optional | (20 Oct 2026, owner decision pending) `1`: alert rows are kept until the company's analysis data retention (Keep analysis data, 730 days by default), their text, facts, note and Other texts removed 90 days after their date, so older causes and actions can still be counted. Unset (the default, as before the cause & action): every alert row is deleted 90 days after its date ([3.20](#320-operations-alerts), `lib/jobs/delivery-janitor.ts alertRowsKeptForAnalysis`) |
| `ROUTEIQ_DISABLE_IVMS` | optional | (IVMS live link, 16 Oct 2026) `1` stops all GPS tracking work whatever the company setting: no call to Ayun, the webhook answers 200 and stores nothing (`lib/ivms/env.ts`) |
| `AYUN_BASE_URL`, `AYUN_API_KEY`, `AYUN_TENANT_SLUG` | only for the IVMS link | The provider's origin (`https://<host>`, nothing else: RouteIQ adds the fixed API path and never follows a redirect), the user API key (server only, never logged, never stored) and the one company the Ayun account belongs to. Missing or unusable: no call is made, and the startup log names the variable (never its value) |
| `AYUN_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `AYUN_WEBHOOK_SECRET_PREVIOUS` | only for the IVMS webhook | The secret in the webhook URL's path (32-128 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -); the previous one is still accepted during a rotation |
| `AYUN_API_TIME_OFFSET_MIN`, `AYUN_WEBHOOK_TIME_OFFSET_MIN` | optional (0) | Minutes added to the provider's times of that channel when it does not send UTC (-720..720; Muscat local time would be -240). A bad API offset stops the calls (it would shift every time) |
| `FEASIBILITY_GATE` | optional (enforce) | (PR4, review F04) `warn` is an **emergency operator switch**: trucks whose times break a planning rule can then be locked, loaded and dispatched, and each such change records the violations in its `LOAD_*` audit row. Anything else, or unset, enforces the gate. A startup warning is logged while it is `warn` (`lib/startup-checks.ts`) |
| `KEPT_CHANGES` | optional (on) | (24 Oct 2026) The kept-load warning's **kill switch**: `off` (also `0`, `false`, `no`) stops listing locked and loading loads planned with older customer data - on Daily dispatch, the plan screen, the re-plan dialog and answer, and the audit fields, and the kept stop's "Changed after planning" hours rule reads as before - so every screen and sheet answers as before it existed (the RE-PLAN buttons still ask `GET /api/runs/:id/kept-changes` once, which answers null); read on every request (no restart). Anything else, or unset, keeps it on. A startup warning is logged while it is off, or set to a value it does not read (`lib/startup-checks.ts`) |
| `PLAN_EDIT` | optional (off) | (Moves by hand, 24 Oct 2026, [3.7](#37-step-5-reviewing-the-plan)) `off` (the default; anything else unknown counts as off, with a startup warning): no Move button, the routes answer 404 `FEATURE_OFF`; `check`: dispatchers can Check a move (the solver re-times it, nothing is written) but Save answers 409 `CHECK_ONLY`; `on`: Check and Save. Read on every request (`planEditMode` in `lib/dispatch/plan-edit-view.ts`), so a change needs no deploy of its own beyond the web restart Railway does on a variable change. A startup line says `check` / `on` (`lib/startup-checks.ts`). Rollback: `off` (no migration to undo; versions saved by hand stay as they are) |
| `PLAN_EDIT_OVERRIDES` | optional (on) | (Moves by hand, part 2 of 25 Oct 2026, [3.7](#37-step-5-reviewing-the-plan)) Allow anyway: only the value `off` turns it off. On: a check asks the solver what the change needs allowed by hand (a late arrival, capacity up to 20 % over the truck's own capacity, the driver break) and a SUPERVISOR or TENANT_ADMIN may save it with a reason. `off`: no relaxation asked, no allow-by-hand panel, a save with `overrides` answers 409 `OVERRIDES_OFF`, nothing is carried; allowances already stored are still honoured by the timetable gate, the kept-load box and the sheets, so switching it off never blocks a load. Read per request (`planEditOverridesOn`), named in the `PLAN_EDIT` startup line. Rollback: `off` (no migration). Rolling the web back to a release before part 2 while allowances exist: the old gate does not know them and refuses Lock / Loading / Dispatch of those trucks with `TIMES_NOT_VERIFIED` (fail-closed) - set `FEASIBILITY_GATE=warn` (audited) until the new web is back, or re-plan the day / unlock and re-plan those loads |
| `SOLVER_MAX_CONCURRENT` | optional (2) | Solve admission (PR3): how many optimizations run at once over all companies; one company may use one less (at least 1) per search mode, and THOROUGH solves at most one less than this over all companies; more wait in a queue (`lib/dispatch/solve-admission.ts`). Keep it at or below the solver's `MAX_CONCURRENT_DISPATCH`, sized to the solver's CPUs, and at least 2 (with 1 a THOROUGH search holds the only slot for up to 20 minutes). Set both to 3 to let one company run 2 solves at once |
| `UPLOAD_WORKER_MAX_HEAP_MB` | optional (512) | (P5) Heap cap in MB of the process that reads an uploaded file (`--max-old-space-size`, `lib/upload-parse/config.ts`). A file that needs more is refused "needs too much memory"; the process as a whole uses about this plus 100-150 MB. A whole number from 64 to 16384; anything else takes the default with a `[config]` warning at startup |
| `UPLOAD_PARSE_TIMEOUT_MS` | optional (15000) | (P5) Time limit of that process, from its start; then it is killed and the file refused "takes too long". 250 to 600000 |
| `PDF_RENDER_MAX_HEAP_MB` | optional (1024) | (Review M3) Heap cap in MB of the process that makes the driver sheets (`--max-old-space-size`, `lib/pdf-render/config.ts`). A pack that needs more is refused "needs too much memory"; a whole day of 300-400 stops used about 460-560 MB for the whole process (its heap under 256 MB), one load about 130 MB. 128 to 16384; anything else takes the default with a `[config]` warning at startup |
| `PDF_RENDER_TIMEOUT_MS` | optional (120000) | (Review M3) Time limit of that process, from its start; then it is killed and the pack refused "takes too long to make". 1000 to 600000 |
| `PDF_RENDER_CONCURRENCY` | optional (2) | (Review M3) Such processes at once in one web process; a further pack waits up to 60 s, then gets 503 "RouteIQ is making other driver sheets right now". 1 to 16. The web service's memory must hold its own plus this many whole-day packs (about 600 MB each) next to the upload parsers ([5.6](#56-deployment-on-railway)) |
| `UPLOAD_PARSE_CONCURRENCY` | optional (2) | (P5) Such processes at once in one web process; a further upload waits up to 5 s, then gets 503 "RouteIQ is reading other files right now". 1 to 16. The web service's memory must hold its own plus this many times (heap cap + about 150 MB) ([5.6](#56-deployment-on-railway)) |
| `THOROUGH_MAX_SEC` | optional (1200) | How long a THOROUGH optimization may take in all, 10 s to 60 min (`lib/dispatch/search-mode.ts`): sent to the solver as `max_search_sec`, stated on the screens, and the web waits it + 2 min. A same-day THOROUGH plan's new loads count from its start + this. Set the solver's to the same value (the solver uses the lower one). Keep it at 10 min or more in production: below a cap of about 2-2.5 min for NMWC's days (up to 120 stops), up to 9.5 min above 350 stops, THOROUGH searches no longer than QUICK and may skip the alternatives ([4.9](#49-worker-pool-budget-and-deadlines), per day size). CI sets 60 |
| `NEXT_MANUAL_SIG_HANDLE` | recommended on Railway (`1`) | Next.js then leaves SIGTERM to the app: the shutdown handler fails this process's optimizations in progress (plain message, retryable) before it exits (`lib/jobs/shutdown.ts`). Without it Next exits at once and those writes may not land (the heartbeat then fails the jobs within about 6 minutes) |
| `RATE_LIMITS_DISABLED` | tests only | `1` bypasses the in-memory limiter (CI sets it) and the hourly solve quotas (PR3; the concurrency caps stay on); `NODE_ENV=test` bypasses them too. Ignored on Railway, and logged as an error on any other production server outside CI (PR1) |
| `NODE_ENV`, `NEXT_RUNTIME`, `PORT` | set by the platform | Log level and limiter bypass; instrumentation branch; Railway port |
| `SEED_PASSWORD` | seed only | Demo logins in `prisma/seed-nmwc-dispatch.ts` |
| `TEST_BASE_URL`, `TEST_EXPECT_OSRM` | tests only | Integration test target; assert road distances |

**Solver (`apps/solver`).**

| Variable | Required? | Purpose / read in |
|---|---|---|
| `SOLVER_TOKEN` | yes | Must equal the web's value. If unset, every protected endpoint returns 500 (`main.py`), and the web's `/api/health` answers 503 `SOLVER_NOT_CONFIGURED` (audit PR4) |
| `OSRM_URL` | strongly recommended | OSRM base URL for the matrix, geometry and the `/health` routing probe (`providers.py`). Unset means Haversine, labelled Estimated. The legacy `distance.py` has no public default either since PR1 |
| `OSRM_MAX_SNAP_M` | optional (5000) | Beyond this snap distance a point uses estimated legs |
| `OSRM_TABLE_TILE` | optional (90) | Coordinates per OSRM `/table` call (PR5). Raise it up to the OSRM server's `--max-table-size` (1000 in `infra/osrm`) so a normal day needs one call |
| `OSRM_PARALLEL` | optional (2, max 4) | `/table` calls in flight at once when a matrix needs several (PR5) |
| `MATRIX_BUDGET_SEC` | optional (min(90, 20% of the budget)) | Road routing time within the request; after it the matrix is estimated with a "road routing too slow" warning (PR5) |
| `SOLVER_BUDGET_SEC` | optional (540) | Whole-request time budget (QUICK) |
| `THOROUGH_MAX_SEC` | optional (1200) | The ceiling of a THOROUGH request's time budget, 10 s to 60 min; a request's `max_search_sec` may only lower it (`thorough_cap_sec`). Below 20 min the alternatives and the load re-check shrink in proportion (`thorough_tail`); keep 10 min or more in production |
| `THOROUGH_STALL_SEC`, `THOROUGH_STALL_SHARE` | optional (300, 0.5) | THOROUGH stops RECOMMENDED's search once it has not improved for max(`THOROUGH_STALL_SEC`, `THOROUGH_STALL_SHARE` × the time searched so far), never before QUICK's time (`stall_rule`; the values are measured in `docs/OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md` §11). Tests use small values |
| `SOLVER_ALT_GRACE_SEC` | optional (20) | Worker grace for alternative scenarios |
| `SOLVER_BEST_OF`, `SOLVER_BEST_OF_QUICK` | optional (**1**: off) | (16 Oct 2026) Best-of-N route search (`best_of.py`): how many times RECOMMENDED's search runs at once, 1 to 8, for a THOROUGH and a QUICK solve. 1 (the default; also any value that cannot be read or is out of range) is one search, exactly as before. The main search stays the one-search search; the other K-1 run in their own optional pool from other stop orders, and their plans only add load re-check candidates, used only with a gain the dispatcher can see (4.11). Capped by the CPU gate (effective CPUs // `MAX_CONCURRENT_DISPATCH`, one kept for PyVRP). Off by default (owner decision 16 Oct 2026) until a replay of saved real requests with `scripts/bench_search.py` (arm `best_of` against `base`) passes the tool's pre-written rule and shows a gain (`RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT.md` has how to run it and the rollback triggers); read on every solve, shown in `/ready` (`best_of`) and the startup line (which names a value it could not read). A production switch: change it only outside planning hours (a variable change restarts the solver) |
| `SOLVER_BEST_OF_SOURCES`, `SOLVER_BEST_OF_JOIN_SEC`, `SOLVER_BEST_OF_STRATEGIES` | **benchmarks and development only** (1, 60, `PARALLEL_CHEAPEST_INSERTION`) | Best-of-N with K > 1 only: how many of the other searches' plans go to the load re-check (0 to 2, never more than K-1; each keeps one more repack cap free, taken from RECOMMENDED's limit); THOROUGH, how long the other searches may go on after the main one ended (0 to 300 s, never into the alternatives' and re-check's reserve); the other searches' first-solution strategies (comma-separated, from `best_of.STRATEGY_WHITELIST`; others can be very slow on large days). Production sets only `SOLVER_BEST_OF` |
| `SOLVER_PRIORITY_REPAIR` | optional (**off**) | `on` (also `1`, `true`, `yes`): after the load re-check, a P1-P3 stop left out while a lower priority rides is put back in its place where it fits (`_repair_inversions`, at most 10 s per solve; 4.11). Off by default (owner decision 16 Oct 2026) until a replay of saved real requests with it on and off shows what it does (`scripts/bench_search.py`, arm `repair_on` against `base`, and its pre-written rule passes); read on every solve, so setting it is a restart only; another value is off, and the startup line names it |
| `SOLVER_JOIN_TRIPS` | optional (**off**) | (24 Oct 2026) Join small trips (`join_trips.py`, 4.11): `off` (the default and the kill switch; also `0`, `false`, `no` and any value it cannot read) / `report` (computed, built and checked, reported in `search.join_trips`; plans unchanged, no note) / `on` (also `1`, `true`, `yes`: a company truck's small load rides on its other loads when that passes every check, with the note "Small loads joined after the load re-check: ..."). Moves onto another truck are reported only. Never on the hire check's what-if (SKIPPED `HIRE_CHECK`). Read on every solve, shown in `/ready` (`join_trips`) and the startup line (which names a value it could not read). Rollout: deploy unset, then `report` for at least 5 planning days (read `RunJob.responseJson->search->join_trips`), then `on` once no option was `NOT_VERIFIED` or `ERROR` (`status` `FAILED`) and a dispatcher has looked at 3 days the report would have joined (each change's `stops_after`: the truck's loads as the join would make them); change it only outside planning hours (a variable change restarts the solver) |
| `SOLVER_PYVRP` | optional (`on`) | The second route search (PyVRP): `on`, `off` (also `0`), or `thorough` (Thorough solves only). Its reason shows in `/ready` (`pyvrp`) and the startup line |
| `SOLVER_PYVRP_ALLOWED` | optional (`skip`) | (16 Oct 2026) The second search on a day where a small-truck-only customer's list leaves out a truck that can still load: `skip` (the default, and any other value: SKIPPED / `ALLOWED_TRUCKS`, as since 13 Oct 2026), `model` (it runs with the lists modelled, `pyvrp_candidate.build_model`, on every solve, hire checks included) or `thorough` (the same on Thorough solves only; enable this one first). Read on every solve; a change is a restart, so never during planning. Shows in `/ready` (`pyvrp.allowed`) and, when not `skip`, at the end of the PyVRP startup line. Turn on only after a replay of saved real requests passes (`scripts/bench_search.py`, arm `pyvrp_model` against `base`; the plans of such days change) |
| `SOLVER_PYVRP_MIN_CPUS` | optional (2) | CPU gate: the second search runs only with at least this many effective CPUs (affinity, capped by the container's cgroup quota) |
| `SOLVER_PYVRP_SEED`, `SOLVER_PYVRP_STOP_GRACE_SEC` | optional (1, 10) | PyVRP's seed; how long a solve waits for its answer after telling it the engine's searches ended |
| `SOLVER_PYVRP_MAX_ITERS`, `SOLVER_PYVRP_STALL_SEC`, `SOLVER_PYVRP_STALL_SHARE` | **tests and development only** | Stop PyVRP after N iterations; Thorough, once the engine's searches ended: stop when its last better plan is older than max(STALL_SEC, STALL_SHARE x its search time) (defaults 30 s and 0.1) |
| `SOLVER_PARALLEL` | **tests and local debugging only** | `0` solves in-process with no worker processes: **no deadline and no time budget at all** (nothing keeps a solve under the web's 600 s), and `/health` blocks while solving. `main.py` logs a warning at startup when it is set, an error on Railway (PR4). Never set it on a deployed solver |
| `SOLVER_ALLOW_INPROCESS_FALLBACK` | **tests and local development only** (rule 22) | Exactly `1`: a worker pool that cannot start makes the solve run in-process, as before rule 22 (no deadline, the API frozen for the search). Unset (production): such a solve is refused within seconds with 503 `WORKERS_UNAVAILABLE`. `main.py` logs a warning at startup when it is set, an error on Railway. Never set it on a deployed solver |
| `SOLVER_WORKER_START_SEC` | optional (30) | Rule 22: how long a new worker pool may take to run its first task before the solve is refused (1 to 600 s) |
| `MAX_CONCURRENT_DISPATCH` | optional (2) | At most this many `/optimize-dispatch` solves at once; another one is refused at once with 503 "solver busy" (PR3, `main.py`). Size it to the solver's CPUs (each solve uses up to 3 OR-Tools processes, plus K-1 with best-of-N (`SOLVER_BEST_OF`, off by default) and one for the PyVRP second search) and keep the web's `SOLVER_MAX_CONCURRENT` at or below it |
| `RETIME_MAX_CONCURRENT`, `RETIME_BUDGET_SEC`, `RETIME_MATRIX_SEC`, `RETIME_BEST_TRIES` | optional (4, 10, 6, 24) | (Moves by hand, PR M1) `/retime-truck-days` (`retime.py`): checks at once (1-16, read once at startup; more answer 503), seconds per check (1-60), seconds of road routing within it (1-30; then estimated distances, labelled), places timed for a best place (1-200). The last three are read on every check. A value that cannot be read, or is out of range, takes its default and is named in the startup line `Re-timing for moves by hand (...)`; `/ready` shows the values in use (`retime`). v2 adds no setting: the lateness penalty of "allow anyway" (`load_repack.RELAX_LATE_OMR_PER_MIN`, 5 OMR a minute) and the strict phase's share of the budget (`retime.RELAX_SHARE`, 0.5) are constants, and the 20% that may be allowed over a truck's capacity is the web's (`capacity_factor` in each request) |
| `MAPBOX_TOKEN` | legacy only | Mapbox matrix for legacy `/optimize` (`distance.py`) |
| `PORT` | optional (8000) | uvicorn port (Dockerfile `CMD`) |
| `ROUTEIQ_TEST_{HANG,FAIL,KILL}_SCENARIO`, `ROUTEIQ_TEST_{FAIL,HANG}_REPACK`, `ROUTEIQ_TEST_WORKER_START_EXIT`, `ROUTEIQ_TEST_{HANG,FAIL,KILL,NO_STALL}_VARIANT` | **tests only** | Fault-injection hooks in `dispatch_solver.py`; must never be set in production |
| `BENCH_TIME_LIMIT` | script only | `scripts/bench_day1.py` |

**OSRM (`infra/osrm`).** Runtime variables: `PORT` (5000), `OSRM_BIND` (`0.0.0.0`; `::` on Railway for IPv6), `MAX_TABLE_SIZE` (1000). Build args: `OSRM_IMAGE`, `PBF_URL`, `BBOX`, `PROFILE`, `MAP_REFRESH` (cache-buster for the monthly refresh).

**CI.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` sets `DATABASE_URL`, `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`, `NEXTAUTH_URL`, `SOLVER_URL`, `SOLVER_TOKEN`, `JANITOR_TOKEN`, `RATE_LIMITS_DISABLED`, `SIGNUP_MODE=open`, a test `SUPER_ADMIN_EMAILS` and `THOROUGH_MAX_SEC=60` (so `tests/integration/long-search.spec.ts` runs a THOROUGH optimization end to end in a minute) at job level, with throwaway CI-only values.

### 2.10 Multi-tenancy, authentication and roles

**Tenant isolation: `tenantDb(tenantId)` in `lib/tenant.ts`.**

- **How it works.** It is a Prisma client extension (`prisma.$extends({ query: { $allModels: { $allOperations } } })`). For every model in `TENANT_SCOPED_MODELS`, it merges `tenantId` into:
  - `where` for `find*`, `count`, `aggregate`, `groupBy`, `update*`, `delete*` and `upsert`;
  - `data` for `create`, `createMany` and `upsert`.
- **Scoped models (31 named here):** TenantConfig, Depot, Truck, Driver, Region, Customer, Product, UploadBatch, Order, RunPlan, RunJob, ManualBaseline, AuditLog, DriverShift, TruckLocation, DeliveryProof, PlanLoad, CustomerTypeProfile, IntakeLineKey, (4 Oct 2026) DriverLink, StopVisit, StopEvent, DeliveryPhoto, (6 Oct 2026) HireOption, HireSuggestion, DriverLeave, (13 Oct 2026) Helper, PlanLoadHelper, (16 Oct 2026) OpsAlert, OpsAlertDigest, and (19 Oct 2026) SalesLink; the list in `lib/tenant.ts` (40) also holds the IVMS tables (TruckPosition, TruckTrailPoint, IvmsEvent, IvmsState, IvmsTruckDay) and the analysis facts (FactTruckDay, FactVisit, FactLeg, FactDepotTurn).
- **Guard.** An empty `tenantId` throws.
- **Not covered by the wrapper:**
  - `Tenant`;
  - `User` and `PasswordResetToken`: both have a `tenantId` column but are filtered by hand (for example `where: { tenantId }` in `app/api/users/route.ts`);
  - child tables without a `tenantId` column: `OrderLine`, `ScenarioResult`, `RouteAssignment`, `ManualBaselineAssignment`, `UnservedOrder`. They are reached through a tenant-checked parent or filtered with `where: { run: { tenantId } }`;
  - raw SQL (`$queryRawUnsafe` / `$executeRawUnsafe`). The janitor uses raw SQL on purpose, across all tenants;
  - code that imports `prisma` directly. That includes most of `lib/dispatch/*`, `lib/jobs/*` and `lib/driver-auth.ts`, which pass `tenantId` by hand.
- **Resolving the tenant.**
  - Pages use `getCurrentTenant(slug)`. A session is required (without one the browser goes through `/api/auth/end-session` to `/login`), the tenant must exist and be active, and the slug must match `session.user.tenantId` unless the user is SUPER_ADMIN. Any mismatch → `notFound()`, i.e. 404 rather than 403, so tenant existence does not leak. A SUPER_ADMIN viewing another tenant writes one `CROSS_TENANT_VIEW` audit row there per hour (PR1).
  - API routes use `withTenantApi`, which takes the tenant from the session.
- **Tests.**
  - `tests/tenant-isolation.spec.ts` covers Depot, Product, Region, Customer, Truck, AuditLog, TenantConfig, `updateMany`/`deleteMany`, the delivery outcome tables, DriverLeave (6 Oct 2026: reads, writes and the leave of a delivery day), and the empty-tenantId guard.
  - `tests/integration/cross-tenant.spec.ts` is the HTTP-level matrix.
  - `lib/tenant.ts` exports `_internal.TENANT_SCOPED_MODELS` "to prevent drift", but no test uses it.

**Authentication.**

- **Dispatchers and admins** (`lib/auth.ts`):
  - NextAuth v5 beta with a single **Credentials** provider. `verifyCredentials` (`lib/auth-credentials.ts`, PR1): Zod checks the email and password; the user is looked up by lowercase email; the password is checked with bcrypt (cost 12 in `hashPassword`), with a throw-away compare for unknown emails; the user and the tenant must be active; soft throttles per IP + email and per IP; one generic error.
  - `session.strategy = 'jwt'`, `maxAge` 8 h (idle), **12 h absolute** (PR1), `trustHost: true`, sign-in page `/login`.
  - The `jwt` callback stores `userId`, `tenantId`, `role`, `pwf` and `authTime` at sign-in. **Since PR1 every later session read in Node re-checks the user** (`lib/session-principal.ts`, 30 s cache): an inactive user or tenant, a changed tenant or a changed password ends the session, and role/tenant come from the DB. The edge middleware checks only the lifetime. The `session` callback copies the claims onto `session.user`. Details: [`docs/SECURITY.md`](./SECURITY.md).
  - The `signIn` event writes a `LOGIN` audit row (skipped for users without a tenant).
  - Handlers are mounted at `app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts`. The middleware matcher excludes `api/auth` and `api/health`.
- **Signup** (`app/api/auth/signup/route.ts`) is public (owner decision: stays open; `SIGNUP_MODE=closed` turns it off) and rate-limited. In one transaction it creates the Tenant, a TenantConfig (OSRM for Oman/UAE, otherwise HAVERSINE) and the first user, always a TENANT_ADMIN.
- **Password reset:** `lib/password-reset.ts` with `app/api/auth/{forgot,reset}` (email link), and the admin reset `app/api/users/[id]/reset-password` (Users screen, "Reset password": a one-time password shown once; works without email).
- **Change password** (owner request 24 Oct 2026: every user changes their password): every signed-in user, every role and a platform admin without a company too, changes their OWN password from the user menu (top bar of the tenant pages, header of `/admin`): `POST /api/account/password` (`withAccountApi`, `lib/own-password.ts`, rules in `lib/password-rules.ts`). The current password is checked with bcrypt and wrong ones are throttled per user; the hash is replaced in one transaction under the same per-user lock as the resets, only while it is still the one checked; reset links are retired; a `PASSWORD_CHANGED` audit row. The session design sets the password fingerprint only at sign-in, so every open session ends, the caller's too: the dialog signs out to `/login?reason=password` ("Your password is changed").
- **Drivers** have no User accounts. The legacy driver phone app (PIN login, `DriverShift` session tokens, `lib/driver-auth.ts`) is **retired** since PR1: its routes answer 410 and the migration `20260926090000_retire_driver_app_scrub_secrets` ended the open shifts and cleared the PIN hashes. Drivers work from the PDF sheets and WhatsApp.
- **Service to service.**
  - Solver endpoints other than `/health` require `X-Solver-Token` (`_check_token()` in `apps/solver/main.py`, `hmac.compare_digest` on bytes).
  - `/api/cron/janitor` requires `JANITOR_TOKEN` (outside production `SOLVER_TOKEN` as the fallback), compared with `constantTimeEqual()` (`lib/janitor-auth.ts`).
  - OSRM has no authentication and relies on private networking.

**Roles.** `enum Role` is in `schema.prisma`. The ranks are in `RANK` in `lib/rbac.ts`, duplicated as `ROLE_RANK` in `lib/api.ts`. The check is hierarchical: a role passes when `rank(user) >= rank(required)`.

| Role | Rank | Can do (as enforced in code) |
|---|---|---|
| `SUPER_ADMIN` | 100 | Everything. `/admin` page. Pages may cross tenants (`getCurrentTenant`, audited as `CROSS_TENANT_VIEW`), but API calls still use the session's own tenant. Since PR1 granted only by the owner-run `prisma/grant-platform-admin.ts` **and** honoured only while the email is in `SUPER_ADMIN_EMAILS`; sign-up and the tenant UI cannot grant it, and a TENANT_ADMIN cannot change such an account |
| `TENANT_ADMIN` | 80 | Master data CRUD (depots incl. hours, trucks - every field; the dispatcher may change only the usual driver since 6 Oct 2026 -, cost per load, km per litre, max loads and availability - PR5 -, a driver's code and delete (deactivate), regions, products), delete customers, users, tenant settings (PR5: incl. the planner economics - driver cost per hour, overtime, fuel, road factor, preferred-window penalty, cutoff); audit, onboard, users and settings pages and (PR1) their read APIs (`canManageMasterData`; sidebar `ADMIN_ONLY` in `lib/nav.ts`) |
| `SUPERVISOR` | 60 | Everything PLANNER can do, plus the job debug JSON (`canApproveOverride`: the solver request holds revenue and margins; support data, not dispatch work). Until the owner decision of 5 Oct 2026 also dispatch/complete loads, legacy run dispatch/unlock, **Reset stuck plan** and **Use the best plan found so far** |
| `PLANNER` | 50 | **The dispatcher** (owner decision 4 of 5 Oct 2026: "the dispatcher is the planner; he just doesn't have the privileges of an admin like changing a location"). Upload/confirm orders; create/edit customers and set a location a customer does not have (a saved location stays the admin's); optimize, re-plan (with the location / weight overrides), late orders, delivery times, choose scenario; every load status change - Lock, Loading, Dispatch, Back to locked, Unlock, Completed - and the driver per load; Record outcome, driver links, daily drivers, Bring forward and its undo, the Delivery actuals Excel; **the Drivers page** (owner request 6 Oct 2026: add drivers, edit name / phone / Active, make a daily driver regular, enter driver leave with a cover driver, set or clear a truck's usual driver - only that truck field, `truckFieldsRefused` / `driverChangesRefused` in `lib/rbac.ts`); **Reset stuck plan** and **Use the best plan found so far**; legacy run dispatch/unlock, route edits and baseline (`canPlan`; the plan screens pass it as `canDispatch`) |
| `VIEWER` | 10 | Read-only: every GET endpoint without a role option, and the tenant pages |

## 3. Daily dispatch process flow

This section follows one NMWC delivery day through the web app, in the order the dispatcher works:

1. upload tomorrow's orders;
2. fix customer locations;
3. OPTIMIZE;
4. review the plan;
5. lock and dispatch loads;
6. hand out driver sheets;
7. handle late orders.

Each step names the page or component, the API route, the library functions and the database tables involved. The dispatcher's own guide to the same screen is `docs/DISPATCHER_GUIDE.md`; how the optimizer decides is in [section 4](#4-optimizer-logic).

### 3.1 Where the flow code lives

| Layer | Path | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| Page | `apps/web/app/t/[slug]/dispatch/page.tsx` | Server page. Resolves the tenant and role (`canPlan`, `canApproveOverride` from `apps/web/lib/rbac.ts`) and renders `DispatchClient`. "Daily dispatch" is the first menu item in `apps/web/lib/nav.ts` |
| Day screen | `apps/web/app/t/[slug]/dispatch/dispatch-client.tsx` | Steps 1 to 3 (upload, resolve issues, optimize) and the card that holds `PlanView` |
| Plan screen | `apps/web/app/t/[slug]/dispatch/plan-view.tsx` | KPIs, reconciliation bar, plan options, truck loads, drivers, exports, unserved list, map, versions. Also used by `apps/web/app/t/[slug]/dispatch/plan/[id]/page.tsx` + `plan-version-client.tsx` (one plan version on its own page) |
| Dialogs | `location-dialog.tsx`, `customer-dialog.tsx`, `late-order-dialog.tsx` (same folder); their pure helpers `location-requests.ts` (which Read / Save answer may reach the dialog, audit F06) and `customer-details.ts` (the Details form: strict times, unloading minutes, only changed fields, audit F07) | Add a location, edit customer details, record a late order |
| Bring forward (PR9) | `carry-over-panel.tsx` (same folder), in Step 1 of the day screen | The orders of the 7 days before not delivered, with why - today's (when the day is later than today) in their own group "Today (27 Sep) - may still leave today", with a warning, unticked - and "Bring forward to <day>" |
| Client helper | `apps/web/app/t/[slug]/dispatch/client-api.ts` | `api()` fetch wrapper for the `{ data, error }` envelope, time formatters, `REASON_TEXT` labels for unserved reason codes |
| API routes | `apps/web/app/api/dispatch/*`, `apps/web/app/api/orders/*`, `apps/web/app/api/runs/[id]/*`, `apps/web/app/api/customers/[id]/*`, `apps/web/app/api/locations/parse` | Thin handlers, almost all wrapped in `withTenantApi` |
| Business logic | `apps/web/lib/dispatch/*` | Intake, locations, customer attributes, plan building, versions, load rules, reconciliation, summary, exports |
| Background job | `apps/web/lib/jobs/dispatch-job.ts`; shared in-flight map and stuck-job janitor in `apps/web/lib/jobs/optimize-job.ts` and `apps/web/lib/jobs/janitor-loop.ts` | Calls the solver and saves the result |
| Solver client | `apps/web/lib/solver-client.ts` | `callDispatchSolver` (POST `SOLVER_URL` + `/optimize-dispatch`) and `callRouteGeometry` (`/route-geometry`) |
| Wire types | `packages/shared-types/src/dispatch.ts` | `DispatchRequest`, `DispatchResponse`, `DispatchScenario` and friends; the Python side is `apps/solver/dispatch_models.py` |
| Schema | `apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma` and `apps/web/prisma/migrations/20260924090000_nmwc_dispatch_mvp` onward | See [3.15](#315-data-model-used-by-the-dispatch-flow) |
| Tests | `apps/web/tests/lib/dispatch-*.spec.ts`, `plan-continuity.spec.ts`, `driver-pack.spec.ts`; `apps/web/tests/integration/dispatch-mvp.spec.ts`, `dispatch-split.spec.ts`, `dispatch-timing.spec.ts`, `driver-pack.spec.ts` | Unit tests for the pure functions; integration tests against a running web server and solver |

### 3.2 The day at a glance

| # | Dispatcher action | UI | API | Main functions | Tables written |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Pick delivery date and depot | `DispatchClient` | `GET /api/dispatch/day` | `getDayOverview` | none |
| 2 | "Check file" | Step 1 card | `POST /api/orders/upload` | `parseUploadIsolated` (runs `parseUpload` in the parser process), `validateIntake` (`normalizeOrderRows`, `resolveOrderLines`) | `UploadBatch`, `AuditLog` |
| 3 | "Add N lines to the day" | `ValidationPanel` | `POST /api/orders/:batchId/confirm` | `revalidateIntake`, `confirmIntake` | `Customer` and `Product` stubs, `Order`, `OrderLine`, `IntakeLineKey`, `UploadBatch`, `AuditLog` |
| 4 | ADD LOCATION | `LocationDialog` | `POST /api/locations/parse`, `PUT /api/customers/:id/location` | `resolveLocationInput`, `coordStatus` | `Customer`, `AuditLog` |
| 5 | Details (priority, type, hours) | `CustomerDialog` | `PATCH /api/customers/:id` | none beyond the route | `Customer`, `AuditLog` |
| 6 | OPTIMIZE | Step 3 button | `POST /api/dispatch/plan` (no applied plan yet) or `POST /api/runs/:id/replan` | `getOrCreatePlan`, `startDispatchOptimize`, `buildDispatchRequest`, `applyWeightChanges`, `scheduleDispatchOptimize`, then `persistDispatchResult`, `applyScenario`, `refreshPlanFacts` | `OrderLine.weightKg` / `weightFromMaster` / `Order.totalWeightKg` (lines that take the product's case weight), `RunPlan`, `RunJob`, `ScenarioResult`, `UnservedOrder`, `PlanLoad`, `RouteAssignment`, `Order.status`, `AuditLog` |
| 7 | Review | `PlanView` | `GET /api/runs/:id/plan`, `GET /api/runs/:id/load-geometry`, `GET /api/drivers` | `getPlanDetail` | none |
| 8 | "Use instead" | Plan options table | `POST /api/runs/:id/choose-scenario` | `applyScenario` | same as 6, same version |
| 9 | Driver, Lock, Loading, Dispatch, Completed | Load row | `PATCH /api/runs/:id/loads/:loadId` | `updateLoad`, `checkTransition`, `checkDriverChange` | `PlanLoad`, `Order.status`, `RunPlan.status`, `AuditLog` |
| 10 | Export Excel, Driver sheets, WhatsApp | Plan header and load row | `GET /api/runs/:id/export/excel`, `GET /api/runs/:id/export/pdf` | `buildDispatchWorkbook`, `driverPackModel`, `renderDriverPackIsolated` (the layout `renderDriverPackPdf` in the PDF renderer process, review M3), `whatsappText` | none |
| 11 | Late order, then Re-plan | "Late order", "Re-plan" | `POST /api/dispatch/late-order`, `POST /api/runs/:id/replan` | `replan`, `createNextVersion` | new `RunPlan` version, then as 6 |
| 12 | Bring forward orders not delivered on earlier days (PR9), then OPTIMIZE or Re-plan | Step 1 box "Not delivered on earlier days" | `GET` / `POST /api/dispatch/carry-over` | `carryOverPreview`, `bringForward` | `Order` (the copy, and `carriedToOrderId` / `carriedAt` / `carriedById` on the original), `OrderLine`, `IntakeLineKey`, `AuditLog` |

**Who can do what in this flow** (role ranks in [2.10](#210-multi-tenancy-authentication-and-roles)):

- **Any signed-in user of the tenant:** read the day, the plan, the drivers list and both exports. Those routes have no role gate.
- **PLANNER or above:** upload, confirm, location, customer edit, optimize, re-plan, late order, choose scenario, set a driver, and lock/unlock/loading.
- **PLANNER or above, also DISPATCHED and COMPLETED** (owner decision 4 of 5 Oct 2026; they needed SUPERVISOR before). The route admits PLANNER; `changeStatusTx` still checks the role returned by `checkTransition`, which is PLANNER for every move.
- **TENANT_ADMIN:** settings, the audit log page, truck default drivers and adding drivers.

**Tenant isolation.** The child tables `ScenarioResult`, `RouteAssignment`, `UnservedOrder` and `OrderLine` have no `tenantId` column. The dispatch code reaches them through a run or order it has already scoped, or with an explicit `run: { tenantId }` filter.

### 3.3 Step 1: upload and validate the order file

**UI.** The Step 1 card in `dispatch-client.tsx` has a file picker (`.xlsx`, `.xls`, `.csv`), "Check file" (`upload()`), the `ValidationPanel`, then "Add N lines to the day" (`confirmBatch()`). Nothing is saved as orders until confirm.

**Check file: `POST /api/orders/upload`** (`apps/web/app/api/orders/upload/route.ts`). Multipart form fields `file`, `depotId`, `deliveryDate`. PLANNER role, rate limit `LIMITS.ordersUpload` (`apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts`).

1. `parseUpload` (`apps/web/lib/csv.ts`) reads CSV or XLSX with the file-size, row-count and content-type guards, since P5 in a separate parser process (`parseUploadIsolated`, `apps/web/lib/upload-parse`; a file that takes longer than 15 s or needs more than 512 MB there is refused with 400 "This file takes too long to read ..." / "... needs too much memory ...", and when two files are already being read and a third waited 5 s, 503 "RouteIQ is reading other files right now. Try again in a moment."; nothing is saved in either case). Since the CSV intake review fix (9 Oct 2026) the reader is chosen by the file's content, never by the type the browser sends: an .xlsx / .xls (zip or compound-file bytes) goes to SheetJS through the guard, and CSV text always to Papa Parse with every value as written, also when Chrome or Edge on a Windows PC with Excel send it as `application/vnd.ms-excel` (before, SheetJS read it and guessed types: 11/10/2026 became 10 Nov, 00123 became 123). The bytes are decoded explicitly (byte-order marks, strict UTF-8; a file with a few bytes that are not UTF-8 but more well-formed UTF-8 letters than such places is still read as UTF-8, each place as "�", with the warning "This file is saved as UTF-8, but N characters in it are not UTF-8 text and were read as "�". ..."; only a file that is clearly not UTF-8 is read as Windows-1256, with the warning "This file is not saved as UTF-8 ..."; before the follow-up of the same day one stray byte made the whole file read as Windows-1256, its Arabic garbled). Every line break is read as a line feed: Papa takes one kind of line break for a file, so a bare LF in a file of CR LF lines joined two orders into one row (a line break inside a quoted value stays in it, as a line feed). An Excel `sep=;` first line sets the separator and is not read as the header (rows are numbered as Excel shows the file, without it; a "Line N" refusal counts it). A whole `="00123"` value, which ERP exports write to keep leading zeros in Excel, reads as `00123` (any other value with "=" is kept as written). A quote never closed refuses the file ("Line N of this file has a quote (") that is not closed where it should be ..."; before, it swallowed the rest of the file into one note); U+0000 is taken out of cells and the file name; a web page or binary content is refused; a `.csv` / `.xlsx` / `.xls` sent as `application/octet-stream`, `text/plain`, `text/comma-separated-values`, `application/csv` or `text/x-csv` is accepted (`fileRefusal`, `lib/upload-limits.ts`). A database error while the checked file is saved answers 500 `CHECK_FAILED` like a failed check (it was an empty 500). An Excel workbook (PR6, scenario test S04 / B2): the one sheet whose header row has the order columns (customer code, product code and cases, built-in or tenant aliases; `isOrderSheet` in `order-intake.ts`) is read, wherever it is in the workbook, and every other sheet with data is named in a warning (kept in `validationJson.warnings` with the CSV parse warnings since PR6, so the upload page shows them too). A sheet whose rows are all blank cells (a template) does not count, nor (A1 review) one whose first 50,100 rows hold no value while its used range goes on past them (formatting only). **Order rows on two or more sheets are refused**: 400 `MULTIPLE_SHEETS` with `sheets` (name and rows), e.g. "This workbook has order rows on 2 sheets: "Orders" (1,082 rows), "LateOrder" (116 rows). Nothing was read. Upload each sheet as its own file ...". Nothing is saved (no `UploadBatch`). Before PR6 only the first sheet was read and the others dropped without a word. There is no sheet choice on the screen or the API. A workbook with no order sheet reads its first sheet with rows (its check names the missing columns). The customer import and the baseline upload keep reading the first sheet with rows and name the sheets they did not read in a warning (the baseline upload since the PR6 review: its answer, the upload message on the old run page and `ManualBaseline.notes` carry the note; it used to drop it). The 50,000-row limit counts the rows of the sheet that is read, not of the whole workbook (PR6 review): a large sheet that is not read, such as a customer list next to the orders, is only named in the warning; a sheet that is read with more rows is refused with its name ("Too many rows: 50001 on sheet "Orders". Max 50000."). **Before any sheet is read (A1, audit E2)** an .xlsx is measured by unpacking it with a hard cap (`checkWorkbookZip` in `lib/workbook-guard.ts`; the sizes in the zip headers are never trusted): over 50 MB unpacked, over 1,000 parts, a part whose header size is not its real size, a password-protected part, or an archive that is not an Excel workbook (OpenDocument, Numbers, an archive inside) is refused with a plain message; then a workbook with more than 10 sheets is refused ("This workbook has 12 sheets; at most 10 can be read. ...", from the sheet list alone). **A1 review**, also before SheetJS reads the file (`guardSpreadsheet`): a file read as Excel must be an .xlsx, an old .xls or CSV text, because SheetJS picks its reader from the first bytes and several of its readers do far more work than the file's size; a web page or XML file ("This file is a web page or an XML file, not an Excel workbook or CSV. Open it in Excel, save it as .xlsx and upload that."), an OpenDocument, .xlsb ("This is an Excel binary workbook (.xlsb) ..."), SYLK, DIF, Lotus, dBASE, RTF or SocialCalc file is refused. An .xlsx is also refused with more than 2,500,000 cells with a value, 10,000 comments or hyperlinks over more than 200,000 cells in all ("This workbook has links over 17,179,869,184 cells; at most 200,000 can be read. Remove the links ..."), when a part's name in its local header is not its name in the zip directory ("damaged"), and an .xls with such links; a CSV sent as Excel with more than 2,500,000 cells (counted from its separators; since the CSV intake review fix of 9 Oct 2026 no CSV reaches the guard, and every CSV is counted as a CSV sent as text, below). Binary parts (.bin) are hidden from SheetJS. Formulas are not read: each formula cell gives its saved value (one without a saved value reads as blank; it read as 0). Before any sheet is turned into rows (`sheetRanges`), each sheet's range is checked: a range that claims more than its cells (a size record, formatting) is cut to its last cell when it is over the caps, which drops only empty trailing columns, and a sheet wider than 200 columns ("Sheet "Orders" has 16,384 columns; at most 200 can be read. Delete the columns you do not need, ...") or sheets that span more than 2,500,000 cells are refused. **Since the P5 second review a CSV sent as text** (Papa Parse, not SheetJS; most browsers send a .csv so) has the same two caps: a header of more than 200 values is refused before Papa makes a row object ("This file has 1,000,000 columns; at most 200 can be read. Delete the columns you do not need (also empty columns after your data) and upload again."), and after the row limit a line of more than 200 values ("Row 3 of this file has 201 columns; ...", the header being row 1) or more than 2,500,000 values with the header's (the words of a CSV sent as Excel). Every value counts as it is in the file, empty ones too, so a CSV saved from Excel with empty columns after the data can be refused; since the CSV intake review fix (9 Oct 2026) also when the browser sends it as Excel (before, SheetJS read that copy and dropped those columns; an open owner question, [7.5](#75-open-questions-for-the-owner)). Each sheet is read to at most `READ_ROWS` = 50,100 rows (SheetJS `sheetRows`; a CSV with Papa's `preview`). A sheet that goes on past those rows is **never cut short without a word**: when it is the sheet that is read it is refused ("Too many rows: more than 50000 on sheet ...", or, when the rows read hold 50,000 or fewer because of empty rows, "the sheet goes on past row 50,100 ... If the rows below your data are empty, delete them and upload again"); another sheet is named in the warning as "N rows or more". **Since P5 the file is read in its own process, never on the web process's event loop**: that process is killed after `UPLOAD_PARSE_TIMEOUT_MS` (15 s) or ends at its heap cap `UPLOAD_WORKER_MAX_HEAP_MB` (512 MB), the file is refused, and the web process keeps answering every other user meanwhile. The answer it sends back is at most 128 MB, each text sent once (P5 review), with no row of more than 200 cells and no more than 2,500,000 cells, checked in the web process before a row is built, which keeps the rows compact there (P5 second review: the widest legal file holds about 20 MB), so a small file cannot fill the web process either ([2.8](#28-timeouts-budgets-and-limits); how it works and what it costs: the P5 blocks in [7.4](#74-review-leads-found-while-writing-this-handbook)). The caps still bound one upload's work: crafted files that blocked the app for minutes or crashed it before A1 are refused or read in milliseconds. They do not bound the request itself (still open, P5 third review): Next.js 14 reads the whole body into the web process before the route answers, keeping a copy for its middleware, which runs on the upload routes, and the route's `req.formData()` reads the file before the 10 MB check. A 300 MB request without a session (answered 401) took the web process from about 360 MB to about 860 MB here, still held 1.5 s later; the review measured about 740 MB. Capping the body before that is an owner question ([7.5](#75-open-questions-for-the-owner)).
2. `validateIntake` (`apps/web/lib/dispatch/intake-server.ts`):
   - loads `TenantConfig` and the depot (`intakeDepot`, audit PR A5: every order file is for one depot, never a guessed one). The depot sent (`depotId`, the dispatch screen always sends the one on screen) must be an active depot of the company, else 422 `DEPOT_NOT_ACTIVE` ("The depot chosen for this file is not active. Choose an active depot on the Daily dispatch screen, then upload the file again."). Without `depotId` (the legacy `/upload` page) the company's **only** active depot is used; with none, 422 `DEPOT_REQUIRED` ("There is no active depot, so these orders cannot be linked to one. Add a depot under Depots, then upload the file again."), with two or more, 422 `DEPOT_REQUIRED` ("This company has more than one depot. Upload the file on the Daily dispatch screen after choosing its depot, so every order is linked to the right depot."). Nothing is saved. Before A5 the first active depot by code was taken silently, and an unknown or inactive depot answered 400 "No active depot. Create a depot first.";
   - runs `normalizeOrderRows` (`apps/web/lib/dispatch/order-intake.ts`, pure). It maps the file headers through `HEADER_ALIASES` plus tenant extras from `TenantConfig.orderColumnMapJson`, and parses dates with `TenantConfig.dateOrder` (DMY by default; ISO dates and Excel serials also work). Every row becomes either a line or a row error. A row is named by its row in the file (`ParsedFile.rowNumbers`: an Excel sheet's own row numbers, a CSV's records as a spreadsheet shows them), also when the file has blank rows, which the reader leaves out; before the review fix of 9 Oct 2026 (web-intake-4) rows were counted from 2 again after the blank ones, so with blank separator rows the errors, the "added together" warnings and `OrderLine.sourceRow` named rows above the real ones:
     - required columns: customer code, product code, cases, and a delivery date (or the date picked on screen);
     - the salesman's route (Salesman ETA, owner request 17 Oct 2026): an optional column `route` (also *Sales route*, *Salesman route*, *Route code*, *Salesman code*, *Salesman*; field `sales_route`, declared last in `HEADER_ALIASES`, so it never takes another field's column and a file without it maps exactly as before). Each row's route is kept as `normSalesRoute` gives it (`lib/dispatch/sales-route.ts`: trimmed, inner spaces collapsed, upper-case, at most 40 characters, blank = none) in `NormalizedLine.salesRoute`, set only when the file has the column; rows added together into one line keep the first route one of them gives. The route is in no duplicate or intake key (`lineDupKey`, `IntakeLineKey`, `contentFingerprint`) and never changes planning;
     - row errors: empty customer or product, cases not a whole number above 0, bad date, priority not 1 to 5 or P1 to P5, non-numeric weight, value or margin; a delivery date before the company's today (`todayIso` in `TenantConfig.timezone`), naming the date and today ("Delivery date "06/10/2026" (6 Oct 2026) is before today (8 Oct 2026): that day is over, ..."; review fix s6-messy-intake-2: it only got the "after the cutoff" late note and could be confirmed);
     - a delivery date more than 14 days after today (`FAR_AHEAD_DAYS`) is a warning per date with its rows. A date is always read by `dateOrder` and never turned round; a cell that reads either way round (both numbers 12 or under) says in these messages how it was read and what the other reading would be. A cell read the wrong way round lands a month or more from the date meant, so it is caught as a past day or a day far ahead;
   - reads the tenant's customers and products and the already confirmed lines for the same dates, then calls `resolveOrderLines` (pure):
     - an inactive customer or product is an error, **except** a line already confirmed with the same cases (PR6, scenario test S05: the customer was deactivated after its orders were added). That line is a duplicate like any re-sent line: "Already confirmed: sales order ..., skipped. Customer X is inactive now: its confirmed orders are not planned until it is reactivated." (a product: "its confirmed lines stay on the day"). The same line with other cases is the inactive error plus the "already confirmed with N cases" text;
     - a line equal to a confirmed one (same date, sales order, customer branch and product; `lineDupKey`, sales order trimmed and upper-case) with the **same cases** is a duplicate and is skipped ("Already confirmed: ..."); with **other cases** it is an error ("changing a confirmed line is not supported yet"), since there is no amendment flow. Since PR6 these messages and the inactive errors name the master codes ("S05-C05", "TEST-W330"), not the file's spelling ("s05-c05");
     - the same sales order already confirmed for **another** delivery date (from `IntakeLineKey`) is a warning. The file's sales orders are asked for in parts of 10,000 (`IN_LIST_PART`, `inParts`) and the file's own dates are left out after the query, since the P5 third review: PostgreSQL takes at most 32,767 bind parameters in one query, Prisma does not split such a list next to other conditions, and a file of 32,766 or more different sales orders (legal: up to 50,000 rows) was refused with Prisma's own text;
     - an unknown customer or product is not an error; it is listed as new;
     - the same sales-order line twice in one file (same sales order, customer branch, product and date) is added together, with a warning per row. Since the audit PR "Intake and master data" (F02 / F04) the result does not depend on the row order: the line gets the **highest priority** of its rows (P1 wins; a row without a priority never removes another row's), **every distinct note** (joined with ` | `, each once), and a sales value or margin only when **every** row has one (a blank is unknown, never 0). Each row as it was in the file (row, cases, priority, note, value, margin) is kept with the check in `validationJson` (`ResolvedLine.mergedRows`), and when the rows differ in priority, note or money one more warning names them ("Rows 2 and 3 are one line (sales order 901, ...), 15 cases in all. Different priorities (row 2 P5, row 3 P1): P1 is used, the highest. Notes kept: row 2 "routine"; row 3 "URGENT call receiving"."). Before, the first row's priority and note won and the others were lost (a P1 on a second row after a row without priority disappeared completely), and 100 OMR + a blank was saved as a complete 100 OMR. The notes carry no row numbers (drivers read them); the rows are in the check and the warning. Rows without a sales-order number are never added together. Rows of one sales-order line whose depot column names **different depots** are never added together either (review fix web-intake-6, 9 Oct 2026): each is a row error with its own cases naming the rows and their depots ("Rows 2 and 3 are one sales-order line (...) for different depots (row 2 NZW, row 3 SHN). A sales-order line is planned at one depot: ..."), in either row order, since a sales-order line has one `IntakeLineKey` whatever the depot. A row without a depot joins its line, which keeps the depot its other rows name. Before, such rows became one line at the first row's depot: uploaded for that depot, the other depot's cases were planned there; uploaded for the other, the whole line was refused;
     - customer identity is `customerKey(code, branchKey)` (`lib/customer-code.ts`): the code and the branch, trimmed, whatever the letter case; every other character is itself (`C_1` is not `CX1`, `%` is not a wildcard). Master rows whose codes differ only in letter case ("twins") resolve to one row, always the same one (`preferredCustomer` / `preferredProduct`: active, then with a location / a case weight, then code, then id), with a warning;
     - product identity is `productKey(code)` (`lib/product-code.ts`): the item code is read as the tidy code (`normalizeProductCode`: spaces at both ends cut, each run of spaces inside one, a non-breaking space a space), so `" TN1.5L  (6) "` is `TN1.5L (6)` in every message, in the duplicate keys (`lineDupKey`), in `contentFingerprint` and in the product that confirm creates, and it is matched to the master ignoring the letter case and the spacing the master code was saved with (`JA1.5L(6)` matches `ja1.5l(6)`). A space or bracket that is there counts: `TN1.5L(6)` and `TN1.5L (6)` are two products. A code that matches no master product must be one the Products page could hold (letters, digits, spaces and `. ( ) - _ / + &`, at most 40, not starting with `+` or `-`): otherwise the row is an error (`Item code "A,B" cannot be used: ...`, with its cases, so the totals still add up) instead of a product made from it; a product already in the master keeps matching whatever its code looks like. Master twins of a code resolve like customer twins, with a warning. `confirmIntake` reads the company's products once and matches them with `twinsOf` in the program (never `equals` + `mode: 'insensitive'`, an ILIKE that reads `_` as a wildcard), and creates each new product once, with the tidy code;
     - weights: a file weight of 0 counts as blank (the product's case weight applies); a merged line keeps the cases of its blank-weight rows in `weightMissingCases` (such a line is weighed from the master at confirm, see below); products (existing without weight, or new) with rows that carry no file weight are listed in `issues.productsWithoutWeight`; a file kg per case under half or over twice the product's case weight is a warning (the column must be kg per line). When the file itself shows its weight column is not kg per line (`weightColumnEvidence`: two rows of one product with the same weight for different case counts, or kg per case more than twice apart), the column is **not used for products without a case weight** (review fix web-intake-5, 9 Oct 2026): their lines are weighed from the master like lines without a file weight, so they are listed in `issues.productsWithoutWeight` and OPTIMIZE asks for the case weight, with one warning naming the two rows. Ignored, not only warned about: a file kg is kept for good (`weightFromMaster = false`), so a per-case "Weight" column (21.5 kg for 100 cases of 5 L) was planned and dispatched as the line kg while NMWC's products had no case weight to check it against. Without such evidence (each product on one row) the column is taken as kg per line;
   - turns rows whose depot column names another depot into errors (a line added together from several rows names them all: "Rows 2 and 3 (one sales-order line) are for depot SHN, ...");
   - decides late per delivery date: late if `isAfterCutoff(now, date, planningCutoffMin, timezone)` (`apps/web/lib/dispatch/time.ts`; default cutoff 18:00 the day before), or if `currentPlan(...)` for that date already has a chosen scenario. Each reason is stored as text in `late.reasons`: "Received after the 18:00 cutoff for D." or (PR6, `planExistsReason`) "A plan (version N) already exists for D (2 of its loads are dispatched, 1 is locked or loading)." - the counts only when there are such loads;
   - computes `contentHash`: SHA-256 of `contentFingerprint(lines)`, the normalized lines (delivery date, sales order, customer, product, cases, kg, value, margin, priority, depot) as text, sorted. Row order, column order and the export do not matter; the delivery date does (also when it came from the screen).
   - anything else that fails while the file is checked (the database, a bug) is answered 500 `{ code: 'CHECK_FAILED', message }`: "RouteIQ could not check this file. Nothing was saved. Try again in a moment. If it happens again, tell your administrator." (`INTAKE_CHECK_FAILED`); the error itself goes to the server log as `[orders-upload] checking the file failed`. Before the P5 third review the route answered 400 with the error's own text, which for a database error was Prisma's (file paths and code lines included).
3. The route adds an error ("These orders were already confirmed for D (file ...)"; since PR6 D is the file's own dates when every line was skipped, not "this date") when a batch with the same `fileHash` (= `contentHash`, so for the same dates) was already CONFIRMED for this depot, or (`findSameConfirmedFile`) a batch confirmed before the stabilization release, whose `fileHash` was SHA-256 of the raw rows (`legacyRowsHash`, stored as `validationJson.legacyHash`), for one of the same delivery dates. Without that, a no-SO file confirmed before the deploy could be confirmed again after it (review of PR2). It creates an `UploadBatch` with status `PARSED` (has errors) or `VALIDATED` (no errors), stores the full validation result (including every resolved line) in `validationJson`, and writes audit `CREATE UploadBatch`. The `deliveryDate` form field must be a real date (`isRealIsoDate`).

**Confirm: `POST /api/orders/:batchId/confirm`** (`apps/web/app/api/orders/[batchId]/confirm/route.ts`). Body `{ lateReason? }`.

- **Refusals before the transaction:** a batch that is already confirmed, rejected or deleted (409); a batch with `errorRows > 0` (400, code `FILE_HAS_ERRORS` since PR6: "This file has N errors: nothing was added. Fix the rows ... and upload the file again"); a batch validated by an older version (409); late lines without a reason (400, code `LATE_REASON_REQUIRED`). Since PR6 its message names the real reasons (`lateReasonRequiredMessage` in `intake-server.ts`: "These orders are late. A plan (version 1) already exists for 2026-10-07 (2 of its loads are dispatched). Enter the reason for accepting them."); before, it always said "after the planning cutoff", also for a day that only had a plan (scenario test S04).
- **Re-check inside the transaction** (review F05). The transaction first takes `lockIntake` (`pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('intake:' || tenantId, 0))`, the same lock as the late-order route and batch delete), then `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the batch row, then `revalidateIntake` (`intake-server.ts`). Each conflict answers 409 with a `code`, saves nothing and leaves the batch `VALIDATED`:
  - `STALE_VALIDATION`: the batch is older than `VALIDATED_BATCH_MAX_AGE_HOURS` (24): upload the file again. Also (audit F02, `mergedTheOldWay`) a file checked before the audit PR "Intake and master data" with a line added together from several rows: that line kept only its first row's priority and note, so the file must be uploaded again (`MERGED_THE_OLD_WAY` says so);
  - `MASTER_CHANGED` for the depot (audit F03, `batchDepotProblem`): the file's depot was deactivated after the check ("Depot NZW was deactivated after this file was checked. Nothing was added: reactivate the depot under Depots, or upload the file again for another depot.") or is not found. A file that had no depot before audit PR A5 is on the history-only depot since the migration and is refused with "This file was checked before every order file had a depot. Nothing was added: upload the file again on the Daily dispatch screen for an active depot." (never "reactivate"). The depot row (`code`, `active`, `historyOnly`) is locked `FOR SHARE` until the orders are written, so a deactivation at the same moment is waited for;
  - `DUPLICATE_FILE`: another batch with the same `fileHash` and depot is CONFIRMED (or a pre-release batch with the same raw-row hash for one of the dates);
  - `DUPLICATE_LINES`: a line of the file is now confirmed (another file, tab or late order), with the rows;
  - `MASTER_CHANGED`: a customer or product of the file was deleted or deactivated after the check;
  - `LATE_REASON_REQUIRED`: the cutoff passed, or a plan was applied, since the check, and no reason was sent ("These orders became late after the file was checked." and the reasons, PR6). The day screen then shows the late-reason field;
  - `INTAKE_BUSY`: the transaction timed out (Prisma P2028), e.g. waiting for the intake lock behind another large confirm, or (the same answer) the confirm itself ran past its 60 s. Nothing was saved; confirm again. A file of 33,000-50,000 lines of one customer is confirmed in 15-20 s on this PC since the P5 third review (its lines were put into their order by copying the order's list for each line: 40 s for 40,000 lines before a single row was written, so such a file could be refused as busy). Batch delete, the late order and the optimize start answer the same way.
- **Writes.** `confirmIntake`:
  - creates stub `Customer` rows for new customers (`createdFromUpload = true`, `geocodeConfidence = 'MISSING'`, no coordinates) and stub `Product` rows (`createdFromUpload = true`, case weight 0 = unknown). An existing row whose code differs only in case is reused (a deactivated one is `MASTER_CHANGED`). The company's customers are read once and matched in the program with `customerTwinsOf` (`lib/customer-code.ts`), the identity the check used; until 7 Oct 2026 confirm asked the database with `equals` + `mode: 'insensitive'`, an ILIKE in which `_` and `%` are wildcards, so a new `C_1` was attached to an existing `CX1` and its location while the check listed it as a new customer;
  - creates one `Order` per customer branch and delivery date, with one `OrderLine` per SKU line (sales order number, product, cases, kg, value, margin, source row, notes, and since 17 Oct 2026 the sales route `salesRoute`, null without one). Line kg (`intakeLineWeight` in `weights.ts`): the file kg when every row of the line had one (`weightFromMaster = false`, never changed later); otherwise cases × the product's case weight, or 0 kg (unknown) when it has none, with `weightFromMaster = true`. A merged line whose rows only partly carry a weight is weighed from the master as a whole: a partial kg (e.g. 100 kg for 15 cases of which 5 had no weight) would count as known and too low for good. Lines weighed from the master follow it: a case weight entered or corrected later reaches them at the next optimize ([3.6](#36-step-4-optimize)). Order totals are summed from its lines;
  - writes one `IntakeLineKey` per line with a sales-order number (`createIntakeKeys`). Its unique index makes a second confirm of the same line fail; the route maps that (Prisma P2002) to 409 `DUPLICATE_LINES`;
  - sets the order's `priority` to the lowest number found in the file for that order, else the customer's; `priorityFromFile` records which. `status = 'VALIDATED'`. `isLate`, `lateReason` and `lateRecordedById` are set for late batches (late as re-checked). `salesValue` and `marginValue` are set only when every line carries one (a merged line with a blank on one row carries none, audit F04). Distinct line notes are joined with ` | `, each note once also when a merged line already holds several (`joinNotes`);
  - marks the batch `CONFIRMED`, stores `lateReason` and `isLate`, and writes audit `UPDATE UploadBatch`.

**Delete: `DELETE /api/orders/:batchId`** (`apps/web/app/api/orders/[batchId]/route.ts`, legacy `/upload` page only; review F20). One transaction under `lockIntake` and the batch row lock. Refused with 409 when the batch is already `DELETED`, when a plan for its depot and date(s) is `OPTIMIZING` (`PLAN_OPTIMIZING`), and when any of its orders has a `RouteAssignment`, an `UnservedOrder` row or sits in the scope of a chosen scenario (`BATCH_IN_PLAN`, naming the dates and plan versions). Otherwise the orders (their lines and `IntakeLineKey` rows cascade), the `DELETED` status and the audit row are written together. The 409 says the file cannot be deleted because a plan keeps every order it was made for, and that removing planned orders is not possible in the app yet. A late order only adds orders and a re-plan plans the same orders again, so neither removes a wrongly uploaded file's orders: until the "cancel orders from this file" flow exists (deferred, owner decision on F20), only an administrator can correct them.

The screen then switches to the first delivery date found in the file.

### 3.4 Step 2: customer locations and details

**What blocks optimizing.** `customerIssues` in `apps/web/lib/dispatch/customer-attrs.ts`, using `coordStatus`.

- **Blocking:** `LOCATION_REQUIRED` (no coordinates) and `INVALID_LOCATION` (0,0 or out of range, or outside the service area and never verified: "Saved location is outside Oman/UAE and was never confirmed. Drop the pin on the customer's exact location." - it said "Confirm or correct it on the map", but the dialog never confirms such a point as it is, A5 review - or - owner's location rule, audit PR A5 - a LOW reading never verified: "Saved location is not exact (low confidence). Drop the pin on the customer's exact location."). One predicate, `locationBlocksDelivery`, is used by the day screen, `buildDispatchRequest`, the load changes LOCK / LOADING / DISPATCH (`locationGate`, [3.8](#38-step-6-load-states), A5 second review) and the legacy run dispatch. Before audit PR A5 no writer stored LOW; since the A5 review the customer import marks an unconfirmed saved point LOW when the file points somewhere else (below), also for a customer already on a plan.
- **Notes only:** `LOCATION_UNVERIFIED` (a HIGH or MEDIUM import not confirmed yet: still planned, by owner decision of 28 Sep 2026, [7.5](#75-open-questions-for-the-owner)), `NEW_CUSTOMER`, `PRIORITY_UNCONFIRMED`, `TYPE_MISSING`, `NO_RECEIVING_WINDOW` and `WINDOW_UNCONFIRMED` (since 1 Oct 2026: receiving hours that are not the customer's own confirmed hours, `windowIssue`).
- **Service area:** `parseServiceArea` uses `TenantConfig.serviceAreaJson` if set, else an Oman + UAE box (`DEFAULT_SERVICE_AREA` in `location-input.ts`) for tenants based there, else no area check.

**Effective attributes** (`effectiveAttrs` in `customer-attrs.ts`). The `CustomerTypeProfile` used is the one for the customer's `customerType`.

- **Priority:** the customer's own value if `priorityConfirmed`, else the type profile's `defaultPriority` if set, else the customer's stored (unconfirmed) priority (`effectivePriority`). There is no tenant default priority. The Customers list and the customer page show the stored priority and, when it is not confirmed, the one the planner uses (review ui-rest-2: a grocery stored as 3 with a P4 type default read "3" there while it was planned, and dropped first, as P4).
- **Service minutes** (since PR5, [3.12](#312-settings-that-change-the-plan) "Default service time"): the customer's confirmed value (`serviceTimeConfirmed`), else the type profile's `serviceTimeMin` if set, else the tenant `defaultServiceTimeMin`. An unconfirmed stored `avgServiceTimeMin` is not used; migration `20260928090100_keep_imported_service_times` confirmed the times earlier imports had stored, and the pre-deploy count is in [5.12](#512-how-to-verify-a-deploy) check 11. The customer page shows the value in use and its source (`describeServiceTime`).
- **Hard and preferred windows:** the customer's own four window fields are used if any of them is set **or its hours are confirmed** (`windowConfirmedAt`; confirmed with all four empty = open all day, any time), else the type profile's four if any of those is set, else there is no window. There is no tenant default window. `windowConfirmed` (owner decision 1 Oct 2026, "own confirmed window") is true only when a dispatcher or admin entered or confirmed the hours; a type default never counts, and stored hours nobody confirmed are used but shown "(not confirmed)" (`windowLabel`).

**Add location** (`location-dialog.tsx`, map `apps/web/components/pin-map.tsx` on MapLibre):

1. "Read" calls `POST /api/locations/parse` (`apps/web/app/api/locations/parse/route.ts`), which runs `resolveLocationInput` (`apps/web/lib/dispatch/location-input.ts`). Nothing is saved. Rate limit 120 per minute per user.
   - **Accepted inputs:** "lat, lng"; degrees-minutes-seconds; Google Maps URLs (the `!3d...!4d...` pin, `q=`, `query=`, `destination=`, `daddr=`, `/search/`, and the end of a `/dir/` directions link when the end is a point; a map centre - `/@lat,lng`, `ll=`, `center=`, `sll=` - is accepted but needs a pin; A5 third review: `ll=` used to be read as exact, and a directions link was read at its first waypoint whose coordinates, which Google fills with the start when the route starts at "Your location" or a dropped pin, so the dispatcher's own position could be saved as the customer's; now only the end of the route is read, a directions link that does not end at a point needs a pin, and its data part is not read); `geo:` URIs; short share links (`maps.app.goo.gl`, `goo.gl/maps`), which the server resolves by following redirects to Google hosts only.
   - Uncertain results come back with `needsPin`: every LOW reading and the MEDIUM ones (map centre only, fewer than 4 decimals, Google's pin included, degrees and minutes only, a pair with fewer than 4 decimals written as degrees, minutes and seconds, swapped latitude and longitude, outside the delivery area). An accepted reading without `needsPin` is always HIGH.
   - **Decimals: one zero at the end counts** (owner decision of 28 Sep 2026, "Same rule everywhere", [7.5](#75-open-questions-for-the-owner)). Of the zeros at the end of each coordinate only one counts, as in the customer import, with the import's own function (`countedText` in `location-input.ts`, used by `parseLocationInput` and `readImportedPair`): "23.5800, 58.4100" is 3 decimals and needs a pin, with the warning "Fewer than 4 decimals (only one zero at the end counts)." (the zeros made the difference; a pair written with fewer than 4 keeps "Coordinates have fewer than 4 decimals ..."); "23.5850, 58.4105" is 4 and "23.585900, 58.405900" 5, both exact. The same holds for a pair written as text inside a link: `geo:`, `q=`, `query=`, `destination=`, `daddr=`, `/search/`, `/place/<pair>` and the end of a `/dir/` link.
