Padding reaches those: `/search/` and `q=` carry the text searched for, as it was typed, and other programs write such links with a fixed number of decimals (Java `%f`, JavaScript `toFixed(6)`), so a rough 23.58 comes out "23.580000". Google's own pin (`!3d...!4d...`) needs 4 decimals too, counted as Google wrote them (A5 sixth review): Google repeats a coordinate searched for as the pin, so "23.58, 58.41" (or "23.5800, 58.4100") searched in Google Maps and shared comes back as `!3d23.58!4d58.41`; Google writes no zeros at the end, so its digits are not cut; a real place marker has 6 or 7 decimals. Before, the pin was read with no decimals check. A map centre needs a pin whatever its digits. RouteIQ's own driver links (`driver-links.ts`) never pad a number. Before, ADD LOCATION and `POST /api/customers` counted every zero, so "23.5800, 58.4100" read as exact, HIGH, and was saved as confirmed. The price, as for the import: a real 4-decimal coordinate ending in 00 (about 1 in 100 per axis) needs its pin placed by hand, or more decimals.
   - **Owner's location rule** (27 Sep 2026, audit PR A5: "locations should always be correct ... no item will be delivered without location"). A reading with `needsPin`, or one that could not be read, is never saved as read: Save location stays off, with "This reading is not exact. Drop the pin on the customer's exact location, then save." (or "This could not be read. ..."; for a pair padded with zeros "Fewer than 4 decimals (only one zero at the end counts). Drop the pin on the customer's exact location.", `notExactMessage`, and the preview does not repeat that reason under it), until the dispatcher clicks the map or drags the pin (`PinMap` reports only a click or a drag, so `pinMoved` means placed by hand). Before, Save was the confirmation and stored the reading as read, verified HIGH. The customer's saved pin, which the dialog opens on, is saved again as it is only when it is exact (`savedPointProblem` in `customer-attrs.ts`, the server's own test: verified, or HIGH and inside the company's delivery area; the day overview passes `geocodeConfidence` and `serviceArea`, the customer page its `tenantServiceArea`). Otherwise Save location stays off with the reason: "This saved location is not exact. Drop the pin on the customer's exact location, then save.", "This saved location is outside the delivery area and was never confirmed. ..." or "This saved location has latitude and longitude swapped. ...". The digits of the stored number are never counted (A5 review): "23.5850" is stored as 23.585, so reading the number again as text called about 1 in 5 exact points "not exact". The dialog used to judge the saved pin with no area at all, so a pin outside the area kept Save on and the server then refused it as "not exact". Save sends the address a short link led to at the Read (`resolvedUrl`) with the text it was read from.
   - Degrees-minutes-seconds (audit F17, `parseDms`): minutes and seconds must be below 60, seconds need minutes, latitude at most 90° (N/S) and longitude at most 180° (E/W). Anything else is refused with the reason ("Latitude: minutes must be 0 to 59 (got 99')") instead of being rolled over into another real point (23°99'00"N used to become 24.65°N, high confidence, no pin asked). Whole degrees only (about 110 km) come back LOW with `needsPin`, degrees and minutes without seconds (about 1.8 km) MEDIUM with `needsPin`, like decimals with fewer than 4 places. Seconds that are a pair with 3 decimals or fewer written another way (both coordinates within 0.05" of such a value, `dmsIsRoughPair`; A5 sixth review) come back MEDIUM with `needsPin` and "These degrees, minutes and seconds are 23.58, 58.41 written another way: fewer than 4 decimals ...": Google shows a searched "23.58, 58.41" as 23°34'48.0"N 58°24'36.0"E, which was read HIGH. A real point written to a tenth of a second looks like that about once in 1,300 (whole seconds once in 324) and its pin is placed by hand; one coordinate alone is not enough (a real point does that once in 36). The same rules apply to DMS inside a Google Maps link.
   - One request at a time, bound to the dialog (audit F06, `location-requests.ts`). Each Read and Save carries the dialog generation (bumped when the dialog opens, closes or shows another customer) and the input generation (bumped when the text changes or a pin is dropped by hand). A Read whose dialog or input changed since is aborted and its answer dropped, so customer A's slow short link can no longer land in customer B's dialog. The Enter key goes through the same guard as the Read button (it used to start a second Read while one ran). A Save answer that arrives after the dialog was closed or opened for another customer is reported for its own customer only (a toast, and the day and plan are refreshed) and never closes the dialog on screen or turns its Save into "Confirm & save". The text saved as the location's input is the text the point was read from, never text that was not read (a pin dropped by hand without a Read is stored as "map pin").
   - A point read earlier is out of date once the text in the box is no longer the text it was read from (A2 review, `textUnread` in `location-dialog.tsx`). The preview turns grey, the dialog says "Text changed - press Read", and Save location stays off until a Read of the text on screen comes back (typing the read text back makes the preview current again). Text typed but never read does the same ("Press Read to find this point before saving"): a customer's existing pin is no longer saved under a link nobody read. An empty box with nothing read still saves the pin on the map as it is, when that saved pin is exact (owner's rule above). A pin the dispatcher drops by hand is the point: Save stays on, with the note that it keeps that pin. The `save()` function checks the same rule as the button. Before, Read text A, replace it by text B and Save stored A's point, with the green "Found A" box next to B.
   - "Confirm & save" (after a 422 `OUTSIDE_AREA`) confirms only the point it was asked for: a new point from a Read or a hand pin puts the button back to "Save location", so a new point outside Oman/UAE is asked about again (before, the next Save sent `confirmOutsideArea` for it unasked).
2. "Save location" calls `PUT /api/customers/:id/location` (`apps/web/app/api/customers/[id]/location/route.ts`) with `{ lat, lng, source, input, resolvedUrl?, confirmOutsideArea? }`. The route enforces the owner's rule itself, whatever the screen sends (audit PR A5; the company's area from `tenantServiceArea`, `lib/dispatch/service-area.ts`):
   - **A reading** (`source` not `MAP_PIN`): `checkManualLocation` (`location-input.ts`) reads the text again with the same parser and **no network call**. A short link is read from `resolvedUrl`, the final Google Maps address the Read found (`rereadSavedInput`: only an http(s) Google Maps address that is not itself a short link; else "Press Read again, or drop the pin on the map"). 422 `PIN_REQUIRED` with the plain remedy when the reading needs a pin, cannot be read or is missing (for a pair padded with zeros, with the dialog's words: "Fewer than 4 decimals (only one zero at the end counts). Drop the pin on the customer's exact location."); 422 `LOCATION_MISMATCH` ("The point sent is not where this text points. Press Read again, or drop the pin by hand, then save.") when the point sent is not the point the text reads as, to the 6th decimal (`samePoint`). The source and confidence stored are the parser's (always HIGH once accepted), never the client's. Resolving the short link again on Save was not chosen: it would be a new outside call per save and could land on a consent page and refuse an honest save; a forged `resolvedUrl` gains nothing a hand pin does not already allow.
   - **A hand pin** (`MAP_PIN`): stored as `MAP_PIN`, HIGH. Two exceptions, 422 `PIN_REQUIRED`: the customer's saved point sent back unchanged is not a hand pin, so it is confirmed as it is only when it is already verified, or HIGH and inside the company's area (`savedPointProblem`, the dialog's test; else 422 with the reason: not exact, outside the delivery area, or latitude and longitude swapped, also when `confirmOutsideArea` is sent; a confirmed saved point keeps its source, e.g. `IMPORT`); and a "hand pin" exactly on the point of a reading that needs a pin was never moved (the message says why, as for the reading).
   - It also accepts `{ input }` alone. It resolves it (short links too, as the Read does) and answers 422 `PIN_REQUIRED` unless the result is exact (was `CONFIRM_ON_MAP` before A5; one code for "needs a pin by hand").
   - `GEOCODER` is no longer accepted as a source (400): nothing geocodes, and a client cannot choose the source stored.
   - A point outside the service area gets 422 `OUTSIDE_AREA` until the dispatcher confirms. Only a hand pin can get there: a reading outside the area always needs a pin.
   - It writes `lat`, `lng`, `locationInput`, `locationSource`, `locationVerified = true`, `locationVerifiedById`, `locationVerifiedAt`, `geocodeConfidence` (a hand pin HIGH, a reading the parser's, a saved point confirmed its own) and audit `CUSTOMER_LOCATION_SET` (before: point, source, verified, confidence; after: point, source, input, confidence and `check` = `HAND_PIN`, `READING` or `SAVED_POINT`), in one transaction since the A5 third review: LOCK, LOADING and DISPATCH read the row's "before" point ([3.8](#38-step-6-load-states)), so a saved pin without its row is not possible. Since the A5 fifth review the "before" is the customer as it is when the change is written (the row locked, `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, and read again in the transaction), not as the route read it at the start: a point a customer file marked LOW in between is recorded as LOW. The customer import writes the same row (`check` = `IMPORT`) for every location it writes (data collection item 6, so "Changed since" can say who set it; a row whose "before" was usable never refuses a load); when an exact pair from the file replaces a saved point that was not usable, since the A5 fifth review in one transaction with the new pair, the customer locked and judged as it is then (before: the row was written after the pair, so a restart or a failed insert in between left the change without its row, and the decision used the customer as the import read it at the start). A row whose customer is still as the import read it and needs no row is written in one conditional statement (still not confirmed, same point, same confidence); any other goes through the locked transaction.
   - **The customer page and the Customers list** (A5 third review) say when a saved point blocks delivery, with the day card's test and words (`locationIssue` in `customer-attrs.ts`, the company's area): the customer page shows "Pin: ... (not usable)" and a red note, for example "Saved location is not exact (low confidence). Drop the pin on the customer's exact location. Its orders are not planned or sent out until then."; the list marks the row **needs pin** (the reason on hover) and counts them at the top ("N need a pin", next to "N missing geocode"; since the review fixes of 9 Oct 2026 both count the whole company, not only the rows loaded, and a click lists those customers). Before, a point an import had marked LOW looked like any usable import on both, so the blocked customers could only be found once they had orders.
   - **Other writers of coordinates** (audit PR A5): the customer page's **Set location** opens this same dialog and route (`customer-editor.tsx`; the page used to save a map click or two typed numbers through `PATCH /api/customers/:id` as verified HIGH with no check at all: not 0,0, not the area). `PATCH /api/customers/:id` now refuses coordinates (400 `USE_SET_LOCATION`, not silently dropped). `POST /api/customers` (no screen uses it) reads the pair as sent like a Read and refuses one that needs a pin (422 `PIN_REQUIRED`) or one coordinate without the other (400). Since the owner decision of 28 Sep 2026 it counts one zero at the end like the Read: "23.5800" / "58.4100" sent as text is refused with "This location is not exact. Fewer than 4 decimals (only one zero at the end counts). Create the customer without coordinates, then set its location on the map (Set location on the customer page)." (it was created HIGH; each reason is now a sentence of its own, it read "not exact (... (accurate to ~100 m or worse).)."); a JSON number has no zeros at the end. The customer import stores no pair that needs a pin (below). Order-file stubs (`confirmIntake`) and late orders store no coordinates at all (LOCATION REQUIRED).
   - The location stays on the customer master. A later customer import (`apps/web/app/api/customers/import/route.ts`) does not overwrite a verified location, also not one verified while the import runs (audit F05): the import writes a customer's coordinates with their own update whose condition is "still not verified" (`updateMany` where `locationVerified = false`), which PostgreSQL checks on the row as it is at that moment, not on the list the import read at its start; "N customer location(s) confirmed by a dispatcher were kept" counts what those updates did. Before, a pin verified between the import's read and its write was overwritten and stayed marked verified, with the dispatcher's name on the imported point.
   - **The import and the owner's rule** (audit PR A5): each `lat` / `lng` pair is read like ADD LOCATION reads "lat, lng" (the text as in the file, with the company's area; `readImportedPair` in `lib/dispatch/import-location.ts`). A pair that needs a pin (fewer than 4 decimals, swapped, outside the area, 0,0) is never stored as a usable location: a new customer gets no coordinates (`MISSING`, LOCATION REQUIRED on the day). An existing customer keeps its saved point when the file's pair points at the same place within the file's own precision (23.586 stands for 23.5855 to 23.5865) or within 150 m (`fileAgreesWithSaved`); when the file points elsewhere (A5 review: the customer moved, or one of the two is wrong) its saved point, if nobody confirmed it, stays on the map but is marked LOW, so it blocks planning until a dispatcher drops the pin (an update conditional on "still not verified and still at the point compared", like F05). A confirmed location is never changed. A saved point the file agrees with but that is itself not usable (LOW, or outside the area, and never confirmed: `locationBlocksDelivery`, for example after an earlier import marked it LOW) is kept but listed as not used, with its own warning, and is not marked again (A5 second review; it used to say "The location it already has is kept."). The row is listed in `locationsNotSaved` (row, code, reason, `kept`: `SAVED_LOCATION`, `SAVED_LOCATION_NEEDS_PIN`, `SAVED_LOCATION_NOT_USABLE` or none) with the reason in the import's own words ("Fewer than 4 decimals.", "Latitude and longitude look swapped.", "Outside the delivery area.", "0,0 is not a location.", plus "The file points about 12 km from the saved location." when it contradicts the saved point), shown on the import screen with what happens to the customer's location and what to do, plus one warning (and one more for saved points not used: "... Their orders are not planned or sent out until then. Drop the pin on each one ...", which is what planning and `locationGate` enforce; it said "Nothing is delivered to them until then", which neither held before the gate nor holds for a load already on the road, A5 second review); it is not an error, so the rest of the row and the file are imported. The screen's column hints say the rule before the import (at least 4 decimals, inside the delivery area, every decimal typed or pasted, the column formatted as Text when Excel drops a trailing zero). Before, any pair within -90..90 / -180..180 was stored as HIGH, 0,0 included. Of the zeros at the end of a coordinate's decimals **one counts, whatever the file** (`countedText` in `location-input.ts`, A5 fifth review; since the owner decision of 28 Sep 2026 the same function judges ADD LOCATION and `POST /api/customers`, above): 23.5850 is 4 decimals, 23.5800 is 3 (padding is not precision), in a CSV (typed, or saved by Excel from cells formatted to show 4 decimals, which writes each cell as it shows it), sent as CSV or as Excel, in an Excel Text cell, and in a number cell formatted to show more decimals; the row's reason is then "Fewer than 4 decimals (only one zero at the end counts)." when the zeros made the difference. So a rough pair is never made exact by its format, and the verdict no longer depends on whether the workbook or the CSV Excel saves from it is imported (the A5 fourth review applied the one-zero rule to number formats only). The price: a real 4-decimal coordinate ending in 00 (about 1 in 100 per axis) is not exact either; its pin is placed by hand, or the file gives more decimals. Excel: a number holds no trailing zeros (23.5850 is the number 23.585), so for `lat` / `lng` the import reads the text a number cell shows when its number format shows more decimals than the number has (`decimalTextColumns` in `lib/csv.ts`: 23.585 in a cell formatted 0.0000 reads "23.5850", 4 decimals; 23.58 reads "23.5800", counted as 3). A cell in General format shows 23.585 in Excel too, and is read as 3 decimals. A CSV sent as Excel is read as the text in the file, also one whose first header is "ID" (A5 fifth review: SheetJS reads such a file with its SYLK reader first, and every such file was read without its text, so a trailing zero was lost only when the browser sent a semicolon "ID" CSV as Excel; now only a file whose SYLK part formats a value, never a CSV, is, `idFileFormatsCells` in `lib/workbook-guard.ts`). The import's warning and its result box ask for a pin only for the rows whose customer has no usable location after the import (`kept` none, `SAVED_LOCATION_NEEDS_PIN`, `SAVED_LOCATION_NOT_USABLE`); rows whose customer keeps a usable saved location (`SAVED_LOCATION`) are counted on their own line, "nothing to do" (A5 fifth review: every listed row was told to be set on the map, with "No item is delivered without a correct location"). The remedy says to type or paste each coordinate with all its decimals and, if Excel drops a trailing zero, to format the column as Text before typing or pasting (it said "or to show 4 decimals", which turned rough pairs into exact ones).

**Data collection rules** (owner decisions of 1 Oct 2026; all six items built - items 3, 4 and 6 are described after item 5):

- **Item 1, a delivery time for one order** (`lib/dispatch/order-window.ts`, `app/t/[slug]/dispatch/delivery-times.tsx`, `PUT /api/dispatch/delivery-time`). Step 2's **Delivery times** list shows every customer of the day with its receiving hours (`windowLabel`: "(confirmed)", "(not confirmed)" or "(default - not confirmed)") and each order with its own time if it has one. **Set time / Change time** opens with the order's own time, else prefilled from the customer's own confirmed hours (hard, else preferred) - never from a company or customer-type default or hours nobody confirmed (they never count as a delivery window; the dialog then opens empty and says why, `orderTimeFormOf` / `orderTimeHint`) - and with no reason chosen; the dispatcher sets a start and / or an end and picks a reason (Urgent / Promised to customer / Other + note; `checkOrderTime` refuses none). Stored on the order (`Order.deliveryStartMin`, `deliveryEndMin`, `deliveryTimeReason`, `deliveryTimeNote`, `deliveryTimeSetAt`, `deliveryTimeSetById`), audited `ORDER_DELIVERY_TIME_SET` / `ORDER_DELIVERY_TIME_CLEARED`; the customer master is not changed. Refused (409) for an order on a locked (or later) load of the plan in use (`ORDER_ON_FROZEN_LOAD`) and for one brought forward to a later day (`ORDER_CARRIED`); a bring-forward copy does not take the time with it. The check, the order update and the audit row run in one transaction under the day lock and then the plan row lock (the lock LOCK takes), with the order and its loads read again under them, so a LOCK committed meanwhile is seen and nothing is written (frozen loads never change); a lock held more than 5 s is 409 `PLAN_BUSY`. Only a new time (start or end) sets `deliveryTimeSetAt`: the same time saved again changes nothing (no write, no audit row), and another reason or note alone is saved and audited without making the plan out of date (the outputs show the time only). **Planning** (`stopWindowFor`): all open orders of a customer go in one visit, so a timed order with both ends replaces the customer's hours (hard and preferred) for that visit; a time with one end only ("from 14:00", "by 10:00") keeps the customer's own closing or opening time on the other side (finish-by-closing holds) and its preferred hours inside what is left, and when the two do not meet the promised time alone is used with the plan warning *Delivery time outside the customer's receiving hours* (`outsideHours`); several overlapping times: within all of them; times that do not overlap: the one that ends first, with the plan warning *Orders of one customer have delivery times that do not overlap*. LOCK of a PLANNED load is refused with 409 `DELIVERY_TIME_CHANGED` (`orderIds`; "RE-PLAN first"), whatever the loading rule's setting (`deliveryTimeGate`, `deliveryTimeChangedRefusal`), when an order of the day of a customer on the load - on this load, on another load (a split customer's other part) or left unserved - had its time set, changed or removed after the plan was made, and the time the stop would be planned with now (`plannedVisitOrders` + `stopWindowFor`) is not the one it was planned with (`StopFacts.promised`): a time removed again, or saved again as planned, is not refused. "After the plan was made" is after its optimization read the orders: `BuiltRequest.builtAt`, kept as the plan inputs' `capturedAt` and the stop snapshots' `capturedAt`, so a time set while the search was queued or running counts (data collection review: it was the time the result was saved, up to 40 minutes later). The time is kept with the stop (`BuiltRequest.promised` → `StopFacts.promised` → the stop snapshot), so the plan screen, the Excel workbook, the driver PDF (`DetailStop.window` / `promised`) and the WhatsApp line say **Promised 10:00–11:00** ("by 10:00", "from 14:00"). A time set, changed or removed after planning makes the day out of date (`plannedLoadsMasterChanged`) and the stop says *Delivery time changed after planning* - also a promised time with the same hours as the stop was planned with (the stop was not planned with a promised time: LOCK asks for a RE-PLAN, so step 3 says out of date and RE-PLAN is on); a reason or note alone is no change. The day screen, the plan screen (and so the Excel, the driver PDF and WhatsApp) and LOCK judge a stop the same way: with all of its customer's orders of the day, except what its plan left out, as `buildDispatchRequest` leaves it out (`plannedVisitOrders`): an order with every case on loads locked before the plan was made, whole or in split portions (`OrderPlacement.lines`, `allCasesOn`), and an order the plan left unserved whole as heavier than any truck (`leftOutWhole`, passed for stops on PLANNED loads only), so a split part holding no timed order is not marked changed. Third review: a split customer stores every order of every part as a portion, so the rule used to leave out only whole orders; an order wholly on a locked part 1 then counted for the re-planned part 2, step 3 asked for a RE-PLAN that built the same stop again (the warning never went away), and a time set and removed on another order of the customer still made LOCK refuse with `DELIVERY_TIME_CHANGED`. The solver request is unchanged (the time is sent as the stop's hard window).
- **Item 2, own confirmed window** (`Customer.windowConfirmedAt`, `windowConfirmedById`). `PATCH /api/customers/:id` confirms hours sent with a time (who, when) and unconfirms hours all cleared; `windowConfirmed: true` confirms the hours as stored (all empty = **open all day**). The Details dialog has **Open all day** and **These hours are confirmed with the customer**, and says who confirmed them and when. The customer page shows the receiving hours and their confirmation, and (data collection review) has **Details** too (`customer-details-button.tsx`, the same dialog), since the Lock refusal and the Data to collect links send the dispatcher there. Existing customers start unconfirmed (nobody recorded who entered their hours).
- **Item 5, location admin-lock** (`savedLocationLocked`, `LOCATION_ADMIN_ONLY_MESSAGE` in `customer-attrs.ts`). A dispatcher (PLANNER, SUPERVISOR) sets a location only while the customer has no usable one (`locationBlocksDelivery`); changing a usable one needs TENANT_ADMIN or SUPER_ADMIN: `PUT /api/customers/:id/location` answers 403 `LOCATION_ADMIN_ONLY` ("Only an admin can change a saved location"), judged again on the locked row; confirming the saved point as it is stays allowed. A dispatcher's customer import never changes a usable saved location (the pair is ignored, never marked LOW; the row says why and a warning counts them); it still sets a missing or unusable one. An admin's import works as before (A5's rules; a verified location is still never overwritten by a file, F05). `PATCH` and `POST /api/customers` were already safe for coordinates (refused, or a new customer); since the data collection review `PATCH` also refuses a dispatcher's change of the code or branch (letter case aside, `customerKey`) of a customer with a usable saved location (403 `LOCATION_ADMIN_ONLY`): orders are matched to customers by code and branch, so renaming it away and creating one under its old code would send its orders to a point the dispatcher chose. Since the third review `PATCH` also refuses a dispatcher's change of `active` on one of two customers whose code and branch differ only in letter case when it moves the code's new orders (the order intake picks one with `preferredCustomer`: the active one first, then the one with a location) away from the twin with a usable saved location (403 `LOCATION_ADMIN_ONLY`, "Only an admin can deactivate this customer: new orders of its code would then go to x (...) instead of X (...), which has a saved location ..."); moving them to that twin from one without a usable location only fills a missing location and stays allowed, as does a customer without a twin. ADD LOCATION and the customer page show **Location (admin changes)** / **Confirm location** with the reason and only allow confirming the saved point; while locked the dialog offers no input, Read or map pin (`PinMap readOnly`). A usable saved point that is not exact (MEDIUM, never confirmed) cannot be confirmed as it is, so the dialog, the customer page and the day card's button say "This saved location is not exact and only an admin can change it" (`LOCKED_NOT_EXACT_MESSAGE`, `locationButtonText`), and Save reads **Ask an admin** (off). A dispatcher's import counts a pair that differs from a pin confirmed on the map apart: no import changes such a pin, an admin's neither, so that warning sends the dispatcher to the admin's Set location, not to an admin's import.
- **Item 3, location and delivery window before loading** (`TenantConfig.requireDataBeforeLoading`, Settings card **Customer data before loading**; off by default, switched on at launch). Only a company admin switches it: it is management's control over the dispatcher's own loads (a dispatcher who could switch it off, lock and switch it on again would bypass it), so it is not in `DISPATCHER_SETTINGS_FIELDS` and a dispatcher's or supervisor's PATCH of it is 403 `ADMIN_ONLY_SETTING`; the dispatcher's Settings shows **On** / **Off** without a switch, and the dispatcher still sets **Data to collect: days ahead**. On: a load leaving PLANNED (LOCK) is refused with 409 `DATA_REQUIRED` while a customer on it has no delivery window - neither its own confirmed hours nor a delivery time its planned stop carries (`StopFacts.promised` in the stop snapshot, so every part of a split customer counts; a stop without a plan snapshot is judged by its orders' times) - listing each customer, what it misses (a location too) and the remedy (`dataGate` in `plan-service.ts`, rules and words in `lib/dispatch/data-collection.ts`; [3.8](#38-step-6-load-states)). The location part is the always-on `locationGate` (A5). Planning is still allowed: with the switch on, step 2 shows **Loading rule is on** with the day's customers that miss data (`loadingGaps` of the day overview, `dayLoadingGaps`). A load already locked or loading is never judged again by it (frozen loads): it goes to LOADING and out also when the switch is turned on, or hours are un-confirmed, after it was locked. Data collection review: (1) a customer's confirmed hours count only when its stop was planned with them - a stop without a delivery time of its own planned with other hours (a customer-type default, or hours changed since) is refused with 409 `HOURS_CHANGED` (`hoursChangedRefusal`: planned with, confirmed, RE-PLAN first); (2) the **Loading rule is on** box (`dayLoadingGaps`) leaves out customers whose orders are all on locked, loading or dispatched loads (the rule never stops those loads; every case of the order, `DayOrderTime.allFrozen`: since the third review an order only partly there - a split part, the other part on a PLANNED load that LOCK judges - keeps its customer listed, although its **Set time** stays hidden, `frozen`), and with gaps step 2 stays orange (`resolveIssuesStep`) and its white list says receiving hours are needed (`confirmNotesSummary`); (3) a legacy run (`POST /api/runs/:id/dispatch`, dispatched whole) is refused with 409 `DATA_REQUIRED` too when a customer on it has no delivery window (`legacyRunDataRefusal`).
- **Item 4, data to collect** (`buildWorklist`, `loadWorklist` in `lib/dispatch/customer-master.ts`, `GET /api/customers/data-to-collect`, PLANNER). Active customers with open orders (not out, not brought forward) from today to `dataCollectDays` days ahead (Settings **Data to collect: days ahead**, default 3, 0-14; `?days=` overrides) that miss a usable location or their own confirmed receiving hours (a delivery time on an order lets that order be loaded but does not fill the master, so the customer stays on the list). Soonest delivery first; counted per depot (customers, no location, no hours) and per depot and day. Step 2's **Data to collect** panel (`data-to-collect.tsx`) shows the depots' counts and this depot's list with links to the customer pages, an Excel per depot or for all (`?format=xlsx`: sheet **Data to collect** with the master's columns, importable back, **Per depot and day**, **About this file**), and **Open on Customers** (`/customers?show=collect`: the Customers page's **Data to collect** switch, read in the database like the page's other filters, soonest delivery first, each row with what it misses and its first delivery). A customer whose code and branch differ only in letter case from the one the import updates (`preferredCustomer` among all the company's customers) is put on its own sheet **Same code, other case** of the Excel, for reading only, with `imported_as` (`LoadedWorklist.importedAs`; data collection review: on the first sheet two such rows made the import refuse the whole file, or sent one customer's data to the other).
- **Item 6, daily customer master** (`buildMasterWorkbook`, `GET /api/customers/master?since=YYYY-MM-DD`, PLANNER; Customers page **Download customer master** with a **Changed since** date, empty = the last 24 hours). Sheets: **Customers** (every customer, `MASTER_COLUMNS` / `masterValues`: code, branch, name, region and depot, type, priority and whether confirmed, the priority in use, lat / lng, a Google Maps link, location status, source and who confirmed it when, the customer's own hours, open all day, whether confirmed and by whom, the hours in use, unloading time, payment type, address, the phone for the driver (owner request 12 Oct 2026), active, created and updated), **Changed since ...** (`changeSummary`: customers created or changed since then, from the audit log and `Customer.createdAt` / `updatedAt`, with when, who and what), **Still missing** (the data to collect), **Same code, other case** (only when older customers' codes differ only in letter case: the import matches one of them, `preferredCustomer`, so only that one is on the Customers sheet and the others are listed here for reading, with `imported_as`; a second row would make the import refuse the file) and **About this file**. The first sheet's headers are the customer import's columns, so the file is corrected and imported back (Customers > Import): lat / lng are written only for a usable exact or confirmed point (never laundering a point that is not usable or not exact into a usable one), the hours are the customer's own (never a default; 1440 is written "24:00", which the import reads back), "yes" or blank for confirmed, the unloading time only when confirmed. Owner request 12 Oct 2026: both workbooks have a `phone` column (the customer's phone, for the driver to call before arrival - optional; a Text cell) that the import reads back, also from `customer_phone`, `mobile`, `contact_phone` or `tel` (`importedPhoneCell`; checked by `readCustomerPhone`, a bad one an error of its row; a blank cell keeps the saved phone, as for every optional column); `rowVersion` includes the phone only when the customer has one, so files downloaded before the phone existed keep their row versions; `what_to_do` asks for a missing phone as optional. The phone never puts a customer on the list and is not part of the loading rule. The data-to-collect sheets have a **what_to_do** column (`collectText`): hours already shown that are not confirmed stay not confirmed when the row is left as it is, so the collector writes yes in `hours_confirmed` (the About sheet, the import page and the guide say so). The import reads `hard_from`, `hard_to`, `preferred_from`, `preferred_to`, `open_all_day` and `hours_confirmed` (`readImportedHours`: hours entered or changed are confirmed by the importer unless it says no; unchanged hours are confirmed only by yes; nothing un-confirms unchanged hours) and `priority_confirmed` (`importedPriority`: without the column every priority is confirmed, as before; blank confirms only a changed one). A row that changes nothing writes nothing (so the master imported back as downloaded changes nothing, and `updatedAt` moves only on a real change; a saved point that is confirmed or HIGH is the same point whatever its source); each customer the import changes gets its own audit row: `UPDATE` for its fields and for a point marked LOW (what it was, what the file made it, `source: IMPORT`), `CUSTOMER_LOCATION_SET` for each location it writes, `CREATE` for each customer it creates. Rows without lat / lng whose customer has no usable location are counted in one warning (not one line per row). Item 5's admin-lock and A5's exact-location rules apply as for any import. Data collection review: (1) every downloaded row has a hidden `row_version` (`rowVersion`: a hash of every field the import can change); a row whose customer was changed in RouteIQ after the download is not imported at all, and the rows it would have changed are listed (`staleRows`, one warning: "Download a new file and enter those changes again") - compared with the customer as it is now, an old file undid later edits and confirmed hours nobody checked under the importer's name; (2) a code the import's own format refuses (an order file accepts any non-blank code, "AB 12") is accepted when it matches an existing customer, and refused only for a new one; (3) in an end column (`hard_to`, `preferred_to`) an Excel time of 1 (a typed 24:00) is the end of the day; (4) **Changed since** also lists customers deleted in the period (from their `DELETE` row: code, branch, name, "Deleted") and changes to the customers of **Same code, other case** (marked), and `since` goes back at most `MASTER_SINCE_MAX_DAYS` (31) days (400 otherwise: every customer audit row of the period, with its whole before and after, is read into the web process).

**Details** (`customer-dialog.tsx`, form helpers in `customer-details.ts`) calls `PATCH /api/customers/:id` (`apps/web/app/api/customers/[id]/route.ts`) with **only the fields the dispatcher changed** (audit F07, owner decision 9): customer type, priority (which also sets `priorityConfirmed`), unloading minutes (`avgServiceTimeMin`), the hard and preferred windows and, since the owner request of 12 Oct 2026, **Phone (for the driver to call)** (`Customer.phone`, optional: digits, spaces and + - ( ) / only, 6 to 20 digits, `readCustomerPhone` in `lib/dispatch/customer-phone.ts`, the same rule in the dialog and in `customerSchema`; empty = no phone; sent only when it changed as stored). The phone is printed on the driver sheet ("Tel ..."), is a "Phone" column of the Excel route sheets, a "Call customer" link on the driver page (`telUrl`: a local number gets the company's calling code, as the WhatsApp links) and a column of the customer master and data-to-collect workbooks (imported back; a blank cell keeps it). It is not a loading-rule requirement. A window is sent whole: when its start or its end changed, both ends go as the dialog shows them (A2 review). One end sent alone was merged by the route with the other end as stored, and the day screen does not poll outside an optimization, so a dialog opened with hours changed since (by another dispatcher or tab) could save a window nobody typed: 06:00-10:00 on screen, 12:00-15:00 stored since, end set to 16:00, saved as 12:00-16:00. Now 06:00-16:00 is saved, replacing the other change as a whole. Nothing changed = no request ("Nothing changed."). Audit `UPDATE Customer`.

- **Opening.** A priority or unloading time that is a default (`prioritySource` / `serviceSource` TYPE or DEFAULT, from the day overview) opens as a default, never as the customer's own value: the priority list has "P3 - default, not confirmed" (picking any P, P3 included, confirms it), and the unloading box is empty with the default as placeholder ("15 (customer type default)"). A window ending at midnight (1440) shows "24:00", which reads back (it used to show "00:00 +1", which could not be saved).
- **Checks before anything is sent.** Times with the shared strict `parseHhmm` (`lib/dispatch/time.ts`): "06:90" or "25:00" is refused (the dialog's own parser read "06:90" as 07:30; that `toMinutes` is removed). Both ends of a window or neither, end after start. Unloading time: whole minutes 0 to 480 (`MAX_SERVICE_MIN`); "10 min", "ten" or "1.5" is refused (it used to become 0 minutes, confirmed).
- **Unloading time left empty** = no own time: the customer-type or Settings default applies (`effectiveAttrs`). The dialog sends `avgServiceTimeMin: null` when the dispatcher cleared an own time; the route then stores the column default (10, `CUSTOMER_SERVICE_COLUMN_DEFAULT`) with `serviceTimeConfirmed = false`. An explicit 0 is kept and confirmed. This is the only way to put a customer back on the default: a customer import can give a new own time (a number, always confirmed) but cannot clear one, because a blank `avg_service_time_min` cell or a missing column keeps the stored time and its confirmation, and text such as "default" is refused (`customer-import-service-time.spec.ts`).
- **API.** `customerPatchSchema` takes `avgServiceTimeMin` as a JSON whole number 0 to 480 or null, and the four window fields as JSON whole numbers 0 to 1440 or null: a string ("", "420", "10 min") is 400, never coerced (a coerced "" used to be 0, i.e. midnight or no unloading time). Fields not sent are not changed and not confirmed.
- **Answers after a switch.** A Save answer that arrives after the dialog was closed or opened for another customer is reported for its own customer only.

After either dialog saves, the day **and** the plan below it are read again, the plan in place (audit F13, `afterCustomerSaved` in `dispatch-client.tsx`, `PlanView` `reloadSignal`). A READY plan does not poll, so its "changed after planning" notes, the load's **Changed after planning** badge, its warnings and the "New pin" line of the WhatsApp texts built from it used to appear only after a page reload, also for LOCKED loads, which the day's `outdated` count leaves out.

What the reload does **not** change: a stop keeps the point it was planned with. `getPlanDetail` takes the stop's pin from its snapshot, so the map, the stop's pin link, the route link and the stop's link in the WhatsApp text stay the planned ones (also after a page reload). The WhatsApp text (`whatsappText`) and the driver sheet (`driverPackModel`) add the change and "New pin - ask the dispatcher which one to use: <link>" under the stop, for a pin moved more than 50 m (`PIN_MOVED_M`). The planned pin is replaced only by a re-plan of the load: a PLANNED load at RE-PLAN, a LOCKED or LOADING load after it is put back to Planned. Since the A5 third review a stop still planned at a point that was **not usable** when a new pin replaced it cannot be locked, loaded or dispatched until that re-plan (409 `STOP_PIN_REPLACED`, [3.8](#38-step-6-load-states)); an ordinary correction of a usable point keeps the "New pin" path above (see "Changed after planning", [3.7](#37-step-5-reviewing-the-plan)). That is the owner's decision of 28 Sep 2026 ("Allow, driver gets new pin", [7.5](#75-open-questions-for-the-owner)): a pin corrected by more than 50 m after planning does not block the load; it can go, and the driver's text and sheet show "New pin".

### 3.5 Step 3: the day overview

`GET /api/dispatch/day?date=&depotId=` runs `getDayOverview` (`apps/web/lib/dispatch/day-overview.ts`). The screen re-reads it after every action, and every 3 s while a plan is optimizing. It returns:

- the date (default tomorrow in the tenant timezone), the cutoff, the active depots and the selected depot;
- the orders in scope. `ordersInScopeWhere` in `plan-service.ts` selects the same depot and delivery date. Every order has a depot (owner rule, audit PR A5: `Order.depotId` is NOT NULL since migration `20260930120000_orders_always_have_depot`); before A5 orders without a depot were included when the tenant had exactly one active depot, and the migration gave them that depot. Counts, cases, kg and late count;
- one issue card per customer branch, with effective priority and unloading minutes and where each comes from (`prioritySource`, `serviceSource`: CUSTOMER, TYPE or DEFAULT; the Details dialog opens a default as a default, audit F07), window text, issues and a `blocking` flag, blocking ones first. A deactivated customer that still has open orders (not on a frozen load, not dispatched) shows only `CUSTOMER_INACTIVE` (blocking; its open orders are left unserved at optimize). When the plan in use still has those orders on PLANNED loads (it was made before the customer was deactivated), the card says so and asks for a RE-PLAN. A deactivated customer whose orders are all on frozen loads gets no card (frozen loads keep them);
- weights per order **line**, not per product (`lineWeightStatus` in `apps/web/lib/dispatch/weights.ts`), for the open cases of each line (cases on frozen loads of the plan in use are subtracted per line, as `buildDispatchRequest` counts them, so a partly locked split order is still checked. The open rest of such an order is planned with the product's weight at every optimize and never saved on the line it shares with the frozen part, so a weight entered or corrected since is listed only while a PLANNED part of the plan in use carries another case weight than the product has now - planned at 0 kg, or corrected since - read with the timetable check's rule (`portionPlannedKgPerCase` in `split.ts`: the part's `kgPerCase`, else a 0-kg line whose part weighs no more than its weighed lines). Second review of PR4: these were never listed, so the day screen said "up to date" with RE-PLAN off while the check blocked the PLANNED load they now overload (`CAPACITY_KG_NEW_WEIGHT`)): `productsWithoutWeight` (0 kg and no case weight on the product: counted as 0 kg, the same lines the `WEIGHT_REQUIRED` check names) and `weightsToApply` (the product's case weight gives the line another kg: 0 kg and entered since, or weighed from the master and corrected since; applied at the next optimize), each with lines and cases per product;
- the live plan from `currentPlan`: the highest version for (tenant, depot, date) that is not `SUPERSEDED` or `ARCHIVED` and has no `supersededAt`, with its latest `RunJob`, loads by status, summary and whether the cases reconcile;
- `pending`: orders of the day that are not in the applied scenario's `scope.orderIds` or `scope.frozenOrderIds`, i.e. orders that arrived after the plan was made;
- `openOrders` (PR3): orders with cases not yet on a locked, loading or dispatched load of the plan in use. 0 while the day has orders means there is nothing left to plan;
- (PR9) `carriedIn`: the orders of the day brought forward from earlier days (customer, cases, the date first due, and whether the plan in use contains them yet), the day screen's list with the badge "Carried over from 26 Sep"; `pending.carried`: of the pending orders, those brought forward (a re-plan adds them with reason LATE_ORDER); `carriedOut`: orders of this day brought forward to later days since (how many, their cases, the days). Those orders are not in `orders`, `openOrders`, `pending` or the issue cards any more: `ordersInScopeWhere` leaves out an order with `carriedToOrderId` set. The "Not delivered on earlier days" box has its own request (`GET /api/dispatch/carry-over`, [3.11](#311-step-9-late-orders-and-plan-versions)), read when the day loads and when its orders change, not on the 3 s polls; `plan.loadsOfDay` (PR9 second review): the plan's loads by status without the loads that never left the depot and hold only orders brought forward to a later day (a load counts when it left, holds an order not brought forward, or holds nothing), next to `plan.loadsByStatus` (every load);
- `outdated` (only with an applied plan; the keys of `UP_TO_DATE`, all 0 when up to date): open cases in its scope whose case weight was entered or corrected since (`weightCases`, including the open rest of a partly frozen order above), and orders of customers deactivated since that are still on its PLANNED loads (`inactiveOrders`). The plan view shows the same as warnings (`outdatedNotes` in `plan-detail.ts`). Since PR4 also customers on PLANNED loads whose pin or receiving hours were corrected (`masterChanged`) and trucks with PLANNED loads whose capacity or payload was corrected (`trucksChanged`, PR4 review), both from the snapshots (`plannedLoadsMasterChanged` in `snapshots.ts`). Since audit PR A5's second review also active customers on PLANNED loads whose location is not usable any more (`locationBlocked`: `locationBlocksDelivery` on the customer now, for example a saved point a customer import marked LOW after planning; the snapshots compare only the pin and the hours, so this was not counted and the day said "The plan is up to date"). Step 3 then says "the location of N customer(s) on planned loads can no longer be used (drop the pin on each one, or RE-PLAN to leave their orders unserved)" and offers RE-PLAN; their loads cannot be locked meanwhile (`locationGate`, [3.8](#38-step-6-load-states)). A customer only on LOCKED or LOADING loads is not counted (a re-plan keeps those loads): LOADING and DISPATCH of such a load are refused instead. Since the pallets review also the cases on PLANNED loads planned by pallets whose rows give other pallets with the cases per pallet known now (`palletFactorCases`: a factor corrected under Products since planning, `rowPalletUnitsNow` in `split.ts`; before, only the manifest's grey `palletNotes` line said so and the day read "ready"); a load the new figure puts over its bays cannot be locked meanwhile (`CAPACITY_PALLETS_NEW_FACTOR`, [3.8](#38-step-6-load-states)). Review of 9 Oct 2026: also trucks with PLANNED loads taken out of service since (`trucksInactive`: deactivated under Trucks, `truckOutOfService` in `snapshots.ts`; a one-day hired truck retired because its day is over is not counted). Before, deactivating a truck was silent: the day said "up to date" and its loads could be locked and dispatched; now LOCK, LOADING and DISPATCH of its PLANNED loads are refused (409 `TRUCK_INACTIVE`, `truckGate`; locked and loading loads are kept as they are, and the plan says how to move their orders). And open orders the option in use left unserved for their customer's data that a re-plan would plan now (`unservedNowPlannable`: `MISSING_COORDINATES`, `INVALID_LOCATION` or `INVALID_CUSTOMER` whose customer is active with a usable location now, `unservedNowPlannable` in `left-out-note.ts`; before, the day said "up to date" after ADD LOCATION and only the plan's own Re-plan planned the order). The plan view says both too;
- `kept` (the kept-load warning, 24 Oct 2026): the plan in use's LOCKED and LOADING loads whose customer data changed since they were planned (`keptChangesOf` in `lib/dispatch/kept-changes-server.ts`, the same reader as the plan screen, the re-plan and `GET /api/runs/:id/kept-changes`; [3.7](#37-step-5-reviewing-the-plan)). It is **not** a key of `outdated`: a re-plan keeps those loads exactly as they are, so it never turns RE-PLAN on or marks the day out of date. Step 3 shows it as the box "Locked loads planned with older customer data" under the out-of-date box, also when RE-PLAN is off (unlocking is then the only way to plan them again). Null without an applied plan, while the plan is optimizing (the screen polls every few seconds then), for a day that is over, or with `KEPT_CHANGES=off`. A read error is logged and read as null: it never stops the day screen;
- `unserved` (review of 9 Oct 2026): the option in use's unserved orders still open on the day (orders, cases; not those brought forward or dispatched since), and `replan` (review of 5614ba9): of them, the orders a re-plan could place now (`replanCouldPlace` in `left-out-note.ts`): not those left out for their customer's data (`MISSING_COORDINATES`, `INVALID_LOCATION`, `INVALID_CUSTOMER`) until it is fixed (`unservedNowPlannable`), not cases heavier than any truck (`EXCEEDS_ANY_TRUCK_CAPACITY`) while every line the row left out still is, with the planning case weight and the day's trucks now (`caseHeavierThanAnyTruck` / `maxCasePayloadKg`), and none on a day before the company's today (bring them forward instead). Every other reason counts (no room or time slot found, receiving hours, the shift: a truck added or another search may place them). Step 3 uses it below;
- active trucks with their cases per load round, and the last 20 upload batches for the day.

The Step 3 button reads OPTIMIZE when no plan is applied yet and RE-PLAN when one is. It is enabled when the day has orders and there is either no applied plan, at least one pending order, an order the plan leaves unserved that a re-plan could place now (`unserved.replan`; review of 9 Oct 2026: before, Step 3 said "The plan is up to date with all orders" with a green tick and RE-PLAN off, for example after a truck was added; now it says how many orders are unserved and the step is not done. Review of 5614ba9: only `replan` keeps RE-PLAN on and the step not done - every unserved order did, as the plan screen's Re-plan still does (`nothingToReplan`), so a day with a customer still without a pin or a day that is over never showed done. Step 3 still says how many are unserved, never "up to date with all orders", and, only to those who can plan, the next step: "RE-PLAN tries them again", "RE-PLAN tries N of them again; the others stay unserved until what their reasons say is fixed", "RE-PLAN cannot place them until ..." or, on a day that is over, to bring them forward from a later day's screen), an `outdated` plan (the Step 3 card then says why), or a failed last optimization ("the previous plan was kept"). It is disabled with "nothing left to plan" when `openOrders` is 0 and nothing is pending (PR3, review F03), and while an action of the plan below it runs (PR3 review, [3.11](#311-step-9-late-orders-and-plan-versions)). The words under it come from `dayNothingLeftText` (`carry-view.ts`, PR9 second review), which says what the server's 409 `NOTHING_TO_PLAN` says: when orders of the day were brought forward to a later day (`carriedOut`), "Nothing left to plan: N order(s) of this day were brought forward to 28 Sep and are planned there", that the loads still showing them stay for the record, and, for a LOCKED or LOADING load holding only brought-forward orders (it was loaded), to unload those cases before the loads of 28 Sep are picked and put the load back to Planned - never "To change a load, unlock it first" for such a load, and never "Every load has left the depot" while it is still at the depot (it is not counted in `loadsOfDay`). The unlock advice and Step 4's "every load is out" count `loadsOfDay`. Step 4 shows done when the plan is DISPATCHED, or when every load of the plan in use is out although its last re-plan failed (the version then stays FAILED, holding the plan that was dispatched).

**Stale-day guard** (PR3, review ADD-STALE-DAY-CLIENT). `DispatchClient` loads the day only through the day loader (`app/t/[slug]/dispatch/day-loader.ts`), and every load is for the day selected **now**: the first load, polling, "Try again", and the reload after an action (a load change, OPTIMIZE / RE-PLAN, a confirmed file, a saved dialog) that ends after the dispatcher picked another date or depot. Second review of PR3: those reloads closed over the date of the render the action started in, so they reloaded the old day and the screen stayed on "Loading <new date>..." for good (no load on its way, no error, no Try again). As a backstop, an answer for a selection the dispatcher has left, with no other load on its way, is not shown; the selection is loaded instead. The loader uses a gate (`request-gate.ts`): an answer for a date or depot the dispatcher already left is dropped, whatever order the answers arrive in. An answer for the day being loaded is shown when it is newer than the one on screen, even if a later refresh of that day has started, and the 3 s polling while optimizing skips a tick while the previous load of the day is still on its way (at most 5 ticks in a row). Review of PR3: the first version kept only the newest answer, so a day overview slower than 3 s dropped every answer and froze the screen on "Optimizing...". After a date or depot change the screen shows only the pickers and "Loading <date>" until that day has loaded; a failed load shows the error with "Try again" instead of the previous day. A day shown after a failed load (`afterError`) also reloads the plan below it, in place: `DispatchClient` bumps `PlanView`'s `reloadSignal` prop, which runs the plan's own load, so an open late order, the opened loads and a running action stay (fourth review of PR3: this used to bump the plan's key, and one failed day poll during an optimization remounted the plan and closed the late order being typed). The plan is remounted only when its id changes, after OPTIMIZE / RE-PLAN reached the server, and after a plan action whose day reload was shown (`refresh()` answers true), so a failed day reload leaves the plan on screen (third review of PR3: the day's Try again brought the day back while Step 4 stayed replaced by an error). A file check that answers after the dispatcher picked another day is not offered on the new day, and a confirmed file moves the screen to the file's delivery date only while the dispatcher is still on the day it was added on (`dayAfterConfirm`; third review of PR3: the answer took the screen and the URL back to the file's date). `api()` (`client-api.ts`) never rejects: a request that does not reach the server (offline, a connection reset while Railway redeploys) answers `{ ok: false, status: 0 }` with "The server could not be reached (...). Check the connection and try again." like any refusal (second review of PR3: a rejected request skipped the clean-up, so one network error left OPTIMIZE and every plan action disabled until the page was reloaded). Upload, Confirm, OPTIMIZE / RE-PLAN and the plan's actions are enabled only while the day on screen is the selected one; their payloads are built from the loaded day, and OPTIMIZE / RE-PLAN send `expect: { date, depotId }` (the server answers 409 `DAY_MISMATCH` for a plan of another day).

### 3.6 Step 4: OPTIMIZE

**Which route runs.** `optimize()` in `dispatch-client.tsx`:

- **No applied plan:** `POST /api/dispatch/plan { date, depotId, optimize: true, allowMissingLocations, expect }` (`apps/web/app/api/dispatch/plan/route.ts`). It calls `getOrCreatePlan`, which returns the live plan or creates version 1 (`status DRAFT`, `reason INITIAL`, audit `CREATE RunPlan`), then `startDispatchOptimize`. Version 1 is created by `createInitialPlan` under the **day lock** (`lockPlanDay`, a PostgreSQL advisory lock per company, depot and date; PR3, review F06): the check for a live plan and the create run in one transaction, so concurrent first requests (two dispatchers, two tabs, the legacy "New run") get the same plan. The legacy `POST /api/runs` uses the same helper and answers an existing plan with 200.
- **Stale screen guard** (PR3, review ADD-STALE-DAY-CLIENT). The day screen sends `expect: { date, depotId }` of the day it shows; `/api/dispatch/plan` and `/replan` answer 409 `DAY_MISMATCH` when the plan is for another day or depot.
- **Plan already applied:** `POST /api/runs/:id/replan` with reason `LATE_ORDER` when late orders are pending, else `REOPTIMIZE` ([3.11](#311-step-9-late-orders-and-plan-versions)).
- **409 `LOCATION_REQUIRED`:** the browser asks whether to optimize anyway (`askOverride` in `client-api.ts`; since the A5 third review the question says what is wrong: "N customer(s) still have no location ... reason 'location missing'" when every one is missing, "N customer(s) have a saved location that cannot be used (not exact, outside the delivery area, or not valid). Their orders will be UNSERVED until the pin is placed on each one." when every one is `INVALID_LOCATION`, and both counts when mixed; it used to call all of them "no location ... location missing"). If yes, it sends the request again with `allowMissingLocations: true`, and those customers' orders become unserved with reason `MISSING_COORDINATES` or `INVALID_LOCATION` (never sent to the optimizer: `locationBlocksDelivery`, owner's location rule, [3.4](#34-step-2-customer-locations-and-details)).
- **409 `PALLET_FACTOR_REQUIRED`** (truck capacity in pallets, owner decision 4 Oct 2026; checked first, no override): the depot has an active truck with bays and an open line the request plans has a product without a usable cases per pallet (a whole number 1-10,000, `validPalletFactor` in `lib/dispatch/pallets.ts`): not on a frozen load, and not a line `buildDispatchRequest` leaves out before (a deactivated customer's, a customer's without a usable location, a case heavier than any truck). `buildDispatchRequest` lists them (`missingPalletFactors`: product, lines, cases) and the start gate (`palletFactorGate`) refuses OPTIMIZE and RE-PLAN before the location question: "Cannot plan by pallets: 3 product(s) on this day's orders have no cases per pallet: TN1.5L (120 cases), ... Enter the cases per pallet under Products (company admins can edit products), then optimize again." The screens show it as a red message with an **Open Products** link (`palletRefusalToast`), never a confirm; the day overview shows the same list in red (`productsWithoutPalletFactor`, with the same exclusions: `planningKgPerCase` in `weights.ts` and `maxCasePayloadKg` / `caseHeavierThanAnyTruck` in `split.ts` are shared with the builder; before the pallets review it also named lines OPTIMIZE does not refuse for). A re-plan refused by it creates no version.
- **409 `WEIGHT_REQUIRED`** (review F02): open lines still have no weight and an active truck of the depot has a payload (`capacityWeightKg > 0`; payload 0 = no weight limit, so a depot whose trucks all have 0 - NMWC since the owner decisions of 4 Oct 2026 - is never asked, and no "Planned without weights" note is added). The body lists `unknownWeights` (product, lines, cases). The browser asks (`askOverride` in `client-api.ts`: "Cancel, and add the case weight under Products - or optimize anyway (treated as 0 kg)?"; only TENANT_ADMIN can edit products, so PLANNER and SUPERVISOR users read "ask a company admin to add the case weight under Products", `weightFixText`); yes sends `allowMissingWeights: true`. The plan then carries a warning ("Planned without weights for N order line(s) ...") in its scenario warnings, and `OPTIMIZE_STARTED` records the override. The plan's Re-plan button asks the same questions.

`POST /api/runs/:id/optimize` (`apps/web/app/api/runs/[id]/optimize/route.ts`) calls the same `startDispatchOptimize`. The dispatch screen does not use it; the legacy run page does. Its old per-company limiter is gone (PR3): every solve entry goes through the shared solve admission ([2.7](#27-background-job-model)).

**`startDispatchOptimize`** (`apps/web/lib/dispatch/start-optimize.ts`) checks, in order:

1. the plan exists;
2. it is for the `expect`ed day and depot, when the caller sent one (else 409 `DAY_MISMATCH`);
3. it is not superseded (status `SUPERSEDED` or `supersededAt` set);
4. it is not a legacy plan, else 409 `LEGACY_PLAN`. `isLegacyPlan` is true when the plan has `RouteAssignment` rows without a `loadId`, or its chosen scenario has no dispatch `scope` and `loads`;
5. (audit PR4, F09) a version OPTIMIZING whose current job has ended is reset first (`repairEndedJobPlan`: FAILED, `OPTIMIZE_FAILED` reason `STUCK_PLAN`, the user as actor); then, if a job is QUEUED or RUNNING in the database, it answers 202 with that job (before audit PR4 also for an ended job, or when only the in-memory map held the run: a 202 that started nothing); a version still OPTIMIZING without such a job (the reset could not take the row) answers 409 `PLAN_STUCK`, decided only in the start transaction on the locked plan row (review of audit PR4: the plan row read before the job checks may be out of date - a job ending in between moved the plan to FAILED or READY - and was answered `PLAN_STUCK` for a plan that was not stuck; `unstickIfEnded` also reads the plan again after the job checks);
6. it is not already applied (`chosenScenarioId` set, whatever the status - also FAILED, since a failed re-plan still holds the previous plan), else 409 `NEW_VERSION_REQUIRED` (use re-plan). A version a re-plan just created carries a copy of the previous plan; it counts as not applied while it has never had a job (`freshVersion`). Review of PR3: a FAILED version with a plan could be re-optimized in place (a second tab's OPTIMIZE, `POST /api/runs/:id/optimize`), replacing loads the dispatcher had seen without a new version.

It then calls `buildDispatchRequest`, and refuses missing locations and unknown weights (unless allowed, `gate` in `start-optimize.ts`), nothing left to plan (409 `NOTHING_TO_PLAN` when every order is on a locked, loading or dispatched load - its text says to unlock a load only when a LOCKED or LOADING one exists, otherwise that every load has left the depot and a late order can still be planned; 400 "Upload orders first" only when the day has no orders at all) and a depot with no active trucks (400). Then it reserves the solve admission (429 / 503, [2.7](#27-background-job-model)); every answer below that starts no job gives the reservation back.

**Weights from the product master** (`resolveOrderLineWeights` / `masterLineKg` in `weights.ts`). A line weight of 0 means unknown. A line at 0 kg, or weighed from the master (`weightFromMaster`), whose product's case weight now gives another kg, is planned with cases × that weight; the order total is summed again. File weights never change, and orders whose kg lives on the order only (older orders: lines at 0 kg, order total above 0) are left as they are. `buildDispatchRequest` does this **in memory** and lists what it would save in `weightChanges` (orders with no part on a frozen load of this version, not DISPATCHED / DELIVERED; the open rest of a partly frozen order is planned with it but not saved). So a re-plan probe that is refused leaves the live plan's orders, loads and portions exactly as they were (review of PR2). The job saves `weightChanges` only when it applies the plan made with them (step 5 of the background job below, PR3 review): a failed or stale optimization saves nothing, so after a failed re-plan the copied loads still match their orders' kg and the "planned with the old weight" warning stays.

**Start transaction** (timeout 30 s, maxWait 10 s; everything below commits together or not at all - PR3, review F07 / ADD-JOB-AUDIT). It takes `lockIntake` (the lock that confirm, late order and batch delete take), then the plan row (`lockRunForWrite`, 5 s lock timeout) and checks again on the locked row: superseded (409), another job won the race (202 with that job; OPTIMIZING without a QUEUED or RUNNING job is 409 `PLAN_STUCK`, never a 202 - audit PR4), already applied (409 `NEW_VERSION_REQUIRED`), and the frozen loads are still the ones the request was built around (else 409 `LOADS_CHANGED`). It checks that every order of `scope.orderIds` / `scope.frozenOrderIds` still exists (else 409 `ORDERS_CHANGED`: a batch delete committed after the request was built), creates the `RunJob` (`attemptNo` + 1, `QUEUED`, `requestJson`), sets `RunPlan.status = OPTIMIZING` and `currentJobId`, and writes audit `OPTIMIZE_STARTED`. An audit failure therefore leaves no QUEUED orphan, and an immediate retry starts. Once OPTIMIZING is committed, a batch delete for that day is refused. A wait for the intake lock past the timeout (Prisma P2028, e.g. a large confirm holding the lock) answers 409 `INTAKE_BUSY` ("try again in a moment"), and one for the plan row 409 `PLAN_BUSY`, not 500. It then calls `scheduleDispatchOptimize` without waiting and answers 202 (`queued: true` when the job waits for a solver slot).

**`buildDispatchRequest(tenantId, runId, scenarios?, { now? })`** (`apps/web/lib/dispatch/plan-service.ts`) turns the day into a `DispatchRequest`. `now` is the time the plan is made (default: the clock; `startDispatchOptimize` and `replan` pass it through, so tests can fix it):

| Input | How it is built |
|---|---|
| Orders | `ordersInScopeWhere`, oldest upload first, with customer and lines |
| Frozen loads | This run's `PlanLoad` rows with status other than PLANNED. Orders wholly on them go to `scope.frozenOrderIds`. For a split order partly on frozen loads, the frozen cases are subtracted per line (`frozenLineCases`) and only the rest is planned |
| Stops | All open orders of one customer branch become one stop: `stop_id` = customer id, `order_ids` = the order ids, or `<orderId>~open` for the open part of a partly frozen order |
| Priority | Per order (`prOf`): `priorityFromFile ? min(order.priority, effective priority) : effective priority`. The stop takes the lowest `prOf` of its orders, and every order of that stop stores that stop priority in `scope.orderPriority`, not its own `prOf`. Only orders pre-dropped for a missing or invalid location store their own `prOf`. The summary's per-priority service % uses these stored values. `strict_priorities: true` is always sent |
| Late flag | `late` is true if any order of the group is late |
| Weights | Per line: its own kg (`weightKg / cases`), or cases × the product's case weight now for a 0-kg or master-weighed line (see above); for an order whose kg lives on the order only, the order kg per case. Lines still at 0 kg are counted in `unknownWeights` (the `WEIGHT_REQUIRED` gate) |
| Deactivated customers | All open orders of an inactive customer are pre-dropped as `INVALID_CUSTOMER` ("customer deactivated after the order was confirmed - reactivate it ..."), with a request warning. Not blocking. Reactivating the customer plans them again at the next re-plan. Orders on frozen loads are untouched. Deactivated products are planned as ordered, with a warning |
| Missing locations | Pre-dropped (`preDrops`, unserved before the solver runs) and reported as a `BlockingIssue` |
| Cases heavier than any truck | When every usable truck has a payload, a line whose case weight exceeds the largest one is pre-dropped as a portion `EXCEEDS_ANY_TRUCK_CAPACITY` ("One case of X weighs N kg, more than any truck payload (M kg) - check the product weight."), with a request warning. The rest of the order is planned (review F01) |
| Windows | Effective hard and preferred windows. A window that ends before it starts is ignored with a warning (`usableWindow`) |
| Split deliveries | When `TenantConfig.splitDeliveries` is on and no truck that still has a load left can carry the customer's cases or kg (`partCapFor`), `choosePartCapacity` (`apps/web/lib/dispatch/split.ts`) picks a part size and `splitIntoParts` cuts the SKU lines into parts. Each part becomes its own stop (`<customerId>#k`) with order ids `<orderId>~k`. The exact lines of every part are kept in `scope.portions` as `PortionRecord`s ([4.4](#44-how-the-web-shapes-the-request)) |
| Service time | `stopService(base, serviceMinPerCase, cases, totalCases?)` (`apps/web/lib/dispatch/service-time.ts`): the customer's service minutes plus unloading minutes per case. A split part gets its proportional share of the base time (at least 5 minutes) plus the per-case time of its own cases. Rounded and capped at `MAX_SERVICE_MIN` (480), the solver's `service_min` limit; a capped stop gives a request warning with the minutes it needs. Customer, tenant-default and imported service times accept at most 480 |
| Money | `margin` and `revenue` per stop only when every order carries a value (`portionMoney` for split parts); otherwise `null` |
| Plan continuity | Only when `usesPlanContinuity(run)` is true, i.e. the plan has a `parentRunId` and its reason is not `REOPTIMIZE` (so `LATE_ORDER` or `MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT`). Each stop then gets `previous_truck_id`: the truck that carried most of its cases in the parent version (`previousTruckOf`, a vote per order line weighted by cases). The solver charges `change_penalty_per_stop` (default 3.0 in `apps/solver/dispatch_models.py`, not sent by the web) for moving it. A `REOPTIMIZE` sends no previous trucks, so every scenario starts from scratch (commit `19831f0`) |
| Trucks | Active trucks of the depot: cases, kg, fixed, trip and per-km cost, km per litre, availability window, `maxTripsPerDay`, and `frozen_trips` (depart, return and cases of each frozen load) |
| Config | From `TenantConfig` (mapping in [4.4](#44-how-the-web-shapes-the-request)). `time_limit_sec: null` lets the solver choose. The provider comes from `routingProviderFor`. Scenarios: RECOMMENDED, MIN_TRUCKS, MIN_DISTANCE |
| Same-day start (PR8) | When the plan is built **on its own delivery day** in the company timezone (`TenantConfig.timezone`, Asia/Muscat), `sameDayPlanFrom` (`apps/web/lib/dispatch/plan-from.ts`) takes now + the turnaround between loads (`reloadMinutes`, the preparation time; at most 24:00). If that is later than the first departure setting and the depot opening, it is sent as `shift_start_min`, a plan warning says "Planned from 09:30 (now 09:00 + 30 min preparation): the plan is for today, so no new load leaves the depot before 09:30. ..." (the first of the optimizer's warnings; the plan screen can show other notes above it), and the plan's settings keep it (`PlanSettings.planFrom`, for the ASSUMPTIONS sheet; `shiftStartMin` stays the setting). Whenever the plan is built on its delivery day (also before the first departure) the time it is made is sent as `loading_from_min` and kept as `PlanSettings.loadingFromMin` (`planDayNowMin`, PR8 review): loading starts then, so every new load leaves no earlier than now + turnaround + loading per case x its cases ([3.11](#311-step-9-late-orders-and-plan-versions)). Frozen trips, truck availability and everything else are sent as before. A plan for a future day is unchanged |

It returns `{ request, preDrops, scope, blocking, warnings, unknownWeights }`. `scope` also records `frozenLoadOrderIds` and `frozenLoadIds`, so the result can later be checked against the loads that were frozen when it was computed.

**Background job** (`apps/web/lib/jobs/dispatch-job.ts`). `scheduleDispatchOptimize` registers the promise in the shared in-flight map (`trackInflight` in `optimize-job.ts`; this assumes one web replica). `runJob` then:

1. waits for a solver slot when the solve admission queued it (PR3);
2. sets the `RunJob` to `RUNNING`, 20 % (only if it is still QUEUED);
3. calls `callDispatchSolver` (`apps/web/lib/solver-client.ts`): POST to `SOLVER_URL` + `/optimize-dispatch` with header `X-Solver-Token`, waiting up to 600 s for QUICK or the cap + 2 min for THOROUGH ([2.6](#26-runtime-architecture), [2.8](#28-timeouts-budgets-and-limits)). A 503 from the solver ("busy") fails the job with "busy, optimize again in a minute"; a 503 `WORKERS_UNAVAILABLE` (rule 22: the solver could not start its worker processes, refused within seconds) with "The planner is busy or restarting - try again in a minute. Nothing was changed.", audited with its code and alerted in the log ([2.7](#27-background-job-model));
4. stores `responseJson`, 80 % ("Saving plan");
5. in one transaction (timeout 120 s) locks the plan row and checks it is still `OPTIMIZING` with this job as `currentJobId` and the job still `RUNNING` (else "Stale result", nothing applied), saves the request's `weightChanges` with `applyWeightChanges` (set-based `UPDATE ... FROM unnest(...)`, each row only if it still has the kg the request was built from, else the job fails with "The orders of this day changed ... Optimize again"; one audit row `ORDER_WEIGHTS_RESOLVED`, entity RunPlan, each line and order before and after; PR3 review: before, this ran in the start transaction, so a failed re-plan left copied loads with the old kg and no warning; saved weights may change orders on the superseded parent's PLANNED loads, whose stops then show the new kg, never frozen ones), runs `persistDispatchResult`, runs `applyScenario` with the RECOMMENDED scenario, marks the `RunJob` `SUCCEEDED` at 100 % with a message such as "N loads on M trucks, K stop(s) unserved" (on a re-plan with kept loads "N new loads + K kept (locked or dispatched) on M trucks", M counting the kept loads' trucks, read from the version's rows of `scope.frozenLoadIds`: PR7, B3), and writes audit `OPTIMIZE_SUCCEEDED` with per-scenario figures (PR3: in the same transaction).

Any error goes to `failJob` (conditional, [2.7](#27-background-job-model)); lost jobs are reaped by the janitor ([5.9](#59-job-failures-and-the-janitor)).

**`persistDispatchResult(tx, tenantId, runId, built, resp)`** deletes the run's old `ScenarioResult` rows (including the option a re-plan copied from its parent) and writes one per scenario with its totals and `detailsJson`. `ScenarioDetails` is the solver scenario plus engine, distance provider, estimated flag, warnings and `scope`. Each scenario gets its `UnservedOrder` rows: the pre-drops plus the solver's unserved stops, with split parts merged per order and reason into `portionLinesJson`.

**`applyScenario(tx, tenantId, runId, scenarioId, userId, opts)`** turns a scenario into loads:

- Its first statement locks the plan row (`lockRunForWrite`, PR3, review F07). It refuses a superseded version (status `SUPERSEDED` or `supersededAt` set), an `OPTIMIZING` one unless the caller is its current job (`opts.jobId`), and a scenario without dispatch details (legacy). A dispatcher's choice (`opts.requireOptimized`) must be an `OPTIMIZED` option: `NO_SOLUTION` gives 409 `SCENARIO_NOT_USABLE`.
- It refuses when the frozen loads differ from `scope.frozenLoadIds` / `frozenLoadOrderIds` ("Loads were locked/unlocked after this optimization").
- It picks a driver for every new load with `planDrivers` ([3.9](#39-step-7-a-driver-per-load)) before anything is deleted: the evidence is this version's loads as they are then (for the re-plan job, the copies of the previous version's loads). It keeps the driver notes (a trip that lost or changed its driver, a hand-set driver whose trip the plan does not have).
- It deletes this run's PLANNED loads and any legacy `RouteAssignment` without a load.
- It creates one `PlanLoad` per solver load: truck, `loadNo`, depart and return, km, minutes, cases, kg, utilisation, fuel, cost, return leg, estimated flag, `driverId` and, for a driver the dispatcher chose by hand for that truck and trip, its marker (`driverSetById`, `driverSetAt`). The load's kg is `loadKgFromRefs`: the sum of its portions' kg and its whole orders' `totalWeightKg`, the same figures its stops, manifests and driver sheets show. A solver `kg` that differs by more than 0.5 kg is recorded in the `SCENARIO_CHOSEN` audit (`loadKgMismatches`) and logged.
- It creates one `RouteAssignment` per order (or split portion) per stop: `sequenceInTruck` (numbered from 1 within each load), `orderInStop`, `etaMin`, `serviceStartMin`, `departureMin`, `waitMin`, `cumulativeKm`, window flags and the `portionCases` / `portionWeightKg` / `portionLinesJson` columns.
- It sets `Order.status` to `ASSIGNED` (at least one part on a truck) or `UNSERVED`. It never touches orders that are already `DISPATCHED` or `DELIVERED`.
- It sets `chosenScenarioId` and the status by the loads: `DISPATCHED` (with `finalizedAt`) when every load of the version is already out, otherwise `READY` (PR3: before, always READY). The write is conditional (never over a superseded row). It then calls `refreshPlanFacts` with the driver notes and writes audit `SCENARIO_CHOSEN` (with `driverChanges`: truck, trip, from, to, reason, when any). It returns `{ driverChanges }`: `chooseScenario` passes them on (choose-scenario answers `driversChanged`, the count the screen's toast names: "N driver note(s)"), and the job's message adds "N driver note(s) (see the plan)" (on `RunJob.message`; the dispatch screens show a job's message only while it runs or after it failed). This happens on every optimize, not only when the dispatcher switches options.

**`refreshPlanFacts(tx, tenantId, runId, { driverChanges? })`** recomputes and stores on `RunPlan`:

- `reconciliationJson` = `reconcile(orders, planned, unserved)` (`apps/web/lib/dispatch/reconcile.ts`). It checks:
  - uploaded = planned + unserved cases, in total, per SKU and per sales order;
  - every order appears exactly once (whole), or in portions that add up per line;
  - no order is planned for another customer or branch;
  - every unserved row has a reason;
  - every order of the scenario's scope (`orderIds` + `frozenOrderIds`) still exists. An order deleted after planning is a problem, so the plan cannot be DISPATCHED until it is re-planned (review F20).

  `ok` is false when any problem is found.
