- `summaryJson` = `computeSummary` (`apps/web/lib/dispatch/summary.ts`): orders served, partial and unserved; cases; service % per P1 to P5; trucks, loads, km, hours, utilisation, fuel, cost; revenue and margin served (null unless every order has a value); late orders; unserved by reason; loads by status; provider and solver info; `driverChanges`, the driver notes of the applied plan (`DriverChangeNote`: truck, trip, times, `from` and `to` with their names, reason `CLASH`, `INACTIVE` or `TRIP_GONE`, and for `CLASH` the trip that got the driver). `applyScenario` passes the new list (the key is left out when it is empty); a refresh after a load change keeps the list already stored. `createNextVersion` copies the summary with the notes; they are never read as evidence, and the next applied plan replaces them. A `parkedDrivers` list written by earlier builds of this PR is ignored, and the next refresh leaves it out.
- `changeSummaryJson`, for version 2 and later, = `computeChangeSummary`: orders added, assignments changed and unchanged, trucks unchanged, locked loads preserved, and the sentence shown in the blue bar.
- `totalOrders` and `unservedCount`.

It runs after `applyScenario` and after every load status change. It does not run after a driver change, because a driver does not change the plan facts.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor D as Dispatcher
    participant UI as dispatch-client.tsx
    participant API as POST /api/dispatch/plan
    participant DAY as GET /api/dispatch/day
    participant SO as start-optimize.ts
    participant PS as plan-service.ts
    participant JOB as dispatch-job.ts
    participant SV as Solver /optimize-dispatch
    participant DB as Postgres via Prisma
    D->>UI: Click OPTIMIZE
    UI->>API: date, depotId, optimize true
    API->>PS: getOrCreatePlan
    PS->>DB: live RunPlan, or create version 1 as DRAFT INITIAL
    API->>SO: startDispatchOptimize
    SO->>PS: buildDispatchRequest
    PS->>DB: read orders, lines, customers, type profiles, trucks, frozen loads, TenantConfig
    PS-->>SO: request, preDrops, scope, blocking, warnings, unknownWeights, weightChanges
    alt customers without a location and allowMissingLocations not set
        SO-->>UI: 409 LOCATION_REQUIRED
        UI->>D: window.confirm to plan without them, then resend
    else lines without weight, a truck has a payload, allowMissingWeights not set
        SO-->>UI: 409 WEIGHT_REQUIRED
        UI->>D: window.confirm to plan them as 0 kg, then resend
    end
    SO->>DB: one transaction - intake lock, scoped orders still exist, applyWeightChanges with AuditLog ORDER_WEIGHTS_RESOLVED, RunJob QUEUED with requestJson, RunPlan OPTIMIZING
    SO->>JOB: scheduleDispatchOptimize, not awaited
    SO-->>UI: 202 with runJobId
    loop every 3 s while optimizing
        UI->>DAY: poll the day overview and plan status
    end
    JOB->>DB: RunJob RUNNING 20 percent
    JOB->>SV: POST with X-Solver-Token, up to 600 s (QUICK) or the cap + 2 min (THOROUGH)
    SV-->>JOB: RECOMMENDED, MIN_TRUCKS, MIN_DISTANCE
    JOB->>DB: RunJob responseJson 80 percent
    JOB->>DB: one transaction - persistDispatchResult, RunPlan READY, applyScenario RECOMMENDED, refreshPlanFacts, RunJob SUCCEEDED
    JOB->>DB: AuditLog OPTIMIZE_SUCCEEDED
    Note over JOB,DB: on any error failJob sets RunJob and RunPlan to FAILED and audits OPTIMIZE_FAILED
```

### 3.7 Step 5: reviewing the plan

`PlanView` loads `GET /api/runs/:id/plan` (`apps/web/app/api/runs/[id]/plan/route.ts`), which returns `getPlanDetail` (`apps/web/lib/dispatch/plan-detail.ts`). The same `PlanDetail` object feeds the Excel workbook and the driver sheets, so the screen and the paper always agree. The view polls every 2.5 s while the plan is optimizing, and is read again in place (`reloadSignal`) when the day screen saved a customer's pin or details (audit F13). A failed load of a plan already on screen keeps it, with the error and "Try again" (`planAfterLoad` in `plan-actions.ts`); only a plan that never loaded shows the error alone, also with "Try again" (third review of PR3: once `api()` stopped rejecting, a network error during an action replaced the whole plan, every load button included, until the page was reloaded). Fourth review of PR3: a load's answer is shown only when it is newer than the answer on screen (`createLoadOrder`), so a slow "Try again" read before a Lock never shows the load PLANNED again after the Lock's own reload, and a failed first "Try again" never puts the banner back over the answer of a later load; an older answer that arrives first is still shown, so answers slower than the polling never freeze the screen. "Try again" is disabled while a load newer than the answer on screen is on its way and while an action runs. The banner reads "Could not reload the plan: <message>. The plan below may be out of date." (`planReloadErrorText` adds the period the server's messages leave out). A driver change that fails (a refusal, or an answer lost after the server saved it) reloads the plan like a status change, so the driver list and the WhatsApp link show the driver the server has, or the banner with "Try again".

| Part of the screen | Where the data comes from |
|---|---|
| Header: version, depot, date, status, reason badge, "RECOMMENDED PLAN" or "(alternative)" | `detail.run` |
| Superseded, optimizing and failed banners | `run.status` and the latest `RunJob` |
| Blue bar "Changes vs version N" | `run.changeSummaryJson.text` |
| Yellow warnings | request and solver warnings from the chosen `ScenarioDetails`; the driver notes of `summaryJson.driverChanges` (`driverChangeWarnings` in `driver-links.ts`, fed with `getPlanDetail`'s own load rows and their marker, `driverSetByDispatcher`): "Driver changed by this plan: ..." for a trip that lost or changed its driver, until the dispatcher sets that trip's driver (another driver, **Keep**, or "No driver" on a trip that has a driver; it does not come back after; a trip the plan left without a driver keeps its note until a driver is picked for it, as a re-sent "No driver" changes nothing); "Driver picked by hand, not in this plan: ..." for a `TRIP_GONE` note while the plan has no load for that truck and trip |
| Driver clash warning | `driverClashNotes` in `apps/web/lib/dispatch/driver-links.ts` |
| KPIs | `summaryJson`: Orders served, Cases planned, Trucks · loads, km ("Road km", "Road km (N legs estimated)" when some legs are straight-line estimates - PR5, or "Estimated km"), Hours on road · paid (PR5: time on the road vs paid truck days), Avg utilization, Fuel (l · OMR), Operating cost (PR5: the whole day under the one cost model - every load of the version, carried locked loads included; its tooltip gives the breakdown; `*` = some loads were costed the earlier way, `costBasis` MIXED_LEGACY), P1 to P5 service (P1 or P2 below 100 % is highlighted), Late orders served, Revenue served, Margin served ("not supplied" when null) |
| Green or red reconciliation bar | `reconciliationJson` |
| Plan options table | every `ScenarioResult` of the run, each as the whole day with that option (`getPlanDetail` with `lib/dispatch/plan-options.ts`): **Trucks** (PR7, B3: the physical trucks - its new loads' trucks + the trucks of the locked, loading and dispatched loads it was planned around, counted from the stored loads, so options saved by an older optimizer are right too), **Loads** (PR7: kept + new, "(N new)" on a re-plan), **km** (PR7 review: the whole day - the kept loads' stored km + the option's new loads', rounded like the KPI, so the option in use shows the KPI's km; "(new X)" shows the new loads alone on a re-plan, with the number of estimated legs; before, only the new loads' km, under whole-day trucks, loads and cost), **Day cost** (PR5: the locked, loading and dispatched loads the option was planned around + its new loads, so the option in use equals the KPI; "(new X)" shows the new loads alone on a re-plan), **Preference cost** (PR7, N1: what RECOMMENDED also values, in OMR-equivalent - preferred hours + early delivery of P1/P2 + moved orders, `preference_penalties`; the tooltip splits it; an option saved by an optimizer that did not report the parts - before PR5, so every plan made on main - shows only its preferred-hours part, marked "(hours only)", and is compared as "preferred-hours cost", never as "preference cost": PR7 review), unserved, **Timing checked** (PR4: the optimizer's own check of the option - Yes, "No - N rule(s) broken", "Not verified", or "not checked" for options from before the check), **Search**: the search time and how it ended in plain words (PR6, `solverStatusText` in `lib/dispatch/solver-status.ts`: "best plan found in the time allowed", "... (search stopped at its limit)" for `ROUTING_PARTIAL_SUCCESS_LOCAL_OPTIMUM_NOT_REACHED`, "no plan found in the time allowed"; the longer wording in its tooltip; the raw OR-Tools name is no longer shown), **What it gains** (PR7, N1: `optionTradeoffs`; RECOMMENDED against the cheapest option that is a different plan, each alternative against RECOMMENDED: "vs MIN TRUCKS: P1/P2 delivered on average 40 min earlier, preference cost 19.5 OMR lower; but costs 35.4 OMR more, 87 km more, 1 more truck"; minutes are the average difference in service start over the P1/P2 stops both options serve; "Same plan as RECOMMENDED", "Same plan as MIN TRUCKS" or "Same plan as the other options" when the loads, trucks and stop order are identical; audit F22: an option whose own timing check is VIOLATED or UNVERIFIED gets no trade-off, never "cheaper" or "1 more order served", but "Breaks the timing rules (N problems): it cannot be dispatched. Re-plan, or use another option." (UNVERIFIED: "Its timing could not be checked, so it cannot be dispatched. ..."); it is never the option another one is compared with, and RECOMMENDED with no other rule-keeping option says "Every different option breaks the timing rules."; options from before the check are compared as before); "In use" or "Use instead" (an option whose times break a rule can be used for review, but its trucks cannot be dispatched). The Excel SUMMARY repeats the table under **PLAN OPTIONS** (trucks, loads, day km and day cost with the new loads' part, preference cost or "preferred hours only" for an older option, unserved, the option's timing check - "timing VERIFIED" / "timing VIOLATED" (audit F22) - and the trade-off line) |
| Red "Times not verified" box (PR4) | `detail.feasibility`: the blocking violations per truck (up to 8, all in the Excel SUMMARY), the remedy (`timingRemedy` in `feasibility-view.ts`) and a **Re-plan** button. The remedy is "Re-plan …" unless a blocking violation sits on a LOCKED or LOADING load: a re-plan carries such a load over unchanged, so the box names it and says to put it back to Planned first ("Back to locked", then "Unlock"), then re-plan. Unlock is refused while a later load of the same truck is still locked or loading, so the box lists those loads too, latest first ("put loads T01 L2, T01 L1 back to Planned first, in this order"; second review of PR4). The box's Re-plan button is off, with the reason next to it (`timingReplanOff`), when nothing is left to plan or when every blocking violation is on a locked or loading load (a re-plan would change none of them); the plan's own Re-plan button stays on. Amber lines for warnings (cases planned with no weight, a truck corrected below its planned load, problems on loads already out). Each load row shows "Times not verified" when its truck-day fails (its tooltip says when the load itself must be put back to Planned, with the later locked loads of its truck), and Lock / Loading / Dispatch are disabled with the reason while the gate is on |
| "Changed after planning" (PR4) | `DetailStop.masterChanged` / `DetailLoad.masterChanged`: a pin moved more than 50 m, receiving hours, name or address changed in the customer master, or the truck's capacity changed, since the stop was planned. Windows are compared the way they were planned: a window that ends before it starts was planned as "any time" (`usableWindow` in `snapshots.ts`), so such legacy data is no change. The plan keeps what it was planned with; the note is shown under the stop and as a badge on the load, and a warning says what to do (re-plan a PLANNED load; unlock and re-plan a locked one). A stop on a locked, loading or dispatched load is judged with the orders it was planned with only (`keptVisitOrders` in `order-window.ts`, through `keptStopLive` in `kept-changes.ts`, 24 Oct 2026): a new order of its customer is another visit, so its delivery time never reads as the kept stop's hours - the same rule as the kept-load box below, so the two never disagree. With `KEPT_CHANGES=off` the note is read as before this rule (review S2: the kill switch takes back the whole warning). "current customer data" marks a stop planned before snapshots existed. **Access notes are not frozen**: like the driver's name and phone they are contact details, printed as they are now (the snapshot keeps the planned notes for the record) |
| "Locked loads planned with older customer data" (24 Oct 2026) | `detail.kept` (`GET /api/runs/:id/plan` asks for it: `getPlanDetail(..., { kept: true })`; the driver and salesman pages do not) - the kept-load report of `lib/dispatch/kept-changes.ts`, in the same snapshot as the loads. Per LOCKED or LOADING load, each stop whose data changed since it was planned: **receiving hours** (the planned unloading judged against the hours now by the load's own rule, START or FINISH: still keeps them, or outside them), **pin** (listed from 50 m, "check" from 500 m; the load still goes to the planned pin, its sheets add "New pin - ask the dispatcher which one to use" with the new pin; no usable location now breaks, and so does a new pin over a planned point that was not usable - the location gate's 409 `STOP_PIN_REPLACED`, read with the gate's own `stopsAtReplacedPoints`, moved to `lib/dispatch/replaced-pin.ts` so the reader can use it, review W-4), **small truck only** on a truck that is not small, a **deactivated** customer, an **order cancelled or moved** to a later day, and **new orders** of the customer since (another visit, and where they are now). Red: a rule fails with the data now; amber: check it; grey: still keeps every rule. Each load has its **Unlock** (PLANNER, LOCKED only): the load and every later locked load of its truck, latest first, the ones without a change named under the button ("No change on T05 L3 ...", review W-6; [3.8](#38-step-6-load-states)). A loading load says what to do instead (Back to locked first). DISPATCHED and COMPLETED loads are never listed. On Daily dispatch the box is Step 3's (the plan below does not repeat it). The yellow "changed after planning" note stays as it was |
| Truck loads table | one row per `PlanLoad`: truck · load, driver picker with PDF and WhatsApp links and who chose the driver ("picked by hand" when `DetailLoad.driverHandSet`; else a **Keep** link when `driverPickLink` says so: an active driver on a load not yet out that the dispatcher can change, exactly when the server takes the re-sent driver as a Keep (`isDriverKeep`), [3.9](#39-step-7-a-driver-per-load)), status, depart to return, stops, cases against capacity, utilisation, km ("est. km" when some of its legs are estimates), time, fuel, cost (its tooltip: fixed, trip, distance, fuel, driver share with the paid minutes, overtime; `*` = costed the earlier way), action buttons. Expanding a row shows the loading manifest (SKU totals from `aggregateSkus`: cases and kg per product, the TOTAL line with the load's kg to 0.1 kg; A6 review; on an older version whose orders a later re-plan re-weighed, `manifestKgNote` says under the TOTAL that the load was planned at N kg and the products now add up to M kg, as the Excel's MISMATCH does; A6 second review) and the delivery route (ETA, window, cases, SKUs, sales orders, km, "Part k of n" for split deliveries) |
| Unserved orders | the chosen scenario's `UnservedOrder` rows with the `REASON_TEXT` label and the reason message; "REST OF SPLIT" when the rest of the order is on a truck. A reason saved by an older solver with a raw status code in it ("... (ROUTING_FAIL_TIMEOUT).") is shown in plain words (`withPlainSolverCodes`, PR6) |
| Map | `apps/web/components/plan-map.tsx` (MapLibre) with `GET /api/runs/:id/load-geometry`, which asks the solver's `/route-geometry` for a road polyline per load and falls back to straight lines flagged as estimated (see **Plan map road shapes** below). Since PR4 it draws through the pins each stop was planned with and from the depot the plan was made from; since audit E1 (owner decision 13) each load from the depot pin **it** was planned from (`DetailLoad.origin`, kept in its truck snapshot), so a locked or dispatched load kept from before the depot pin moved is still drawn from the old pin (a grey marker "Depot pin these loads were planned from"), and the road-shapes route routes it from the same pin (the same `pointsKey`) |
| Plan versions | every `RunPlan` of the same depot and date, with reason, note (`reasonNote`, since 24 Oct 2026: it tells the two `MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT` versions apart, "Unlocked for changed customer data: ..." or "By hand: ...") and change text, linking to `/t/[slug]/dispatch/plan/[id]` |

**Plan map road shapes.** The map draws each load as its road shape (solid) or, when it has none, as straight dashed segments between the stops; the dashed lines are only a drawing and change no km figure (the plan's km come from the solver's distance matrix at optimize time: "Road km" or "Estimated km").

- `GET /api/runs/:id/load-geometry` (`resolveLoadGeometries` in `lib/dispatch/load-geometry.ts`) asks the solver for 4 loads at a time (`callRouteGeometry`, 15 s per call) within one 20 s deadline. A load that fails or that OSRM cannot route is drawn straight on its own; the others keep their shapes. Two answers stop new calls: a clear "not configured" (web without `SOLVER_URL`/`SOLVER_TOKEN`, or solver without an OSRM URL), since every load would get the same; and a timeout, since routing is then hanging and the solver's `/route-geometry` (a sync handler in its 40-thread pool, OSRM timeout 30 s with 2 tries) keeps each abandoned call for up to about a minute after the web gives up. Calls already running may finish and cached loads keep their shapes, so a hanging OSRM costs at most 4 solver calls per request (review: without the stop it was 8 per request, 16 per page view with the automatic retry). Before, the route asked one load after the other and the first failure turned every later load straight, so a solver restart (every deploy) or a slow answer gave a whole day of straight lines.
- Each load's path is depot -> located stops in sequence order -> depot, one stop per sequence at its first order's **planned** pin (the stop snapshot; today's customer pin for rows planned before snapshots existed), from the depot the option was planned from (`ScenarioDetails.inputs`; the live depot for options from before inputs), exactly what `getPlanDetail` shows (PR4, review F08). The route and the map build it with the same `loadPath` (`lib/dispatch/load-path.ts`), so a pin corrected after planning neither redraws a locked or dispatched load nor makes the answer look stale.
- Each straight load carries a `reason`: `ROUTING_OFF` (Settings: distance provider Haversine), `OUTSIDE_COVERAGE` (the company is outside the shared Oman + UAE road map and has no OSRM URL of its own; Settings may still say OSRM), `NOT_CONFIGURED` (also: no `TenantConfig` row); no call is made for these three (`routingOffReason`). Then `NOT_ROUTABLE` (OSRM itself refused that path: `NoRoute` / `NoSegment`, sent as HTTP 400, or an empty route list), `ROUTING_ERROR` (solver or OSRM error, including network trouble between them such as "[Errno 113] No route to host", which is an outage and not a stop far from any road) or `TIMEOUT`; the last two are the ones a retry can fix. A server answering HTTP 400 to every request (a wrong own OSRM URL) also reads as `NOT_ROUTABLE`: the solver's message does not carry OSRM's code, so the web cannot tell the two apart. The rows keep their first fields (`loadId`, `truckCode`, `loadNo`, `estimated`, `coordinates`) and add `pointsKey`, the fingerprint of the path the row is for (`loadPathKey(loadPath(depot, stops))` in `lib/dispatch/load-path.ts`: depot, the located stops in order, depot; exact numbers, 16 hex digits). A load with no located stop away from the depot (none located, or all on the depot's pin) is `noPath: true` with `estimated: false` and no reason, whatever the routing: nothing is routed and it has no line. It used to come back as a road shape with no reason, so the caption counted it "on the road": with routing not set up it said "1 load of 2 ... The other lines follow the road network (OSRM)" instead of "not set up", and alone it said "Lines follow the road network (OSRM)" (review).
- Road shapes (never straight-line estimates) are cached in the web process for 12 h, at most 500 shapes and 300,000 points (about 5 MB), keyed by the routing namespace (the tenant's own OSRM URL, else the solver's default) and the exact coordinate list. The loads always come from the tenant's own run, so a tenant only gets shapes for its own points. The cache is per process (one web replica, [2.7](#27-background-job-model)); a restart empties it, and a moved pin is a new key.
- The screen (`components/plan-map.tsx`) draws only the depot and the stops while the shapes load, then the lines (`linesToDraw` in `lib/dispatch/plan-map-state.ts`: road shape solid, anything else dashed, no line for a load with no located stop away from the depot). A row counts only for the load it was made for: same load id and, when the server sent it, the same `pointsKey` as the map computes from the stops it shows. A load on screen without such a row is drawn straight. The caption comes from `roadShapesCaption` (`lib/dispatch/map-caption.ts`) over what is drawn (`drawnShapes`: one row per line drawn, a load without its row counted straight, `noPath` loads in no count), never over the answer's rows as such: "Lines follow the road network (OSRM)" only when every line drawn is a road shape; otherwise how many loads are straight and why, or "Road shapes could not be loaded - straight lines shown" with a **Retry** button (for `ROUTING_ERROR` and `TIMEOUT`, or a failed request). When some loads came back `ROUTING_ERROR` (or the request failed) the map asks once more by itself after 5 s; the cache makes that second call cheap. Loads that only timed out get the Retry button but no automatic second round, which would put another 4 abandoned calls on a hanging solver. The shapes are kept per run and stop list, so an answer asked for other content is never drawn.
- **An answer for other content than the screen is stale** (`answerIsStale`): a load on screen has no row for its stops as shown, or the answer has a load the screen does not. The shapes are always asked for after the plan was read, so the screen is then behind the server: another dispatcher's "Use instead" (`chooseScenario` → `applyScenario` deletes the PLANNED loads and makes new ones under the same run, and a READY plan does not poll), or the pin of a stop planned before snapshots existed moved (no `stopSnapshotJson`, so its path is today's customer pin: same load id, other path; a stop planned with a snapshot keeps its planned pin, see above). Asking for the shapes again would give the same answer, so the map reloads the plan instead (`onStale`, PlanView's `load`), once per plan content by itself (it takes the place of the automatic retry); new plan content asks for its own shapes, and when the reload brings the same loads the map asks for the shapes once more. **Retry** on a stale answer does the same. Until then those loads are dashed and counted straight. Review: the caption counted only the rows, so after a "Use instead" elsewhere every load on screen was dashed under "Lines follow the road network (OSRM)", and a load whose pin moved (then any stop; since PR4 only a stop planned before snapshots) was drawn solid along the other path.
- **Drawing waits only for the map's style (`style.load`, or a style already loaded), never for its tiles** (`createDrawGate`). Sources, layers and markers can be added once the style has loaded, whatever the base-map tiles do. Not the map's `load` event: in maplibre-gl 4.7.1 it fires only when every tile of the first view has loaded or failed, so with slow OSM tiles the map stayed empty (no depot, stops or lines) until the slowest tile came, and with a tile request that never answers (maplibre has no tile timeout) or fails late it stayed empty until the dispatcher moved the map, while the caption already said OSRM (review, reproduced in headless Chrome: with 3 s tiles the map drew at about 3.5 s, now at about 0.4 s; with hanging tiles never, now at once). Not `map.isStyleLoaded()` either: it is false whenever a tile or GeoJSON source is still loading. The map used to call `isStyleLoaded() ? draw() : once('load', draw)`: when the road shapes arrived right after the map fitted itself to the stops (new tiles loading) or while the dispatcher zoomed, the draw waited for an event that never came again, so the map kept the straight lines (or no lines at all) under a caption saying OSRM, until something else re-rendered it. This, and not the solver, is the likely cause of the "sometimes straight lines" seen in production. The component has no DOM test (jsdom is not a dependency); `tests/lib/dispatch-plan-map-state.spec.ts` tests the helpers, including the gate against a fake map that models maplibre's `style.load` / `load` / pending tiles, and holds the component to them with static guards. The legacy run-detail Map tab uses its own route (`route-geometries`, through the solver's `/route-geometry` since PR5, review F22), one truck at a time and no call after a failed one; it draws a straight 'fallback' tour (no answer, or the solver's own straight-line estimate) dashed.

**Three options and "Use instead".** The job always applies RECOMMENDED; MIN_TRUCKS and MIN_DISTANCE are kept for comparison. "Use instead" calls `POST /api/runs/:id/choose-scenario { scenarioId }` (`apps/web/app/api/runs/[id]/choose-scenario/route.ts`).

- `chooseScenario` (`plan-service.ts`) does every check in one transaction **after** locking the plan row (PR3, review F07): it is refused while the plan is OPTIMIZING or superseded (status or `supersededAt`), when any load was locked in this version (a frozen load whose `carriedFromLoadId` is null), and for an option that found no plan (`NO_SOLUTION`: 409 `SCENARIO_NOT_USABLE`; the screen shows "No plan" instead of the button). A "Use instead" queued behind a re-plan therefore gets 409 once the re-plan has superseded the version, and never writes it READY again.
- Otherwise it runs `applyScenario` on the same version. No new version is created, and `planDrivers` sets the drivers ([3.9](#39-step-7-a-driver-per-load)); the toast says how many driver notes the option left (`driversChanged`).
- While any action of the plan screen runs (a load change, Lock all, Use instead, Re-plan), every other one is disabled, so one dispatcher cannot race themselves (PR3). Two users racing get 409 "Plan is being saved - retry" when one waits more than 5 s for the other.

**Moving stops by hand (24 Oct 2026, owner decisions; `PLAN_EDIT` check or on).** A **Move…** button on each stop of a PLANNED load (shown disabled on a LOCKED load: "unlock it first", latest load first) and **Put on a truck…** on each whole unserved row (not a REST OF SPLIT, cancelled or brought-forward row) open the Move dialog (`app/t/[slug]/dispatch/move-stop-dialog.tsx`): the truck, the load (a PLANNED load; a new load after the last load, before a load or at the best place in the day; or **Take it off the plan**) and the position (**Best place** by default, or first, after a stop, last). **Check** (`POST /api/runs/:id/edit/check`, one solver call per press, never on every change) answers the preview: per edited truck its day now and after (loads, times, stops, pallets, km, money; under *now* also the same loads timed again with today's data, which the change is counted from), the hard rules the change breaks in red with by how much (bays at 98% for several customers or 100% for one, cases, kg, small truck only, receiving hours, latest return, shift, loads a day, the driver break: never relaxed by `FEASIBILITY_GATE=warn`), the soft costs in amber (money or km up, preferred hours of the stop moved and of the stops the change pushes out of theirs, overtime, a truck used for this change alone, estimated legs, current loads that no longer keep the rules with today's data), what changed since planning on those trucks' stops and trucks and in the settings (they are re-timed with today's data), and for a best place the other places found (never the stop's current place; a best place where the stop already is answers *already at its best place: nothing changes*). **Save as version N+1** (`POST /api/runs/:id/edit`, only with `PLAN_EDIT=on`) makes the next version `MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT` in which only the edited trucks' PLANNED loads are made again - every other load, row, snapshot, driver and helper stays exactly as it was - and the toast asks to print the sheets of those loads again, to throw away the sheets of a load no longer in the plan and to resend the driver link. The option's own unserved list (`details.unserved`, which the hire box reads) follows the rows: an order put on leaves it, a stop taken off joins it as `REMOVED_BY_HAND` (never a capacity reason: no hire check for it). The Move buttons show only on a day that is not over. The header shows "RECOMMENDED PLAN · adjusted by hand" from the option's `details.manual` (never from the version's reason). The rules, the save's transaction and its guards are in `lib/dispatch/plan-edit.ts` and `plan-edit-apply.ts` (top comments). A RE-PLAN plans unlocked loads again and may undo a hand move: lock the load to keep it. One change per check; a stop is one customer visit with all its orders on that load, or one split part (never a single order out of a multi-order stop).

**Moves by hand, part 2 (25 Oct 2026, owner feedback of 24 Oct 2026: "switch loads between two trucks", "free one load to move another customers", "it should show me issue and ask if i want to override").** *Several stops at once*: each stop of a PLANNED load has a tick (and **Select all stops** on the load), each whole unserved row too (ticking one ticks the customer's visit); the selection bar ("3 stops selected · 145 cases - from T03 L2 (2), unserved (1)") offers **Move to…** (a load, a new load after the last load / before a load / at the best place in the day; one stop keeps its position choices, several go to the best place for each) and **Take off the plan** (`REMOVE_STOPS`). *Whole loads*: an expanded PLANNED load has **Move this load…** (`MOVE_LOAD`: any truck of the day, its own truck a reorder; after the last load, before a load or the best place in the day; the load keeps its stop order and is timed again) and **Swap with another load…** (`SWAP_LOADS`: each load keeps its order and is timed again on the other truck); drivers and helpers stay with their trucks (`planCrew`). *A change list*: after any check whose list is explicit (`draftable`, also a red one) **Add another change** keeps it in a banner ("Changes checked, not saved yet: 1) ... (red on its own) · Open · Discard"); the next change is checked after it and the list is saved as one version (at most 10 operations; only the whole list must keep the rules or be allowed by hand - e.g. stops exchanged between two full loads in two steps). *Allow anyway*: the issues of a red check are each tagged **Can be allowed by hand** or **Cannot be allowed** (with why: small truck only, the shift and the latest return, loads a day, arriving early, more than 20 % over capacity, figures that do not agree). When only issues that can be allowed remain (a late arrival - judged in seconds, shown as at least 1 min -, pallets / cases / kg up to 120 % of the truck's own bays, cases or payload in whole units, the driver break), the panel **Allow by hand and save (supervisor or company admin)** lists each with a tick and a required reason (**Allow all N**, **Use this reason for all**), the timetable with them allowed, and **Skip the driver break on T08 instead** where that times the truck. A PLANNER sees it but cannot save it (403 `OVERRIDE_ROLE`). The save stores each allowance on its new load (`TruckSnapshot.handAllowed`: what, by how much, the reason, who, when) and audits it (`RULE_ALLOWED_BY_HAND`). *Carried allowances*: a later hand change on such a truck keeps an allowance without asking (any role) when the issue is the same and no worse (the same stop and hours, no more minutes late; a load made of a subset of the same rows, no more than allowed and the truck's capacity unchanged; the same truck-day's break); a new or worse one needs a supervisor again, with the earlier reason pre-filled. *Where it shows*: a violet **ALLOWED BY HAND** badge on the load row (its title the lines with who), the stop's time violet with "allowed by hand", the header "· N rules allowed by hand", a violet list of the allowed findings above the timing box and a yellow line "Rules allowed by hand on this plan: T08 L2 (receiving hours), ..."; the load sheet's **ALLOWED BY HAND** box (with who), the driver sheet's badge and the stop's line (no "Outside receiving hours"), WhatsApp (`! Allowed by hand: ...`), the driver page and the Excel workbook (SUMMARY **RULES ALLOWED BY HAND**; a stop's note `ALLOWED BY HAND: LATE (<reason>)`, never `HARD WINDOW MISSED`). *The gates* (design D5): the timetable gate (`checkPlanFeasibility`, so Lock / Loading / Dispatch and the plan screen) turns a finding an allowance covers into a WARN "Allowed by hand: ... - <reason>", as long as the load is no worse than allowed (later, more pallets with today's cases per pallet, more kg with a case weight entered since, above the 120 % cap: BLOCK as before; an allowance above the cap is ignored). The kept-load box judges a stop whose hours changed against what was agreed (CHECK within the minutes allowed, BREAKS beyond them); the operations alert *after closing* fires only after the agreed latest time. A RE-PLAN plans the Planned loads again with every rule, so their allowances go; the RE-PLAN, hire *Use this plan* and *Use instead* confirmations list them ("lock a load first to keep what was allowed"); locked and loading loads keep theirs.

**Pallets on the plan screen (truck capacity in pallets, part B).** Only a load planned by pallets (its stored `PlanLoad.palletUnits` and a truck snapshot with bays and room, both kept only from the optimizer's echo: `loadPallets` in `lib/dispatch/pallets.ts`) shows pallets, always beside its cases: `getPlanDetail` gives such a load `palletUnits`, `bays`, `palletFillPct`, `palletRoomUnits` and each manifest product `casesPerPallet`, `fullPallets`, `looseCases` and `palletUnits` (`withManifestPallets`; the factor a split part was cut with, else the option's `PlanInputs.palletFactors`, else the product's today; each order line rounded up and added up, so the products add up to the load), plus `palletNotes` when a product's cases per pallet changed under Products since planning (the load keeps its pallets). The loads table's **Load / capacity** column reads "1,045 cs" over "11.1 / 12 plt" (title: the limit at the fill; a load by cases keeps "1,045 / 1,140"); the manifest adds "3 pallets + 12 cases" per product, the TOTAL in pallets and "1,045 cases = 11.1 pallets (8 full pallets + 293 loose cases on mixed pallets)"; the KPI row adds **Pallets · bay fill** (`summaryJson.palletUnits`, `avgBayFillPct`, `palletLoads`, only when a load of the day was planned by pallets: `computeSummary` leaves the keys out otherwise). Options carry `palletRule` (the echo's fill).

### 3.8 Step 6: load states

The rules are in `apps/web/lib/dispatch/load-state.ts` (`checkTransition`, `ALLOWED`). They are applied by `updateLoad` then `changeStatusTx` in `plan-service.ts`, reached through `PATCH /api/runs/:id/loads/:loadId { status }` (`apps/web/app/api/runs/[id]/loads/[loadId]/route.ts`).

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> PLANNED: applyScenario
    PLANNED --> LOCKED: Lock (planner)
    LOCKED --> PLANNED: Unlock (planner)
    LOCKED --> LOADING: Loading (planner)
    LOADING --> LOCKED: Back to locked (planner)
    LOCKED --> DISPATCHED: Dispatch (planner)
    LOADING --> DISPATCHED: Dispatch (planner)
    DISPATCHED --> COMPLETED: Completed (planner)
    COMPLETED --> [*]
```

| From and to | Button | Role | Extra rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| PLANNED to LOCKED | Lock, or "Lock all loads" (locks every PLANNED load in load-number order) | PLANNER | every earlier load of the same truck is already frozen |
| LOCKED to PLANNED | Unlock | PLANNER | no later load of the truck is frozen |
| LOCKED to LOADING | Loading | PLANNER | none |
| LOADING to LOCKED | Back to locked | PLANNER | none |
| LOCKED or LOADING to DISPATCHED | Dispatch | PLANNER (SUPERVISOR until 5 Oct 2026) | every earlier load of the truck is DISPATCHED or COMPLETED, and the plan's stored reconciliation is `ok` |
| PLANNED to LOCKED, LOCKED to LOADING, LOCKED or LOADING to DISPATCHED | as above | as above | **(PR4) the truck-day's timetable passes the feasibility check** (below), and the plan's reconciliation is `ok` for LOCK and LOADING too (409 `NOT_RECONCILED`: locking freezes what later re-plans build on) |
| DISPATCHED to COMPLETED | Completed | PLANNER (SUPERVISOR until 5 Oct 2026) | none |
| DISPATCHED or COMPLETED to anything else | none | none | refused: these loads are immutable |
| PLANNED to LOCKED, LOCKED to LOADING, LOCKED or LOADING to DISPATCHED | as above | as above | **(PR9) no order of the load was brought forward to a later day** (`carriedOrdersGate`, 409 `ORDERS_CARRIED` naming the customers and the day they went to): it is planned there now, so the load would deliver it twice. The remedy (`carriedLoadRemedy` in `carry-view.ts`, PR9 review) depends on what else the load holds and on its status: with other orders, re-plan this day (a PLANNED load), or unload the brought-forward cases, put the load back to Planned and re-plan (the re-plan leaves carried orders out); with nothing else, a PLANNED load is left as it is - it stays in the plan for the record and was never loaded - while a LOCKED or LOADING one **was loaded** (in NMWC's flow the trucks are loaded the night before): its cases are on the truck but planned on the day they went to, so the answer says to unload them back to stock, or tell the warehouse, before the loads of that day are picked, then put the load back to Planned (PR9 second review: it used to say "never loaded or dispatched" and "needs nothing" for these too). A re-plan of a day with nothing else open answers 409 `NOTHING_TO_PLAN` saying its orders were brought forward (`nothingLeftCarried`, with the same unload advice when such a loaded load exists), never "every load has left the depot" or "upload orders first". A load of the company's **today** is refused the same way when one of its orders was brought forward to tomorrow in the evening (owner decision on today's orders, [3.11](#311-step-9-late-orders-and-plan-versions)); its words then say today: "Re-plan today (27 Sep) to plan its other orders without them.", or, when it was loaded, "Unlock it (put it back to Planned)" and unload those cases (`carriedLoadRemedy` with the load's day; `updateLoad` takes the clock). The way back to Planned is named with the plan screen's own buttons: a LOADING load has no Unlock (LOADING goes only to LOCKED or DISPATCHED), so its words say "Put it Back to locked, then Unlock it", and, since Unlock is refused while a later load of the same truck is still locked or loading, "A later locked or loading load of the same truck must be unlocked first" (review of the owner decision: a LOADING load was told to "Unlock it", a button it does not have). Stepping back and Completed are never refused |
| PLANNED to LOCKED, LOCKED to LOADING, LOCKED or LOADING to DISPATCHED | as above | as above | **(audit PR A5, second review; owner's rule "no item will be delivered without location") every customer of the load has a usable location now** (`locationGate`, 409 `LOCATION_REQUIRED` with `customerIds` and `customers`, message "T01 L1: 1 customer on this load has no usable location: K1. A load cannot be locked, loaded or dispatched while a customer on it has no correct location. ..."). The test is the planner's own, `locationBlocksDelivery` with the company's delivery area, on the customers as they are at that moment, not on the stop's planned pin: a stop is planned with a usable point, but a customer import can mark that point LOW afterwards (the file points elsewhere), and a changed delivery area can put it outside; "Use instead" and a failed re-plan's copy then hold such a stop too. The remedy (`noLocationLoadRemedy`) says to drop the pin on each one (ADD LOCATION, or Set location on the customer page), then RE-PLAN so the stops go to the new pins, after unlocking a LOCKED load (a LOADING one goes Back to locked, then Unlock), or to go without them: RE-PLAN leaves their orders unserved (a loading load's cases come off the truck). Until the A5 third review it said "try again" for a LOCKED or LOADING load, and trying again after the pin sent the load out with the stop, its links and the WhatsApp text still at the old point. **(A5 third review) and no stop is still planned at a point that was not usable when a new pin replaced it** (`stopsAtReplacedPoints`, 409 `STOP_PIN_REPLACED` with `customerIds` and `customers`, message "T01 L1: the stop for K1 still goes to its old point, which was not usable. A new pin was placed after this load was planned. A load cannot be locked, ... RE-PLAN so the stops go to the new pins.", a locked or loading load unlocked first, `replacedPinRemedy`): the stop's planned pin (`stopSnapshotJson`) is more than 50 m (`PIN_MOVED_M`) from the customer's point now, and a `CUSTOMER_LOCATION_SET` audit row (ADD LOCATION, Set location, or a customer import that wrote an exact pair over it) moved the customer out of that point's place while the point it started from blocked delivery (`locationBlocksDelivery` on the row's "before": LOW or outside the area and never confirmed, 0,0). The planned point's place is `PIN_MOVED_M` (50 m) around it, the distance at which this gate and the sheets' "New pin" note count a pin as the same place (A5 fifth review; it was the exact point, within 5 cm). Only the change that moved the customer out of it counts (A5 fourth review): a row that started there and ended there too moved nothing (a flagged point confirmed where it is: its own coordinates typed, or a hand pin a few metres off, which is how a pin confirms a flagged saved point, since a pin exactly on it is refused, `PIN_REQUIRED`), and of the rows that moved it the newest decides, so a point confirmed where it is, or set back by hand, and then corrected is an ordinary correction; a flagged point replaced by a pin more than 50 m away is refused, whatever came after. An ordinary correction of a usable point is not refused (frozen plan facts; the owner's decision of 28 Sep 2026, "Allow, driver gets new pin", [7.5](#75-open-questions-for-the-owner): the load can go, and the sheets and the WhatsApp text show the planned stop with the new pin noted). Verified points, and HIGH or MEDIUM points inside the area, pass as before, so NMWC's locked loads are not affected. Stepping back and Completed are never refused. **(Data collection rules, item 3, owner decision of 1 Oct 2026) with Settings' "Require location and delivery window before loading" on (`TenantConfig.requireDataBeforeLoading`, off by default), every customer of a load leaving PLANNED also has a delivery window**: its own confirmed receiving hours (`windowConfirmedAt`, "open all day" included), or a delivery time its planned stop carries (`StopFacts.promised`; `dataGate` before `locationGate`, `dataGaps` in `lib/dispatch/data-collection.ts`; company and customer-type defaults do not count). Refused with 409 `DATA_REQUIRED` (`customerIds`; `customers` with code, branch, name and `missing`: "delivery window" or "location and delivery window"), the message listing each customer and what it misses, the rule and the remedy for each kind (`dataGateRefusal`: confirm the hours in Details or tick Open all day, or a delivery time for the order and RE-PLAN; the location remedy as above). A load whose customers miss only a location is left to `locationGate`'s own words. With the setting on, a customer whose confirmed hours are not the hours its stop was planned with (no delivery time on the stop) is refused too: 409 `HOURS_CHANGED` (`customerIds`; planned with, confirmed, RE-PLAN first; data collection review). A load already LOCKED or LOADING is never judged again by it (frozen loads); planning is never refused by it (the day screen warns). **(Item 1) and no order of the day of a customer on a load leaving PLANNED got a delivery time after the plan read its orders that the stop was not planned with** (`deliveryTimeGate`, 409 `DELIVERY_TIME_CHANGED`, "RE-PLAN first": every order of those customers counts, also on another load or left unserved; a time removed again or saved again as planned does not), whatever the setting |
| PLANNED to LOCKED, LOCKED to LOADING, LOCKED or LOADING to DISPATCHED | as above | as above | **(owner request 13 Oct 2026) no customer marked *Small truck only (3-ton)* rides a truck that is not small now** (`smallTruckGate` in `plan-service.ts`, after `locationGate`; 409 `SMALL_TRUCK_ONLY` with `truckId`, `truckCode`, `truckBays`, `smallTruckMaxBays`, `customerIds` and `customers`; message from `smallTruckGateMessage` in `lib/dispatch/small-truck.ts`: "T10 L2: cannot lock this load. T10 (12 bays) is not a small truck, but this customer takes small trucks only (at most 6 bays): ... RE-PLAN: RouteIQ puts them on a small truck. If the customer accepts this truck today, untick ... on the customer until this load is dispatched, then tick it again."; a LOCKED or LOADING load is told to go back to Planned first). The day overview counts the same breach on PLANNED loads (`DayOutdated.smallTruckBlocked`), so step 3 calls the plan out of date and keeps RE-PLAN on. Read live - the customers' `smallTruckOnly`, the truck's `bays` and `TenantConfig.smallTruckMaxBays` as they are now - so a mark or a setting changed after planning is caught. A truck without bays is never small. `FEASIBILITY_GATE=warn` does not apply; stepping back and Completed are never refused |

Around every change, `lockOpenRun` (`lockRunForWrite`) takes a row lock on the `RunPlan` and refuses superseded (status `SUPERSEDED` or `supersededAt` set) and OPTIMIZING plans. The transaction waits at most 5 s for that lock (for example behind a plan being saved) and then answers 409 "Plan is being saved - retry in a moment" (`PLAN_BUSY`), not a 500 (PR3). A version **without an applied plan** (no chosen option; only versions left behind by a failed re-plan before PR3) allows only Unlock (LOCKED to PLANNED), Back to locked (LOADING to LOCKED) and Completed (DISPATCHED to COMPLETED: no plan facts change and no reconciliation is needed), 409 `NO_PLAN_APPLIED` otherwise, so the day can be optimized again and its dispatched loads closed (review F03; the review of PR3 added Completed, which was refused, so a stranded version whose loads were all out had no action left). The `NO_PLAN_APPLIED` text gives advice the dispatcher can follow on that version: OPTIMIZE when a load is still PLANNED, unlock first when only LOCKED or LOADING loads could be freed. After the change:

- an order becomes `Order.status DISPATCHED` once every part of it is on a DISPATCHED or COMPLETED load and no part is unserved;
- when the version has an applied plan, it becomes `DISPATCHED` (and `finalizedAt` is set, kept from the first time) when every load is DISPATCHED or COMPLETED, otherwise `READY`. A DRAFT or FAILED version without one keeps its status: it never becomes READY without a summary and reconciliation (PR3, review L14);
- the audit row is `LOAD_LOCKED`, `LOAD_PLANNED`, `LOAD_LOADING`, `LOAD_DISPATCHED` or `LOAD_COMPLETED`;
- `refreshPlanFacts` runs.

**Unlock from the kept-load warning (24 Oct 2026).** The box "Locked loads planned with older customer data" ([3.7](#37-step-5-reviewing-the-plan)) and the re-plan dialog ([3.11](#311-step-9-late-orders-and-plan-versions)) unlock with this same route, one load at a time, latest first (`unlockKeptLoads` in `kept-changes.ts`), with `via: 'KEPT_DATA_CHANGED'`. They stop at the first refusal (another dispatcher moved a load to Loading, the plan is optimizing, a later load was locked meanwhile) and say what was unlocked and what was refused; a load already Planned ("Load is already PLANNED.": another dispatcher unlocked it) counts as unlocked and the chain goes on (review N2); what was unlocked stays Planned (nothing is lost; it can be locked again). The box asks first, naming every load that goes back. One click is offered only for LOCKED loads: a LOADING load is named with "press Back to locked on it first". With `via`, `changeStatusCore` reads what changed on the load (`keptChangesOf`, `loadId`) **before** it moves - the report reads only locked and loading loads (review W2) - and the `LOAD_PLANNED` row adds `via` and `keptChanges` (customer codes, kinds, effect, and the hours planned with and now; never names, addresses or pins). The server never takes the screen's text. With `KEPT_CHANGES=off` the row is as before. The report runs on the unlock's own transaction: an error of its own is logged and left out, but a failed SQL read there aborts the transaction, so the unlock then fails like any failed read (review N1; plain reads only).

"Frozen" means any status except PLANNED (`FROZEN`, `isFrozen`). A re-plan copies frozen loads exactly as they are.

**The feasibility gate (PR4, review F04).** LOCK, LOADING and DISPATCH (forward moves only: `isGatedMove`) run `timingGate` in `changeStatusTx`, under the plan's row lock. It recomputes the timetable check of the version from the plan's own facts (`loadFeasibilityInput` + `checkPlanFeasibility` in `lib/dispatch/feasibility.ts`; the stored `RunPlan.feasibilityJson` is only compared by its `inputHash`) and refuses the move with **409 `TIMES_NOT_VERIFIED`** (`{ error, code, truckId, truckCode, status, remedy, unlockFirst[], violations[] }`, message "Truck T01: the timetable is not verified … Re-plan to get a timetable that keeps every rule", or, when a blocking violation is on a LOCKED or LOADING load, "… put load T01 L1 back to Planned first ("Back to locked" if it is loading, then "Unlock"), then re-plan": a re-plan copies such a load unchanged, so re-planning alone would bring the problem back. `unlockFirst` also lists every later LOCKED or LOADING load of that truck, latest first, because Unlock is refused while a later load of the truck is frozen: "… put loads T01 L2, T01 L1 back to Planned first, in this order …") when the load's **truck-day** is not OK. Checked per truck-day over every load of the version, frozen copies included, from the plan's own facts (the snapshots, the stored rows and the optimizer's inputs and report). Only three checks read the master data now: the product's case weight for cases planned at 0 kg (`CAPACITY_KG_NEW_WEIGHT`, blocks), the product's cases per pallet on a load planned by pallets (`CAPACITY_PALLETS_NEW_FACTOR`, see below) and the truck's capacity now (`CAPACITY_CHANGED`, a warning):

- cases per load (from its stops) against the truck it was planned on (`truckSnapshotJson`); **physical kg** (a split portion's own kg, else the order's) against that payload (review F01), with one rounding tolerance (`KG_ROUNDING_TOL` = 0.5 kg in `weights.ts`, the same as `applyScenario`'s kg cross-check and the workbook's Kg check). Cases **planned** with no weight are `KG_UNKNOWN`, a **warning** only: the dispatcher accepted them at optimize ("treated as 0 kg", review F02). "Planned with no weight" is read from the plan's rows, never from today's product master: a split part keeps the case weight each line was planned with (`portionLinesJson[].kgPerCase`); a part stored before that counts its 0-kg lines as unknown when its own kg shows it; a whole order's lines hold the kg it was planned with. When a case weight was entered under Products since and the load would now be over its payload, it is `CAPACITY_KG_NEW_WEIGHT` and blocks like any overload;
- a load planned by pallets (its truck snapshot keeps the room, bays x Pallet fill) against that room by the units stored on its rows (`CAPACITY_PALLETS`, blocks; never its case capacity, never a load whose rows have no units). **One customer on a truck** (owner rule 13 Oct 2026): a load whose rows are all one customer (`Order.customerId`, `loadCustomerCount`), planned when the optimizer echoed the one-customer rule (the snapshot's `singleCustomerFillPct`), is checked against every bay (`plannedLoadRoom` in `pallets.ts`, used by `feasibilityInputFromRows` for the room and the room now, and by `getPlanDetail`), with the words "(12 bays at 100% fill, one customer)"; a load of several customers keeps the Pallet fill; a load planned before the rule keeps its room and its check hash (`FeasCapacity.oneCustomer` only when set; and only when the rule gives more room than the fill - at Pallet fill 100% a one-customer load reads *limit 12.0 at 100% fill*, as before). Rollout note: a one-customer load planned at 95% before the deploy (11,027 on 12 bays) and still PLANNED or LOCKED when the fill goes back to 90% shows the WARN *... the truck was changed to 12 bays (10.8 pallets at 90% fill) after planning* (a warning, never a block); change the fill to 90 only after that day's plans were re-planned or dispatched, or re-plan to clear it. Pallets review: a cases per pallet corrected under Products since planning works the rows out again with today's factors (`FeasStop.palletUnitsNow`, `rowPalletUnitsNow` in `split.ts`: each line rounded up as the request builder does, so an unchanged row gives exactly its stored units); a load that then needs more than its room is `CAPACITY_PALLETS_NEW_FACTOR` ("T01 load 1 was planned with 11.4 pallets; with the cases per pallet corrected under Products since (JA0.5L) it needs 13.0 pallets, more than the truck takes: 12.0 (12 bays at 100% fill). Re-plan to load it by the cases per pallet now."), blocking on a PLANNED load and a warning with the unlock order on a LOCKED or LOADING one (a re-plan keeps it). Before, nothing but the manifest's grey line said so;
- each service start inside the receiving window the stop was planned with (`stopSnapshotJson`; a window that ends before it starts was planned as "any time"), and the stored `hardWindowOk`;
- the turnaround: each load leaves after the previous load's return + reload + loading per case × its cases, with the rules the later load was planned with (`truckSnapshotJson.rules`); first departure after shift start / depot opening / truck availability, returns before the depot closes and the availability ends (each load with its own rules), the whole day within the shift maximum and the loads-per-day limit;
- the optimizer's own report for the option in use (`ScenarioDetails.feasibility`, [4.11](#411-post-solve-stage)): VIOLATED blocks the trucks it names, UNVERIFIED blocks.

Rules: 1-minute tolerance (the solver rounds seconds to minutes). A problem on a load that has already left (DISPATCHED or COMPLETED) is history: a warning that never blocks, so it can never lock the truck's later loads for good. A problem on a LOCKED or LOADING load is flagged `frozen` (the remedy is to put it back to Planned first, with the later locked or loading loads of its truck, see above). A truck whose capacity or payload was corrected since planning below what a load not yet out carries gives the warning `CAPACITY_CHANGED` (the load keeps the truck it was planned with; on a LOCKED or LOADING load the warning names the same unlock order, e.g. "Put T01 L2, T01 L1 back to Planned first, in this order, and re-plan to use the new capacity."; the day screen also says the plan is out of date, [3.5](#35-step-3-the-day-overview)). Stepping back (unlock, back to locked) and Completed are never gated. A version made before the check (options without a report, loads without snapshots) is checked structurally (`LEGACY_STRUCTURAL_ONLY`: windows, overlaps, and for loads of its own successful job the truck and rules from that job's stored request) and blocked only on a concrete violation. `FEASIBILITY_GATE=warn` ([2.9](#29-environment-variables-by-service)) lets the move through and records `timing: { ok: false, gate: 'warn', overridden, violations }` in the `LOAD_*` audit row; every gated move records `timing` there. The result is stored by `refreshPlanFacts` (after every applied option and load change) and `createNextVersion`, and shown on the plan screen ([3.7](#37-step-5-reviewing-the-plan)). With a loading time per case of 0 (NMWC today) practically every plan verifies; the gate matters once real loading minutes are entered (backlog #1).

**Moves by hand and load states** (24 Oct 2026). Only PLANNED loads are changed by a move by hand ([3.7](#37-step-5-reviewing-the-plan)): a LOCKED load is refused with 409 `LOAD_FROZEN` "T08 L2 is locked: unlock it first to move its stops." (Unlock as usual, latest load first), and LOADING, DISPATCHED and COMPLETED loads never change. An edited truck's frozen loads stay as they are and its new loads are numbered after them. A load made by a move is timed and checked like an optimized one, so the timetable gate treats it the same; the save is rolled back (409 `EDIT_CHECK_FAILED`) when the web's own check of an edited truck disagrees with the solver's.

### 3.9 Step 7: a driver per load

- **Default (usual) driver per truck.** `Truck.defaultDriverId`, set on the Trucks page by a company admin, or (owner request 6 Oct 2026) on the Drivers page's **Usual driver of each truck** by the dispatcher (`PATCH /api/trucks/:id { defaultDriverId }`, PLANNER for that field alone, audited `TRUCK_USUAL_DRIVER_SET` with `{ truck, from, to }` by code and driver name, *none* for no driver, plus the ids). The message after the change is one short line (`usualDriverChangedMessage`: *Usual driver of T03 is now Rashid. Re-plan days already planned to use him.*); what a re-plan does with each trip is in the dispatcher guide.
- **Driver leave (owner request 6 Oct 2026: "our drivers change a lot, or one of them is on leave and we bring another one, or they take a whole month of leave; it will be his job to monitor those").** `DriverLeave`: a driver, from and until (delivery dates, both included), an optional note and an optional **cover driver**; entered on the Drivers page (**Leave** button) by the dispatcher (PLANNER) and up, read by every role. Rules (pure, `lib/dispatch/driver-leave.ts`): one driver's periods never overlap (checked under the driver's row lock, `driver-leave-service.ts`); a period is entered for today or later; one that has ended is kept as it was, one that has started keeps its first day (end it early down to yesterday) and is not removed (the Leave dialog offers **Remove** only for a period that starts tomorrow or later, `leaveActions`: a period from today is *On leave now* with **Change / end early**, though the API still removes it); the cover is another driver, active when he is chosen (a cover deactivated after the save is kept and does not block a change or ending the period early: `checkLeaveChange`; the dialog lists him *(inactive)*), and CHECK constraints `DriverLeave_dates_in_order` and `DriverLeave_cover_not_self` hold in the database too. The Drivers page lists **Drivers on leave** (today and the coming 14 days) and shows *on leave until 12 Oct* beside the driver; a cover who will not drive is marked (`coverCaveat`: *inactive*, *on leave himself ...*, or *usual driver of T03: he covers only on days T03 does not run*), there and in *Usual driver of each truck → Today*. The save warns when the cover is away part of the time, when he is another active truck's usual driver (`coverOwnTruckWarning`) and when the driver is still on loads of those days. The Leave dialog reads the periods first: a failed read shows the error with **Retry** and the form stays off. On a delivery day inside a period:
  - RouteIQ never puts him on a load (`planDrivers` pass 2 skips him; a driver picked by hand stays - pass 1 - and frozen loads never change);
  - a trip still without a driver whose truck's usual driver is away gets the **cover** (pass 3), when he is active, not on leave himself that day, free at that time and drives no **other** truck that day - of the plan (frozen, hand-set or given earlier) or of another depot (`driversOnOtherDepots`: the drivers on the loads of the other depots' live plan versions of that day; plans are per depot, drivers the company's); else no driver. The trip is marked `PlanLoad.driverIsCover`;
  - a cover is never kept as "the driver the trip already had" (review of 6 Oct 2026): pass 2 offers neither candidate (a) when the evidence load's driver was the cover (the marker, or the current cover of the truck's usual driver on leave) nor (b) when it is the current cover, so he comes again as the cover only through pass 3 and its rules (he can still get the trip as the driver of the truck's nearest trip, pass 2 (b), once he is no longer the current cover - for example when a trip of that truck he drives has left). A re-plan therefore gives the driver of the truck's nearest trip that already has one (frozen, picked by hand or given earlier in pass 2), else: the usual driver when the leave was ended early or moved, the new cover when another was named, the new usual driver when the truck's usual driver changed, and the cover's own usual truck first when it runs that day. Such a change is a driver note with reason `COVER` and `cover` = `ENDED` / `OTHER_TRUCK` / `OTHER_DEPOT` / `TRUCK_DRIVER` (*... Bob → Ali, because Bob is no longer the cover of this truck's usual driver ...*). A driver RouteIQ filled in for another reason stays on a re-plan after a usual-driver change while he is active, not on leave that day and free at that time (plan continuity, pass 2 (a)): the dispatcher picks the driver on those loads. The guide (and, until the demo of 7 Oct 2026 made it one short line, the message after a usual-driver change, `usualDriverChangedMessage` in `drivers/usual-drivers.tsx`) promises only what a re-plan can do (second review of 6 Oct 2026: the first wording - every other trip keeps its driver, the new usual driver gets the cover's trips, clearing takes the cover off - broke for a trip given to a driver now on leave, a truck whose other trip was picked by hand and a cover whose earlier trip had left): a trip without a driver, a trip a cover drove and a trip whose driver is on leave that day can go to the new usual driver (pass 2 (c)) or to the driver of another trip of the truck (pass 2 (b), the nearest trip that already has its driver: so a trip earlier in pass 2's order than a filled-in one can still get the usual driver, or nobody), cleared to the driver of another trip or nobody; a driver picked by hand stays while active (pass 1); the dispatcher checks the drivers after the re-plan. `dispatcher-drivers.spec.ts` checks nine one- and two-trip cases, set and cleared, against `planDrivers`, each against what the guide allows, and the two short messages word for word;
  - the plan screen shows on the load (`DetailLoad.driverNote`, read live, `loadLeaveNote`) *No driver: Ali is on leave until 12 Oct - pick a driver*, *Ali is on leave until 12 Oct* (his load picked by hand, or planned before the leave was entered) or *Covers Ali (on leave until 12 Oct)* - with *- but Bob also drives a truck of another depot that day: pick another driver* when the other depot, planned later, gave the cover his own truck; the Driver list labels a driver on leave that day *Ali - on leave* (`driverOptionLabel`, short so the closed list shows it whole; the until date is in its tooltip `onLeaveTitle` and the note) (`PlanDetail.driversOnLeave`) and asks before he is chosen (`leaveQuestion`); **Keep** under such a driver asks the same question (`keepTitle` names the leave), and the daily-driver quick add answers 409 `DRIVER_ON_LEAVE` for a driver used again who is on leave that day until the dialog sends `leaveConfirmed` (`PHONE_BELONGS_TO` carries `leaveUntil`); rule 20 keeps a load without a driver from leaving;
  - after the period he is used again by himself (the next day's plan has no evidence: his truck's default driver; a day planned during the leave gets him back at its next re-plan, the cover's trip being marked). A leave saved for days already planned answers a warning naming his loads (re-plan, or pick another driver); the plans are not changed by the save. Two depots optimized at the same moment can still give one cover twice (no lock spans depots).
- **Per load.** The driver picker calls `PATCH /api/runs/:id/loads/:loadId { driverId }` (`null` = no driver), which runs `updateLoad` then `setDriverTx`.
- **Owner rule 20 (30 Sep 2026): a load never leaves without a driver.** `changeStatusTx` refuses a move to DISPATCHED of a load without a driver with 409 `DRIVER_REQUIRED` ("T05 L1: a load never leaves without a driver. Pick the driver in the Driver list, or add a daily driver, then dispatch."). It runs **last**, after every other gate (their refusals keep their words), on the load as it is after the driver step of the same request. LOCK, LOADING and COMPLETED are not affected (a load dispatched before the rule can still be completed). The plan screen disables Dispatch without a driver.
- **A driver on leave at Lock, Loading and Dispatch (end-to-end demo of 7 Oct 2026).** RouteIQ had put Salim on T03 L1 for 13 Oct, his leave for 13 Oct was saved afterwards (the save warned), nobody re-planned, and Lock and Dispatch went through silently. Now `changeStatusTx` (`leaveGate`, after every other gate and before rule 20, on the load as it is after the driver step of the same request) refuses a forward move (`isGatedMove`: PLANNED -> LOCKED, LOCKED -> LOADING, LOCKED / LOADING -> DISPATCHED) of a load whose driver is on leave on the plan's day with 409 `DRIVER_ON_LEAVE` `{ driverId, name, day, until }` (*T03 L1: Salim Nasser is on leave on 13 Oct - pick another driver, or confirm that he drives.*, `onLeaveMoveRefusal`), nothing changed. With `leaveConfirmed: true` in the body (`PATCH /api/runs/:id/loads/:loadId`) it goes through and the status change's audit row keeps `driverOnLeave: { driverId, driverName, until, confirmed: true }`. The plan screen sends every status change through `moveLoad`: on that refusal it asks (`onLeaveMoveQuestion`: *... Lock T03 · L1 with Salim Nasser anyway?*) and OK sends the move again with the answer; **Lock all** asks per load. Each step asks again. Stepping back (Unlock, Back to locked) and Completed never ask: a load that has left is never judged by leave entered afterwards. Rule 20 is unchanged.
- **One truck or driver on two depots' plans (review web-plan-service-1, 9 Oct 2026; `lib/dispatch/cross-depot.ts`).** Plans are per depot, trucks and drivers are the company's. A truck lent to another depot for the day (its depot changed under Trucks) kept its loads on the first depot's plan, and each plan saw only its own loads, so both depots could send it (and one driver) out at the same time with a VERIFIED timetable. Now:
  - `buildDispatchRequest` reads the truck's loads on the other depots' live plan versions of that day (any status: a PLANNED load there is that depot's plan for it) and narrows its hours (`available_from_min` / `available_to_min`, which the optimizer, its check and the timetable gate honour) to the longest free stretch around them inside the planned day, counting the straight-line drive between the depots (distance multiplier, average speed for estimates) and the reload and loading (that load's cases before it, a full truck after it); with none left, an empty window: no new load here (and not counted as an idle truck). The load numbers stay the depot's own. A plan warning names the loads (*Truck T01 is on another depot's plan this day (North depot: L1 06:00–10:00 dispatched): new loads here leave from 11:44, ...*).
  - `planDrivers` (passes 2 and 3) never gives a driver who is on a load of another depot's live plan at an overlapping time, the drive included (`driverTripsElsewhere`); a trip that loses its driver to one gets a CLASH note naming that load with its depot. A driver picked by hand is kept (pass 1).
  - Lock, Loading and Dispatch (`changeStatusTx`, after the timetable gate and before the leave question) refuse a load whose truck or driver (after the driver step of the same request) is on a LOCKED, LOADING, DISPATCHED or COMPLETED load of another depot's live plan that day at a time both cannot be driven, the drive counted: 409 `TRUCK_BUSY_ELSEWHERE` / `DRIVER_BUSY_ELSEWHERE` with the other load (`otherDepotClash`), nothing changed. A PLANNED load there does not refuse: the depot that locks first keeps the truck or driver, so two plans never refuse each other for good. Read under the truck-day and driver-day advisory locks (`lockTruckDriverDay`, taken last), so two depots moving the same truck or driver at the same moment are checked one after the other. `FEASIBILITY_GATE=warn` does not apply.
  - Not covered: the Trucks page still moves a truck to another depot without a check or a warning about its loads on the old depot's plan (that plan keeps them until it is re-planned; the other depot plans around them), and the plan screen's driver clash note shows one plan only.
- **Daily (casual) drivers (4 Oct 2026).** The Driver list ends with "+ Add daily driver…": name and mobile, saved as a daily driver (`Driver.casual`, no account, code `DAY-<yyMMdd>-<n>` under an advisory lock per company and date) and put on the load in one load-change transaction (`addCasualDriver`, `POST /api/dispatch/casual-driver`, PLANNER; `inLoadChange` in plan-service). The same phone and name reuses that daily driver (reactivated if needed); a phone that belongs to another driver answers 409 `PHONE_BELONGS_TO` and the dialog asks "This phone belongs to <name>. Use <name>?" (`useExisting`). Only a daily driver is ever reactivated here: an inactive regular driver (a company admin switched them off) is not offered, and `useExisting` naming one answers 409 `DRIVER_INACTIVE` ("Driver X is inactive: ask a company admin."). A unique-key race answers 409 `CODE_TAKEN` (never retried inside the aborted transaction). The Driver list shows "Salim (daily)"; the Drivers page has a Daily badge and filter, and an admin can clear `casual`. Since the delivery outcome Part 3 the retention janitor hides a daily driver with no load for 30 days (the quick add finds and reactivates them by phone) and erases their phone after the location retention (the name stays: plans and audit rows show it).
  - `checkDriverChange` refuses a real change once the load is DISPATCHED or COMPLETED. Re-sending the current driver changes nothing, with one exception, **Keep** (`isDriverKeep`): the driver RouteIQ filled in (not hand-set) re-sent for a load not yet out is marked as the dispatcher's choice, with a `LOAD_DRIVER_SET` row (`kept: true`). The plan screen's **Keep** link sends it; the Driver list cannot (choosing the option already selected fires no change).
  - The driver must exist and be active. Audit `LOAD_DRIVER_SET`.
  - The load is marked as the dispatcher's choice: `driverSetById` (the user) and `driverSetAt` (fourth review of PR3, migration `20260926110000_plan_load_driver_set_by`). "No driver" chosen for a load that has a driver is marked the same way (who, when), so a driver note on that trip ends for good (`driverSetByDispatcher`; review of the simplified rules: "No driver" used to clear both, and a note that had left the trip without a driver came back after the dispatcher picked a driver and then "No driver"). "No driver" for a load that has none changes nothing (`checkDriverChange`: unchanged; the Driver list does not even send it): a note that left the trip without a driver ends only when a driver is picked for it. `createNextVersion`'s copies keep them. A driver is **hand-set** when the load has a driver and either column is set (`isHandSetDriver`: deleting the user clears `driverSetById`, `driverSetAt` stays); "No driver" is never hand-set, there is no driver to keep. `getPlanDetail` gives the screen `driverHandSet`, read from each load row. A driver set before that migration has no marker and counts as filled in by RouteIQ until the dispatcher presses **Keep**. No backfill: a `LOAD_DRIVER_SET` row names the load it was written on; a copy-forward copy links back to it (`carriedFromLoadId`), but a load `applyScenario` created does not, so a backfill would mark some of the choices made before the update and not others.
  - When one request carries both a driver and a status, both run in one transaction and the driver is set first.
  - The picker is filled from `GET /api/drivers` and offers active drivers plus the load's current driver.
- **After every optimize, re-plan or "Use instead".** `applyScenario` calls `planDrivers(trips, evidence, usable)` (`load-state.ts`) before it deletes anything. A **trip** is a truck and load number. The **evidence** is the loads of the version the plan is applied to, as they are right before the apply: for "Use instead", the version's own loads; for the re-plan job, the copies `createNextVersion` made of the previous version's loads, with any driver the dispatcher set on a copy between the new version and the start of its job (nobody can change them while the job runs), never the previous version's own loads. So both read the same kind of evidence, and the same evidence, with the trips in the same order, gives the same drivers and notes. The order matters only on a tie in pass 2 (below): the job and "Use instead" both read the optimizer's list, which is sorted by truck code, then trip. A trip's **evidence load** is the evidence load on the same truck and trip, if any. `usable` = the tenant's active drivers.
  - **Pass 0, frozen loads.** Locked, loading, dispatched and completed loads (any status but PLANNED) stay as they are, drivers included; their times take their drivers.
  - **Pass 1, hand-set drivers.** A trip whose evidence load has a hand-set driver keeps that driver and its marker, even when the new times overlap a frozen load or another hand-set trip of that driver: the overlap shows as the yellow clash warning (`driverClashes`). A filled-in trip at those times gives the driver up (pass 2). The marker is copied from the evidence row (its foreign key keeps `driverSetById` valid; it is never read from JSON). A hand-set driver who is no longer active is not kept: the trip goes to pass 2, and an `INACTIVE` note says why.
  - **Pass 2, drivers RouteIQ fills in.** Never a driver on leave that day (6 Oct 2026). Every other trip, the one that moved least first (how far its departure moved from its evidence load's; trips without an evidence load last; stable: on a tie - the same move, or no evidence load - the trip the optimizer lists first goes first: it lists by truck code, then trip), gets the first of these that is active and not on an overlapping trip already given out (a frozen load, a hand-set trip, or an earlier trip of pass 2):
    1. its evidence load's driver;
    2. the driver of the same truck's trip in the new plan that is nearest in time (the smallest gap between the two trips, the earlier one on a tie) and already has a driver - a frozen load counts, so the driver of a locked Load 1 takes the new Load 2;
    3. the truck's default driver.

    None of them: no driver, for the dispatcher to fill. So of two filled-in trips that now overlap with the same driver, the one that moved loses it, and a driver RouteIQ fills in never overlaps another trip of that driver.
  - **Pass 3, the cover driver (6 Oct 2026).** A trip still without a driver whose truck's default driver is on leave that day gets that leave's cover driver, in pass 2's order, when the cover is active, not on leave himself, free at that time and on no other truck of the plan that day. `applyScenario` reads the leave of the plan's delivery date (`leaveRowsOn`, `leaveOnDay`) and passes it as `planDrivers`' fourth argument.
  - **Overlap** is the planned times alone (`timesOverlap`: back at 10:00 and out at 10:00 is no overlap). Trip 1 and trip 2 of a truck share a driver unless their times really overlap, which a valid plan never has.
  - **The first optimization of a day** has no evidence: pass 2 with 2 and 3 only, so each truck's default driver in the optimizer's order, never one driver on two overlapping trips - the same drivers as before these rules.
  - **Driver notes.** A note only when a trip loses or changes the driver its evidence load had: `CLASH` (another trip of the plan got that driver at an overlapping time; the note names that trip), `INACTIVE` (that driver is no longer active), `ON_LEAVE` (6 Oct 2026: that driver is on leave that day; the note keeps `leaveUntil`, "because Ali is on leave until 12 Oct"), and `TRIP_GONE` (a hand-set driver whose truck and trip the new plan does not have). Filling a trip that had no driver is not a note. `applyScenario` stores the notes with the names in `summaryJson.driverChanges`, audits them in `SCENARIO_CHOSEN` and returns them (the "Use instead" toast and the job's message count them; the dispatch screens show a job's message only while it runs or after it failed, so after a re-plan the dispatcher sees the yellow notes). Every apply replaces the stored notes, also with none: a re-plan's version starts with a copy of the previous version's summary, notes included (shown while the copy is in use), and its job's plan replaces them. A load change keeps them. The plan lists a note in yellow until the dispatcher sets that trip's driver - any driver, the same one with **Keep**, or "No driver" when the trip has a driver - and never again after (the row's marker decides, `driverSetByDispatcher`; a note that left the trip without a driver stays until a driver is picked for it, since a re-sent "No driver" writes no marker), and a `TRIP_GONE` note while the plan has no load for that trip ([3.7](#37-step-5-reviewing-the-plan)). A `TRIP_GONE` note is information about this version only: nothing brings that driver back later. A later plan with that truck and trip fills it in like any other trip, and the dispatcher picks the driver again.
  - These rules replaced a multi-step design after the sixth review of PR3 (owner decision, [7.4](#74-review-leads-found-while-writing-this-handbook)).
- **Clashes.** A clash the dispatcher sets by hand is allowed but shown (`driverClashes`, `driverClashNotes`). A re-plan or "Use instead" keeps it when a hand-set trip overlaps another hand-set trip of that driver or one of their frozen loads: the same warning. A driver RouteIQ fills in never creates a clash.
- `setLoadDriver` and `changeLoadStatus` in `plan-service.ts` are exported single-purpose wrappers that nothing calls; the route uses `updateLoad`.
