- **Deleting a driver**: since the audit PR "Intake and master data" (F20, owner decision 8) a driver is **always deactivated, never deleted** (`DELETE /api/drivers/:id` answers `softDeleted: true`, `defaultOfTrucks` and a `warning` naming the trucks that still have them as default driver; the Drivers screen's button says **Deactivate**). PR1 deactivated only a driver on a load or a legacy shift and deleted the others, but its count raced with dispatch: a driver assigned and dispatched between the count and the delete lost the load (`PlanLoad.driverId` was `ON DELETE SET NULL`), and a delete cleared every truck's default driver without a word. A deactivated driver stays on their loads and as their trucks' default; new plans skip an inactive driver. The database refuses a delete of a driver still on a load or still a truck's default (`NO ACTION`, migration `20260930093000_master_data_no_orphans`). Switching a driver to inactive with Edit gives the same warning.

- **Helpers (truck crew), owner request 13 Oct 2026** ("management asked to track helpers in each truck, so add that like drivers too. We need to know who were the helpers in each truck and load"; `lib/dispatch/load-helpers.ts`, migration `20261013150000_load_helpers`). The optimizer never reads helpers.
  - **Register.** `Helper` (code unique per company, name, optional phone, active), the **Helpers** page next to Drivers (same roles: VIEWER reads; PLANNER adds, edits, deactivates and reactivates; a search box; a code change is the admin's). Never deleted.
  - **Usual helper per truck.** `Truck.defaultHelperId` (NO ACTION, as the default driver): the Helpers page's **Usual helper of each truck** (PLANNER) or the Trucks page's **Default helper** (admin); `TRUCK_USUAL_HELPER_SET`.
  - **On a load.** `PlanLoadHelper` (0 to 3 per load, `position` 1-3, CHECK `PlanLoadHelper_position_range`, unique (`loadId`, `helperId`) and (`loadId`, `position`), CASCADE with its load). `applyScenario` calls `planHelpers` before it deletes the PLANNED loads: frozen loads keep theirs; a trip whose evidence load had helpers set by hand (`helpersSetById` / `helpersSetAt` with at least one helper) keeps the active ones and the marker, even over an overlap (as a hand-set driver); every other trip gets the truck's usual helper when he is active and on no overlapping trip already given out - nor on a load of another depot's live plan that day, the drive between the depots included (`helperTripsElsewhere` in `cross-depot.ts`, as `driverTripsElsewhere`) - else none. "No helpers" set by hand is not kept (as "No driver"). A hand-set helper the plan drops is a helper note (`TRIP_GONE`: the trip is not in the plan; `INACTIVE`), as a driver note: kept in `summaryJson.helperChanges`, shown as a plan warning (`helperChangeWarnings`) until that helper is on a load again (a `TRIP_GONE` note also ends when the trip is back, an `INACTIVE` one when the trip's helpers are set after the plan), in the `SCENARIO_CHOSEN` audit (`helperChanges`) and returned by `applyScenario`. Accepted gap (owner decision pending): LOCK / LOADING / DISPATCH do not refuse a helper on another depot's overlapping load (drivers get 409 `DRIVER_BUSY_ELSEWHERE`), and the plan screen's clash warning covers the same plan only. No leave for helpers. `createNextVersionTx` copies every load's helpers to its copy (`copyLoadHelpers`).
  - **Changing them.** `PATCH /api/runs/:id/loads/:loadId { helperIds }` (PLANNER; `loadHelperIdsSchema`: 0-3, each once) runs `setHelpersTx` in the load-change transaction: the same states as the driver (409 `HELPERS_AFTER_DISPATCH` once DISPATCHED or COMPLETED), a new helper must be active (one already on the load may stay), re-sending helpers RouteIQ filled in marks them as the dispatcher's (`kept: true`). Audited `LOAD_HELPERS_CHANGED` with ids and names before and after. A helper on two loads at overlapping times is allowed; the plan screen warns (`helperClashes`).
  - **Shown** on the plan screen (**Helper(s)** column with a multi-select), the driver sheet PDF ("Helper: Saif" / "Helpers: Saif, Omar", WinAnsi-safe), the Excel (LOAD PLAN **Helper(s)** column; a load sheet's Driver cell "Ali · Helper(s): Saif", merged D:E and wrapped so no name is cut), the warehouse load sheet and return note (**Helper(s)** head cell), the Delivery actuals Excel (**Helper(s)** column after *Daily driver*) and the driver page header ("Helper:" / "Helpers:" by the count; the truck-day's helpers; the manifest memo stamp includes `helpersSetAt`).
  - **Crew report (Excel).** On Daily dispatch (every role): From / To (31 days at most), this depot or every depot. Sheet *Loads*: one row per load of the plan in use of each depot-day, any status - date, depot, truck, trip, load status, driver, helper 1-3, departed (the time the load was marked Dispatched - the `LOAD_DISPATCHED` row of the load or of the load it was copied from - else the planned departure, with the basis in *Departed from*), back at depot (the driver's tap), stops, cases; the driver and helpers as "Name (CODE)" (names are not unique). Sheet *Helpers*: Code, Helper, loads, days and trucks, counted by helper id (two helpers who share a name are two lines). Every role may download it, as the plan's Excel; Delivery actuals is PLANNER and above (owner decision pending on whether the crew report should be too).

### 3.10 Step 8: exports

| Export | Route | Built by | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Excel master workbook | `GET /api/runs/:id/export/excel` (`apps/web/app/api/runs/[id]/export/excel/route.ts`) | `getPlanDetail`, then `buildDispatchWorkbook` and `tenantAssumptions` (`apps/web/lib/dispatch/workbook.ts`, ExcelJS) | Offered for every dispatch plan (`PlanDetail.isDispatchPlan`), also one in which every order is unserved and that has no load (audit F16: it had no Excel at all; its UNSERVED - EXCEPTIONS, RECONCILIATION and ASSUMPTIONS sheets matter most then). Sheets: SUMMARY, LOAD PLAN, one sheet per load ("T01 - L1": manifest and route), SKU LOADING SUMMARY, UNSERVED - EXCEPTIONS, RECONCILIATION, ASSUMPTIONS. Audit E3: the LOADING MANIFEST and the SKU LOADING SUMMARY weigh each row's SKU lines by the kg it was **planned** with (`rowLinesKg` in `split.ts`: the portion's kept case weight, per case for an order weighed at order level, else the lines' kg; in 0.1 kg, adding up exactly to the row's kg), so the sheet's kg is the load's kg - also after a product weight correction and for orders weighed at order level (before: 200 kg on a 300 kg load, and 0 kg). Both check kg as well as cases: "MISMATCH: load records N kg (order weights changed since planning)" on the load sheet and "MISMATCH (kg)" in the summary's Check row, for an older version whose orders were re-weighed by a later re-plan (the per-row planned kg of a whole order is not stored). Audit E1: the load sheet's DEPOT rows link to the depot pin the load was planned from, with "Depot moved since planning ..." when it moved. A6 review: the ASSUMPTIONS **Weights** row and the Overtime row's "not counted again for new loads" clause are stated only for a plan whose option reports those rules (`solverRules`: `weight_unit_kg` 0.1 and `new_overtime_only` in its `detailsJson`); a plan made by an optimizer before them reads "earlier rule: the route search rounded each stop up to a whole kg and each payload down to a whole kg (a small margin below the payload)" and has no clause. File name `nmwc-dispatch-<depot>-<date>-v<version>.xlsx`. A superseded version carries a "do not load or dispatch" line. Since PR4: SUMMARY has a TIMETABLE CHECK section; a plan (or truck) whose times are not verified carries **TIMES NOT VERIFIED** at the top and in the page header of SUMMARY, LOAD PLAN and that truck's load sheets; LOAD PLAN has Payload kg, **Kg check** (the load's kg against its stops and the payload, with the 0.5 kg rounding tolerance of the dispatch check: OK / OVER PAYLOAD / OVER PAYLOAD at the case weights entered since planning / MISMATCH / SOME CASES HAVE NO WEIGHT) and Timing columns; the route table has a **Changed after planning** column; ASSUMPTIONS shows the settings stored with the plan in use ("Settings this plan (vN) was built and costed with", including whether the plan was outside the Oman + UAE routing map, `PlanSettings.outsideCoverage`), or, for a plan from before they were stored, today's settings under "Current settings, at export time …" (review F08). The web server's own `OSRM_URL` never appears there: it only draws the legacy Map tab.
