**Salesman ETA (owner request 17 Oct 2026).** Every evening after planning the owner prints one page per sales route (the salesman: the order file's `route` column, `OrderLine.salesRoute`, [3.3](#33-step-1-upload-and-validate-the-order-file)) so the salesmen can tell their customers when the truck comes; an offline tool did it before. **Salesman ETA** on the plan screen (beside Load sheets, `data-testid` `export-salesman-eta`) opens it in a new tab; **Print** or Save as PDF. Built from `getPlanDetail` like the load sheets (`planOf` in `warehouse-export.ts`: 404 for another company's run or one that is not a dispatch plan, 404 `NO_LOADS` without loads), plus `loadSalesmanEtaFacts` (each line's route and its product's cases per pallet, read through the order so every read names the company; whether an order was cancelled or brought forward since; the day's orders added after the plan, read only for the version in use with `pendingOrders`), sent with `sheetHtmlResponse` (the load sheets' headers and Print-only CSP). Each route page: "Route R1 · deliveries Sunday 18 October 2026", the company and depot, "N customers, M cases", the plan version and the printed time (company time zone), "Not locked yet: times can change if the day is re-planned" when a load with the route's customers is not LOCKED, LOADING, DISPATCHED or COMPLETED, VOID on a replaced version. One row per customer of the route, sorted by the first expected arrival: the window (`etaSlot`: planned arrival -15 min down to the quarter hour, +45 min up to it; kept inside the order's promised time, else the hard hours the stop was planned with: never before opening when planned after it, never after closing when planned by it, but always up to the quarter hour after the planned time) big and "planned HH:MM" small, one line per part for a split customer; the customer (name, code / branch); the route's invoices and cases only (a customer can buy from two salesmen); an *Open map* link of the stop's pin (`https://www.google.com/maps?q=lat,lng`) or "no location"; the receiving hours ("any time" without any; "this order: HH:MM-HH:MM" for an order's own time). Orders of the route on no stop of the plan are listed under the table ("Not in the plan for this day (the office will advise)": left out, moved to another day - also an order brought forward from a load that has not left - or added after the plan was made), once however many unserved rows the plan keeps for them (one per reason for a split order's parts); a split order's rest that is on no truck is listed line by line under each line's own route (each line's cases less its cases on the plan's stops: the rest can be a whole invoice of another salesman), and only those routes' rows say "More of this customer's cases are not on a truck" (review of 17 Oct 2026); cancelled orders are left out; lines without a route make the last page, "Route not given". Routes sort naturally (R1, R2, R2X, R10, R11X). Pallets are `palletUnits` of each line with its product's cases per pallet now, shown to 0.1, with "+" and a footnote when some products have none. There is no per-truck table and no driver name or phone anywhere. A late order may carry the route too (*Sales route* in the Late order dialog, `salesRoute` in `POST /api/dispatch/late-order`), and the copies of Bring forward and Postpone keep each line's route (`carryCopyData`).

Both export routes first ask `isDispatchPlan` (`apps/web/lib/dispatch/legacy-runs.ts`: the plan has loads, a RECOMMENDED option or a later version; the plan screen reads the same rule as `PlanDetail.isDispatchPlan`, `isDispatchPlanShape`). A dispatch plan gets the dispatch export above; since audit F16 this no longer depends on the load count, which sent a plan with every order unserved to the legacy route sheet. The PDF stays driver sheets only: a dispatch plan without loads answers 404 `NO_LOADS` ("This plan has no loads, so there are no driver sheets. Its unserved orders are in the Excel export."), and the plan screen shows no PDF button for it. Only legacy runs fall back to the old route sheet: `buildRouteSheet` (`apps/web/lib/exports/route-sheet-data.ts`) with `buildRouteSheetExcel` (`apps/web/lib/exports/excel.ts`) or `buildRouteSheetPdf` (`apps/web/lib/exports/pdf.tsx`).

**Loading instruction in the exports (owner request 16 Oct 2026, `lib/dispatch/loading-instruction.ts`).** A customer's `loadingInstruction` is read live by `getPlanDetail`, like `accessNotes` (`DetailStop.loadingInstruction`, folded to one line, control and invisible direction characters dropped so a hidden right-to-left override cannot reverse the joined lines; a longer value written to the database by hand is cut at 200 characters with "…", never dropped). `loadInstructions` lists it per load: one line per customer with its stop numbers ("Stops 3, 5 Shop Example A (C100 / B2): ..."), leaving out a stop none of whose orders is loaded (every order cancelled or brought forward; `DetailStop.carriedOrderIds` is set only on a stop with an instruction). The warehouse load sheet prints a **SPECIAL LOADING** box under the title (on a VOID paper, after the VOID banner): a 4 px black border and a 22 pt bold heading, no shading, so it shows on a black-and-white print with background graphics off. It also tags the customer's invoice rows ("SPECIAL LOADING - see the box at the top"). The box's style is added to the page only when a sheet has a box, and no script is added (the CSP and the Print script hash do not change). The driver sheet PDF prints the lines in a bordered box under TIMES NOT VERIFIED (kept whole on one page up to 12 lines; a longer box continues on the next page, because a whole box taller than the room left was squeezed and its lines printed over each other) and "LOADING: ..." under the customer (PDF-safe: Arabic prints `[?]`); every word of it travels in the model (`DriverSheet.loadingInstructions` and `loadingInstructionsTitle`, `SheetStop.loadingInstruction`), because the renderer bundle may hold only its own modules (`scripts/pdf-renderer-build.cjs`), never `loading-instruction.ts`. The Excel load sheet gets one boxed row above LOADING MANIFEST (*SPECIAL LOADING* in A, the lines in D:U) and "Loading: ..." in the stop notes. A day without instructions exports byte for byte as before (pinned by SHA-256 in `warehouse-sheets.spec.ts`, `driver-pack.spec.ts` and `dispatch-workbook.spec.ts`).

**Special-loading lines (owner request 20 Oct 2026, `lib/dispatch/loading-split.ts`).** Such a customer's products carry their own barcodes and are loaded apart; with only the box, the warehouse took those customers' cases off each product's total itself and made mistakes. So every per-load list of products is split: the normal lines (every other customer) with their total, then one block per instruction text with its own lines and total, then the load's total as before. A block is one text folded as the box folds it, letter case ignored, so two branches with *SPECIAL* on one truck share one block (both stops, the cases added up; the per-branch figures stay in the invoice list); another text is its own block, in stop order. An order line goes to a block when its stop has the instruction, its order is neither cancelled nor brought forward to a later day, and it has cases: exactly the box's stops, and a split order's part counts only its cases on this load. Every other line stays in the normal lines, the cancelled and brought-forward orders of any customer included; on a split load sheet their banners say so (*Their cases are in the normal lines, never in the special-loading lines.*), so a block never needs anything subtracted. Normal + every block = the products, per product and in total, in cases, kg (each order line's planned kg, `DetailOrderLine.weightKg`) and pallet units (`DetailOrderLine.palletUnits`, only on a load planned by pallets); full pallets and loose cases are worked out per line shown (a block is built as its own pallets), each line at its product's own cases per pallet, the same factor as its normal line. Each block also has its pallets for the loader (owner, 20 Oct 2026: *"pallets separate is correct, but they still have the same cases per pallet and they can be put in one pallet together"*; `blockPallets`): each product's full pallets (its cases div its cases per pallet), plus the loose cases of ALL the block's products stacked together on shared mixed pallets, ceil(sum of loose cases / cases per pallet) with the fractions added exactly (BigInt, so a third + a third + a third is 1 mixed pallet, not 2); the cases of a product without a usable cases per pallet are on neither and are said to be counted separately. Only on a load planned by pallets, as the other pallet figures (`LoadingGroup.pallets`); the normal lines' pallet figures are unchanged. Its words (`specialLinesPalletTotal`): *SPECIAL total: 70 cases - 2 full pallets + 1 mixed pallet (the loose cases of all SPECIAL products together)*, a 0 part left out. Every block line carries a short tag: the text, cut past 24 characters at a word with "…" (the whole text once in the block heading), " (2)" when two tags would read the same. The printable load sheet prints each block as a framed `<tbody>` (4 px black border, bold lines, a bordered tag, no shading; the style only on pages with such lines; still one script); the Excel load sheet prints the normal lines with their total, then each block boxed with a thick edge, numbered on, its lines' descriptions starting with the tag, and the TOTAL row, the MISMATCH check and the pallet line unchanged (full and loose pallets added up from the lines shown); on a load planned by pallets each block's box closes with its pallet words on a merged line; SKU LOADING SUMMARY gets a normal section and one boxed section per text over the day (labelled as on its first load), on a day planned by pallets closed by *SPECIAL full pallets* and *SPECIAL mixed pallets* rows per load (each load builds its own; blank for a load planned by cases; *SPECIAL cases without cases per pallet* only when there are any), TOTAL, *Load cases (plan)*, *Check*, pallets and bays unchanged; the printable load sheet's block total line carries the same words (the tag in `<bdi>`); the driver sheet's *Load check* lists each block with its tag and total after the normal lines (`DriverSheet.loadCheck.groups`, the words in the model); the plan screen's loading manifest shows the blocks on amber with a warning badge. On a load planned by pallets the driver sheet's block total reads *(SPECIAL total: 70 cases - 1 mixed pallet (the loose cases of all SPECIAL products together))* (`loadCheck.groups[].totalText`) and the plan screen has the same line under the block's total. Order lines that do not add up to the products (never expected: both come from the same plan rows) split nothing: the load sheet prints the products as before with a banner to load those customers from their invoices, the Excel load sheet a bold line. A load without such a customer prints exactly as before (the pinned SHA-256 checks hold). The return note lists returned cases, not load quantities, and is unchanged.

**Pallets in the exports (part B).** Only for loads planned by pallets, so a plan without bays exports exactly as before. Excel: LOAD PLAN gets a **Pallets / bays** column after the case capacity ("11.1 / 12 (limit 12.0 at 100% fill)", "by cases" for a load of a truck without bays, whose case capacity cell then reads "by pallets" on a bay load) and the TOTAL in pallets; the load sheet's header shows **Cases · pallets / bays** ("1,045 · 11.1 / 12 (limit 12.0 at 100% fill)") instead of "Cases / capacity" - one row, so the block stays on rows 4-9 and the driver break keeps row 10 (pallets review: a seventh header row landed on row 10 and cut the break's text off) - its LOADING MANIFEST adds **Cases per pallet**, **Full pallets**, **Loose cases** and **Pallets** per product (each Pallets cell holds the exact pallets, `palletsExact`, shown to 0.1 by its format, so the column adds up to its TOTAL; before, cells rounded one by one could add up to 0.1-0.2 pallets less), the TOTAL in pallets and the line "1,045 cases = 11.1 pallets (8 full pallets + 293 loose cases on mixed pallets)", plus any `palletNotes`; SKU LOADING SUMMARY adds **Pallets (plan)** and **Bays** rows; SUMMARY adds **Pallets planned** and **Average bay fill %**; ASSUMPTIONS has **Truck capacity**, worded by the solver's echo (`solverRules().pallets`): "trucks with bays: pallets up to bays x 100% (Pallet fill) and the payload ...; a payload of 0 is no weight limit ..." or "cases and payload (no truck of this plan was planned by pallets); a payload of 0 is no weight limit". The driver sheet's header reads "9 stops · 1,045 cases · 11.1 / 12 pallets" and its load check "= 1,045 cases (11.1 pallets)" (`DriverSheet.pallets`); the WhatsApp header "Depart 07:10 · 9 stops · 1,045 cases · 11.1 pallets". The stops, the driver page, orders, invoices and the reconciliation stay in cases.

**Salesman link (19 Oct 2026).** The same routes live, for the salesmen's WhatsApp group: [3.23](#323-the-salesman-link). Its *Delayed* is judged against each delivery's printed window (`etaSlot`), so the page and the printout agree.

### 3.11 Step 9: late orders and plan versions

**Recording a late order.** There are two ways:

- upload a small file in Step 1 (confirm then asks for the late reason); or
- use "Late order" on the plan (`late-order-dialog.tsx`; the reason field reads "Reason for adding this order late (after the cutoff, or to a day already planned)" since PR6). It calls `POST /api/dispatch/late-order` (`apps/web/app/api/dispatch/late-order/route.ts`) with customer code, optional branch and name, priority, reason (at least 3 characters) and lines (product code, cases, sales order). In one transaction the route:
  - takes `lockIntake` (the same per-tenant lock as confirm, batch delete and the optimize start). The transaction has a 30 s timeout (maxWait 10 s); waiting longer for the lock (e.g. behind a large confirm) answers 409 `INTAKE_BUSY` ("try again in a moment"), not 500;
  - finds the customer by code and branch whatever the letter case (`customerTwinsOf` on the company's customers, in the program: `C_1` is never `CX1`, `%` never "any customer"; twins resolve like the file intake), or creates a stub (location required). An inactive customer is refused with 409 `CUSTOMER_INACTIVE` naming it ("Reactivate it in Customers or use another code");
  - finds or creates each product, matching the tidy item code (`productKey`: letter case and spacing, `TN1.5L  (6)` is `TN1.5L (6)`; the company's products are read once and matched in the program, so `A_B` is never `AxB`); an inactive product is refused with 409 `PRODUCT_INACTIVE`. A new product starts at 0 kg per case (unknown) and is listed in the answer's `productsWithoutWeight`, with `weightLimited` (an active truck of the depot has a payload, so the re-plan asks; false = payload 0 everywhere, the screen's warning then says its kg counts as 0 on the plan and the sheets); a new code the Products page could not hold (comma, quote, control character, over 40 characters, a leading `+` or `-`) is refused with 400 `PRODUCT_CODE_INVALID` and nothing is saved, while a product already in the master is found whatever its code looks like. A line's item code is the tidy code (`normalizeProductCode`), so the same product twice on one sales order is refused whatever its case or spacing;
  - refuses (409 `DUPLICATE_LINES`) a line whose sales order + product is already confirmed for that customer and date (`IntakeLineKey`, looked up over every case-variant twin id of the customer and of the product, since which twin is preferred can change; the file intake compares by code the same way), and (400) the same product twice on one sales order. The 409 says to record extra cases of a confirmed line without a sales-order number or under a new one;
  - creates one `Order` with its lines: `status VALIDATED`, `isLate` = after the cutoff or a plan is already applied, `lateReason`, `lateRecordedById`. `lateReason` and `lateRecordedById` are stored even when `isLate` is false. Line kg = cases × the product's case weight (0 = unknown), `weightFromMaster = true` (it follows later corrections of the case weight). One `IntakeLineKey` per line with a sales order.

  `date` must be a real calendar date (`isoDateSchema`). After the transaction commits, it writes audit `LATE_ORDER_RECORDED` through `audit()` and answers with `replanNeeded`, `locationRequired` and `productsWithoutWeight`. Nothing is planned yet. The dialog then offers "Re-plan now?", or asks for the location first; it warns about products without weight.

**Re-plan.** `POST /api/runs/:id/replan { reason, note?, allowMissingLocations?, allowMissingWeights?, expect?, searchMode?, keptSeen? }` (`apps/web/app/api/runs/[id]/replan/route.ts`) runs `replan` in `start-optimize.ts`. Since PR3 (review F03) **every known reason to refuse is checked before a new version exists**, and the new version starts as a usable copy of the previous plan (copy-forward):

1. a plan of another day than the screen's `expect` answers 409 `DAY_MISMATCH`; a superseded plan (status or `supersededAt`) 409; a legacy plan 409 `LEGACY_PLAN`;
2. a plan not applied yet is simply optimized again in the same version (`startDispatchOptimize`);
3. a plan that is optimizing or has a job running answers 409;
4. otherwise it probes `buildDispatchRequest(parent)` and answers 409 `LOCATION_REQUIRED` or `WEIGHT_REQUIRED` (same `gate` as optimize, with `allowMissingLocations` / `allowMissingWeights`), **409 `NOTHING_TO_PLAN`** when every order of the day is already on a locked, loading or dispatched load ("To change a load, unlock it first"), and 400 when the depot has no active truck - all before any version is created. The probe plans weights from the product master in memory only and saves nothing: a refused re-plan leaves the parent (still the live plan) with its order, load and portion kg unchanged. The weights are saved by the child's job when it applies its plan (step 7), never when it fails;
5. `REOPTIMIZE` becomes `LATE_ORDER` when `pendingLateOrderIds(parent)` is not empty (late orders of the day that the applied scope does not contain); then (24 Oct 2026) the parent's kept-load report is read (`keptChangesOrNull`): never a refusal, a read error leaves it out;
6. the solve admission is reserved (429 / 503 leaves no version behind), then `createNextVersion` runs one transaction under the day lock and then `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the parent, and refuses a superseded or OPTIMIZING parent (or one with a job running). It:
   - creates a `RunPlan` with `version + 1`, `parentRunId`, `reason` and `reasonNote`;
   - copies **every** `PlanLoad` of the parent - PLANNED ones too - (new id, `carriedFromLoadId` = old id, same status, driver and times, and since PR4 the same `truckSnapshotJson`; since audit E1 that snapshot holds the load's `origin`, the depot pin it was planned from, so a locked or dispatched load keeps it through every re-plan and is never redrawn from a depot pin moved since - owner decision 13, not the customer-pin rule of A5 where the driver gets the new pin. A load planned before origins were kept gets, on this copy, the depot its version was optimized from: an earlier copy's origin, else its root load's option `inputs.depot`, `plannedOriginOf`; a load with no snapshot keeps today's behaviour) with its `RouteAssignment` rows (with their `stopSnapshotJson`; rows planned before snapshots existed copy as SQL NULL through `copyRowData`). Only a copy that is frozen (carried **and** not PLANNED, `isCarriedFrozen`) counts as "kept from the previous version": the "kept" badge on the plan screen, "KEPT FROM PREVIOUS VERSION" on the driver sheets, "(kept from previous version)" in the workbook and the change summary's "locked/dispatched loads preserved" (review of PR3: the PLANNED copies were labelled kept and counted too);
   - copies the parent's **chosen** option (`ScenarioResult`) with its `UnservedOrder` rows (not the alternatives: they were computed around the parent's loads); the copy's `scope.frozenLoadIds` name the copied loads. It also copies `summaryJson`, `reconciliationJson`, `totalOrders` and `unservedCount`, and sets the child's `chosenScenarioId` to the copy. The child's status follows its loads: READY, or DISPATCHED when every load is out. Null Json columns are copied as SQL NULL by `copyRowData` (`lib/dispatch/prisma-copy.ts`), which finds a model's Json columns from the Prisma schema;
   - computes the child's own timetable check (`refreshFeasibility`, PR4);
   - marks the parent `SUPERSEDED` with `supersededAt`;
   - writes audit `PLAN_VERSION_CREATED` (`frozenLoadsCarried`, `loadsCopied`, `planCopied`; since 24 Oct 2026 `keptChanged`: the kept loads planned with older customer data, codes only, at most 50 stops, `keptTruncated` beyond - `createNextVersion`'s optional `extra`, which the hire path does not pass);
7. `startDispatchOptimize(child, { freshVersion, ticket, now })`. In `buildDispatchRequest(child)`, PLANNED loads are ignored as before, the copied frozen loads keep their orders and cases, each truck's `frozen_trips` are fixed, and `previous_truck_id` is sent only when `usesPlanContinuity` is true. On the delivery day itself the request starts from now + preparation (see "Same-day re-plans" below). The background job then runs exactly as in [3.6](#36-step-4-optimize), on the child: on success `persistDispatchResult` deletes the copied option and `applyScenario` replaces the copied PLANNED loads, and `refreshPlanFacts` writes the change summary against the parent.

**Kept loads planned with older customer data (24 Oct 2026).** A re-plan never changes a LOCKED or LOADING load, so a customer whose hours, pin or orders changed after its load was locked stays planned the old way. Both RE-PLAN buttons (Step 3 and the plan screen; the late-order "Re-plan now?" and the red timing box too) read `GET /api/runs/:id/kept-changes` right before the Quick / Thorough dialog (a READY plan does not poll). The dialog lists up to 6 changed stops ("and N more on the plan screen") with one **Unlock ... first** choice per changed load - its own unlock chain only (owner decision: no offer to join loads; a load that only goes back because a truck's later loads go first is named "no change", review W5) - **unticked by default**, as NMWC loads trucks the night before. Ticked loads go back to Planned first, latest first, one at a time ([3.8](#38-step-6-load-states)); any refusal stops there (no re-plan). After an unlock the re-plan is sent as `MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT` (plan continuity: the unlocked stops prefer the truck they were on) with the note "Unlocked for changed customer data: T05 L2" - unless the late-order re-plan was asked (it has continuity too; review W6). Never `REOPTIMIZE` (review W-1): step 5 above turns it into `LATE_ORDER` only for a late or brought-forward order, so with only on-time orders waiting it stayed a full re-optimize and the unlocked stops could move to other trucks; any other reason is kept as sent, and waiting late orders are planned all the same (`keptReplanBody`). `keptSeen` carries the fingerprint of the list shown, without the loads just unlocked (`keptSeenAfter`, review S1: the re-plan reads the list again after the unlock, where they are gone, so the dialog's own fingerprint always read as changed); the 202 answer adds `kept { loads, breaks, labels, lines, more, fingerprint, unseen }` (`unseen`: the list changed since the dialog), and the toast says what stays kept with older data. When the unlock went through but the re-plan was refused (429, 409 `OPTIMIZING`, 503 ...), the toast says both: "T05 L2 is back to Planned; re-plan not started: <reason>" (review W7). Not done in this version (open): the old yellow "changed after planning" sentence for locked or dispatched loads still shows next to the box on the plan screen; a load whose only change is a new order of the customer (another visit, grey) stays listed with its Unlock while it is locked (owner decision pending); a per-load badge and a banner in the load's detail, a confirmation at Loading and Dispatch of a load with a breaking change, the unloading-time comparison, a warning in the customer edit's answer, and the exact what-if with the manual move's re-time.

**Same-day re-plans start from now (PR8, scenario finding S04 / N2).** Before PR8 RouteIQ had no notion of the current time: a late order re-planned at 09:00 for today was put on new loads leaving at 06:00 (5 of 10 new loads in the scenario run left before 09:00, and 5 of 6 late clinics were "delivered" before their orders existed). Now, when an OPTIMIZE or a re-plan is built on its own delivery day (company timezone), no new load leaves the depot before **now + the turnaround between loads** (`reloadMinutes`, 30 min for NMWC): `buildDispatchRequest` sends that as `shift_start_min` ([3.6](#36-step-4-optimize)), and the time the plan is made as `loading_from_min` (PR8 review, below). Every job counts both from when its search really starts, after any wait for a solver slot (ISSUE 6: a Quick queued at 09:05 that started at 09:20 let a load leave at 09:05); a THOROUGH plan from the end of its search instead: its start + the cap ([2.7](#27-background-job-model)). The optimizer then:
- lets every truck's first new load leave at the later of that time, the depot opening and the truck's own availability ([4.6](#46-truck-days-and-prefilters));
- counts the loading per case from now on every truck (PR8 review): a new load leaves no earlier than now + turnaround + `loadingMinPerCase` x its cases, on a truck standing at the depot exactly as on one coming back;
- locked, loading and dispatched loads keep their times; a truck that is still out (for example back at 09:57) leaves again only after its return + turnaround + loading minutes per case of the next load, as before;
- the early-arrival preference for P1 / P2 is measured from that time instead of 06:00, and so is the early part of the options table's **Preference cost** (PR7, `preference_penalties.early`). *What it gains* shows two things: the P1/P2 minutes-earlier figure, which compares service starts between options and so does not depend on the start, and the preference-cost difference, whose early part counts from the same-day start like the column;
- a customer whose hard window closes before any truck can get there is unserved `HARD_WINDOW_INFEASIBLE` with its earliest possible arrival;
- when now + preparation is at or after the depot's closing time, the warning says no new load can leave today, and every open order is unserved `SHIFT_LIMIT` for that reason ("Planned on the delivery day from 18:15: the depot closes at 18:00, so no new load can leave today.", PR8 rebase review, [4.6](#46-truck-days-and-prefilters)), not as if the trucks were taken up by locked or dispatched loads.

The plan says so: a plan warning ("Planned from 09:30 (now 09:00 + 30 min preparation): the plan is for today, so no new load leaves the depot before 09:30. ..."; the first of the optimizer's warnings, but notes about outdated weights, changed master data or drivers, and the timing warnings, are shown above it), the ASSUMPTIONS row "Planned from (plan made on the delivery day)" (from `PlanSettings.planFrom`, kept with the option), and `planFromMin` in the `OPTIMIZE_STARTED` audit row. The new loads are timed with 09:30 as their first departure (`rulesFrom`, the truck snapshot), so the dispatch gate checks them against it; a carried load keeps the rules it was planned with. "Now" is taken when the optimization is started (the request is built then), not when a queued job reaches the solver. Loads that already left but are still PLANNED in RouteIQ are planned again from now: dispatch them before re-planning. A plan for a future day is unchanged; a plan for a past day is built as before.

**Loading starts now too (PR8 review, scenario review finding "same-day preparation leaves out the loading minutes per case").** With only `shift_start_min` = now + turnaround, the optimizer added the loading minutes per case only after a frozen return (`frozen_return_s`): a truck idle all morning, or one back before now, left at 09:30 with a 700-case load whose 35 min of loading were never counted, while a truck back at 09:00 left at 10:05 with the same load. Now `buildDispatchRequest` also sends `loading_from_min` (the time the plan is made, `planDayNowMin`) whenever the plan is built on its delivery day, and the solver treats it like a frozen return for the loading gap, without using a trip, moving the shift anchor or changing driver pay: `TruckDay.ready_s` = the later of the last frozen return and that time, used by the route search's start bound, the repack's departure range (`load_repack._first_departure_s`), the exact timing and `timing_ok` ([4.6](#46-truck-days-and-prefilters)). The solver's own check (`feasibility.py`) and the web's dispatch gate (`feasibility.ts`, `PlanRules.loadingFromMin` from the truck snapshot) check the same rule (`TURNAROUND`, "... the plan was made at 09:00 on its delivery day, so loading starts then: the truck needs 65 min to reload and load 700 cases: ready 10:05"); where it is later than the previous return or the first departure, only it is reported. The same rule holds on a plan made on the delivery day before its first departure (05:15 for 06:00: no "Planned from", but a full truck may leave after 06:00); the plan then warns "Planned on the delivery day at 05:15: loading starts now, ..." when a full truck of the depot would be later than the first departure, and ASSUMPTIONS has a "Loading from (plan made on the delivery day)" row. The "Planned from" warning and ASSUMPTIONS row name the loading per case ("... Loading starts now too, so each new load also waits for its own loading time, 0.04 min per case: a full 800-case truck leaves at 10:02 at the earliest."). A solver without the field ignores it (Pydantic drops unknown fields): its plans are then refused by the web gate where they break the rule, so deploy the solver first.

**A failed re-plan keeps the previous plan.** If the child's optimization fails (solver error or timeout, the solver finding no plan, a deploy killing the solve and the janitor reaping it), the child is FAILED but still holds the previous plan intact: its loads can be locked, loaded and dispatched (its reconciliation is the parent's), and the screen shows "Optimization failed - previous plan kept". Weights entered under Products since are not saved (the copied loads keep matching their orders, and the "planned with the old weight" warning stays). A load change turns it READY. Re-plan again to retry: that creates the next version; the FAILED version itself is never optimized again in place (409 `NEW_VERSION_REQUIRED`). If the start itself is refused after the version was created (for example `LOADS_CHANGED` or `PLAN_BUSY`), the answer carries `previousPlanKept: true` and the new version stays READY with the copy.

**Bring forward: orders not delivered on earlier days (PR9).** Before PR9 an order that was not delivered stayed on its own delivery date: the next day's plan never saw it. Now Step 1 of the day screen for day D and a depot shows "Not delivered on earlier days: N orders (M cases)" (`carry-over-panel.tsx`) with a list and "Bring forward to <D>" (PLANNER, like confirming a file and a late order); when D is later than today, today's own leftovers follow in a group of their own, "Today (27 Sep) - ...", whose heading says which rows are ticked ("driver-confirmed not delivered (ticked)": the driver's result is settled and the truck is back) and which are not ("may still leave today (not ticked)"; owner decision; `carryTodaySplit`, `carryTodayTitle`, `carryTodayHint`).

- **What is listed** (`GET /api/dispatch/carry-over?date&depotId` → `carryOverPreview` → `carryCandidates` in `lib/dispatch/carry-over.ts`, pure): the orders of the tenant and depot (like `ordersInScopeWhere`; every order has a depot since audit PR A5) with a delivery date in [D-7, D-1] - **never after the company's today** (`carryWindow`, in the tenant timezone; the PR9 review had capped it at yesterday, the owner's decision on today's orders moved the cap to today) - not carried already and not `DISPATCHED` / `DELIVERED`, whose cases were not delivered. Per order line: its cases minus the cases on loads of its day's **live plan** (`currentPlan`) that left the depot (`DISPATCHED` or `COMPLETED`; a split part by its `portionLinesJson`). So an order unserved in that plan (`UnservedOrder` of the option in use), on a load that never left (`PLANNED`, `LOCKED` or `LOADING`), or of a day with no plan (or never optimized, or added after the plan was made) is listed with only its open cases, each with why (`UNSERVED` with the reason, `NOT_LEFT` with the loads, `NEVER_PLANNED`). Orders on loads that left are delivered and never listed. **Today's orders** (owner decision after the PR9 reviews: NMWC loads tomorrow's trucks tonight after 20:00, and the dispatcher plans tomorrow in the evening, today's leftovers included): when D is later than today (tomorrow, the day screen's default), today's orders qualify exactly like an earlier day's - on a load of today that has not left (`PLANNED`, `LOCKED`, `LOADING`: "has not left the depot yet"), unserved in today's live plan, or not planned yet; never on a `DISPATCHED` or `COMPLETED` load - and are marked `ofToday`. The panel lists them after the earlier days in a group of their own, **"Today (27 Sep) - may still leave today (not ticked)"** (with settled rows: "- 1 driver-confirmed not delivered (ticked), 2 may still leave today (not ticked)"), with the warning "Today's loads that have not left yet may still go out today; tick only orders you know will not be delivered today." for the rows that may still leave (`carryTodaySplit`, `carryTodayTitle`, `carryTodayHint`, `CARRY_TODAY_WARNING`; the hint also shows with the list closed), **unticked by default** except a row whose open cases the driver recorded as not delivered with the truck back (`confirmed`); the earlier days stay ticked. The preview counts them apart (`todayOrders` / `todayCases`; `orders` / `cases` are the earlier days'). An order is never brought forward to its own day (D is always later than the order's date: for D = today the window ends yesterday), and orders of a day not due yet are never listed (before the PR9 review, D = 30 Sep listed 28 and 29 Sep as "never planned", ticked). `bringForward` reads the same window in its transaction.
- **Listed but not carried** (`blocked`, with the reason on screen): a deactivated customer (`CUSTOMER_INACTIVE`); a sales-order line already confirmed for D (`ALREADY_ON_DAY`: the file intake's duplicate identity `lineDupKey`, so a line entered again for D is never added twice); a sales-order line that is also on an order of a **later delivery date** (`SAME_LINE_LATER`, PR9 second review): the same identity without the date (sales order, customer and branch, product) on any order after the candidate's own date, in **any depot and any state** - open, brought forward, dispatched or delivered - read from the intake keys of those sales orders and the lines of the same customers' later orders (`laterLinesOf`), in the preview and inside `bringForward` alike. Only the newest open order with the line is carried ("Sales order SO-9 (W500) is also open on 26 Sep: only that order is brought forward."); none when the newer one was brought forward, dispatched or delivered, or is on today or a day still to come ("... was entered again for 26 Sep (brought forward to 27 Sep): not brought forward, so it is not delivered twice."). Before the second review only open orders of the window and the lines on D counted, so once the newer order was carried to 27 Sep (or dispatched), opening 28 Sep offered the older one again, ticked, and the line was delivered and invoiced twice. A day whose plan is `OPTIMIZING` (`DAY_OPTIMIZING`).
- **The selection** (`carry-over-panel.tsx`): every order of an earlier day that can be carried is ticked, and of today only those the driver's result settled (`carryTickedByDefault`). The panel keeps what the dispatcher ticked or unticked by hand (`CarryChoices`; `carrySelected` / `toggleCarry` in `carry-view.ts`, PR9 second review, extended for today's orders), not the ticked set, so reading the list again - after a 409, a partial bring forward, an OPTIMIZE or RE-PLAN of the day, a new file, **Look again** - never ticks an unticked order again, never ticks an order of today by itself, and keeps one the dispatcher ticked; an order new to the list gets its default. Another day or depot starts afresh. The button shows the count whenever the selection is not "every earlier order" (with how many of today; `carryButtonSuffix`), each row's reason is labelled by `carryWhyLabel` ("Load not left yet" / "Not planned" for today's orders, never "Load never left" / "Never planned", which would contradict "may still leave today"), the question before it names today's orders (`carryConfirmText`, given the listed orders - their `ofToday` is required by its type, so the POST body, which says `today`, cannot be passed by mistake): they are closed on today (today's plan stays as it is, for the record) and a load of today still holding one cannot be locked, loaded or dispatched today - never "they come off today's plan", which the plan rows contradict. The warning above today's group shows also with the list closed. The toast afterwards says how many were today's and to re-plan today or unlock their loads (a loading one goes Back to locked first; `carryDoneText`). The button is off while D's plan is being optimized (or queued).
- **Bring forward** (`POST /api/dispatch/carry-over { date, depotId, selected: [{ orderId, cases, today? }] }` → `bringForward`; `cases` is what the list showed, the expected state; `today: true` marks an order ticked in the Today group). **An order of today is carried only when it is sent with `today: true`**: sent without it - as "select every order", or a screen opened before this change, would - it answers 409 `TODAY_NOT_SELECTED` and nothing is carried (`checkSelection` → `todayNotSelected`), so it is never implied by selecting the earlier days. **D must be the company's today or later** (PR9 second review): a D before today answers 409 `DAY_OVER` ("24 Sep is over (today is 27 Sep): orders can only be brought forward to today or a later day. ...") and the preview of such a day lists nothing (`dayOver`), so the box is not shown when looking back at an earlier day; before, opening 24 Sep on 27 Sep offered every order of 17-23 Sep, ticked, and one click put them on a day whose loads had left. One transaction (60 s): `lockIntake` (confirm, late order and batch delete take it too), then the day lock (`lockPlanDay`, in date order) of every day it reads - today's too when its orders are listed: its loads are still moving, so a load of today dispatched meanwhile is seen, and one locked, loaded or dispatched after the carry is refused (`ORDERS_CARRIED`) - `createNextVersion` and `createInitialPlan` take it, so no new version of those days appears meanwhile - then `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on their live plans (in id order), checked to still be the live plans (409 `PLAN_BUSY` otherwise: nothing is read from a version that is not locked, so a load of it cannot be dispatched unseen; PR9 review), then everything is read again from exactly those plans. The lock order is intake → day → plan row. `checkSelection`: an order already carried is skipped (`ALREADY_CARRIED`, not an error), so running it twice, or twice at the same time, carries nothing new; an order no longer a candidate, blocked now, or with other open cases than shown answers **409 `CARRY_OVER_CHANGED`** (with `changed`) and nothing is carried. For each order it creates the copy on D (`carryCopyData`): same customer (so branch), depot D's, priority and `priorityFromFile` (**no automatic bump**), notes, and one line per open line with the same product, sales order, `weightFromMaster` and weight per case (kg, value and margin shared out by cases), `status VALIDATED`, no upload batch (deleting the original's file can never delete the copy), `carriedFromOrderId` = the original and `carriedFromDate` = the date first due (the first order's date when carried again). Late like a late order: `isLate` = after the cutoff of D or D already has a plan in use; `lateReason` "Brought forward from 26 Sep: not delivered on that day.". The copy's sales-order lines get their `IntakeLineKey` on D (the original keeps its own on its day): a file or late order for D with the same line is a duplicate, the copy is never a duplicate of its original. The original gets `carriedToOrderId`, `carriedAt` and `carriedById`. One audit row `ORDERS_CARRIED_OVER` (entity Order) lists every carry. Unique indexes on `carriedFromOrderId` and `carriedToOrderId` back the lock: an order has at most one copy. A timeout waiting for the intake lock answers 409 `INTAKE_BUSY`, for a plan row 409 `PLAN_BUSY`.
- **On the original's day** the original is no longer open, unserved or pending: `ordersInScopeWhere` leaves out an order with `carriedToOrderId`, so the day overview, the plan's pending orders, `pendingLateOrderIds`, the next re-plan of that day and the customer and product deactivation warnings (`open-orders.ts`) no longer count it, and the dashboard subtracts it from that day's orders and unserved, and its carried cases (the copy's) from that day's cases, so cost per case counts every case once (`CARRIED_OUT_OF_PLAN` in `lib/dashboard.ts`; the cases since the PR9 review). The Orders list (`GET /api/orders` and the upload page's Orders tab, `lib/orders-list.ts`) marks the original "Carried over to 28 Sep" and the copy "Carried over from 27 Sep"; a filter on an open status (UPLOADED, VALIDATED, ASSIGNED, UNSERVED) never returns a carried original (`status=CARRIED` lists them), and the tab's totals count its cases once (PR9 review). **Its plan versions stay exactly as they were** (no row is changed; the stored reconciliation still balances): the plan screen shows such an order as "Carried over to 28 Sep" (on its stop, in the unserved list instead of the reason, and a line under the reconciliation bar: history, not a problem), the Excel SUMMARY has a **CARRIED OVER** part. A stop is marked only on a load that never left (`carriedLoadShows`): the part of a split order on a dispatched or completed load was delivered, so that load, its driver sheet and its Excel load sheet show no mark and it counts no carried order (PR9 review; the unserved rest still says "Carried over to"). A load of that day that still holds such an order cannot be locked, loaded or dispatched ([3.8](#38-step-6-load-states), 409 `ORDERS_CARRIED`; for a load of today the words say "re-plan today" or "unlock it"); a load holding only such orders stays for the record (the plan screen's Re-plan is off when nothing else is open: `replanWork`): a PLANNED one needs nothing, a LOCKED or LOADING one was loaded, so its cases are unloaded before the later day's loads are picked and it is put back to Planned (`carriedLoadRemedy`, PR9 second review), and an optimize start whose open orders were carried meanwhile answers 409 `ORDERS_CHANGED`. Frozen loads of that day keep their carried orders in scope (history). A re-plan made after the carry reconciles such an order against the parts it still holds on those frozen loads (`carriedHeldCases` in `refreshPlanFacts`; the rest is the copy's, on its new day), so a split order with a dispatched part and a carried rest reconciles and the day's other loads can still be locked and dispatched (PR9 review: before, that version stayed "uploaded 100 != planned 60 + unserved 0" and every lock was refused 409 `NOT_RECONCILED`). The plan's summary still counts the order with all its cases (its carried rest as not delivered on that day), and the dashboard subtracts the carried cases. The batch delete refuses a file whose orders were carried (409 `BATCH_CARRIED`).
- **On day D** the copies are ordinary orders: with no plan yet, OPTIMIZE plans them with the others. While D's plan is being optimized (`OPTIMIZING`, also queued), that optimization was started without them: `bringForward` answers `replanNeeded` and `optimizing`, and the toast says RE-PLAN adds them once it finishes (PR9 second review: it said OPTIMIZE plans them); the day screen keeps the button off meanwhile. With a plan in use they are pending like late orders (`pending.carried`; `pendingLateOrderIds` counts them, so RE-PLAN runs with reason `LATE_ORDER` and plan continuity): the new version keeps the locked, loading and dispatched loads exactly as they are and plans the copies on the rest, or leaves them `LATE_ORDER_NO_CAPACITY`. They are marked everywhere a dispatcher or driver looks: the day screen's list of orders brought forward, "Carried over from 26 Sep" on the plan's stops and unserved rows, "CARRIED OVER from 26 Sep (not delivered that day)" on the driver sheet (PDF) and in the Notes of the Excel truck-load sheet, and the **CARRIED OVER** part of SUMMARY ("Brought forward from earlier days: N orders · M cases", per first-due day with the customers and loads).
- **Not in PR9** (possible owner settings later, [7.5](#75-open-questions-for-the-owner)): raising the priority of a carried order (it keeps its own), a window other than 7 days, and bringing orders forward by themselves (it is always the dispatcher's click).

**Which button sends which reason:**

- "Re-plan" on `PlanView` always sends `REOPTIMIZE`; it becomes `LATE_ORDER` when late orders are waiting.
- The late-order dialog's follow-up sends `LATE_ORDER`.
- The Step 3 RE-PLAN sends `LATE_ORDER` when pending late orders exist, else `REOPTIMIZE`.
- The API also accepts `MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT`; since 24 Oct 2026 the re-plan after an **Unlock** of the kept-load warning sends it, with the note "Unlocked for changed customer data: T05 L2" (`keptReplanBody`, above). (24 Oct 2026) **Save** of a move by hand ([3.7](#37-step-5-reviewing-the-plan)) makes a `MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT` version itself, through `createNextVersionTx`, without an optimization: the note is "By hand: Move C7 from T08 L2, stop 1 to ..."; only the edited trucks' PLANNED loads are made again, timed with today's data. The save checks again, at most 10 minutes after its check and with the day read as it was then, and refuses with 409 `PREVIEW_CHANGED` (and the new preview) when the result differs; under the intake, day and plan locks it reads the touched trucks again and refuses with 409 `DAY_CHANGED` when anything of them changed (a load locked, an order in, another option chosen) - a change on another truck never blocks it (the stale check covers the touched trucks only). The versions list tells the two `MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT` versions apart by their note ("Unlocked for changed customer data: ..." or "By hand: ..."); only a move by hand marks the option in use (`details.manual`), so only it adds "adjusted by hand" to the plan's header badge, never the version's reason (`PlanDetail.manual`).

Older versions stay readable at `/t/[slug]/dispatch/plan/[id]`. A version is superseded when its status is SUPERSEDED **or** `supersededAt` is set (`isSupersededRun` in `lib/dispatch/plan-status.ts`, PR3: before a race could write READY over a superseded version). On a superseded version every editing control is hidden, its driver sheets, workbook and WhatsApp messages say "do not use", the versions list shows it as SUPERSEDED, `currentPlan` never returns it, and the server refuses changes anyway (`lockOpenRun`, `applyScenario`, `startDispatchOptimize`, `replan`, choose-scenario, the legacy whole-run dispatch).

**When Re-plan is offered.** The plan screen's Re-plan is disabled while any action runs, while optimizing, and when there is nothing to plan: no PLANNED load, nothing unserved and no new order waiting (`PlanDetail.pendingOrders`, `nothingToReplan`). The day screen's OPTIMIZE / RE-PLAN is off with "Every order of this day is already on a locked, loading or dispatched load" when the day overview's `openOrders` is 0 (followed by "unlock it first" only when a LOCKED or LOADING load exists, from `plan.loadsByStatus`), and on again after a failed optimization. The day screen and the plan screen share one busy state (`onBusyChange` / `externalBusy` on `PlanView`, PR3 review): while "Lock all loads", a load change, Use instead or the plan's Re-plan runs, Step 3's OPTIMIZE / RE-PLAN is disabled, and while Step 3's request runs, the plan's actions are disabled, so one dispatcher cannot re-plan in the middle of their own "Lock all". Each side stays busy until the day screen shows the result of its action, not only until its request answers: the plan's actions run through `runPlanAction` (`plan-actions.ts`) and await the day's reload (`onChanged` returns it), and OPTIMIZE / RE-PLAN keeps its flag until its own reload; both give the busy state back in a `finally`, so an error never leaves the buttons disabled. After a late order is saved (`afterLateOrderSaved`), "Re-plan now?" re-plans without reloading the day first (the re-plan reloads it when it ends, also after a refusal or a declined location / weight question); "no", or a new customer without a location, reloads the day. Second review of PR3: the day was reloaded before the re-plan, which replaced the plan screen before the re-plan took the busy state, so Step 3's RE-PLAN stayed clickable while that re-plan ran (a second click: 409 `SUPERSEDED`).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor D as Dispatcher
    participant UI as plan-view.tsx
    participant LO as POST /api/dispatch/late-order
    participant RP as POST /api/runs/ID/replan
    participant SO as start-optimize.replan
    participant PS as plan-service.ts
    participant DB as Postgres via Prisma
    D->>UI: Late order dialog - customer, lines, priority, reason
    UI->>LO: record the order
    LO->>DB: one transaction - find or create Customer and Products, create Order VALIDATED with isLate
    LO->>DB: after commit - AuditLog LATE_ORDER_RECORDED
    D->>UI: Re-plan now
    UI->>RP: reason LATE_ORDER, expect date and depot
    RP->>SO: replan
    SO->>PS: day of the screen? superseded? legacy? (409 DAY_MISMATCH, SUPERSEDED, LEGACY_PLAN)
    alt parent has no applied scenario
        SO->>SO: startDispatchOptimize on the same version
    else parent is applied
        SO->>DB: optimizing or a job running? (409)
        SO->>PS: buildDispatchRequest on the parent as a probe (weights in memory only)
        Note over SO,PS: refused before any version exists - 409 LOCATION_REQUIRED or WEIGHT_REQUIRED, 409 NOTHING_TO_PLAN, 400 no active truck
        SO->>PS: pendingLateOrderIds - a REOPTIMIZE with late orders waiting becomes LATE_ORDER
        SO->>SO: reserve the solve admission (429 or 503 leaves no version)
        SO->>PS: createNextVersion
        PS->>DB: day lock, then parent FOR UPDATE (refused if superseded, optimizing or a job runs)
        PS->>DB: create child N+1 with parentRunId and reason, copy EVERY PlanLoad with its RouteAssignments (carriedFromLoadId)
        PS->>DB: copy the chosen ScenarioResult with its UnservedOrders, summary and reconciliation - child READY, or DISPATCHED when every load is out
        PS->>DB: parent SUPERSEDED with supersededAt, AuditLog PLAN_VERSION_CREATED
        SO->>SO: startDispatchOptimize on the child (freshVersion, with the reserved ticket)
        Note over SO,PS: the child request keeps frozen trips and sends previous_truck_id only when usesPlanContinuity
    end
    SO-->>UI: 202 with the child runId, version and effective reason
    Note over UI,DB: the job then runs as in the optimize diagram, on the child - on success it saves the weights and replaces the copied PLANNED loads and option, on failure the child stays FAILED holding the copied plan
```

**Cancel or postpone one order (owner request of the first live night, 12 Oct 2026).** Step 2's order list (`delivery-times.tsx`, now "Orders and delivery times") offers **Postpone...** and **Cancel...** on each order, PLANNER and above (`order-actions.tsx`; `POST /api/dispatch/orders/:id/cancel`, `/uncancel`, `/postpone`; service `lib/dispatch/order-cancel.ts`, rules and words `lib/dispatch/order-cancel-rules.ts`). The unit is one RouteIQ order: every invoice of one customer for one delivery date in one file; the dialog lists the invoices (`OrderLine.salesOrderNo`, "no invoice no." for lines without one) and the cases, and says when the order holds several invoices that they go together (one invoice of several is a later step).
- **Which orders** (`orderActionRefusal`, judged on the LATEST plan version of the order's depot and day, `currentPlan`): on no plan, or only unserved: allowed; on a PLANNED load: allowed, and that load is refused Lock, Loading and Dispatch until the day is re-planned (409 `ORDERS_CANCELLED` from `cancelledOrdersGate` in `changeStatusCore`, "re-plan the day: the cancelled order is taken off"; a postponed order gives the existing `ORDERS_CARRIED`); on a LOCKED or LOADING load: refused, 409 `ORDER_ON_LOCKED_LOAD` naming the truck and load ("unlock the load first (a loading load goes Back to locked first), then cancel"), the same rule as a delivery time; on a DISPATCHED or COMPLETED load, or status DISPATCHED / DELIVERED: 409 `ORDER_LEFT` (the driver records the result); brought forward to a later day: 409 `ORDER_CARRIED`; the day's plan OPTIMIZING: 409 `PLAN_OPTIMIZING`. Another company's id answers 404.
- **Cancel** is soft: `Order.cancelledAt`, `cancelledById`, `cancelReason` (`CUSTOMER_CANCELLED`, `WRONG_OR_DUPLICATE`, `NO_ACCESS_SMALL_TRUCK`, `OTHER` with a required note, at most 200 characters), `cancelNote` (migration `20261013090000_order_cancel`); `OrderStatus` is unchanged (the status keeps the day's history). Cancelling a cancelled order changes nothing (`already`). A cancelled order is left out everywhere an order is planned, counted or offered: `ordersInScopeWhere` (`NOT_CANCELLED`: optimize and re-plan scope, pending and late orders, the day overview's counts, issues and data gaps, the plan's pending count, the delivery-time gate, the hire what-ifs), Bring forward candidates (never ticked by default), the data to collect, the open-order warnings, the orders list (`status=CANCELLED` lists them; totals leave them out) and the dashboard KPIs (subtracted like a carried order while a plan still holds it). It stays on its day in Step 1's **Cancelled orders** list (greyed, invoices, reason, who, when, "still on T05 L2: RE-PLAN", or "still shown on T02 L1, which holds nothing else: leave it as it is") with **Undo**. Also left out of the legacy "New run" order count (`app/api/runs/route.ts`) and the baseline's order matching; the intake's "already confirmed for another date" warning marks such a date "(cancelled)", and the late order's duplicate refusal adds the cancelled note. Cancelling an order of a day that is over is allowed (for the record) but cannot be undone: the dialog says so instead of promising Undo. A cancel, undo or postpone stops the day's waiting or running hire checks (`cancelHireChecksOfDay`, after the commit), and "Use this plan" of a finished suggestion whose P1-P3 orders are all gone since answers 409 `NOTHING_TO_HIRE` before renting anything (`hire-use.ts`, `hireNeed` on the day as it is now).
- **Undo cancel** (`undoCancelOrder`): while the order's day is not before the company's today (409 `DAY_OVER`); clears the four columns; the next OPTIMIZE / RE-PLAN plans it. Refused when one of its invoice lines was entered again for another day and is still open there (409 `SAME_LINE_ELSEWHERE`: it would be delivered twice), and while the day's plan is OPTIMIZING (409 `PLAN_OPTIMIZING`, as Cancel: the running job was built without the order and replaces the PLANNED loads, so "still on T02 L1 as planned" would be wrong a moment later).
- **Postpone to a day D** (`postponeOrder`): D after the order's day, at most 14 days after it (`POSTPONE_MAX_DAYS`), not before the company's today (409 `POSTPONE_DATE`); the order's own day must not be over (409 `ORDER_DAY_OVER`: Bring forward does that). Reasons as for cancel plus `POSTPONED_BY_SALES`. It is Bring forward's copy for one order, also of a future day: `carryCopyData` with all its lines, `copyIntakeKeys` on D, late reason "Postponed from 13 Oct: <reason>", the original marked `carriedToOrderId` (it leaves its day). Also refused for a deactivated customer (`CUSTOMER_INACTIVE`), an invoice line already confirmed for D (`ALREADY_ON_DAY`; on a cancelled order of D, whose key stays, `ALREADY_ON_DAY_CANCELLED` naming when and by whom and saying to undo that cancel instead) and an invoice line entered again for any later day than the order's own, open, planned, delivered or moved on (`SAME_LINE_LATER`, as Bring forward). The day screen offers no Postpone for an order of a day that is over (`postponeRange` is null then). Undo: Undo bring forward on D's screen while D is not planned with it (a copy cancelled on D answers 409 `COPY_CANCELLED`: undo the cancel first); refused (`PLAN_BUSY`) while D or the original's own day is being optimized.
- **Locks.** Each action is one transaction under the intake lock, then the day lock(s) (date order), then (postpone) the outcome-day lock of the order's day, then the latest plan version's row lock, with the plan version (its status and option in use), the order and its loads read again under them (another version live meanwhile: 409 `PLAN_BUSY`). An OPTIMIZE start (intake lock) either ran before - the plan is OPTIMIZING and the action is refused - or runs after and refuses a request built with an order cancelled since (409 `ORDERS_CHANGED`); a LOCK (plan row lock) either ran before - the load is locked and the action is refused - or runs after and is refused by the gate.
- **Re-plan.** RE-PLAN of a day whose PLANNED loads hold a cancelled or moved order is sent as REOPTIMIZE and becomes `MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT` (`ordersTakenOffPlannedLoads` in `start-optimize.ts`): plan continuity keeps the other orders on their trucks where it can. The hire suggestion's re-plan with the trucks it just rented keeps REOPTIMIZE (`keepReason`), as its what-if planned it. A day whose open orders were all cancelled answers 409 `NOTHING_TO_PLAN` saying so (`nothingLeftCancelled`). "Use instead" of an option made before the cancel answers 409 `ORDERS_CANCELLED`, and of one made before a postpone or bring forward 409 `ORDERS_CARRIED` (re-plan instead).
- **Marks.** The plan screen shows "CANCELLED - re-plan" on the load (its title is the 409's words) and on the stop, and CANCELLED on an unserved row; the driver sheet and the Excel load sheet say "CANCELLED - do not load or deliver" on the stop, or "1 of 2 orders CANCELLED (SO ...) - do not load or deliver it; the rest of this stop is delivered" when the stop holds another order of the customer (`DetailStop.cancelledOrderIds`, `stopCancelledText`); the warehouse sheet marks only the cancelled order's invoices and has a banner ("N cancelled order(s) on this load"); the WhatsApp text adds the line under the stop and the driver page says "CANCELLED - do not deliver" on that order (`ManifestOrder.cancelled`, English and Arabic). The day's Step 3 counts cancelled orders (`outdated.cancelledOnPlan`) and orders moved to a later day (`outdated.movedOnPlan`) still on planned loads of the plan in use as a reason to RE-PLAN, but only on loads that also hold an order still of the day and only while the day is not over: a load holding nothing else is no work for a re-plan (as `holdsOnlyGone`), so the screen never says RE-PLAN next to "nothing needs to be re-planned", and the cancel's answer says "leave it as it is" for it (`idleLoads`).
- **Re-upload.** The cancelled lines keep their intake keys: the same invoice re-sent for the same day stays skipped, and the message says "It was CANCELLED on 12 Oct by <name>, so it stays cancelled" and how to undo (`cancelledLineMap` in `intake-server.ts`, `cancelledLineNote`).
- Audited `ORDER_CANCELLED`, `ORDER_CANCEL_UNDONE` and `ORDER_POSTPONED` (before / after, invoices, cases, reason, note, the plan version and the planned loads holding it).

### 3.12 Settings that change the plan

Since stabilization PR5 (review F21) the Settings page shows **only the settings the daily dispatch planner uses**, each with its unit and allowed range, and a read-only **Effective planner values** panel that says what the next optimization uses and where each value comes from (a setting, a fixed planner rule, or an operations setting). The page is `apps/web/app/t/[slug]/settings/settings-form.tsx`; it saves through `PATCH /api/tenant/config` (`apps/web/app/api/tenant/config/route.ts`, TENANT_ADMIN). Changes apply to the next OPTIMIZE or re-plan; plans already made keep what they were made with (`ScenarioDetails.inputs`, PR4).

- **One mapping.** `dispatchConfigFromTenant` (`lib/dispatch/planner-config.ts`) turns the settings and the company country into the optimizer's config. `buildDispatchRequest` and the panel (`effectivePlannerValues`) both use it.
- **Bounds.** Every field is validated against `lib/planner-bounds.ts`, a copy of `packages/shared-types/src/planner-bounds.json`; each range lies inside the optimizer's Pydantic contract (`apps/solver/dispatch_models.py`). Tests check both sides against the JSON (`tests/lib/tenant-settings.spec.ts`, `apps/solver/tests/test_dispatch.py`). Overtime after must be at most the shift maximum, checked on the merged settings when a save changes the overtime threshold or the shift maximum (`overtimeSaveProblem`, the route and the form alike). A stored threshold after a lowered shift maximum is a planner warning and an amber note on the page; it no longer blocks saving the company name or another field (PR5 review).
- **Strict.** `tenantConfigSchema` is strict: the old controls that changed nothing (solver time limit, objective weights, cost and penalty defaults, "return to depot", "label estimated distances", the Mapbox provider) answer 400. Their columns stay in the database, marked `@deprecated` in `schema.prisma`; they are dropped in a later expand-then-contract release.
- **No silent overwrite.** The page sends only the fields it changed, with the values it showed (`expect`). The route locks the `TenantConfig` row and answers **409 `SETTINGS_CHANGED`** (naming the fields) when another admin or tab saved a different value meanwhile; nothing is saved. The audit row `UPDATE TenantConfig` lists only the changed fields, before and after.
- **Out-of-range stored values** (a direct database edit) refuse the optimize with **409 `SETTINGS_OUT_OF_RANGE`** naming the setting, instead of a solver 422.

| Settings card | `TenantConfig` field (label) |
|---|---|
| Company | `Tenant.name`, `country` (**pick-list** since PR5: Oman, United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, Other; `lib/countries.ts`; it decides road routing: outside Oman + UAE plans use straight-line estimates unless the company has its own routing server), `currency`, `primaryUnit` |
| Daily dispatch: timing | `shiftStartMin` (First departure; a plan made on the delivery day starts from now + turnaround when later, PR8), `driverShiftMaxMinutes` (Driver shift maximum), `reloadMinutes` (Turnaround between loads; since PR8 also the preparation time of a same-day plan, [3.11](#311-step-9-late-orders-and-plan-versions)), `loadingMinPerCase` (on a plan made on the delivery day it counts from now for every truck, PR8 review), `serviceMinPerCase`, `defaultServiceTimeMin` (Default service time), `maxTripsPerTruck`, `splitDeliveries`, `planningCutoffMin` (Planning cutoff, used by the order intake), `dateOrder` (dates in order files, used by the order intake); `palletFillPct` (**Pallet fill**, 50-100, default 100 = every bay (owner decisions of 4 Oct 2026; it was 95 before the owner was asked: the column default of migration `20261006090000_pallet_capacity`, edited before it was deployed, `PALLET_FILL_DEFAULT` in `lib/dispatch/pallets.ts` and `dispatch_models.py`), company admin only: the share of a truck's bays the planner may fill with mixed pallets, lower = a safety margin; only trucks with bays use it), `smallTruckMaxBays` (**Small truck = at most N bays**, 1-40, default 6, company admin only, owner decision 13 Oct 2026: a truck with bays entered and at most this many is small; customers marked *Small truck only (3-ton)* go on such trucks only, [4.4](#44-how-the-web-shapes-the-request); it changes the request only on a day with such a customer), `windowRule` (**Receiving hours**, company admin only, owner request 13 Oct 2026: *Receiving hours end = latest arrival (unloading may continue after it)* = START, or *Unloading must be finished by the end of the receiving hours* = FINISH, the default; sent as `config.window_rule`, see [4.4](#44-how-the-web-shapes-the-request)) |
| Daily dispatch: costs | `driverCostPerHour` (per hour of the **whole truck day**, [4.10](#410-extraction-and-reported-costs)), `overtimeAfterMin`, `overtimeCostPerHour` (on top of the driver cost), `fuelPricePerLitre`, `prefWindowPenaltyPerMin`, `dailyDriverDayRate` (owner answer 4 of 6 Oct 2026: the casual driver of a truck hired for the day, per day, instead of the hourly cost and overtime; sent as `driver_day_cost` on the trucks to rent and the one-day hired trucks only, [3.19](#319-the-hire-suggestion)) |
| Distances | `distanceProvider` (road distances OSRM, or straight-line estimates), `roadTimeFactor` (truck vs car, road legs only), `distanceMultiplier` and `avgSpeedKmh` (estimates) |
| Effective planner values (read-only) | everything above, plus the operations settings `timezone`, `osrmUrl` (shown as "company server set" or not, never editable: review L11), `serviceAreaJson`, and the planner rules (strict priorities, early-arrival preference, plan continuity, automatic search time - PR7: "5 s up to 25 stops, 20 s up to 120, rising steadily to 50 s at 150 and 150 s at 200, 150 s up to 350, 240 s above", from the schedule in `planner-bounds.json` that the solver tests check, `searchTimeText()` in `lib/dispatch/planner-config.ts` - 600 stops, 90 s road routing) |
| Customer type defaults (read-only) | `CustomerTypeProfile`: default priority, unloading minutes, hard and preferred hours per customer type. No editor yet (backlog) |

**Default service time (PR5).** An unloading time a planner confirmed (customer screen, or an imported column) wins; otherwise the customer type's; otherwise the company default from Settings. Before PR5 an unconfirmed customer kept its column default (10 min) and the Settings default changed nothing for normal customers. A new customer created with an explicit unloading time counts as confirmed. Customer imports before PR2 stored the file's time without confirming it; migration `20260928090100_keep_imported_service_times` marks those times confirmed (only where the type has no time of its own and the value is not the 10 min column default; one audit row each), so they are not replaced by the Settings default. The customer page shows the unloading time in use and where it comes from (`describeServiceTime`): an amber note when a stored time someone entered is not used (never confirmed); nothing for the 10 min column default under a customer type's own time (customers created by an order upload, a late order or a form without a time hold it although nobody entered it; the type's time applied before and after PR5); a neutral line for a stored 10 min under the Settings default (it may be an earlier import's real 10 min: pre-deploy check 11 in [5.12](#512-how-to-verify-a-deploy) asks to confirm those). One constant, `CUSTOMER_SERVICE_COLUMN_DEFAULT`, is kept equal to the schema default and the migration's rule by a unit test.

Other inputs that change the plan:

- **Per truck** (Trucks page, `truckSchema`): **bays** (pallet positions 1-40, owner decision 4 Oct 2026; set = the truck is planned by pallets, bays x Pallet fill and the payload when one is set, its case capacity then not a limit; a truck class such as *3 Ton* or *10 Ton* is only a name - NMWC: 10 Ton = 12 bays, 3 Ton = 6 bays, the Nissan bus = 2 bays; **payload 0 = no weight limit** everywhere (owner decisions of 4 Oct 2026: weight is not a planning limit for NMWC, every truck has payload 0): the solver's kg dimension, kg prefilters, kg fleet total and kg reasons are off (`payload_units` 0, `TruckDay.max_kg_units` 0, the second search without a kg dimension), the independent check and the web gate skip kg, utilization is by bays or cases only, OPTIMIZE / RE-PLAN never ask `WEIGHT_REQUIRED` (`start-optimize.ts` gate: only when a truck of the day has a payload), the day screen (`trucks.withPayload`) and the late order's answer (`weightLimited`) word the no-weight note without "OPTIMIZE asks", the load sheet shows "Weight / payload kg: ... / no limit", the truck form says "0 = no weight limit" and the Trucks table "no limit"; the form field **Bays (pallet positions)** and the Trucks table column since part B; empty = planned by cases), capacity in cases and kg, fixed daily cost, cost per km, and since PR5 **cost per load** (`tripCost`), **km per litre**, **max loads per day** and **availability** (from / until, HH:MM). A new truck starts at 0 costs (the invented 20 OMR / 0.15 per km defaults are gone). "Until 00:00" (or 24:00) is midnight, stored as 1440; since the audit PR "Intake and master data" (F25, `lib/dispatch/time-input.ts`) the edit form shows 1440 as 00:00 and a field left as loaded saves its stored minutes, so a truck available until midnight saves again when another field changes (it showed "00:00 +1", which the form's own save refused).
- **Per product** (Products page, `productSchema`, company admins): **cases per pallet** (`casesPerPallet`, the ERP pallet factor, a whole number 1-10,000, empty = not set; pallets part B: form field, table column, `POST` / `PATCH /api/products`, whose answer notes that loads planned before keep their pallets) and the case weight (empty = 0 = unknown on Add product; on Edit of a product that has one the field is required, at least 0.01 kg, and only **Weight not known** clears it, sent as `clearWeight: true`, without which `PATCH /api/products/[id]` refuses a 0 with 422 `WEIGHT_CLEAR_UNCONFIRMED`: review of da76343, an emptied field had saved the weight as unknown with no warning, and with payload 0 everywhere OPTIMIZE never asks for it again); the whole master in one file with **Import products** (`POST /api/products/import`, `lib/dispatch/product-import.ts`: header aliases such as "Cases per pallet", "Pallet factor", "Qty per pallet" (the owner's prepared master `NMWC-products-for-RouteIQ.xlsx`, sheet "Import", uses the import's own names `code`, `name`, `weight_per_case_kg`, `cases_per_pallet`, `active`; its other columns `volume_per_case_l`, `units_per_case` and `info_*` are named under "Columns not read", and a workbook's first sheet with rows is read, the others named in a warning: Validate only of it on the local database, 4 Oct 2026, gave 97 rows, 0 errors, 97 new on an empty master or 51 new + 46 updated on the pilot's 46 test SKUs, 12 products still without cases per pallet); product codes by the one rule of `lib/product-code.ts` (since the rebase on PR #54): the code is read tidy (`normalizeProductCode`), matched to the master on `productKey` in the program (letter case and spacing; `_` is a letter; twins resolve like the order intake's `preferredProduct`), and a code no product has becomes a product only when the Products page could hold it (`productCodeProblem`, the rule behind `productCodeSchema`), so `JA1.5L(6)` and `TN1.5L (6)` are created as written and an old product with an odd code is still found; two rows of one code in another case or spacing are an error; a blank cell keeps; Validate only; a file with an error imports nothing; `PRODUCTS_IMPORTED`). Case weights (pallets review): a weight of 0 counts as blank, and a product that already has a case weight keeps it unless **Update case weights** is ticked (`updateWeights=1`); a product without one takes the file's. The answer lists every weight it changes (`weightChanges`: code, before, after) and keeps (`weightsKept`), the headline counts the changed ones and a warning says open lines take a new weight at the next optimize. Before, any other figure in the file, 0 included, replaced a weight entered in RouteIQ and Validate only did not show it (the pilot master's `weight_per_case_kg_ESTIMATE` column). A product created from an order file has none: the order check lists the file's products without one in red when the depot has an active truck with bays (`IntakeIssueSummary.productsWithoutPalletFactor`, `validateIntake`: each row judged by the product it resolves to, the one OPTIMIZE plans it with, and named once by that product's code, a new one by its tidy code).
- **Per depot** (Depots page, `depotSchema`): since PR5 **opening and closing hours** (`openMin` / `closeMin`).
- **Per customer type:** `CustomerTypeProfile` (read-only table on Settings; seeded).
- `priorityWeightsJson` (inert while priorities are strict) and `orderColumnMapJson` can only be set in the database.

### 3.13 Audit log

The page is `apps/web/app/t/[slug]/audit/page.tsx` with `audit-client.tsx`, limited to TENANT_ADMIN. It filters through `GET /api/audit` (`apps/web/app/api/audit/route.ts`), TENANT_ADMIN since PR1. Since PR1 `audit()` strips `accessPinHash`, `passwordHash`, `sessionToken`, `tokenHash` and (4 Oct 2026, driver links) `salt` and `prevTokenHash` from before/after JSON, and the API and page strip them on read too.

**One catalog (PR5, review F23).** `lib/audit-catalog.ts` lists every action and entity with a label (`AUDIT_ACTIONS`, `AUDIT_ENTITIES`; the `LOAD_*` events are derived from the load statuses; events no longer written - `LOGOUT`, the retired driver app's `DRIVER_LOGIN` and `DELIVERY_PROOF_CREATED`, entities `RunJob` and `DriverShift` - are kept and marked old). Every writer goes through `audit()` (the plan transactions pass their `tx`), whose `action` and `entity` are typed with the catalog, so an event cannot be written without being findable. The page's filter lists come from it.

**API filters.** `action`, `entity`, `userId`, `from`, `to` (YYYY-MM-DD) and `limit` (1-1000, default 200; the page asks for 500) are zod-parsed; an unknown action, entity or parameter answers **400 `INVALID_FILTER`** with the allowed names (before PR5 an unknown action was dropped and the answer was every row). `from` / `to` are days in the company timezone (Asia/Muscat): `from=2026-09-25` starts at 2026-09-24T20:00Z. The page shows an error instead of "0 rows" when a query fails, and says when only the newest rows are shown.

**User filter** (review db-schema-2). The page lists the 25 users with the most audit rows of the company, most first: a `groupBy` that reads the index on `(tenantId, userId, createdAt)` alone (migration `20261009090000_order_delete_and_audit_indexes`), then the names of those ids only from `User`. A platform admin who opened the company's pages has rows here (`CROSS_TENANT_VIEW`) and is listed too. Before, the names came from a `findMany` with `distinct`, which Prisma 5 does in memory: every visit read every row of those users, JSON included, into the web process. The same index serves the API's `userId` filter.
