### 3.14 Status values and transitions

**`RunPlan.status` (`RunStatus`).**

| Value | Set by | Next |
|---|---|---|
| DRAFT | schema default: `createInitialPlan` (version 1, under the day lock), legacy `POST /api/runs` (same helper) | OPTIMIZING |
| OPTIMIZING | `startDispatchOptimize`, in the transaction that creates the new `RunJob` | READY, DISPATCHED, FAILED |
| READY | `applyScenario` (job or Use instead) and `changeStatusTx` while not every load is out - `changeStatusTx` only on a version with an applied plan; `createNextVersion` for the child (copy of an applied plan) | DISPATCHED, OPTIMIZING (a re-plan child's first job), SUPERSEDED |
| FAILED | `failJob` in `dispatch-job.ts` and `reapStuckJobs`, only from OPTIMIZING with the failing job as `currentJobId`; (audit PR4) `repairEndedJobPlan` for a plan OPTIMIZING behind an ended job, and `resetStuckPlan` (Reset stuck plan) | OPTIMIZING only without an applied plan (a failed re-plan still holding the copied plan answers 409 `NEW_VERSION_REQUIRED`: re-plan instead), READY (a load change on a FAILED version with an applied plan), SUPERSEDED |
| DISPATCHED | `changeStatusTx` or `applyScenario` when every load is DISPATCHED or COMPLETED (sets `finalizedAt`); `createNextVersion` for a child whose loads are all out; legacy `POST /api/runs/:id/dispatch` for runs without loads | SUPERSEDED (a re-plan is not blocked), OPTIMIZING (a re-plan child's first job); legacy `/unlock` back to READY for runs without loads |
| SUPERSEDED | `createNextVersion` on the parent (sets `supersededAt`) | final, read-only. `supersededAt` set means superseded whatever the status (PR3) |
| ARCHIVED | never written by any code; only excluded by `currentPlan` | none |

Every writer of `RunPlan.status` holds the plan's row lock (PR3, review F07), taken by `lockRunForWrite` in `lib/dispatch/plan-locks.ts` after the day lock where there is one. Lock order everywhere: the day (advisory lock), then the `RunPlan` row, then its `PlanLoad` rows; the optimize start takes the intake lock before the row. **Use this plan** (the hire suggestion) takes the intake lock, the hire codes lock and the day lock (its plan way; its re-plan way only the hire codes), then the `RunPlan` row and, ISSUE 7, the `HireOption` rows it rents from (FOR SHARE, in id order: `lockAndRecheck`), before any `PlanLoad` row. The only other lock on a `HireOption` row: the hire-options DELETE and a PATCH that moves an option to another depot take that row FOR UPDATE first, in their own transaction and before anything else (`underOptionLock`: then the rental count and the write); any other PATCH is a single statement that waits for the FOR SHARE. No writer can overwrite a newer state: `applyScenario` writes conditionally (never over SUPERSEDED), `failJob` and the janitor only touch their own job's OPTIMIZING version, and a stale job result is not applied.

**`PlanLoad.status` (`LoadStatus`):** see [3.8](#38-step-6-load-states). Created as PLANNED by `applyScenario`, or copied with its current status by `createNextVersion` (every load, PLANNED included, since PR3).

**`Order.status` (`OrderStatus`).**

| Value | Set by |
|---|---|
| VALIDATED | `confirmIntake`, late-order route |
| ASSIGNED | `applyScenario` when at least one part is on a truck |
| UNSERVED | `applyScenario` when nothing of it is planned |
| DISPATCHED | `changeStatusTx` when every part is on DISPATCHED or COMPLETED loads and no part is unserved (a split order with an unserved rest stays ASSIGNED) |
| UPLOADED, DELIVERED, FAILED | not written by the dispatch flow (UPLOADED is only the schema default; DELIVERED and FAILED are never written in `apps/web`) |

An order brought forward to a later day (PR9) keeps its status (the history of its day); `carriedToOrderId` set is what makes it no longer open there. Its copy starts `VALIDATED`. A load of its day that still holds it cannot move forward (409 `ORDERS_CARRIED`, [3.8](#38-step-6-load-states)); a PLANNED one holding nothing else stays as it is, while a LOCKED or LOADING one holding nothing else was loaded (NMWC loads at night): its cases are unloaded back to stock before the later day's loads are picked and it is put back to Planned (PR9 second review; the answer, the plan badge and Step 3 say so). The same holds for a load of today whose order of today was brought forward to tomorrow in the evening; its answer says re-plan today, or unlock it (a LOADING one goes Back to locked first).

`applyScenario` never moves an order that is already DISPATCHED or DELIVERED.

**`UploadBatch.status`:** PARSED (uploaded with errors) or VALIDATED (no errors), then CONFIRMED, or DELETED (`DELETE /api/orders/:batchId`, which also deletes its orders, allowed only while none of them is in a plan option). A VALIDATED batch older than 24 h cannot be confirmed (`STALE_VALIDATION`); it stays VALIDATED. REJECTED is checked for but never written.

**`RunJob.status`:** QUEUED (also while waiting for a solver slot, message "Waiting: N optimization(s) ahead"), RUNNING, then SUCCEEDED or FAILED (`failJob`; `reapStuckJobs` with `errorJson.reason = 'STUCK'`; a result for a version that moved on with `errorJson.reason = 'STALE_RESULT'`; (audit PR4) Reset stuck plan with `errorJson.reason = 'RESET'`). CANCELLED is never written. **Invariant (audit PR4, F09):** a plan is OPTIMIZING only while its current job is QUEUED or RUNNING.

### 3.15 Data model used by the dispatch flow

```mermaid
erDiagram
    Tenant ||--|| TenantConfig : settings
    Tenant ||--o{ CustomerTypeProfile : "type defaults"
    Depot ||--o{ Truck : bases
    Driver |o--o{ Truck : "default driver"
    Customer ||--o{ Order : orders
    UploadBatch |o--o{ Order : "created by"
    Order ||--|{ OrderLine : lines
    Product ||--o{ OrderLine : sku
    Depot ||--o{ RunPlan : "plan per date"
    RunPlan |o--o{ RunPlan : "parent version"
    RunPlan ||--o{ RunJob : attempts
    RunPlan ||--o{ HireSuggestion : "hire what-ifs"
    Depot ||--o{ HireOption : "trucks to hire"
    HireOption |o--o{ Truck : "rented as"
    RunPlan ||--o{ ScenarioResult : options
    ScenarioResult ||--o{ UnservedOrder : unserved
    Order ||--o{ UnservedOrder : "left out"
    RunPlan ||--o{ PlanLoad : loads
    Truck ||--o{ PlanLoad : trips
    Driver |o--o{ PlanLoad : drives
    Helper |o--o{ Truck : "usual helper"
    PlanLoad ||--o{ PlanLoadHelper : helpers
    Helper ||--o{ PlanLoadHelper : "goes on"
    PlanLoad ||--o{ RouteAssignment : stops
    Order ||--o{ RouteAssignment : "planned as"
```

| Model | Role in the flow | Key fields and relations |
|---|---|---|
| `Tenant` | owner of everything | `country` (service area, OSRM coverage, WhatsApp country code), `currency`, `name` |
| `TenantConfig` | planning settings, one per tenant | see [3.12](#312-settings-that-change-the-plan) |
| `CustomerTypeProfile` | defaults per `CustomerType` | `defaultPriority`, `serviceTimeMin`, hard and preferred windows; unique (`tenantId`, `customerType`) |
| `Depot` | start and end of every load | `lat`, `lng`, `openMin`, `closeMin`; unique (`tenantId`, `code`); `historyOnly` (audit PR A5: the depot `NO-DEPOT` "No depot (kept for history)" that migration `20260930120000_orders_always_have_depot` made for orders and files that had no depot; always inactive, never in a picker, never gets a truck or region; the database refuses it active too, CHECK `Depot_historyOnly_not_active`, A5 fifth review) |
| `Truck` | vehicle at a depot | (the hire suggestion, 6 Oct 2026) `onlyOnDate` (a one-day truck rented with **Use this plan**: planned on that date only - `trucksOfDayWhere` - and retired by the janitor after it; it shows its code now, the plate, not its snapshot's) and `hireOptionId` (its option's max per day counts it); `bays` (column `palletCapacity`; pallet positions, null = planned by cases), `capacityCases`, `capacityWeightKg`, `fixedCostPerDay`, `tripCost`, `costPerKm`, `kmPerLitre`, `maxTripsPerDay`, `availableFromMin`, `availableToMin`, `defaultDriverId`, `active` |
| `Driver` | person on a load | `name`, `phone` (WhatsApp), `active`, `casual` (daily driver); `loads`, `leaves`, `covers` |
| `Helper` | (13 Oct 2026) truck crew on a load | `code` (unique per company), `name`, `phone`, `active`; `defaultTrucks`, `loads` |
| `PlanLoadHelper` | (13 Oct 2026) a helper on one load | `loadId` (CASCADE), `helperId` (NO ACTION), `position` 1-3 (CHECK); unique (`loadId`, `helperId`) and (`loadId`, `position`); copied with the load into each new version |
| `DriverLeave` | (6 Oct 2026) a driver away on some delivery dates | `driverId` (NO ACTION, as every reference to a driver: Start fresh keeps a daily driver named by any period), `fromDate`, `untilDate` (DATE, both included; CHECK until >= from), `note`, `coverDriverId` (NO ACTION; CHECK not the driver), `createdById` / `updatedById` (SET NULL), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`; indexes (`tenantId`, `untilDate`) and (`driverId`, `fromDate`). Rules in `lib/dispatch/driver-leave.ts` ([3.9](#39-step-7-a-driver-per-load)) |
| `Customer` | delivery location (code + branch) | unique (`tenantId`, `code`, `branchKey`); looked up by code and branch whatever the letter case, in the program (`lib/customer-code.ts`, never a database ILIKE); `lat`, `lng`, `priority` + `priorityConfirmed`, `avgServiceTimeMin` + `serviceTimeConfirmed`, `customerType`, hard and preferred windows, `locationInput`, `locationSource`, `locationVerified`, `locationVerifiedById`, `locationVerifiedAt`, `createdFromUpload`, `address` and `accessNotes` (driver sheet), `phone` (owner request 12 Oct 2026: optional, for the driver to call before arrival; read live like `accessNotes`); `smallTruckOnly` (owner request 13 Oct 2026, default false: planned on small trucks only, `lib/dispatch/small-truck.ts`; read live by the plan screen, the sheets and the LOCK gate); `loadingInstruction` (owner request 16 Oct 2026: optional, at most 200 characters on one line, `lib/dispatch/loading-instruction.ts`; the SPECIAL LOADING box of the load sheets, read live like `accessNotes`, never sent to the optimizer nor kept in a snapshot); `siteRadiusM` (owner request 19 Oct 2026: optional, 100-500 m, CHECK `Customer_siteRadiusM_range`; the GPS stop detector ends a stay at this customer only beyond it, `lib/ivms/site-radius.ts`, [3.21](#321-gps-live-link-ayun-times-live-map-tracker-mapping); set in the Details dialog, read live) |
| `Product` | SKU | unique (`tenantId`, `code`); the code is the ERP's own, e.g. `JA1.5L(6)`, `TN1.5L (6)`: letters, digits, spaces and `. ( ) - _ / + &`, tidy (no spaces at the ends, one space between words), at most 40 (`lib/product-code.ts`; the database only holds the text, no migration), matched ignoring the letter case; `weightPerCaseKg` (0 = unknown), `casesPerPallet` (the ERP pallet factor, a whole number 1-10,000; needed on a day planned with trucks that have bays), `createdFromUpload` |
| `UploadBatch` | one uploaded file | `status`, `validationJson` (full validation including resolved lines), `fileHash`, `depotId` (required since audit PR A5, FK Depot NO ACTION), `deliveryDate`, `isLate`, `lateReason` |
| `Order` | one customer branch for one delivery date (or one late-order entry, or one order brought forward) | `customerId`, `depotId` (required since audit PR A5: every order has a depot; FK Depot NO ACTION), `deliveryDate`, `totalCases`, `totalWeightKg`, `priority`, `priorityFromFile`, `status`, `isLate`, `lateReason`, `lateRecordedById`, `salesValue`, `marginValue`, `notes`, `uploadBatchId`; (PR9, migration `20260929090000_order_carry_over`) on a copy `carriedFromOrderId` (unique, FK Order, NO ACTION) and `carriedFromDate` (the date first due); on the original `carriedToOrderId` (unique, FK Order, NO ACTION), `carriedAt`, `carriedById` (FK User, SET NULL); (Cancel order, migration `20261013090000_order_cancel`) `cancelledAt` (set = cancelled: out of planning and the counts), `cancelledById` (FK User, SET NULL), `cancelReason`, `cancelNote` |
| `OrderLine` | one SKU line | `productId`, `cases`, `salesOrderNo`, `weightKg` (0 = unknown), `weightFromMaster` (no file weight: the kg is cases × the product's case weight and follows it; set again at optimize when that weight is entered or corrected), `salesValue`, `marginValue`, `sourceRow`, `notes`, `salesRoute` (17 Oct 2026: the salesman's route from the order file, null = none; read only by the Salesman ETA export and, since 19 Oct 2026, the salesman link, [3.23](#323-the-salesman-link)); cascades with its order |
| `IntakeLineKey` | identity of a confirmed sales-order line | unique (`tenantId`, `deliveryDate`, `salesOrderNorm` (trimmed, upper-case), `customerId`, `productId`); `orderLineId` unique, cascades with the line; `uploadBatchId` (null for a late order). Written by `confirmIntake` and the late-order route; backfilled for existing lines by migration `20260926100000_intake_line_keys` |
| `RunPlan` | one version of the plan for (`depotId`, `runDate`) | `version`, `parentRunId` (self relation "PlanVersions"), `reason`, `reasonNote`, `status`, `chosenScenarioId` (plain id, no foreign key), `currentJobId`, `supersededAt`, `finalizedAt`, `summaryJson`, `reconciliationJson`, `changeSummaryJson`, `feasibilityJson` (PR4: the timetable check per truck-day, [3.8](#38-step-6-load-states)), `totalOrders`, `unservedCount` |
| `RunJob` | one optimize attempt | unique (`runId`, `attemptNo`); `status`, `progressPct`, `message`, `requestJson`, `responseJson`, `errorJson`, timestamps |
| `HireOption` | a truck the company can rent for a day (6 Oct 2026) | unique (`tenantId`, `depotId`, `label`); `bays` or `capacityCases`, `payloadKg` (0 = no limit), `costPerDay`, `costPerKm` (the rental's own km charge; null = none, 0 - fuel is in the hire, owner answer 3: never the fleet's km cost or fuel), `maxPerDay` (counted by option over the day's one-day trucks, wherever they are), `active`; CHECK `HireOption_values_range`; not deleted or moved to another depot while trucks are hired from it for today or later |
| `HireSuggestion` | one what-if of the hire suggestion for one plan version (6 Oct 2026) | `runId` (cascades with the version), `status` (`RunJobStatus`), `trigger` (`AFTER_PLAN` / `ASKED`), `basisJson` (`HireBasis`: what the plan in use left out, the request's fingerprint, the options, the trucks already rented, the daily driver day rate the trucks to rent were priced with), `errorJson` (a check that ended without a suggestion: its `reason`, `NOTHING_LEFT` for a check recorded because every order left out was gone), `requestJson`, `responseJson`, `summaryJson` (`HireSummary`), `message`, `heartbeatAt`, `usedAt` / `usedById` / `usedRunId` |
| `ScenarioResult` | one solver option | `name` (RECOMMENDED, MIN_TRUCKS, MIN_DISTANCE), totals, `detailsJson` (`ScenarioDetails` including `scope`, the solver's `feasibility` report and, since PR4, `inputs`: what the optimization was computed with, [`lib/dispatch/snapshots.ts`](#22-the-web-app)) |
| `UnservedOrder` | an order (or part) left out of one option | `scenarioId`, `orderId`, `reasonCode`, `reasonMessage`, `portionCases`, `portionWeightKg`, `portionLinesJson` |
| `PlanLoad` | one physical truck trip | unique (`runId`, `truckId`, `loadNo`); `status`, `driverId`, `departMin`, `returnMin`, `distanceKm`, `durationMin`, `cases`, `weightKg`, `utilizationPct`, `fuelLitres`, `fuelCost`, `operatingCost`, `returnLegKm`, `distanceIsEstimated`, `truckSnapshotJson` (PR4: the truck code, capacities, costs, availability and the planning rules the load was timed with; null before PR4), `carriedFromLoadId`, `statusChangedAt`, `statusChangedById`, `driverSetById` (FK User, SET NULL) and `driverSetAt`: who chose the driver by hand, and when (null: RouteIQ filled it in); `driverIsCover` (6 Oct 2026, default false): RouteIQ gave the driver as the cover of the truck's usual driver on leave (`planDrivers` pass 3; copied by a re-plan's copies, cleared when the dispatcher sets the driver); `palletUnits` (the pallet need it was planned with, 1/1000 pallet, the sum of its rows'; NULL = planned by cases) |
| `RouteAssignment` | one order (or split portion) at one stop of one load | unique (`runId`, `truckId`, `loadNo`, `sequenceInTruck`, `orderInStop`); `loadId`, `etaMin`, `serviceStartMin`, `departureMin`, `waitMin`, `cumulativeKm`, `hardWindowOk`, `prefWindowOk`, `portionCases`, `portionWeightKg` (the parts of one split stop add up exactly to the kg the optimizer was sent, PR4 review), `portionLinesJson` (`[{ lineId, cases, kgPerCase }]`; `kgPerCase`, the case weight the part was planned with, since the PR4 review), `stopSnapshotJson` (PR4: the pin, hours, service time and priority sent to the optimizer, plus the customer's code, name, type, address and access notes when applied - the notes for the record only, sheets print today's; null before PR4); `palletUnits` (the row's pallet need as sent to the optimizer; NULL without pallets) |
| `AuditLog` | who did what | `action`, `entity`, `entityId`, `beforeJson`, `afterJson`, `ip` |

**Delete behaviour.** Deleting a `RunPlan` cascades to its jobs, scenarios, loads and assignments. `RouteAssignment.orderId` is `ON DELETE RESTRICT` and `UnservedOrder.orderId` is `ON DELETE NO ACTION` (since migration `20260926100100_unserved_order_fk_no_action`; it was CASCADE), so an order that is on any plan option, planned or unserved, cannot be deleted. Deleting a tenant therefore removes its plan data first (as `cleanupTenant` in the integration helpers does). An order brought forward and its copy (PR9) point at each other `ON DELETE NO ACTION`: neither can be deleted from under the other (one statement deleting both, as a tenant delete does, is fine). Since migration `20260930093000_master_data_no_orphans` (audit F03 / F20) `Order.depotId`, `UploadBatch.depotId`, `PlanLoad.driverId` and `Truck.defaultDriverId` are `ON DELETE NO ACTION` too (they were SET NULL): a depot with orders or order files, and a driver on a load or set as a truck's default, cannot be deleted - the app deactivates them instead. `Truck.depotId` and `RunPlan.depotId` were already RESTRICT; `Region.depotId` stays SET NULL (the app deactivates a depot with regions anyway).

**Legacy-only models** (neither read nor written by the dispatch flow): `ManualBaseline` and `ManualBaselineAssignment` (baseline tab of the old run page); `DriverShift`, `TruckLocation` and `DeliveryProof` (the driver PWA, retired in PR1; data kept); `Region` (master-data page only; `Customer.regionId`). `User` and `PasswordResetToken` belong to authentication.

**Legacy-only fields and values.**

- `RunPlan.optimizationMode`: copied into child versions, never sent to the solver.
- `RouteAssignment.lockedByUserId` and `manualOverrideReason`: per-stop locks of the old flow. `plannedArrivalMin`, `plannedDistanceFromPrevKm` and `plannedLoadCases` are still filled.
- `Order.totalServiceTimeMin`, `totalVolumeL` and `paymentCollectionAmount`: written or defaulted, not read by the planner.
- `Truck.capacityVolumeL` (not sent to the solver); `Customer.paymentType`.
- Enum values the dispatch flow never writes: `RunStatus.ARCHIVED`; `OrderStatus` UPLOADED, DELIVERED and FAILED; `UploadBatchStatus.REJECTED`; `RunJobStatus.CANCELLED`; the `OptimizationMode` enum; and the older `UnservedReasonCode` values (`EXCEEDS_TRUCK_CAPACITY`, `NO_AVAILABLE_TRUCK`, `SHIFT_TIME_LIMIT`, `INFEASIBLE_ROUTE`). For old plans, `REASON_TEXT` in `app/t/[slug]/dispatch/client-api.ts` labels `EXCEEDS_TRUCK_CAPACITY`, `SHIFT_TIME_LIMIT`, `INFEASIBLE_ROUTE` and `NO_AVAILABLE_TRUCK`. `INVALID_CUSTOMER` is written again since the stabilization release, for open orders of a deactivated customer ("Customer deactivated"). (The solver does emit `NO_AVAILABLE_TRUCK`; see [4.12](#412-unserved-reason-codes-and-messages).)

Flood limits: the body is read through a byte-counting reader (413 past 64 KB, Content-Length or not); 120 **actions** a minute per link (429); at most 2 requests of a link at once (429, Retry-After 2); at most 40 arrivals, departures and results per stop and 5 Back at depot per load (`INVALID` beyond); a result equal to the stop's current one and not dated after its latest stored result (or clear) is answered `ok` and stores nothing (a newer one is stored: results can arrive out of order and the latest `at` wins, review of 8 Oct 2026); after an action answered `error`, the later actions of its stop in that request are answered `error` unapplied, so the phone sends them again in their order | the driver page's queue (a due action takes the earlier actions of its stop still backing off with it, `nextBatch`) |

### 3.17 Legacy and unused surfaces still in the repo

RouteIQ started as a generic multi-tenant route planner (the `CLAUDE.md` v1.3 specification, with a PyVRP solver). The NMWC dispatch planner (PR #25, `675f3fc`) replaced its planning flow but kept most of the old pages and routes.

### 3.18 Delivery outcomes and the driver page

Owner request of 4 Oct 2026: keep the PDF driver sheets for the record, and put a QR per driver on them that opens **his own page** with his trips and orders; when he reaches the customer a timer starts by itself (stop and unloading time), he records the result with a photo whose position is kept; NMWC also uses **daily (casual) drivers** and sometimes **hires trucks**; the Ayun GPS link comes later. The build spec is `.dev/design-delivery-outcome/SPEC.md` (local). It is built in three parts on one branch, and **all three are built**: Part 1 (foundations), Part 2 (field actions: the stop timer, results, photos, the offline queue) and Part 3 (office side: the results on the plan screen, Record outcome, Bring forward from results, Undo bring forward, measured unloading, the pin check, the actuals Excel, KPIs, the retention janitor). The driver's own guide is [`docs/DRIVER_GUIDE.md`](./DRIVER_GUIDE.md) (English and Arabic).

**Part 1, what works.**

- **One link per truck-day.** One QR / link covers every load of one truck on one delivery date (`DriverLink`, unique per company, truck and date). No account, no PIN, no app: daily drivers and drivers of hired trucks just scan. Where it shows: the plan screen's **Link** action per load (QR, Copy, WhatsApp in English and Arabic, "Works until", "Last opened · Used on N phones", Reissue, Revoke), the first QR on every PDF sheet of the truck-day (PLANNER+ only), and a line in the WhatsApp message.
- **The token.** `K = HKDF-SHA256(DRIVER_LINK_SECRET | NEXTAUTH_SECRET | AUTH_SECRET, "routeiq-driver-link", "v1")`; token = the first 24 base64url characters (144 bits) of `HMAC(K, "<id>.<generation>.<salt>")`. Only its SHA-256 is stored (`tokenHash`, plus `salt`, `generation` and `keyId`); the server derives it again to print the same link. It works until **12:00 company time the day after the delivery date** (`linkExpiry`), with a 72 h upload-only grace (`linkUploadUntil`, used from Part 2). **Reissue** (a new salt and generation) makes the old token answer 410 `LINK_REPLACED` at once, the one before it 404; **Revoke** stops it until a reissue. A rotated secret makes every link answer "replaced" until the dialog or the PDF makes it again.
- **Where the token travels.** Only the QR landing page has it in its path (`GET /d/<token>`, a data-free shell that never reads the database, so a link previewer learns nothing). The page sends it in the header `Authorization: DriverLink <token>` to token-free paths (`/api/d/manifest`; Part 2 adds `/api/d/actions` and `/api/d/photos`). `next.config.js` and `withDriverLink` send `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow, noarchive` and `Cache-Control: no-store` for `/d/` and `/api/d/`; every Sentry init drops traces of those paths and rewrites `/d/<token>` (`lib/observability-scrub.ts`).
- **`withDriverLink`** (`lib/driver-link/guard.ts`): shape check first (404, no database work); resolve (`resolveDriverLink`, the only lookup not scoped by company: a unique hash cannot cross companies); only an **unknown** hash counts against the IP (`dl-bad:<ip>`, 30 per 10 min; never a null or internal IP, never a token that resolves: drivers share the depot Wi-Fi and mobile CGNAT); per-link limits (60 manifest reads a minute); a signed-in session of the link's company is **the office** (reads allowed, writes need PLANNER; Part 2), another company's session 403. The third principal next to users and the janitor token ([2.10](#210-multi-tenancy-authentication-and-roles)).
- **The manifest** (`lib/driver-link/manifest.ts`, `GET /api/d/manifest`): a projection of `getPlanDetail` for the truck's loads on the plans in use of that date (the `currentPlan` rule per depot; while a re-plan runs, the OPTIMIZING version's copies), memoised 60 s per plan version under a stamp of its loads. Per stop: sequence, customer + branch, address, a Google Maps directions link to the **planned** pin, planned arrival and unloading end, the hours or the promised time (the additive `DetailStop.plannedHours` / `promisedWindow`), the cases per order line (`DetailStop.orderLines`, from the row lines with no aggregation), notes and access notes, the customer's phone and its tel: link (`customerPhone`, `customerTel`; owner request 12 Oct 2026: read live from the customer, the link made on the server with the company's calling code by `telUrl`, as the WhatsApp links), split part, carried-over date, changes after planning. Never money, priorities or other trucks.
- **The page** (`app/d/[token]`): mobile first (360 x 640, buttons of 48 px and more), English / Arabic (RTL, Western digits, the toggle in the header; the Arabic must be checked by an NMWC Arabic speaker), the trips in departure order with their status ("Not loaded yet", "On the road", "Done"), the stop sheet with a big Navigate button, the location notice on first open, an "open in Chrome / Safari" card inside in-app browsers (Facebook, Instagram, Line, Snapchat, the Android WebView), the "link does not work / replaced / expired" pages, a **Call customer** link («اتصل بالعميل») on the stop sheet when the customer has a phone (owner request 12 Oct 2026: the driver calls before arrival), and a Call dispatcher button (owner decision 3 of 5 Oct 2026: the number of the depot of the trip the driver is on or goes on next, `Depot.dispatcherPhone`, else the company's `TenantConfig.dispatcherPhone`; `dispatcherPhoneFor` in `lib/driver-link/dispatcher-phone.ts`; hidden without either). It polls every 60 s while visible and stops for good after a 404 or 410. **Part 1 is read-only**: the timer, results and photos come with Part 2.
- **Daily drivers and rule 20** ([3.9](#39-step-7-a-driver-per-load)). Changing a load's driver after the link was made asks "Reissue link?" only when the link was made for another named driver, the change is on the truck-day's earliest open trip and nobody else is on the road with the link (`reissuePrompt`); a link made before any driver was set takes the new driver silently.
- **Hired trucks.** `Truck.hired` ("Hired from outside" on the truck form, company admin): a badge on the plan, "HIRED TRUCK" on the sheets and "Hired truck" on the driver page. The planner never reads it. A dispatcher quick-add of a hired truck for one day is **not** built (it would change which trucks every plan uses): the admin adds the truck and deactivates it afterwards (open question). Delete keeps (deactivates) a truck that anything names - a plan row, and also a driver link or a stop visit (printing the sheets makes a link even for a truck no plan uses any more; both are NO ACTION keys).
- **Late dispatch note.** The truck-day's page was opened (`lastSeenAt`) after a load's planned departure while the load is still Locked or Loading: the plan says "T05 L1: driver page opened 07:15, load still Loading - planned departure 07:10. Dispatch it if it has left."
- **Settings** (company admin): arrival radius (50-500 m, default 100), photo required (default on), keep delivery photos (30-1095 days, default 90 since owner decision 1 of 5 Oct 2026; it was 365), keep driver positions (30 days up to the photo retention, default 90), the company dispatcher phone (used for a depot without its own number, **Depots**). `TenantConfig.outcomesSince` (the migration time for existing companies) scopes the later no-result list and KPIs.
- **Data model** (one additive migration for all three parts, `20261004090000_delivery_outcome_driver_page`): `DriverLink`, `StopVisit` (one physical stop of a load that left, keyed by `(company, depot, date, truck, load number, sequence)`, never by a plan version's row: a re-plan copies the loads), `StopEvent` (append-only, a source per event: PHONE_AUTO, PHONE_MANUAL, DISPATCHER, AYUN, SYSTEM - Ayun's stop events go into the same table later, with keys `ayun:<id>`), `DeliveryPhoto` (compressed JPEG in PostgreSQL). Parts 2 and 3 fill them.

**Part 2, what works (field actions).**

- **The flow on the phone.** The driver scans the QR, taps **Start deliveries** (iOS asks for the location only after a tap), opens a stop, taps **Navigate** ("When you arrive, open this page again"). At the customer the timer starts by itself; he taps **Delivered**, **Partly** (cases per order line, default all, then the reason) or **Not delivered** (the reason; Other needs a note), takes up to 3 photos (required for Delivered and Partly when the company says so, with "Camera not working" as the only way round it) and taps Save. After the last stop he taps **Back at depot**. A result can be changed or cleared until the load is COMPLETED, and never once it was brought forward (`editable` false).
- **The current trip** (`currentTrip`): the DISPATCHED load with the highest load number that is not back at the depot; else, after Start deliveries, the earliest LOCKED or LOADING load whose planned departure is at most 30 min away, whose arrivals are **held** on the phone and sent once it is dispatched (a late Dispatch click loses no timing). Only that trip's stops can arrive automatically.
- **The stop timer** (`lib/delivery/geofence.ts`, pure, 25 required cases in `geofence.spec.ts`). A fix counts only when fresh (30 s), accurate (250 m) and slower than 9 km/h. IN = within the radius plus an accuracy allowance (at most half the radius); a departure needs radius + 50 m. Arrival after 20 s inside for the expected stop (the first one of the trip without a result), 90 s for any other (a roundabout is not an arrival); departure after 60 s outside. Two stops inside together: no automatic arrival, the driver chooses ("Which customer?") and the chosen stop gets the time of the first common fix. A stop whose pin is within radius + 50 m of the depot never arrives by itself. Neighbour shops (pins within radius + 50 m, no gap since the result, no move): the next arrival chains at the result time.
- **Observed or found.** Browsers deliver positions only while the page is visible: in Maps, with the camera or a locked screen, the page sees nothing. An arrival the page **saw** (outside, then inside, no gap) is observed; one **found** when the page came back (already inside) is `observed: false`, asks "Arrived at ACME - when?" (Now / 5 / 10 / 15 min ago: a manual arrival at that time), and never feeds measured times or the on-time KPI. A departure seen only after a gap is dated at the last inside fix and is not observed; it needs two outside fixes at least 20 s apart in the same visible period (`gapConfirmMs`; a new gap, such as Retake, starts again), because the first fix after the camera or Maps is often coarse. A fix is OUT only when its whole error circle is past radius + 50 m (a coarse fix covering the pin is NEAR), and a coarse NEAR fix never counts as "seen outside". GPS lost: the result time ends the stop. After a reload the tracker starts only once the phone's queue was read, so an arrival still waiting to send restores its stop with its own time; a "Back at depot?" suggestion belongs to the trip it was raised for. The page says so: "Keep this page open. If the screen locks, the timer may pause." A screen wake lock is held while at a stop where the browser allows it. When no trip is left to time (the last trip is back at the depot: `timerStep` in `geofence.ts`, run by `use-tracker.ts`) the position watch and the wake lock end and the page shows the timer as off, so the GPS does not run all day; the saved "timer on" is kept, so a trip dispatched later (or a reload during the wait) starts it again without a tap, while a timer the driver stopped by hand is never restarted by itself.
- **The visit** (`StopVisit`, `lib/delivery/visit.ts`): rebuilt from all its events after every write. The result is the latest OUTCOME (by its time; a null outcome clears it); the chosen cycle (phone arrivals closed by the first departure) holds the result; the dispatcher's Arrived / Left are not cycle members: the newest entry of each (latest received) overrides the phone's and any earlier office entry; a "when?" answer overrides the found arrival; no departure, or a phone one more than 15 min after the result, ends the stop at a phone result (never at an office result entered later). After the location purge a visit keeps its `timingSuspect` flag when it is rebuilt. Automatic minutes only from observed automatic events (`autoBasis` DEPARTURE or RESULT); `autoServiceMinutes` counts from the window start (an early truck waiting for the window is not unloading) and is null across the planned break. Plausibility flags (a position equal to the pin, accuracy of 1 m or less, the same non-integer accuracy three times, identical arrival and departure points, an arrival more than 2 x radius from its photo or result) set `timingSuspect`. The load's planned break is read from the live load (frozen loads keep `breakJson`; the visit has no column for it). With the GPS link's events (TIMES) the times shown follow [3.21](#321-gps-live-link-ayun-times-live-map-tracker-mapping) *Precedence* and *GPS times win* (owner decision 21 Oct 2026: GPS wins over late phone times); the driver's own times a GPS one replaced are kept on the visit (`ownArrivedAt` ... `ownDepartedAtOutcome`).
- **Who may write when** (`lib/delivery/outcome-rules.ts`). DISPATCHED: yes. COMPLETED: the link only **fills gaps** (dated before the completion; a result only for a stop that had none at completion - its effective result then, so a result cleared before the completion is none), flagged `late` ("recorded after the trip closed"); a backdated change of an existing result is refused `LOAD_COMPLETED`. LOCKED / LOADING: arrivals and departures are kept on the phone (transient `LOAD_NOT_DISPATCHED`), results refused. A change that would shrink cases already brought forward from the visit (the copy's carry basis, written from Part 3; empty before) is refused `OUTCOME_CARRIED` and kept as a `CARRY_CONFLICT` event; the orders' `carriedToOrderId` is read under the outcome-day lock (`carryBases`), so a Bring forward committing meanwhile is never missed. A changed result needs no new photo when an earlier Delivered or Partly of the driver at that stop named one (`proofPhotoKeys`, counted before the photo arrives: a change sent in the same batch as the first result, or while its photo still waits, is accepted; the phone counts the same keys, `StopResult.proofPhotos` plus its queued results); a photo taken for a Not delivered (a closed shutter) is no proof of a delivery on a return visit. A signed-in office user on the page writes as DISPATCHER with the user id, and closes a trip as themselves.
- **Positions and times are phone-reported.** An automatic arrival without a position or more than radius + allowance + 25 m from the pin is stored as manual (`payload.downgraded`); a chained arrival between pins further apart than radius + 50 m takes its own fix; every phone time is corrected once for the phone's clock skew (over 2 min) and must lie in [day start - 6 h, the link's expiry] (`TIME_OUT_OF_RANGE`).
- **Stop keys (fix of 7 Oct 2026).** A stop is `<depotId>:<loadNo>:<sequence>` and a load `<depotId>:<loadNo>` everywhere in the driver protocol (`lib/driver-link/stop-key.ts`): the manifest's stops and trips, arrivals, departures and results, photos, the action and photo answers' results (`DriverResults.stops` and `back`), the phone's offline queue (IndexedDB items carry `loadKey`; drafts per stop key), Back at depot (`depot` with the load number) and the load's completion (`maybeCompleteLoad` and the janitor's `completeReturnedLoads` by depot and number) - the identity a visit is stored by (`StopVisit`: company, depot, date, truck, load number, stop), and the same across re-plans (frozen loads keep their number and stops). Before, a key was `<loadNo>:<sequence>` only: one link covers every load of the truck that date, two depots' plans can both give it a Load 1, and a Delivered entered for the second depot's 12-case customer was recorded as 40 cases delivered to the first depot's customer (the first load of that number by departure was taken). Keys of the old form still queued on a phone are accepted when exactly one stop of the truck-day fits them (`resolveTarget`: the loads of that number, narrowed to those with that stop) and refused `STOP_AMBIGUOUS` when two do ("Not recorded: this entry was saved before an update and fits two trips with the same number today. Call your dispatcher to record it."; the office records it with **Record outcome**); a key that matches more than one stop is refused whatever its form - never a guess. The phone lays an old item on the one stop it fits (`manifestStopKey`), and a manifest it kept before the update reads with the load numbers as keys (`keyedManifest`).
- **Idempotency.** Each action and photo carries a lowercase UUID made on the phone; the server stores `dl:<uuid>` (actions) and `dlphoto:<uuid>` (photos), so a driver can never take an `ayun:` or `disp:` key. A known key from the same link answers `duplicate`; from another link `INVALID` with nothing echoed. A unique-key error is answered from a fresh read outside the aborted transaction.
- **Photos** (`photo-service.ts`, `jpeg.ts`, `lib/driver-page/photo.ts`). The camera opens from the file input, clicked inside the tap (iOS opens a picker only within the user gesture; the draft is saved without waiting); the page reads EXIF first (GPS is rarely there; used only for "taken earlier", decided by the server), compresses to at most 1600 px at JPEG 0.7 (0.6 and 0.5 above 400 KB; over 1.5 MB "retake"), and takes the better of a fresh high-accuracy fix and the timer's last fix, both asked the moment the file arrives - not when "Use photo" is tapped (Save never waits; a photo waits at most 15 s for its position). Every request has a time limit (30 s; a photo upload 30 s plus its size at 4 KB/s, at least 90 s and at most 10 min, `photoTimeoutMs`, so a large photo on an EDGE uplink still arrives): a stalled one counts as failed and the queue retries. The server checks the bytes (415), **strips every piece of metadata** (`stripJpeg`: EXIF, maker data, thumbnails, comments, data after the image) and stores the JPEG in `DeliveryPhoto.bytes` with its position status and distance from the pin.
- **The offline queue** (`lib/driver-page/queue.ts`, `store.ts`). IndexedDB `riq-driver`: the queue (ready, held, draft), the stop sheet's draft (kept on every change, so a phone that kills the tab while the camera is open reopens the sheet: "Your last entry was kept"), the last manifest (shown without signal with "Last updated") and the link entry (tracking restarts by itself after a reload when location is allowed). Backoff 5 s, 15 s, 30 s, 60 s, then every 5 min; 429 is transient (Retry-After); 404 / 410 stop sending and list what was not sent; the upload grace keeps sending results dated before the expiry; truck-days 5 days old are deleted. The overlay shows unsent results ("Saved on phone - waiting to send"), so a result saved offline is never offered again, and "Changed by office / another phone" when the server's result differs from what the phone sent. Each send's results are laid into the kept manifest before its items leave the queue, and a manifest asked for before a send's results arrived is dropped, so a sent result never disappears for a poll. A service worker scoped to `/d/` reloads the page shell without signal (network first; hashed static files cache first; the API never cached). **The first visit too (ISSUE 8, 7 Oct 2026):** the first QR visit loads the page and its files before any worker exists, so none of them passed through it and a driver who lost signal right after could not reopen the link. On install the worker keeps the driver pages open in the browser (`clients.matchAll`, `/d/` only) fetched again, and the `/_next/static/` files each one's HTML names (scripts, styles, preloaded fonts) and its stylesheets name (the other font files), each fetched once whatever the tabs open - best effort, at most 20 s, never failing the install; a new build's worker does the same when the driver next opens a link, from the network or, without signal, from the copies the older build kept (deleted only when the new one takes over). The HTML names the link's token (Next.js writes the URL into it), so each link's copy stays under its own path, at most 8 (`MAX_PAGES`, oldest first), deleted when the page finds the link revoked, replaced, expired or closed (`forgetDriverPage`: the message goes to the worker in control, to an installing, waiting or active one, and to the active one once the registration has one - a first visit can find the link dead before its registration exists, and that worker's install would keep it; the worker deletes the copy from every build's page cache, and no worker keeps it again - a later build's neither, while the dead tab stays open: review of ISSUE 8, the link is remembered by a hash of its path, never the token, in `riq-driver-gone`, which no build deletes, at most 200) and the older build's copies when a new build takes over. Only pages under `/d/` that answer 200 HTML and this site's `/_next/static/` files are kept; never an API answer. Physical phones: a manual check. A cache that fails (broken or full site storage) never fails a request: every cache step falls back to the network. The page registers the worker in production builds only (`shouldRegisterWorker` in `lib/driver-page/worker.ts`): `next dev` chunk URLs are not content-hashed, so cache first would serve stale JS; a development build removes a worker an earlier visit left.
- **Back at depot and completion.** BACK_AT_DEPOT is a load-level event (its distance from the depot pin kept). A load that is back with a result on every stop is completed at once (`completeLoadAsDriver` in `plan-service.ts`: the same tail as the Completed button, no role check, `userId` null, `afterJson.actor` "Driver link: Salim (T05, back at depot)", no IP; when a signed-in user recorded that last result - Record outcome, or the office on the driver page - the row is theirs); a busy plan or a stop without a result leaves it DISPATCHED, and the janitor (`completeReturnedLoads`, at most every 10 min and the cron route) tries again. The dispatcher's Completed button is unchanged.
- **Leaving for next load (owner decision of 16 Oct 2026).** Offered only while the company has the operations alerts on with rule R2 on (`settings.leaveTap` of the manifest, `leaveTapOffered` in `lib/driver-link/manifest.ts`: merging the alerts with the master switch off changes nothing the drivers see; second review of 16 Oct 2026). After Back at depot of a trip, when the truck has a later trip that day at the same depot (never after the last one), the page shows a **Leaving for next load** bar naming both trips; the driver taps it, after a confirmation, when the truck leaves the depot again. It is a `DEPOT_DEPART` load-level event on the load the truck leaves with (`lib/driver-page/overlay.ts` `leaveOffer`; the queue keeps it offline like any action), with the phone's position only from a fix at most 2 min old (`recentPosOf`). A tap made too early is corrected by tapping again: for `LEAVE_RETAP_MIN` (30 min) after the tap the bar says *Left depot 10:55 with trip 2. Tapped too early? Tap again when the truck really leaves.*; every tap is stored and the latest one before the truck reached a stop counts. The server accepts it on a Locked, Loading or Dispatched load (the dispatcher may press Dispatch later), holds it on the phone for a Planned one until it is locked (the page releases it then), never on the day's first load nor after a trip at another depot, at most 5 per load. Unlock (back to Planned) removes the load's taps (`changeStatusCore`, counted in its audit row), so a load planned again with that number does not inherit them; the readers also ignore taps on a load that is Planned now. Alert rule R2 and the plan screen's load row read it ([3.20](#320-operations-alerts)).
- **Audit.** Results (`DELIVERY_OUTCOME_SET` with before / after and the source), manual arrivals, photos, Back at depot, Leaving for next load (`DRIVER_DEPOT_DEPART`) and refused changes after a carry are audited with the driver actor; automatic arrivals and departures are not (`StopEvent` is their record). Driver-link rows keep no IP and no phone id (`audit({ ip: false })`): those are on the stop events and photos and go with the location retention.
- **Not in Part 2** (Part 3): the results on the plan screen and the day screen, the dispatcher's Record outcome, Bring forward from results, measured unloading times, the pin check, the actuals Excel, the KPIs and the retention janitor (photo bytes, positions, idle daily drivers).

**Part 3, what works (office side).**

- **The results on the plan** (`GET /api/runs/:id/outcomes`, `lib/delivery/outcome-view.ts`, read with the plan and every 60 s while a load is on the road). The Loads table's Status cell of a DISPATCHED or COMPLETED load: "Delivered 7/12", "2 partly", "1 not delivered", "2 no result", "Back 14:32". The open load's stop table gains Result (with the reason, "by driver" / "by Ali (office)", "→ 6 Oct" when brought forward, "recorded after the trip closed", "no photo: camera failed (driver)" / "no photo (office)", a red "changed after it was brought forward"), Arrived ("manual", "set by office", "arrival not observed (page opened at the shop)", "far from pin"), Left ("result time", "not observed"), Unload ("plan 20 / actual 34 min"; "unverified timing"), Photos (the viewer: the image fetched as a blob, the time, "38 m from pin" or why there is no location, "taken earlier") and **Record**. Visits are matched by (depot, truck, load number, stop), so a superseded version shows the same physical results.
- **Record outcome** (`POST /api/dispatch/outcomes`, `lib/delivery/office-service.ts`, `outcome-dialog.tsx`): the dispatcher records or corrects a result on any stop of a load that left, at any time (a driver without a phone, a forgotten stop, a wrong tap): result, reason, note, cases per line, optional Arrived / Left (HH:MM, stored as DISPATCHER events; the boxes show the stored times and only a changed box is sent; the newest office entry overrides the phone's; Left needs an arrival before it, 422 otherwise), Clear result. Stored as source DISPATCHER with the user id and a key `disp:<uuid>` (a double click records once); its time is now, never at or before a result already stored, so a correction always wins. Audited `DELIVERY_OUTCOME_SET` with before and after (`correction: true`). The office is not held to "photo required". A load that reported Back at depot closes once this was its last missing result.
- **The basis rule on the office side** (spec 9.4). A correction that would shrink cases already brought forward from that visit answers 409 `OUTCOME_CARRIED` `{ copyId, copyDate, undoable, copies }` and is kept as a `CARRY_CONFLICT` event per copy it would shrink (each audited `DELIVERY_CARRY_CONFLICT`; the first event holds the request's key and the list of copies, so a repeat answers from it). While every such copy is on no plan, the dialog offers **Undo the bring forward and record this result** (`undoCarry: true`: one transaction under the intake, day and outcome-day locks removes the copies and records the result; the answer's `carriesUndone` lists them, `carryUndone` is the first). **All or nothing** (7 Oct 2026): every copy is checked (`undoCheck`) before anything changes; when one of them cannot be removed (planned, on the road, brought forward again, its day being optimized), none is removed and no result is recorded, and the refusal names each copy that blocks it, why and what to do (`carriedRefusalText` in `office-text.ts`; `copies` gives each copy with `undoable` and `code`; `copyId` / `copyDate` are the first copy that blocks). Before, the copies were taken one at a time: with two orders of a stop brought forward, the first copy was removed and committed, then the second (planned) refused the request and the result was not recorded. A planned copy cannot be removed in the app (F12): the answer says to ask an administrator. The copy's day then shows a red chip on its stop ("May not be needed: the 5 Oct result was changed after it was brought forward (to Delivered)"), and Lock of its load asks "... may not be needed ... Lock anyway?" (the PATCH also answers `warnings`); it is never refused.
- **Bring forward reads the results** (`lib/dispatch/carry-over.ts`). `outcomeShortfalls` reads the visits with a result in the window; an order on a load that left (also DISPATCHED) is open again for the cases a Not delivered / Partly result says, matched by (truck, load number, stop) among the depot's own visits on the day's live plan (a result that matches no stop is ignored). The why reads "Not delivered: Shop closed (driver)", "Partly delivered: 6 of 40 cases not delivered: Damaged goods (dispatcher)", "Not delivered: Other - gate locked (driver)". `confirmed` (ticked by default in the Today group) needs every open case recorded as not delivered, every part that left with a result, the truck back (Back at depot or Completed: `final`) and no late result; earlier days stay ticked unless a result was recorded after the trip closed. The row says why it is not ticked ("truck still out, the result may still change", "other part (T03 L1 stop 1) has no result", "recorded after the trip closed"). `bringForward` takes the outcome-day locks after the day locks and before the plans' row locks, writes `Order.carryBasisJson` on the copy (the visits and not-delivered cases per line, also in the `ORDERS_CARRIED_OVER` row) and the late reason "Brought forward from 5 Oct: not delivered (Shop closed, driver).". A stop that left with no result still counts as delivered, as before.
- **The panel's information lists**: "Dispatched, no result recorded (counted as delivered)" per truck (stops of loads that are back: an earlier day's, or today's Completed, Back at depot or past the planned return + 60 min; only from `outcomesSince`, or a truck-day with a link or a visit); "Not delivered after it was brought forward: 15 cases of GAMMA (T03 L1 stop 1, Customer refused) - add a late order for 6 Oct"; the copies on the day that no plan refers to yet and that were not brought forward again, each with **Undo** (`POST /api/dispatch/carry-over/undo`, `undoCarry`: the original's carry fields are cleared first, then the copy deleted; 409 `COPY_PLANNED` / `COPY_ON_ROAD` / `COPY_CARRIED_AGAIN` / `PLAN_BUSY`). The toast after Bring forward says the orders of today recorded as not delivered need nothing on today's plan.
- **The day screen's Deliveries card** (`getDayOverview().deliveries`, `delivery-summary.tsx`): "212 of 300 stops have a result · 196 delivered in full · 9 partly · 7 not delivered · 88 no result yet", the reasons with their cases, "Arrived inside the window 91 % (of 140 observed arrivals)", the "Camera not working" box (below), "Recorded after the trip closed 1", the no-result list of loads that are back with Record, the late-dispatch notes, and the "Delivery actuals (Excel)" download, for the day or a From / To range (the last 7 days to start with, at most 31). The card is not read again on the day's 3-second polls while a search runs (the plan screen's results neither), the screen keeps the one it shows; after Record outcome (on the card or on the plan) both are read at once, also during a search (`readResultsNow`; the day's loads ask with `deliveries=1` until an answer carrying them is shown). A day before the feature started says "Delivery results started on 5 Oct".
- **KPIs** (`lib/delivery/kpis.ts`, pure): delivered in full %, cases delivered %, not delivered by reason (Not delivered plus the missing cases of Partly), arrivals inside the window (observed arrivals only - automatic ones the page saw, manual, office, Ayun later - not flagged; an early arrival that waits counts as inside; an open end is unbounded), the average unloading delta, no result, and (5 Oct 2026) the results saved without a photo (`cameraFailed`, `photoNotReceived`, `withoutPhoto`, `withoutPhotoPct` of Delivered + Partly, `cameraAlertDays`: truck-days with 3 or more; counted whatever the stop's result is now). In scope only from the local date of `TenantConfig.outcomesSince`, or for a truck-day with a link or a visit. The dashboard has a **Deliveries** tile for the last 7 and 30 days (with the "Saved without a photo" line: the share, Camera not working and photo not received).
- **Measured unloading** (`lib/delivery/measured.ts`, `customer-stats.ts`): per customer the median of the last 10 visits timed automatically from the service start (the window start when the truck waited), 3 needed; delivered or partly only; unverified, late, unobserved, across-the-break and outlier visits (under 1 min, over min(240, plan + 60)) left out; the per-case part taken off, so it is the BASE time, comparable with the planned (effective) one. Each customer's own newest 20 timed visits are read (one small query per customer, 8 at a time), never a limit shared by many customers. Shown in the customer dialog on Daily dispatch ("Unloading: 20 min planned · measured 34 min (median of 7 timed visits, 12 Sep - 3 Oct)", **Use measured time** fills the field; Save keeps it) and in a column of the Customers page (**Use measured time** saves it as confirmed after a question). Nothing changes by itself.
- **Pin may be wrong** (`lib/delivery/pin-check.ts`, `GET /api/customers/pin-check`, company admin, a panel on the Customers page): a visit's evidence is the median of its photo points with an OK position (Geolocation, else EXIF), else its manual arrival point, else its result point, each 100 m accurate or better (an automatic arrival is never evidence); a customer is flagged when at least 2 of its last 3 visits are "far": evidence more than 150 m from the visit's planned pin, or the driver reported "wrong location" (one report alone is not enough; the panel lists such a visit as "wrong location", never with its near distance). Unverified visits and visits planned at an older pin (moved more than 50 m since) are left out; after the location retention the stored distances still count. A suggested point opens in Google Maps; the admin uses Set location (the location lock stays).
- **Delivery actuals Excel** (`GET /api/dispatch/delivery-actuals`, PLANNER, 31 days at most, `lib/delivery/actuals-workbook.ts`): Stops (date, depot, truck, hired, trip, stop, customer, driver, daily driver, planned ETA, window, actual arrival, arrival by, inside window, minutes early / late, planned and actual unloading (the plan screen's figure, `actualMinutes`: automatic, else the office's or the manual times), waiting before the window, timed by (what the actual figure is), unverified timing, result, reason, note, cases planned / delivered / not delivered, brought forward to, recorded after the trip closed, photos, no photo reason (*Camera failed (driver)*, *Photo not received*, *Office result*), "Saved without a photo" (Yes: the row amber), "Saved without a photo: changed after" (*corrected by office: Not delivered*, ...), "Driver link: saved without a photo that day" (3 or more in red), photo location and distance, arrival distance, recorded by, result time), Summary (the KPIs, with the camera count, share and alert days), **Without photo** (5 Oct 2026: every result saved without a photo with date, depot, truck, trip, stop, customer, driver, why, the driver's result and the time he saved it, what changed after, the link's count) and Reasons. No money.
- **Retention janitor** (`lib/jobs/delivery-janitor.ts`, from the janitor loop at most every 10 min and the cron route): photo bytes after `photoRetentionDays` by the server's `receivedAt` (metadata kept); positions, IPs and browser ids of events, visits and photos after `locationRetentionDays` (never longer than the photo retention; every distance kept, `gpsAt` removed from the payload); daily drivers without a load for 30 days hidden (active false), their phone erased after the location retention (their name stays). Batches of 200, at most 5 per sweep; one audit row per company and sweep that changed something. The backups keep deleted data until they expire ([`docs/admin.md`](./admin.md)).
- **"Camera not working", monitored** (owner decision 2 of 5 Oct 2026: allowed "but needs to be monitored and documented well"; `lib/delivery/camera-exceptions.ts`, pure). It reads the driver's OWN last Delivered or Partly result, kept on the visit apart from the current result (`StopVisit.driverResultAt`, `driverResultOutcome`, `driverNoPhotoReason`, `driverPhotoKeys`, rebuilt from the events not written by the office: `driverFacts` in `lib/delivery/visit.ts`; migration `20261005100000_results_without_photo`). Two kinds (`noPhotoKind`): **Camera not working** - that result was saved with `noPhotoReason` CAMERA_FAILED (`isCameraException`; Not delivered never counts) - and **photo not received** - it named a photo, no photo of the stop arrived, and none can arrive any more (`awaitsPhoto` and `photoWaitOver`: the truck-day's link revoked, or reissued after the result, past its upload time, or the load COMPLETED for `PHOTO_WAIT_AFTER_COMPLETED_MIN` (60); `photoWaitOverOf` reads the links and loads); a photo that still arrives takes the stop off. An office Record never changes the driver facts, so a corrected stop stays on every list, count, KPI and Excel row, marked *corrected by office* (`noPhotoAfterText`: also *changed by the driver: ...*, *result cleared*, *photo received later*); only the driver's own new Delivered / Partly with a photo replaces it (review of 5 Oct 2026: before, a Record took the stop off everything and the 3-a-day alert). Every one is listed (`cameraExceptionOf`: truck, trip, stop, customer, driver, the time the driver saved it, why, what changed after) on the day screen's Deliveries card (`DayDeliveries.cameraExceptions`, `dayCameraExceptions`) and on the plan screen (`OutcomeOverlay.cameraExceptions`; the plan version page shows the box, the day screen leaves it to the card right below: `showCameraList={false}`). A driver link (one per truck-day) with `CAMERA_ALERT_PER_DAY` (3) or more in a day is red: the alert line ("T05 (Salim): Camera not working used 3 times on 5 Oct - check the phone's camera with the driver."), a **No photo 3× today** badge on the load row (`OverlayLoad.cameraFailedToday`), counted over every depot of that day (`cameraCountsByTruckDay`). The KPIs, the dashboard and the actuals Excel above carry it too. The audit: `DELIVERY_OUTCOME_SET` and the OUTCOME stop event keep `noPhotoReason`; an office Record's `beforeJson` also keeps the replaced result's `outcomeSource`, `noPhotoReason` and `photoCount`, and its `afterJson` the driver's `driverNoPhotoReason` / `driverResultOutcome`. The plan's stop note says *no photo: camera failed (driver), corrected by office*. The dispatcher guide also warns that a **Reissue link** drops the photos still waiting on the old phone (unless the new link is opened on it). The dispatcher guide says what to check every day and the operations manager's weekly review; the driver guide (English and Arabic) says it is recorded and checked.
- **Audit log page**: a row without a user shows `afterJson.actor` ("Driver link: Salim (T05, 5 Oct) · link #2") in the user column, and the search finds it.
- **GPS (Ayun)** (spec 17; built 16 Oct 2026, see [3.21](#321-gps-live-link-ayun-times-live-map-tracker-mapping)): GPS stop events go into `StopEvent` with source AYUN and keys `ayun:A|D:...`; `deriveVisit` gives them their own cycles and lets the office and the driver win; they never write a result, never complete a load, never feed the measured unloading times, and count as on time only at a Delivered or Partly stop. The ingest is built: live positions of the trucks out for the map (`TruckPosition`), the trucks' history pulled per truck-day for times (`TruckTrailPoint`), depot moves from Ayun's webhook and its backstop (`IvmsEvent`), each call counted against the provider's daily allowance per class (`IvmsState`).

### 3.19 The hire suggestion

Owner request (6 Oct 2026): "when the day's orders are more than the fleet can carry, RouteIQ should not only list the undeliverable orders; it should tell the dispatcher how many and which trucks to RENT, e.g. hire 1 x 10-ton + 1 x 3-ton, assuming the constraints are set correctly". NMWC rents trucks from outside sometimes and uses casual drivers. Branch `hire-suggestion`; migration `20261006120000_hire_suggestion` (additive, nothing seeded). **Owner answers (6 Oct 2026, binding):** (1) only P1-P3 orders justify renting - never a hire whose only gain is P4/P5 orders, though a rented truck carries P4/P5 orders once rented for P1-P3 ones, and the box says plainly when only P4/P5 orders are left out; (2) a rental is for the whole day (as many loads as max loads per truck); (3) fuel is included in the rental price - no fuel or km cost for a rented truck (only the option's own km charge, 0 by default); (4) casual drivers are paid a day rate, the company setting **Daily driver day rate** (`TenantConfig.dailyDriverDayRate`, admin, default 10 OMR); own trucks keep their hourly driver cost; (5) codes `HIRE-...` and plates without spaces as built.

- **Hire options** (`HireOption`, company admin, the Trucks page's **Trucks to hire**, `GET|POST /api/hire-options`, `PATCH|DELETE /api/hire-options/:id`): per depot a label, bays (or a case capacity), payload (0 = no limit), cost per day (fuel included), the rental's own km charge (`costPerKm`; null = none, never the fleet's km cost or fuel), max per day, active. The max per day counts the day's one-day trucks of the option wherever they are (`rentedOnDay` by option alone), and an option trucks are hired from for today or a later day is neither deleted nor moved to another depot (409 `HIRE_OPTION_IN_USE`, `liveRentalDays`; switching it off stays possible) - third review of the hire branch: the cleared link or the other depot no longer counted the rented truck, so the day could be rented past the max. Review of ISSUE 7: the check and the delete or move were apart, so one sent while **Use this plan** rented from the option waited for its lock and then deleted or moved it over the trucks just rented (their link cleared); both now take the option's row FOR UPDATE and count the rentals under it (409 `HIRE_OPTION_BUSY` after 5 s).
- **When a check runs.** After a job saved a plan (OPTIMIZE or RE-PLAN, any day) whose option in use leaves **P1-P3** stops out (`needsHireCheck(unserved, scope.orderPriority)`: a stop's priority is its most important order's; only P4/P5 stops left out: `NOT_SHORT` with the owner's words, `lowPriorityText`, and the box shows them, `HireView.lowNote`) for a reason a truck more can help (`CAPACITY_REASONS`: `SOLVER_DROPPED_LOW_PRIORITY` - the fleet-shortage, no-room, timing and open-drop reasons -, `LATE_ORDER_NO_CAPACITY`, `TRIP_LIMIT`, `NO_AVAILABLE_TRUCK`, `SHIFT_LIMIT`, `HARD_WINDOW_INFEASIBLE` - the solver's window check tries the depot's own trucks from when each is free, so an order no own truck reaches because they are out on locked loads reads so although a rented truck reaches it; the what-if's own check decides -, `EXCEEDS_ANY_TRUCK_CAPACITY`; the web's pre-drops - no location, deactivated customer, a case heavier than any truck - never count), the day is not over (`DAY_OVER`), and the depot has active options: `startHireCheckAfterPlan` (`dispatch-job.ts`, after the job's ticket is released; a check that cannot start leaves its reason for the box, `skipNote`). The dispatcher can run it with **Check hire options** (`POST /api/runs/:id/hire-suggestion`). One check per version at a time: the "already running" test and the create are one step under an advisory lock of the version (`hire-check:<tenant>|<run>`), and the admission ticket is taken before the row, so an optimizer too busy for it (`BUSY`) leaves no row. A check that waited for a slot looks at its version again when it gets one (superseded, optimizing or another option in use: CANCELLED, never run). Each depot-day keeps one check waiting (`reserveBackground(..., hireCheckKey(depot, date))`, at most `BACKGROUND_TENANT_WAITING` (5) per company; review: one per company lost the third depot's check of a company optimizing three depots in quick succession). No check when every P1-P3 order the plan left out is gone from the day since and none was added (`hireNeed` on the built request: `NOTHING_LEFT`; review: it read "0 orders (0 cases) cannot be delivered" and asked to check again). It is recorded as a check that did not run - a CANCELLED row with `errorJson.reason` `NOTHING_LEFT`, audited `HIRE_CHECK_FINISHED`, once per version (`recordNothingLeft`) - so the box stays quiet for that version after a restart too (third review: the process note alone was lost with a deploy or after 10 minutes, and the box came back saying no check had run).
- **The what-if** (`startHireCheck`, `lib/dispatch/hire-whatif.ts`): the request a re-plan of that version would send (`buildDispatchRequest(..., ['RECOMMENDED'], { withPallets })`: frozen loads stay exactly as they are; `withPallets` when an option has bays, so every stop carries its pallet need; products without cases per pallet: `PALLET_FACTORS`, not run) with the customers' split parts sized with every truck the day may still rent too (`splitFleet`: `hireSplitFleet`; fix of 7 Oct 2026: the parts were cut for the own fleet before the bigger trucks to rent were added, each part a visit of the full stop time, so a 300-case order on 100-case own trucks went as three visits and the check rented two 300-case trucks for 120 OMR - or left 100 cases out with one to rent - where one visit on one truck, 60 OMR, delivered it; **Use this plan** reads the day again the same way, `HireBasis.splitWithHires`, and the plan in use's left-out parts count as the what-if's stops that hold their orders, `alignUnserved`), plus one truck per unit the day may still rent (`hireTrucksForRequest`: max per day less the one-day trucks already rented from the option for that date; virtual ids `hire~<optionId>~<n>`, placeholder codes `HIRE-<tag>-<k>` numbered per size tag across the request - review: two options tagged 10T both sent `HIRE-10T-1` and a finding about one named the other -, `hire_candidate: true`, the option's size, its hire as `fixed_cost`, fuel included - `km_per_litre` null, `cost_per_km` the option's own km charge or 0 -, `driver_day_cost` the company's daily driver day rate (`PlanSettings.dailyDriverDayRate`), the fleet's average trip cost (`fleetAverages`: loading only)), the recommended plan only, QUICK. Its own job and a background admission ticket ([2.7](#27-background-job-model)): it never delays or changes the dispatcher's plan.
- **The optimizer: the hire tier** (`dispatch_solver._service_and_hire`, `_hire_tier`): a truck to rent is ranked in a level of the strict service values between the P1-P3 and the P4/P5 stops, in proportion to its real money for the day, `hire_money` = hire + driver day rate + its option's own km charge over a rough day's km (`_hire_day_km`: a round trip of the day's average road distance from the depot - straight line x the road factor - for every load it may make; third review of the hire branch: an option at 50 OMR + 1 OMR/km beat one at 60 OMR with no km charge on a far day, 238 OMR instead of 70; this rough day is for the search's ranking only - the reduction below never rules a set out or keeps one by it, BUG 5 of 7 Oct 2026): u = 1 + the weight of every P4/P5 stop (with margins one more each), a rented truck weighs u x its money in units of `res` OMR (at least one unit), and every P1-P3 weight carries the dearest rented truck's tier on top (`_strict_weights(..., hire_top)`). `res` is 1 OMR, or the finest coarser one (`HIRE_RESOLUTIONS`: 2, 5, 10 ... OMR) that keeps the strict weights uncapped on a day whose own weights are (third review: the tier multiplied them by the money, 60-150, and a 450-stop day got capped priorities - one P1 worth about 7 P2 - in the what-if only); the ranking between options stays in proportion to their money. So P4/P5 stops alone never rent a truck (1 OMR of hire outweighs all of them; once rented for P1-P3 stops it carries P4/P5 stops in its spare room); one P1-P3 stop is always worth the dearest rented truck; the cheapest set in money wins - two small trucks when they cost less than one big one, and the other way round (review of the hire branch: the earlier premium on every rented truck, the dearest own day + 100 OMR, chose a 10-ton at 85 OMR over two 3-tons at 60); and own trucks always go first, an idle own truck never replaced by a rented one however dear its day or km (their whole money is far below 1 OMR of the tier). The tier is in the routing model's vehicle fixed cost (`_vehicle_fixed_units`, scaled like the drop penalties, `_penalty_mult`; an own truck is priced exactly as before), in the post-solve `Score.hire` (`TruckPrice.hire`; every goal compares `Score.service` = service value lost + hire tier first, and the raw plan's own service counts its rented trucks, `_plan_hire`), in the repack's phase 1 (`TruckPrice.hire_w`, `_hire_repair_weights`: an unused rented truck is opened for P1-P3 stops only; the P1-P3 repair weights carry the dearest on top) and in the second search's prizes and vehicle types. The weighted-priority scheme (never sent by the web) keeps the tier too (`_weighted_hire`). Search only: the plan reports the real costs. A driver paid by the day (`DispatchTruck.driver_day_cost`: the rented trucks and the one-day hired trucks): that rate once per truck day with its first new load (`costing.TruckRates.driver_day`; none with frozen loads), no hourly pay or overtime on that truck (routing span cost, the timing LP, the repack, PyVRP's duration cost). A rented truck has no fuel (no km per litre) and no km cost unless its option charges per km. Such a truck cost nothing per km or per hour in the search, so its stops were left in any order (third review: 358 km instead of 232); its km and time get a **search-only tie-breaker** at a TINY price - `HIRE_TIE_KM_OMR` 0.001 OMR per km on top of its own km charge (`_search_km_rate`) and `HIRE_TIE_HOUR_OMR` 0.036 OMR an hour on its span (`_tie_span_units`: 1 objective unit a second, the smallest whole rate the routing models take) - in the routing model, PyVRP, the repack and the timing LP (`TruckPrice.tie_m` / `tie_span`), scored apart from money (`Score.tie`), compared LAST in every goal - RECOMMENDED (service, cost, tie), MIN DISTANCE (service, metres, cost, tie), MIN TRUCKS (service, trucks, loads, operating, cost, tie) - so it only orders that truck's stops and never outweighs a real OMR of saving, while the plan reports no km cost and the day rate (fourth review: priced at the own fleet's average km rate and the hourly driver rate, and added to the cost, it kept a hired 10-ton on the near stops and sent an own truck 160 km at 0.2 OMR/km - 139 OMR instead of 103). That tiny price decides which truck carries what, but within such a truck's loads the customers' time preferences outweighed it (fifth review: with the default early-arrival preference one minute earlier at a P1 order, 0.01 OMR, was worth 10 km, and on a ring of P1, P3 and P2 orders the hired truck drove its P1 orders first - 340 km instead of 250, back at 16:30 instead of 14:16, the what-if plan too). So once each option's plan is picked (`_post_solve`: after the pick, so never which truck carries what), `_shorter_orders` / `load_repack.shorter_orders` route the day of each rented or day-paid truck again with the SAME per-km and per-hour costs as an own truck's - for routing only, never money: its km at `_order_km_rate` (the average km rate of the request's own trucks, or `HIRE_ORDER_KM_OMR` 0.1 OMR/km when none has one) and its paid day at the hourly driver rate (`Pricing.span`). First **which of its stops go on which of its loads** (sixth review of the hire branch: a rented truck making two loads still criss-crossed the area - 249 km where an own truck drives 185 - because only the stops inside each load were re-ordered): `_day_proposals` proposes days of no more loads than it has - the shortest round of all its stops cut into loads that fit the truck (`_split`, route first, cluster second; the loads in their best order in the day) and its own loads, each improved by a local search on a whole-day estimate (`_day_estimate`, `_day_moves`: a stop moved anywhere in the day, two stops of two loads swapped, a run reversed, the ends of two loads exchanged, two loads swapped in the day; a customer's split parts stay together) -; then the order inside each load (a local search - 2-opt and moving one stop - from the shortest order found, from it the other way round and from the load's own order). Each proposal is timed exactly with the truck's other loads (`time_truck`: every hard rule, the driver break), and taken only when the truck drives fewer metres, costs no more money and its time preferences + those km and hours are lower. Same trucks and stops (never more loads); at most `HIRE_ORDER_SEC` 3 s per chosen plan and three times that per request, in-process (Python and LPs only), each truck its share; the plan reports the new day's score; a day without rented or day-paid trucks keeps the very same plan; the safety net (`_retime`) keeps the search's order.
- **The optimizer: the reduction** (`dispatch_solver._reduce_hire`, sixth review of the hire branch: on the real Muscat day - 80 orders, three own 10-tons - the Quick search rented 2 x 10-ton although the same request with ONE 10-ton to rent delivered all 25 P1-P3 orders left out and passed the timing check: the second only carried P4/P5 orders, and the set was not the cheapest; emptying a rented truck needs all its stops moved at once and each move alone gains nothing, so the search stops in such a local optimum). After the search (`optimize_dispatch`, only for a request with trucks to rent), first with **no solve**, every rented truck whose loads carry no P1-P3 stop is given back (`_without_low_hires`, owner answer 1): its loads deleted, its stops left out, every other load as it was (the same stops and order, timed again exactly - each truck's day is timed on its own - and checked; seventh review of the hire branch: on a big day the budget allowed one solve or none, and such a truck stayed) - but its stops go back on the trucks kept with no solve where they fit (`_swap_riders`): with nothing taken off into free room (eleventh review: a P4/P5 order went into free room only when it outranked a stop the trucks kept carry, so adding a P5 order to the 10-ton kept got two P4 orders delivered), or in place of stops it **outranks** (`_outranks`: strictly a higher priority, weighted a higher weight than those taken off together; a P4 order, P5 orders riding along; tenth review: the give-back of a 10-ton carrying a P4 order alone left it out while the 10-ton kept carried two P5 orders it had the room for in their place - strict priorities never drop a P4 order to carry two P5s): highest priority first, into the load where it fits with the fewest such stops taken off (the lowest priority first, the biggest first; never a P1-P3 stop), or on a load to spare, the fewest km added - the places timed in that order (that truck's whole day timed again exactly) and the first that can be timed taken, a stop taken off put back the same way with nothing taken off for it (eleventh review: every load kept was timed for every stop, and the fixed 400 timings ran out on a give-back of 30 P4 orders with 17 loads kept, X28 and X29 left out while P5 orders rode; now each stop may time `HIRE_SWAP_TIMINGS_PER` (2) places for each load the trucks hold (a load to spare counted too) of its own, then draws on a pool all share (that many for each stop given back, `HIRE_SWAP_MIN_TIMINGS` (400) at least), about one a stop in practice, and a give-back that runs out is logged and never *complete*; twelfth review: the budget was one pool, and 30 P4 orders received only after the own trucks' day ends timed each of their 40 places and used it up, so the P4 order Y0 that fit in place of a P5 order was cut while the P5 orders rode along - now a stop that fits nowhere never uses up another's timings, a place is never timed when its load cannot leave and be back within the truck's day for its stops' receiving hours (`load_repack.depart_range`) nor any place on a truck whose day cannot hold the stop's hours at all (the shortest drives into and out of it), and on a truck of a plan kept as found whose day cannot be timed only a place that takes stops off, when its day with all of them off can be timed); an own truck the plan leaves idle takes them too, on a load of its own, never a truck to rent that is not kept (twelfth review: own trucks first - two P5 orders stayed out while a 3-ton of the company stood idle); that plan is taken when it breaks no check the plan without them passes and serves the day better (`_service_rank`). A stop that fits nowhere even with them off stays out and they stay on: they do not keep it out. A P4/P5 stop the plan given back leaves out reads `HIRE_DROP_HEAD` ("Not planned: a truck is not rented for P4/P5 orders alone, and the trucks used had no room or time left ...") with one warning, never counted with the stops the optimizer could not place (twelfth review: it read "could not be placed by the optimizer ... add a truck", asking for the truck just given back). A plan the post-solve stage kept as the search found it (feasibility VIOLATED: its load re-check skipped and its re-time failed - big days, which get no solve) cannot be timed again: it is given back from its **own times** (`_no_worse_checks`), every other truck's day exactly as it was, so it breaks nothing the plan did not, and a truck the swap changes is still timed exactly (eleventh review: it kept its truck for P5 orders alone, and the box read "hire 3 x 10-ton: extra about 150 OMR" with one of them for P5 orders alone).
