Then the **cheapest set** (seventh review: leaving the dearest truck out first kept 2 x 3-ton for 80 OMR, *complete*, where the 10-ton alone delivered every order for 60, and never swapped a rented truck for a cheaper one the plan did not use - 1 x 10-ton kept where 1 x 3-ton sufficed): every set of the trucks to rent - how many units of each option, the plan's own units first; units of one option are alike - whose LEAST cost is below what the plan's rented trucks really cost (as much with fewer trucks), as many trucks as it takes (eighth review: capped at the plan's count, 1 x 10-ton at 85 OMR stayed where 2 x 3-ton at 80 delivered every order, *complete*; at most `HIRE_REDUCE_MAX_SETS` sets are listed, past it the set is not *complete*), is tried by that least cost, cheapest first, fewer trucks first on a tie. **Money (BUG 5, 7 Oct 2026)**: a set's least cost (`_hire_floor_money`) is each truck's hire + driver day rate + its option's km charge over the fewest km a used truck drives (`_hire_km_floor`: out of the depot to the stop nearest to it and back from the stop nearest to it on the request's own road matrix, less 0.01 km for the km a plan rounds; every load leaves the depot for a stop and comes back from one, so no truck that carries a stop drives less) - never above what any plan pays for that set; a plan is judged by what its rented trucks really cost (`_hire_routed_money`: hire + day rate + the km charge on the km their loads drive). Before, sets were ranked and kept by the search's rough day (`_hire_day_km`: the average distance to ALL the day's customers for every load), so a rental that would only serve a near customer was priced as if it drove to the far ones, and the first set that passed was kept: 123.13 OMR suggested where another set with the same deliveries and the same truck for each customer cost 87.59, and that set was never tried, *complete*. A set that passes is kept only when no set left untried can cost less: the walk goes on past a set that delivers while an untried set's least cost is below the best real cost found (a set that delivers but costs more on its km is tried and passed over), within the same solve limit and window. A flat-rate option (no km charge, how production is set today) costs the same least, rough and routed - its hire + day rate - so a flat-rate day lists, orders, solves and keeps exactly as before (the walk stops right after the first set that delivers). A set whose trucks cannot hold the P1-P3 stops the plan delivers even with every load they may make full (pallets, cases or kg: `_hire_room_short`) is ruled out without a solve; any other is solved with exactly the own trucks and that set (`_hire_trial`: the same road matrix, stops and pre-filter, its own worker pool and second search, rule 22). The cheapest (by real cost, BUG 5) plan that passes every check (OPTIMIZED, feasibility VERIFIED, and its load re-check ran: `_post_solve`'s `rechecked`) and delivers every P1-P3 stop the plan delivers - its P4/P5 stops may stay out - is the suggestion (once more without a truck that then carries only P4/P5 stops) - unless such a truck cannot be given back (its plan cannot be built) while the plan held rents none: the walk then goes on, and that plan's trucks for P1-P3 orders, when cheaper than the set suggested, leave it not *complete* (tenth review: that plan, renting a 3-ton for P5 orders alone, was the suggestion, *complete*). A solve whose load re-check was skipped (out of time) neither replaces the plan nor rules its set out. **A solve that leaves a P1-P3 order out while it carries lower priorities proves nothing** (thirteenth review, the real-size demo on `7c3115a`: on the real Muscat day with two own loads locked, the solve of 1 x 10-ton came back with a P3 order left out while it carried a P4/P5 order more in its place - the time-limited repack after the search made that swap - and ruled the 10-ton out: *hire 2 x 3-ton*, 60 OMR + 2 day rates, *complete*, where 1 x 10-ton, 50 OMR + 1, delivered every P1-P3 order in 4 of 4 replays): every plan the reduction judges - each solve's in every step, *one truck fewer* included, and the search's own plan first when it passes the checks - is **repaired with no solve** before it is judged (`_repair_lost`): the P1-P3 stops it leaves out go back where they fit, first by the give-back's swap (`_swap_riders`: into free room, or in place of the stops of one load they outrank, the truck's whole day timed again exactly), then, for one still out, with every stop it outranks taken off one truck's whole day (`_in_place_of_riders`: a load can be held up by another load of the same day), those stops put back where they fit, and failing that by a **chain of two moves** (`_in_chain`: in place of one other stop of a load - the smallest first, any priority - and the stops of that load it outranks, the stop taken out going on another place where it fits; in replays of the real day under load the 10-ton's solve left one P3 order (1.95 pallets) out while P4/P5 orders rode, no load took it even with them off, and it went into an own truck's last load in place of its P4 order and a 0.14-pallet P3 order that fitted on another load - every P1-P3 order delivered, VERIFIED); on a solve's trucks, those it left idle too. The plan so repaired is built and checked as every plan (`_rebuilt`, a truck it does not change keeping its times) and taken when it passes the checks and serves the day better. A solve that still leaves a P1-P3 stop out while a lower priority rides on its trucks **proves nothing** - the moves tried may miss a longer chain (in a replay of the real day the solve of 1 x 10-ton left another P3 order out while a P4/P5 order more rode along and no truck's day took it even with every lower priority off - before the chain of two moves; the next solve delivered every P1-P3 order): that set is solved once more if the limits allow, and while it stays unproven it never rules its set out (the set suggested is then not *complete*) nor tells *one truck fewer*; a solve that leaves one out with no lower priority riding along rules its set out as before. The repair's tries with every lower priority off a truck's day stop after `HIRE_REPAIR_SEC` (10 s, within the request's budget). When trucks were given back (first, or from that plan), the **set left is solved** once more if the limits allow, every earlier solve could run, and no solve of a set alike was made (eighth review: the give-back was the whole step, so the P4/P5 orders of the truck given back were dropped although the 10-ton kept had 6 free bays and 2 loads to spare - and *Use this plan* applied that plan as it was): its plan must pass every check and keep every P1-P3 stop; then, again without a truck that carries only P4/P5 stops, it replaces the give-back when its set is **cheaper** in real money - even serving fewer P4/P5 stops - or as cheap and serving more **as the day's priorities rank it** (`_service_rank`: strictly the stops served per priority, P1 first; weighted, their weights), or as cheap at all when the give-back fails the checks (a plan kept as the search found it, given back from its own times: eleventh review - that set was then no longer a cheaper one to try) (ninth review: money was never compared, so the solve proved 1 x 10-ton enough and 2 x 10-ton for 120 OMR stayed, *complete*, *one truck fewer* saying an order stays out; and raw stop counts let it drop a P4 order to carry two P5s). A plan that still has such a truck (its give-back could not be built) never replaces it, and the set is then not *complete*. Otherwise the give-back without a solve stays, also with time to spare, and a plan built again by it keeps the reason and warning of the stops its load re-check left out for the loading time (`_timing_drops_of`, `TIMING_DROP_HEAD`). **One truck fewer** is a solve of the suggested set less one truck: the one whose removal lost the fewest P1-P3 stops, then the dearest; when the solves hold none for its least useful truck (the least room in one measure for every truck to rent, `_hire_room`: pallets when they all have bays, else cases - eighth review: a truck entered by cases always looked the smallest), that set is solved once more if the limits allow; when that solve keeps every P1-P3 stop and passes every check, its set - cheaper - is the suggestion, given back as above (tenth review: it was thrown away, so 2 x 10-ton for 120 OMR stayed where the solve had proven one enough), and *one truck fewer* is then told from the solves so far only. Budget (seventh review: a solve started with its search time + 23 s had no load re-check, and its raw plan became the suggestion; a 200-350-stop day had room for one solve, a day above 350 stops none): a solve starts only with room for its worker, its search, the search's overhead and the load re-check's whole reserve (`_hire_trial_need`: the search + `HIRE_TRIAL_START_SEC` 5 + `REC_OVERHEAD_SEC` 20 + `STAGE_GRACE_SEC` 20 + 5 + the CP-SAT time); it searches as long as the what-if up to `HIRE_TRIAL_FULL_SEC` (20 s), half as long above it (never less), shortened to what is left down to half of that again (`_hire_trial_limit`); at most `HIRE_REDUCE_MAX_SOLVES` (6) solves within `HIRE_REDUCE_SEC` (180 s) or `HIRE_REDUCE_WINDOW_SOLVES` (2) full solves when that is longer (`_hire_reduce_window`: a 150 s day's solves search 75 s in a 280 s window), and never past the request's budget; a cancel ends the solve, a stop request the reduction. The response's `hire_check` (`HireCheck`): `first` (the search's rented trucks), `used` (the RECOMMENDED plan's, returned in its place; another option's units when they are cheaper), `solves`, `complete` (worked out for the set suggested: every set whose least cost is below its real cost listed and ruled out by its room, a checked solve of a set alike that, once repaired, still lost a P1-P3 stop with no lower priority riding along - thirteenth review -, or a solve of a set alike that delivered at a real cost no lower (BUG 5), no plan a solve proved with cheaper trucks for P1-P3 orders whose give-back could not be built, no truck for P4/P5 orders alone in the suggestion - tenth review: such a suggestion was *complete* -, and its give-back's swap had a timing for every stop it tried - eleventh review), `one_fewer` (`without`, the stops that plan leaves out, as repaired; never from a solve that proved nothing; a solve of one truck fewer that delivers but costs more on its km is not taken), `note` (BUG 5: `HIRE_NOT_PROVEN_NOTE`, "Not proven the cheapest: the hire check ran out of time or tries before it could check every set of trucks to rent that might cost less once its km charge is counted. A cheaper set may exist - press Check hire options to check again." - when such sets are left untried and an option has a km charge; then `complete` is false too; none on a flat-rate day, whose `complete` is as before). Measured on a synthetic 80-stop day shaped like the demo (P1 6, P2 20, P3 38, P4 10, P5 6; three own 10-tons with two loads each; 3 x 10-ton and 2 x 3-ton to rent; Haversine, second search off, Quick 20 s): the search alone rented 2 x 10-ton + 2 x 3-ton (200 OMR of hire and day rates), the reduction kept 1 x 10-ton + 1 x 3-ton (100 OMR), every P1-P3 order delivered, VERIFIED, in 4 extra solves and 90 s (112 s for the whole check). `apps/solver/tests/test_hire.py`.
- **The suggestion** (`summarizeHire`, `hireSuggestionText`, stored as `summaryJson` and the row's `message`): what the plan in use leaves out for the capacity reasons ("14 orders (1,180 cases, 17.6 pallets) cannot be delivered with your fleet"), the rented trucks the what-if used per option ("hire 1 x 10-ton (12 bays) + 1 x 3-ton (6 bays)"), their hire for the day ("extra about 80 OMR"), what is still left out ("none", or the orders and "even with every truck you can rent they do not fit ..."), the running-costs line of the rented trucks (`HireSummary.running`: "Plus about 25 OMR running costs on the hired trucks: 2 drivers at the day rate of 10 OMR, loading about 5 OMR. Fuel is included in the hire." - the rental's km charge only when its option has one, never fuel or the fleet's km), the P4/P5 orders left out apart (`HireSummary.low`: "Also left out: 4 orders, all P4/P5 - renting is not suggested for them; this plan still delivers 1 of them with the hired trucks.") and - with two or more rented trucks - **one truck fewer**, only from the optimizer's own solve of the suggested set less its least useful truck (`hire_check.one_fewer`; sixth review of the hire branch: the estimate of before - the what-if's own loads, *up to* what the dropped truck carried or made room for - said "up to 25 orders stay undelivered" on the real day where a plan with one truck fewer left no P1-P3 order out): the P1-P3 orders that plan leaves out (never one no truck helps; the orders still left out with the hire included are said so, `still`) and the P4/P5 orders this plan delivers that it leaves out, apart ("With one truck fewer (1 x 10-ton (12 bays), extra about 50 OMR): 1 order (100 cases, 1.0 pallets) would stay undelivered - planned without the 3-ton. 2 P4/P5 orders this plan delivers would stay out too."). No such solve (an older solver, out of time): no line; a suggestion stored with the estimate shows none either (`alternative.solved`). `HireSummary.reduction` keeps the reduction's figures (`HIRE_CHECK_FINISHED` too) and its `note` when the optimizer gave one, shown as the box's first detail line (BUG 5: the set is then not proven the cheapest). Counted on the request the what-if used (`hireNeed`; `HireBasis.baseOrders`: the orders the plan in use delivers; an order added after the plan counts - *N of them added after this plan was made* -, one gone since does not); P1-P3 orders only (`HIRE_MAX_PRIORITY`). Nothing left to count: `NOTHING_LEFT_TEXT`, never "0 orders". `OWN_FLEET` when the what-if delivers orders left out with the own trucks alone ("... the hire check fits them on your own trucks: no truck needs to be hired. Re-plan ..."); `NO_HELP` when it delivers none of them. *Still left out* gives its reason only as far as the answer backs it (`stillLeftWhy`: the what-if's reason codes, or every unit the day can rent in use), else "the Quick search did not place them ...". An order the plan in use delivers that the what-if leaves out is `dropped`, said on its own with its priority (`LeftOut.byPriority`, `ordersByPriority`: "But this check leaves out 1 P4 order (3 cases) your current plan delivers", "2 orders (1 P3, 1 P4; 203 cases, 3.0 pallets)" - ninth review of the hire branch: the real-size demo said "1 order (3 cases, 0.0 pallets)"; *Use this plan*'s question says it too), and makes **Use this plan** re-plan. No order count says *0.0 pallets*: under 0.05 pallets (50 units) only the cases are said (`leftOutText`).
- **The box** (`hire-suggestion.tsx`, in `PlanView`, so on the day screen and the plan version page; `GET /api/runs/:id/hire-suggestion`, any role): `hireView` shows the check running, else the newest finished one (a newer FAILED / CANCELLED one after an unused finished suggestion is a note under it, `shownSuggestion`); a suggestion for another plan option than the one in use is not offered (`forOtherOption`); no box for an option that leaves nothing out, and only the owner's line for one that leaves only P4/P5 orders out (`lowNote`, no button); a viewer never reads "press Check hire options", also lowercase or mid-sentence (`forViewer`, review); a day that is over gets no button (`dayOver`). It polls while a check waits or runs or is on its way (`checkExpected`: the plan's job saved its plan less than 20 s ago, or its automatic check is being started), and keeps polling after a failed read - the first one too, saying *Could not refresh the hire check (still trying)* in a box of its own after three (third review: a failed first read left the box out until the page was reloaded). A suggestion whose hire option was switched off or deleted since is not offered: `optionNote` says so (pointing to Check hire options only while the depot has an option left). Otherwise it says *No hire check has run for this plan yet* (with the reason it did not start). One button, **Check hire options**, the one every text names; **Use this plan** when usable. With no hire options and orders left out for the fleet, the dispatcher reads that an admin can enter them.
- **Use this plan** (`applyHireSuggestion`, `lib/dispatch/hire-use.ts`, PLANNER): refused when not finished, already used, hiring nothing, for a version not in use or optimizing, computed for another plan option than the one in use (`HIRE_OTHER_OPTION`, review: a screen opened before **Use instead** applied the check of the other option), a day that is over (`DAY_OVER`), or another day on screen. The day is read again (`buildDispatchRequest` with the same options) and compared with what the what-if was computed from (`staleReasons`: the request's fingerprint - `requestBasisText`: depot, stops, own trucks with their frozen loads, settings without what moves with the clock or the search, the frozen loads' ids -; on the delivery day not more than `SAME_DAY_SLACK_MIN` (10) minutes later; the options used unchanged, their max per day too; no truck of them rented since; the company's daily driver day rate the trucks to rent were priced with unchanged, `HireBasis.dayRate` - third review: a rate changed after the check was not seen, the trucks to rent are not in the fingerprint; the what-if drops no order the plan in use delivers). Both ways ask the weight question first with the trucks to rent in the request (`weightRefusal`: a payload on a truck to hire counts), before anything is rented. Nothing changed: ONE transaction takes the intake lock, the hire codes lock and the day lock (in that order, `plan-locks.ts`), reads the day again under them and compares the fingerprint once more (third review: a colleague's Bring forward or order change committed between the first read and the transaction was applied over - the order planned on two days); changed: it writes nothing and takes the re-plan way (`why` "... changed while the plan was being applied"). Else it claims the suggestion, rents the trucks (`rentTrucks`, under the company lock `hire-codes:<tenant>` so two depots never pick the same code, never past an option's max per day - `HIRE_LIMIT`: one-day trucks `HIRE-<tag>-<DDMM>-<n>`, the smallest free number, `hired`, `onlyOnDate`, `hireOptionId`, the option's size and costs as planned - its km charge or 0, no km per litre; whenever it is planned, `buildDispatchRequest` sends it with the company's day rate, `hiredTruckDriver`), makes the next version (`createNextVersionTx`, reason REOPTIMIZE, note "Hire suggestion: ..."), and saves and applies the what-if's plan on it (`withRentedTrucks`: the rented trucks under their new ids in the loads, the truck days and the optimizer's own timetable findings, their placeholder codes in the findings and warnings under the real ones, no `hire_candidate`; `keepWhatIfTiming`: a same-day plan keeps the first departure and loading start it was computed with - from when the check's search really started (`HireBasis.timedAt`, ISSUE 6; an older row: `builtAt`) -, never the later clock whose timetable check would block its earliest loads; the frozen loads renamed to the copies; `applyWeightChanges`, `persistDispatchResult`, `applyScenario`); then the day's other checks are stopped (`cancelHireChecksOfDay`). Changed: an option switched off or deleted is refused first (`HIRE_OPTION_GONE`, "... switched off or deleted.", pointing to Check hire options only while the depot has an option left), then the re-plan's questions (`replanRefusal`) with the trucks to rent as their options are NOW (`trucksAsOptionsNow`: size, payload, cost per day, own km charge; third review: the truck was rented with the check's old km charge and the weight question asked with the old payload), then the optimizer's admission is reserved (QUICK; refused: 429 / 503 and nothing rented - third review: the trucks were rented and the suggestion used before the admission refused), then the trucks are rented (every figure from the option now) and a QUICK `replan` plans the day with them, starting with that admission ticket (`replan(..., { ticket })`). **Under the transaction's locks, both ways (ISSUE 7, 7 Oct 2026):** everything was checked before the transaction and then rented and applied with what had been read, so a change committed in between was applied over - reproduced: a suggestion used after its hire option was switched off, past an option's newly lowered max per day, and after another plan option was chosen ("Use instead"). Now the transaction that rents takes, after the hire codes lock (and in the plan way the intake and day locks), the plan row FOR UPDATE and the hire options used FOR SHARE (`lockAndRecheck`, the dispatch writers' lock order, [3.14](#314-status-values-and-transitions)) and checks again: the same version, not superseded, not optimizing and no job of it waiting or running, the plan option the suggestion was computed for still in use (`HireBasis.runVersion`, `scenarioId`), and each option used still an active option of the depot with the same size, costs and max per day as the press read (the what-if's options in the plan way, the options now in the re-plan way). Anything changed: 409 `HIRE_CHANGED`, *"The hire options or the plan changed since this suggestion. Press Check hire options again."* (with `why`), nothing rented or applied, the suggestion unused. In the plan way the rest of what the first read decided is read again under the locks too (`staleReasons` on the day read again, review of ISSUE 7: a daily driver day rate changed in between was applied over with the set costed at the old rate): the fingerprint, the same-day timing, the day rate, the options' trucks already rented for the day and the orders the check's plan leaves out - changed: nothing written, the re-plan way, as when changed before the press. The trucks are made from the options as read under the lock, and the max per day is counted under the hire codes lock (`HIRE_LIMIT`). The re-plan way now takes the hire codes lock before it claims the suggestion, as the plan way does (two presses of one suggestion, one each way, could deadlock). Still outside: the re-plan way's `replan` runs in its own transaction after the trucks are rented, so a re-plan or an optimization started in that moment still ends with the trucks rented and the re-plan refused (`TRUCKS_ONLY`, said plainly).
- **One-day trucks.** `trucksOfDayWhere` (`buildDispatchRequest`, the day screen) plans them on their date only; the janitor retires them after it (`retireOneDayTrucks`); `intake-server`'s pallet-factor check of a depot counts every-day trucks only. The dispatcher enters the real plate (**Plate** on its load; `setHiredTruck`, PLANNER; the API also takes a default driver, which no screen sends - the driver is picked on each load; every other field stays the admin's): the plan, the timetable check, the sheets and the driver page show a one-day truck's code now (`shownTruckCode`), not the code it was planned with. A plate is taken only from a hired truck whose day is over (its code becomes `<plate>.<YYMMDD>`, `freedCode`, audited on that truck too, and its own day still shows the plate - its plans, and since the third review also its delivery results, the Bring forward list, its driver link and the driver page's messages, `shownTruckCode` in `day-results.ts`, `carry-over.ts`, `driver-link/service.ts`, `event-service.ts`, since the fourth review its run's route sheets, map shapes and API, and since the fifth the office's delivery photo downloads, `office-service.ts`); a plate of today's or a coming day's hired truck is refused (`CODE_TAKEN`, "e.g. <plate>-2"). Start fresh removes the one-day trucks of the days it removes (retired while a kept row names one) and is refused while a hire check runs (`HIRE_CHECK_RUNNING`). Rule 20 and the driver link apply as to any truck; the sheets say *HIRED TRUCK*. A truck rented for the day works the day with ONE casual driver (sixth review of the hire branch: **+ Add daily driver** put the driver on the load pressed only): `addCasualDriver` puts that driver on its other loads of the version still to plan too (PLANNED, not one whose driver the dispatcher chose by hand, `isHandSetDriver`; `LOAD_DRIVER_SET` each) and makes them its default driver (`HIRED_TRUCK_CHANGED`), answering `alsoOn`. Only the load pressed is the dispatcher's pick: the others are filled in by RouteIQ (`setDriverTx` `filled`: no `driverSetById` / `driverSetAt`, `via: 'whole rental day'`; seventh review - they were marked, and a re-plan that dropped such a trip warned *Driver picked by hand, not in this plan* of a pick nobody made). The dialog says it before saving - the other loads, the default driver, the loads whose driver it replaces and those that keep the driver the dispatcher chose; its button names the loads (`casualDriverPlan`, `casualDriverDialogText` in `lib/dispatch/casual-driver-words.ts`) - and the message lists them in order (`casualDriverToast`: *HIRE-10T-1110-1 Loads 1, 2 and 3: daily driver Salim*; it read *Load 2 and Load 1, Load 3*). The Trucks page shows *1 day: 11 Oct* (`oneDayBadge`), *by bays* for its case capacity (`truckCapacityText`) and the description *Hired 10-ton for 11 Oct (hire suggestion)* (`hiredTruckDescription`; one stored before with its ISO date is shown so, `truckDescriptionText`; seventh review); **Use this plan** asks for the day as *11 Oct* (`hireUseConfirmText`) and says each hired truck works its whole day with one driver (*+ Add daily driver* on one load puts that driver on its others), and the server's words about hired days say the day so too. The plan's Fuel KPI is the own trucks' litres and OMR with *rented trucks: fuel included* under it (`SummaryLoad.fuelInHire`, `DailySummary.fuelIncludedLoads`, `fuelKpi` / `dayFuel` - a summary stored before reads the loads; sixth review: it turned blank, '-', with any hired truck), the Excel's *Estimated fuel* likewise, and a rented truck's load shows *incl.* for litres. A hired truck's casual driver is paid the day rate: a load's cost on the plan says "driver day rate 10.00 (paid with the truck's first load of the day; no hours, no overtime)" (`loadCostTitle`), and the workbook's LOAD PLAN and TRUCK DAYS show *day rate* in the paid-time column, never hours (`DetailLoad.driverDayRate` from the truck snapshot; third review: it read as hourly pay at a zero rate).
- **Join small trips** (`SOLVER_JOIN_TRIPS`, off by default, 4.11): the what-if is never joined (`search.join_trips` SKIPPED `HIRE_CHECK`, and the reduction's trial solves get no join), so its comparisons stay like for like. With `on`, the plan in use may be a joined plan while the what-if stays unjoined: the suggestion's cost comparison is then against an unjoined baseline (no code change; the dispatcher guide says so).
- **Real Muscat day of 26 Sep 2026** (12,482 cases, 143.9 pallets, 82 stops, payload 0, Haversine; the solver with a request shaped like the web's; measured with the first version's pricing, before the owner's answers): the fleet cut to three 10-tons (36 bays, up to 3 loads each) leaves 48 orders (4,038 cases, 49.5 pallets) out; the what-if (31 s) says *hire 1 x 10-ton (12 bays) + 1 x 3-ton (6 bays): extra about 80 OMR. Still left out: none* (one truck fewer: up to 14 orders, 1,379 cases left); cut to three 10-tons and one 3-ton, *hire 1 x 10-ton (12 bays): extra about 50 OMR*; with six trucks the day fits and the what-if rents nothing.

### 3.20 Operations alerts

Owner request (16 Oct 2026): "notify me when a rule I set is broken: (1) a driver's unloading takes more than planned by 30 min; (2) loading in the warehouse takes more than 40 min; (3) a driver's ETA changes to more than 30 min late; plus any other rule you find important, so we can track with ease." Design PR-2 with the adversarial review's fixes. **Off by default**: `TenantConfig.alertsEnabled` is false for every company, so deploying changes nothing until a company admin switches it on (Settings > Operations alerts).

- **GPS** (owner request 18 Oct 2026): only while the company's GPS tracking is `ALERTS` do the rules also read the GPS times, the depot moves and the fresh live position, each text that used them saying "(GPS)"; below it they read the driver's taps, the office's entries and the plan only ([3.21](#321-gps-live-link-ayun-times-live-map-tracker-mapping), *GPS alerts*).
- **Rules** (`lib/alerts/catalog.ts`, the shared contract; one nullable threshold column per rule, NULL = off): R1 unloading longer than planned (30 min), R2 loading between trips too long (40 min; see below), R3 running late (30 min), R4 not dispatched on time, R5 driver silent, R6 after the delivery window, R7 priority stop not delivered, R8 delivered with a note (not a note that only confirms the delivery: `text.ts` `noteOnlyConfirms`), R9 proof far from a verified pin, R10 load not closed, R11 driver page not opened (the one warning a truck-day without an opened driver page gets instead of the phone rules). Tier 1 is WARN, tiers 2-3 HIGH. Nothing that began before the switch-on moment (`alertsEnabledAt`, stamped by the save that switches alerts on, or by the first sweep when a support UPDATE left it empty) raises an alert; the same per rule (`alertRuleOnAtJson`: a rule switched on later, or set to catch more, raises nothing that began before that save), and a row closed because its rule was switched off reopens only for something that began after it closed. Every condition is dated to when it began, also a delay the projection worked out.
- **After the two reviews of 16 Oct 2026** (the replay of a real day): R1, R3, R5 and the projected R6 stop once the truck is back (Back at depot, or out on its next load: a stop of it has activity, or its Dispatch press came no earlier than an hour before this load's planned return) and after the planned return + 60 min (NOT_FOLLOWED; R10 follows the load); a result entered hours later is capped there too. While R1 is raised, R3 and the projected R6 of the load wait (one long unloading is one alert, and R1's text names the next stop's new time). A delivery photo of the driver's phone counts as being at its stop, and the clock pushes a stop not reached only while the phone has been silent since before it was expected. R4 counts a later trip from the later of its planned departure and the previous load's return (a tap; without one the planned return + 60 min) + the planned turnaround. R6: an arrival after the window is a warning, high beyond 2T. R8 keeps a note with any number but a clock time or a date ("18/20", "50%"). R9 reads a visit like "Pin may be wrong": the median distance of the driver's own photos (the phone's position when good, else the photo's own location; old photos and office uploads left out), else the driver's result position when no later stop had activity before it; not for a visit planned at an older pin. R10 is a warning only when every result is in.
- **R2, loading between trips (owner decision of 16 Oct 2026).** Measured from the driver's taps, not from a warehouse press (the Loaded action of the first draft was removed before release): for a truck-day with a later trip, the turnaround is **Back at depot** of trip N to **Leaving for next load** of trip N+1 (`StopEvent` `DEPOT_DEPART`, [3.18](#318-delivery-outcomes-and-the-driver-page)). The latest tap before the truck reached a stop counts (a tap too early is corrected by tapping again). Without the tap, a fallback marked as such in the text: the Dispatch press of trip N+1 (read from its `LOAD_DISPATCHED` audit row through `carriedFromLoadId`, `loadOrigins` in `lib/delivery/day-results.ts`, so completing the load does not lose it) or the first sign of the truck at one of its stops (arrival, departure, the phone's result or photo; an office result is not one) less the planned drive to the first stop ("left by"), whichever came first, never a press before Back at depot (a Dispatch pressed for every load in the morning is not the truck leaving); a tap after the first stop reached gives that stop. A trip planned after Back at depot (a late order, a re-plan: the `createdAt` of the first plan version it was copied from) is counted from then. Not measured: a trip that had started before Back at depot of the trip before was tapped (Back at depot tapped late: no live alert for hours), and a Completed trip that nothing dates (never live on a Completed load). One row per trip N+1 (subject: its load key): live while the truck is still at the depot (now - Back at depot; tiers at T, 2T, 3T; dispatched before Back at depot and no tap: the planned drive to the first stop is allowed first, the truck may be on the road), final once it left (the row closes with the minutes and both times; over T and never seen live: one history row); never for the first trip of the day (loaded the night before: the 21:00 Loading press reports nothing), none without Back at depot (R10 follows that trip), none across two depots, none for a load without stops, no longer followed 4 h after Back at depot. `alertLoadingOverMin` defaults to 40 like the other rules (under the master switch). `lib/delivery/turnaround.ts` is shared with the plan screen, the replay and (18 Oct 2026) the truck's day (`countedLeaveTap`): the load row of a trip after the first shows "After L1: back 11:20, left 12:08, 48 min" (a fallback named; "not left yet, 25 min so far" while waiting; "no leave recorded" past 4 h, on a day that is over or on an undated Completed trip; "not measured" when Back at depot came late), from `GET /api/runs/:id/outcomes` `turnarounds`, only while alerts and R2 are on (like the driver's button), a failure there leaving the line out and never the results. A truck back early that waits for its planned departure counts the wait too: owner decision of 16 Oct 2026 (second review M2: "yes", the wait at the depot counts).
- **Engine** (`lib/alerts/` rules, projection, facts, store and sweep; the janitor every 2 min and `/api/cron/janitor`; `ROUTEIQ_DISABLE_ALERTS=1` stops it): reads what is in the database, writes `OpsAlert` rows (one per rule and physical subject, unique), escalates, closes them (ended, corrected, no longer in the plan, date passed, day ended, rule off, no longer followed), then calls the e-mail digest per company. Each company's last good sweep is kept in the process: the bell and the Alerts page say "Checked hh:mm" and warn when it is older than 10 min or the last one failed; `/api/health` reports `alerts` (`lastRunAt` and how many companies' sweep failed or is overdue, counts only).
- **States** (`lib/alerts/types.ts`): OPEN (counts on the bell), ACKED (seen), RESOLVED (history, needs no acknowledgement). An EVENT row (R6 arrival, R7, R8, R9) stays open until corrected or its day is over (DAY_ENDED, below; EXPIRED for a row older than the sweep's window that no sweep closed, both keeping who acknowledged it); acknowledged, it no longer counts on the bell. A CONDITION row closes when its condition ends. A higher tier clears the acknowledgement.
- **Dates and the day's end** (owner request 19 Oct 2026: "alerts of yesterday looked like today's because only the time is shown"; "ok add the date fix"). Before, a row still open at midnight stayed open, and on the bell, for the whole next day, shown with its time only, and closed one day later when its date left the sweep's window (production closed 17 Oct's at 19 Oct 00:02). Now: (1) the first sweep after the company's midnight (its time zone) closes every row of the day before still open as DAY_ENDED ("Day ended"), a condition still true or an event, acknowledged or not, whatever its rule says, keeping who acknowledged it; only a rule answering in that same sweep with its own final words (over, corrected, no longer followed, a history row) closes it otherwise, and a row of a rule switched off stays "Rule switched off" (`store.ts` `planApply`, `PlanContext.today` = the facts' today; the replay too when it runs past midnight). After that the day is history: none of its rows is escalated, updated or reopened, and a subject of it first found true after midnight (a result tapped late, a late arrival) is written already closed as DAY_ENDED (no toast, no e-mail), so the Alerts page still lists it under its day. Today's and tomorrow's rows are not touched. One exception, the day's follow-up (review of the branch, 19 Oct 2026, finding 2; `catalog.ts` `ALERT_AFTER_DAY_RULES`): *Load not closed* fires only its threshold (120 min by default) after the planned return, so a load planned back at 22:30 that is still not closed first raises at 00:31, and the other rules leave a late load to it; written closed it would never reach anyone. So LOAD_NOT_CLOSED first found true after the midnight is raised OPEN for its day and lives like a row of today (on the bell under "Yesterday, 18 Oct", toasted and e-mailed by its tier, escalated, closed by its own words when the load is closed, or as EXPIRED when its date leaves the window at the next midnight); it is known by its `firstSeenAt` at or after `PlanContext.todayStart` (the start of the company's today). A *Load not closed* row already open at midnight still closes as DAY_ENDED (it was on the bell during its day). (2) The bell reads today and tomorrow only (`bellWindow`; yesterday's open rows are not counted between midnight and that sweep either), and yesterday's *Load not closed* raised after midnight (`bellOpenWhere`); the summary carries the company's `today`. (3) The bell and the Alerts page show the date of any alert that is not today's: "Yesterday 17:20", "18 Oct 17:20" (`view.ts` `alertWhen`: the instant's own date and clock in the company's time zone, so neither a summer-time change nor the browser's zone moves it; "Today 00:40" for yesterday's alert seen after midnight); today's keep the time only. The bell puts a small date header over the rows of another day ("Tomorrow, 20 Oct"; none when every row is today's); the Alerts page says the day in **Since** and **State** ("Over yesterday 17:40", "Day ended (acknowledged by Sam 10:42)"). The day screen's card and the truck's day show one day and keep the time only. (4) The e-mail: open or "over by itself" rows only of the company's today or later, and yesterday's *Load not closed* raised after midnight (a row of yesterday still open because that company's sweep failed this tick is not e-mailed as open). A row closed as DAY_ENDED that was never e-mailed (`emailedTier` 0) goes once, marked "(day ended)" (review of the branch, 19 Oct 2026, finding 1): without it a HIGH raised at 21:50, after the 21:45 e-mail and before the quiet hours, was never e-mailed (closed at 00:02, out of the date guard at 06:00), nor a HIGH of 23:50 when the next e-mail is due after midnight, nor the rows left once the daily cap is reached (within the 12 h look back). A row e-mailed before, even at a lower tier, is never sent again once its day ended.
- **In the app** (every role reads): the **bell** in the top bar (`components/alert-bell.tsx`, only while alerts are on, from the layout, so nothing polls when they are off; reads `GET /api/alerts/summary` every 60 s while the tab is visible and when it comes back into view; today's and tomorrow's open alerts only, a row of another day under a small date header (19 Oct 2026, above); red with a HIGH open alert; a toast only for a HIGH row that is new since the page opened, at most 3 at once; the rows there when the page opened fill the seen list silently); the **Alerts** card above Deliveries on the day screen (`dispatch/alerts-card.tsx`: the day and depot, one block per truck with its worst state first, what is over behind "Show N over", polls only for yesterday, today and tomorrow); the **Alerts** page (`/t/<slug>/alerts`, a nav item for every role, shown only while the company has alerts on; it polls only then).
- **Acknowledge** (PLANNER and up, one shared state for the company): `POST /api/alerts/ack` changes only open rows and never above the tier the screen showed (a row that became worse meanwhile stays open); `{ all }` needs a date (one day, of one depot if given); one `ALERTS_ACKNOWLEDGED` audit row per request ([3.13](#313-audit-log)).
- **Cause & action** (owner request 20 Oct 2026: "a place where a note / reason for the alert to have happened and the solution ... entered by someone after checking and finding a solution ... will help us gather data for what decisions are made when alerts are made"; `lib/alerts/review.ts`, `PATCH /api/alerts`, migration `20261020000000_alert_notes`, design with its adversarial critique applied). After checking an alert the dispatcher and up (PLANNER+) record the main **cause** and the **action** taken or decided - pick-lists that depend on the rule's family (running late; unloading; depot turn and dispatch; delivery result; pin and proof; truck still out - *Driver silent* and *Load not closed*, usually a long trip, with the lateness causes and the move-it actions; driver's page and taps), each ending with *Alert setting too tight*, *False alarm*, *Not found yet* and *Other* (a text of 3-120 characters), and *No action needed*, *Nothing yet* and *Other* - an optional note (500 characters, one line, digit runs removed, so dates and times written with digits go too) and **needs follow-up** (always with *Nothing yet* or *Not found yet*; a follow-up only forced by them is not carried into an edit, so picking the real cause and action clears it). The selects start empty (a default would skew the counts); until a field is changed the dialog shows a hint, not an error, and it shows what a note or an Other text will be saved as when the clean-up changes it. It works on an alert of any state and day (open, acknowledged, over, a day that ended) and while alerts are off; every role sees it with the whole note (a long one opens in place with *more*: no tooltip, which a phone never shows): under the alert on the Alerts page (the button is under the text, so it is in view on a phone), on the day screen's card ("Cause & action saved by Sam", so two dispatchers do not both call the driver, with what changed since), on the bell (with a link that opens the dialog on the Alerts page, also while that page is open: it moves to the alert's date) and on the truck's day. The dialog edits a snapshot (the 60 s poll never resets a half-typed note); the save names the last save the editor saw, so a second editor gets 409 with what was saved and saves over it on purpose; a save or a removal first waits for the company's alert lock and then its e-mail lock (`lockForReview`; held past 5 s: 409 `ALERT_BUSY`), so the sweep never deadlocks with it and an e-mail claim that starts meanwhile answers BUSY and goes with the next check instead of skipping the rows the save holds (review of the branch, finding 1: an alert over by itself is news in one e-mail only). **One incident**: the dialog offers the other alerts of the same truck and day without one (unticked; one whose rule does not offer the codes cannot be ticked); they get the same cause & action, never overwriting one of their own, and share a group (`reviewGroupId`) so the export counts incidents. "Acknowledge it too" (an open alert) acknowledges at the tier the dialog showed. **Remove** clears one saved on the wrong alert. Each row keeps the alert's tier, occurrences and customer at the save: the screens and the export say when it came back, got worse or now names another customer at its stop (the store now writes the stop's current customer on an update or reopen: data only). The sweep, the acknowledgement and the e-mail never write these columns. Saving never acknowledges on the server. Audited per alert with the version before and after - codes, follow-up and the texts with their lengths - so an edit or a removal keeps the earlier note (`ALERT_REVIEW_SAVED`, `ALERT_REVIEW_REMOVED`); the texts leave the audit rows 90 days after the alert's date. The Alerts page filters by it (All, Missing, Saved, Follow-up: lists the last 92 days whatever the dates), counts it on the server for the dates, depot, rule and state chosen, Follow-up too ("12 of 40 ... (2 say Other) · 3 to follow up": the follow-ups of the last 92 days with the same depot, rule and state) and downloads it (Excel: the alerts alone, `only=alerts`; also the last sheet of the Analysis data, [3.22](#322-the-analysis-dataset-facts-kept-for-later-analysis)). **Retention** (owner decision pending, docs/admin.md; review of the branch, finding 4): as before, an alert row is deleted with its cause & action 90 days after its date (the alerts' Excel downloaded before keeps them). Only with `ALERT_KEEP_FOR_ANALYSIS=1` on `web` does it instead lose its text, its facts but "by GPS", the note and the Other texts then (`detailsRemovedAt`; a row still open is closed as EXPIRED first) and become read-only, the row with its codes staying as long as the analysis data (`analysisRetentionDays`, 730 by default, never less than 90). Either way the cause & action audit rows of that alert lose their texts then; one `OPS_ALERTS_PURGED` audit row of counts per night that changed something. Start fresh removes the days' alerts with their cause & action (a line of their own on the panel when there are some, compared for PREVIEW_STALE). To add a code: one line in `lib/alerts/review.ts` (the database checks only the format).
- **E-mail** (`lib/alerts/notify.ts`, `lib/email.ts`): only with `RESEND_API_KEY` AND `RESEND_FROM` on the server, the company's slug on the server's `ALERT_EMAIL_TENANTS` list (signup is open: without the list anyone could send to any address through our sender) and recipients (at most 5) in Settings; at most 80 alert e-mails of all companies together in any 24 h; the subject carries the counts and the day only (no name a user typed); every free text is cleared of long digit runs; each send has an Idempotency-Key over its content (a message Resend accepted but answered late is not sent twice); the first e-mail after the quiet hours leaves out what ended during them; HIGH alerts only by default (`alertEmailMinSeverity`); at most one e-mail every `alertEmailEveryMin` (15) and 40 a day (counted on `OpsAlertDigest` rows: counts only, never an address); none in the quiet hours (22:00-06:00 by default; what is still worth sending goes in the first e-mail after them). One e-mail lists what is new or worse since the last one, grouped by depot, day and truck, with a link to the day screen; a row that ended by itself since the last e-mail says "(over at 10:50)"; rows closed as not in the plan, date passed, rule off or corrected are not e-mailed; a row of a day that is over only when it closed at the day's end never e-mailed (once, "(day ended)") or is yesterday's *Load not closed* raised after midnight (owner request 19 Oct 2026 and review of the branch: *Dates and the day's end* (4) above). The claim runs in one transaction under the company's e-mail lock (`pg_try_advisory_xact_lock`), so two containers during a deploy send once. A failed e-mail puts the rows back for the next one (3 tries). **Send test email** (company admin) goes to the saved recipients.
- **Texts** never contain a phone number: digit runs of 6 or more are removed from free text (the e-mail removes them once more), driver notes are cut to 140 characters. Rows are deleted 90 days after their date (kept longer, without their texts, only with `ALERT_KEEP_FOR_ANALYSIS=1`: *Cause & action* above) and by Start fresh with the day's data.

### 3.21 GPS live link (Ayun): times, live map, tracker mapping

Owner request (Oct 2026): use the trucks' GPS trackers at Ayun (a GPS-Server.net platform) for live positions and arrival and departure times. Design `feat/ivms-live` with the binding review of 16 Oct 2026 (H1-H5, M1-M13). **Off by default**: `TenantConfig.ivmsMode` `OFF` (no call to Ayun, nothing written, nothing new shown except the admin's tracker card and the settings), `MAP` (live trucks on the day screen), `TIMES` (MAP + GPS arrival and departure times), `ALERTS` (TIMES + the operations alerts read the GPS: owner request 18 Oct 2026, below); `ROUTEIQ_DISABLE_IVMS=1` stops everything. `ALERTS` does all `TIMES` does (`ivmsModeAtLeast(mode, 'TIMES')`: the history share of the allowance, the pulls, the webhook's depot moves, the processing step, the clock warning). The company admin switches it on the Settings card **GPS tracking (Ayun)** (mode, Ayun's daily allowance, how often, the operating hours, the stop and depot radii, the dwell, the trail days; the card says how often positions and history come at the allowance set). The ingest (the provider client, the daily allowance, the history pulls, the live-position poll, the webhook: `lib/ivms/ayun-client.ts`, `budget.ts`, `poll.ts`, `webhook.ts`) is described in the lib table; this section is what turns their rows into times and the map.

- **End to end** (integration of 16 Oct 2026): the poller's tick (15 s) asks for live positions of the trucks out (map only) and pulls each truck-day's history (TIMES), then, outside the lease, runs the processing step (`IvmsStore.processTimes` = `processGpsTimesForCompany`) right after a tick that pulled history and otherwise at most every 5 minutes (`PROCESS_EVERY_MS`: a late Dispatch press or a completion changes which trip is which load); its counts are in the tick result (`times`, also in the cron route's answer). Ayun's depot webhooks are stored as `IvmsEvent` (TIMES only, trucks with a load, and only once a depot has its Ayun zone: `Depot.ivmsZoneName` has no setting screen yet, so the runbook says not to register the webhook) and become trip boundaries only when the trail confirms them, at the trail's own time. `tests/lib/ivms-day-simulation.spec.ts` plays a whole invented day (`tests/fixtures/ivms/day-script.json`) through all of it in OFF, MAP and TIMES.
- **The provider's clock** (first review H-1): each live-position answer records Ayun's clock skew with the offset it was read with (`IvmsState.providerSkewSec`, `providerSkewAt`, `providerSkewOffsetMin`, migration `20261016220000_ivms_review_fixes`). History pulls and the processing step run only while `clockCheck` (`lib/ivms/budget.ts`) says OK: a skew measured with the offset in use in the last 12 h, at most 10 min ahead and 2 h behind (a wrong offset is whole hours; a quiet parked fleet looks up to an hour behind). Otherwise nothing is pulled or written (`clock` in the tick result, the health block and an amber line on the Settings card with the offset to set). A history answer cannot show the error by itself (its window is asked in the same shifted time). Second line: a stay that began more than 60 min before its load's Dispatch press (`LATE_PRESS_MAX_MIN`) or after now is never written.

- **Where GPS times come from** (H5): only the trucks' history (`TruckTrailPoint`, pulled with `OBJECT_GET_ROUTE` while a load is out and once at the end, after the truck's return: *The final pull at the return* below), never the live positions, which are for the map only.
- **Stop detector** (`lib/ivms/stops.ts`, pure). Depot moves from the trail (inside the depot radius, out past it + 50 m, held 5 min); an Ayun depot zone move counts only when the trail confirms it within 10 min (a forged webhook never cuts a trip, M6). Trips from depot OUT to IN, matched to the truck-day's DISPATCHED / COMPLETED loads in dispatch order (`LOAD_DISPATCHED` audit time, `lib/dispatch/dispatched-at.ts`; never a completed load's status time), order-preserving, an earlier load always first (lexicographic: a load is left without a trip only when none it can afford is left, never while a later load takes it; second review H-1), then the cheapest: the trip at the load's anchor (its press, or for a load pressed long before it left its planned departure less 2 h, `loadAnchor`) and the trip with stays (not drive-bys) at the load's own pins; a trip that left more than 10 min after the load's Back at depot (the driver's or the office's, `DetectorLoad.backAt`) is never that load's, so a load whose own trip is missing from the trail cannot take the next load's; a load keeps the trips without a load next to its own that stay at its pins before the next load's anchor and its Back at depot (a break at the depot, a run back for goods: M-3); a fuel run gets no load; several loads with no depot boundary match nothing (H3). A depot zone move confirms a trail move but the boundary keeps the trail's time. A stay: from the first point inside `ivmsStopRadiusM` of a pin (the arrival) to the first of two consecutive points past it + 50 m, or the first point at 10 km/h or more outside (the departure); a single drifting point or a long silence of a parked truck never ends it (M11); it needs a slow point and `ivmsStopDwellMin` (6 min for a stop out of sequence). Never automatic (H4): a pin within `ivmsDepotRadiusM` of the depot, two pending pins with stays at the same time, a stop that has a result before the stay or an office arrival, a stay that began before the load's press less 60 min or after now, a stay at the first point of a trail that started outside the depot (L-4); these are kept as **facts** for the office (`IvmsTruckDay.gpsFactsJson`, migration `20261016210000_ivms_gps_facts`) and shown in the live map's popup. At most 4 stays per stop (2 until 21 Oct 2026: owner decision, F3 below); observed only when the point before it is at most 5 min earlier (else an upper bound: shown, never in measured times or the on-time KPI).
- **Writer** (`lib/ivms/stop-events.ts`, `processGpsTimes`, `processGpsTimesForCompany` = the poller's hook after its history pulls): TIMES only; one short transaction per visit in the driver path's lock order (lock timeout, outcome-day lock, the load again: DISPATCHED or COMPLETED only, the planned stop, the visit, the events, `rebuildVisit`). Keys `ayun:A|D:<depot>:<date>:<truck>:<load>:<seq>:<first inside fix ms>`: a rerun writes nothing, and a stay whose start moved (a delayed point) is recognised by an AYUN event of the same kind within 10 min of it, unless that event's own stay is still seen (two stays at one stop, L-1) (first write wins, M2), except that an event that was **not observed** (an upper bound) is corrected in place when a later pull brings the missing points and the same stay is now observed, or still unobserved but earlier (`correctGpsEvent`; the final pull re-reads the whole day, so points a tracker buffered through a coverage gap fix the time the same day); an observed GPS time never moves. A truck-day whose lock was busy is not marked processed, so the next pass retries it. At most 8 AYUN events per stop (4 until 21 Oct 2026, F3), none once a stop holds 32 of the shared 40; detector `ivms-v3` since then (the payload as `ivms-v2`'s). Nothing for a stop the office timed. A tracker on another truck (the driver's own positions and the trail more than 1 km apart at the same moments, 3 times over 10 minutes or more, more often than they agree: `trackerMismatch`) suppresses the truck-day (`MISMATCH`, M8) and deletes its AYUN events, the visits rebuilt (second review M-1). An AYUN event whose stay lies in a trip the detector now gives to another load is deleted and its visit rebuilt (`removeStaleGpsEvents`, second review H-1; never on a mere absence of evidence). Between truck-days the company run gives the event loop back (about 20 ms of detector work for a heavy invented truck-day of 6,400 points and 100 stops); a failure is logged by its code only. A trail move stored before the provider's zone move of it arrived becomes a `DUPLICATE` (M12). **Never** an OUTCOME, a BACK_AT_DEPOT, an audit row, a Dispatch or a completion (H1): `completeReturnedLoads` and `maybeCompleteLoad` read only the driver's or the office's Back at depot (`COMPLETING_BACK_SOURCES`). Undo (`suppressGpsTimes`, dry run by default; for the company admin `POST /api/ivms/trucks/:id/gps-times` and the Trucks page, first review M-3): marks the truck-day suppressed (`UNDO`), deletes its AYUN events and rebuilds the visits; the next run writes nothing (M10), and removes any AYUN event still on a suppressed truck-day (a removal that failed, a run already under way). No trail point from before `IvmsTruckDay.trailFrom` is read. Facts are capped (40, 12 stop numbers each, 7,000 bytes) under the column's 8 KB CHECK.
- **Precedence** (`lib/delivery/visit.ts`, second review H-2): the visit is first rebuilt from the driver's and the office's events only, exactly as with the link off; GPS then only fills what is empty. Arrival: the office's, else the phone's (any, even one found when the page came back), else GPS (of the stay holding the result: observed first, then the earliest); since 21 Oct 2026 an observed GPS arrival wins over a late phone one (*GPS times win* below). Departure: the office's, else the phone's; when nothing else ends the stop, or only the result time stands in for it and the phone's automatic timing does not end there ("Auto to result" is never replaced), the GPS departure of the stay that holds the driver's result (owner request 19 Oct 2026: begun at or before the result and not left before it, else the last stay begun before it, of all the stays not left before the arrival shown; without a result the stay at the arrival shown, begun at most 15 min after it, or none while the truck is back at the pin; the 15-minute rule after the result applies). A stay begun more than 15 min after the arrival shown is taken only from `ivms-v2` events, which carry the stay summary and its minutes away (review of 19 Oct 2026): for the `ivms-v1` events stored 16-19 Oct 2026 the stay at the arrival shown stays the rule, so a rebuild of such a visit or the alerts replay of such a day never counts a trip away as unloading. The minutes the GPS showed the truck away in between are `StopVisit.awayMinutes` (next bullet but one). The automatic timing (`autoArrivedAt`, `autoBasis`, `autoMinutes`, `autoServiceMinutes`) is the phone's only: GPS never feeds "Use measured time" (M3) and never removes the phone's; a GPS-timed stop shows arrival to departure as a non-automatic timing. A GPS arrival counts on time only at a Delivered or Partly stop (`arrivalIsObserved`, M3). Words: "GPS (Ayun)" (`office-text.ts`; `timedByText` says "GPS (Ayun)" for a GPS arrival and "Manual arrival, GPS (Ayun) departure" / "Auto arrival, ..." when only the departure is GPS). Driver page (first review M-2): a GPS-only arrival is sent as `arrivalByGps` (only then; a GPS arrival that replaced the driver's tap shows him his tap) and shown as NOT arrived: the **I have arrived** button stays, no "At stop" timer, not visited for the phone's tracker, only a note "The truck's GPS tracker saw it here at ..." (`StopView.gpsArrivedAt`); it never restores the phone's stop timer (M4). The old-photo check and the office's "Left needs an arrival" never use a GPS arrival (the driver's tap a GPS one replaced: `ownArrivalOf`). A visit without AYUN events is rebuilt byte for byte as before: `tests/lib/ivms-visit-golden.spec.ts` (900 seeded visits, the golden file written by the code before the change).
- **GPS times win** (owner decision 21 Oct 2026: "GPS arrival should win of course"; the GPS timing study of 19-20 Oct 2026 rebuilt every visit from the raw trail: Ayun's detection was right, the times shown were wrong on about 15% of the visits because of the rules above). The office's times still always win; the rest of the Precedence bullet stands. `lib/delivery/visit.ts`: **F1** a phone arrival (a tap, a "when?" answer, the phone's automatic arrival) made more than 2 min (`GPS_ARRIVAL_WINS_MIN`) after an observed GPS stay at the stop began, while the truck was still standing there, at most 240 min after it began (`GPS_TAP_LOOKBACK_MIN`), shows the GPS arrival (a tap before the stay, an unobserved GPS arrival or a tap 1-2 min after it keeps the tap). **F2** the GPS stay that holds the driver's own result gives its observed departure up to 60 min after the result (`GPS_MAX_AFTER_RESULT_MIN`; an office result, any other stay or a departure found after a gap in the trail, only an upper bound: the 15-minute rule), unless the driver tapped an arrival or a result at another stop of the truck-day in between (the neighbour guard, `VisitContext.otherStopTimes`, read by `rebuildVisit` for a visit with GPS events and passed by the alerts replay); the minutes more than 15 min after the result, less any time away in them, are `StopVisit.afterResultMinutes` and never unloading: every unloading time ends at the result (`actualMinutes` "less 30 min after the result", the truck day page, the Excel, UNLOAD_OVER, the analysis' `unloadVisitMin`); on-site time includes them. **F4** an observed GPS departure more than 2 min from the phone's automatic departure replaces it (the automatic timing, "Auto to departure", stays the phone's; without a result, not when the truck came back to the pin before the phone's departure). **F5** the arrival and a phone result tapped within 3 min of each other, at least 10 min and at most 240 min after the last GPS stay at the stop ended (standing at least 3 min; `ivms-v1` events pass; a later stay that ended less than 10 min before the taps is never skipped for an older one) with none in progress, and the visit has a result now (after the driver's Undo the stop is in progress again, as without GPS): the taps were made after leaving, that stay's arrival and departure are shown (only that last stay: a big site with two unmerged stays before the taps is a known limit). The automatic timing, the flags and the result stay the phone's (M3, H-2). The own times a GPS time replaced are kept on the visit (`ownArrivedAt` ... `ownDepartedAtOutcome`, migration `20261022090000_gps_times_win`; set only under an AYUN source, never AYUN themselves), so `withoutGpsTimes` (the alerts below ALERTS, the turnaround, the analysis' "Unloading by taps", the truck day page and the salesman page below TIMES) stays exactly the driver's and the office's for every mix of events. The driver page shows the driver his own taps, never a GPS time that replaced one (no timer jump, "I arrived" never comes back; a GPS-only arrival is as before); the photo old-check and the office's Left check read the driver's own tap (`ownArrivalOf`; a Left between the GPS arrival and the tap is refused with both times); the on-time KPI counts an observed GPS arrival that replaced a tap at any stop; the plan screen and the truck day page show "GPS (Ayun); driver tapped 10:15" and "GPS (Ayun), 30 min after the result". Past visits keep their times until rebuilt: `apps/web/scripts/rebuild-gps-visits.ts` (dry run by default, counts per date and rule; `--write` rebuilds only visits with GPS events: a production write, owner OK). `tests/lib/ivms-gps-wins.spec.ts`.
- **The final pull at the return** (F6, owner decision 21 Oct 2026; the study: on 7 of 16 truck-days the last load was completed while the truck was still out, its depot entry came 22-307 min later and the final pull 10 min after the completion left the drive back, and the last stops' GPS departures, out of the trail). `lib/ivms/poll.ts` `finalPullTarget`: the truck in the depot at the last completion (its last depot move before it an entry) or no depot move known: the final pull 10 min after the completion, as before; out then: the truck-day is pulled as a regular one (it counts with the trucks out, so the final reserve is kept) until its first depot entry after the completion with no exit within 15 min (`FINAL_RETURN_HOLD_MS`: a flap at the gate), the final 15 min after that entry, reaching it + 30 min; not back 3 h after the completion: the fallback final (`FINAL_RETURN_FALLBACK_MS`). A final made before the truck was back (one from before this change, or the fallback's) is repeated once, over what came since (`ROUTE_OVERLAP_MS` before the last pull); the target is never past the next day's operating hours; a final whose tracker is not readable counts as made. After the hours the poller keeps a truck still driving back and a final after the return until 30 min after it was due (the live map is unchanged, M7). The depot moves come with the fleet in one query (`IvmsEvent` DEPOT_IN / DEPOT_OUT from a webhook, the backstop or the trail, never UNCONFIRMED or DUPLICATE; without webhooks the trail's own moves show the return one pull later). `route.finals` in the tick result counts the final pulls due and overdue (due more than 30 min ago and not made), logged once per change as *ivms: final pull overdue (n)*.
- **Big customers** (owner request 19 Oct 2026: "at big customers the truck moves between drop points and the model thinks it left"; the GPS study of 18-19 Oct 2026 on 76 driver-tapped visits: 5 departures shown while the truck was still on site or back again, 3 of them moves between drop points 107-149 m out at 14-32 km/h, 2 real leave-and-returns; crawling alone never made a stop; 11 frozen-position runs; the "jumps" over 150 km/h mostly timestamp jitter). TIMES and ALERTS only; below TIMES nothing changes. (1) GPS cleaning (`cleanTrail`): the same coordinates repeated for 60 s or more at a moving speed are a gap - the repeats are dropped and the event at the next point is not observed; no point is dropped for its speed. (2) A customer's **site radius** (`Customer.siteRadiusM`, 100-500 m, Details dialog; empty = today): the stay still begins within `ivmsStopRadiusM`, but ends only beyond the site radius (one point beyond it at 10 km/h or more, or two beyond it + 50 m); the GPS alerts' "at the stop" reaches it too (`lib/alerts/gps.ts` `atStopRadiusOf`, never narrower than the company's). (3) **Merge** (`mergeStays`): two stays of one stop at its pin are one when the next began less than 10 min after the last ended, every trail point in between stayed within 500 m of the pin, both are stops themselves (a slow point and the dwell) and no other open stop of the load had a stay in between or at the same time; the merged stay keeps the first arrival and the last departure. (4) **Hold-back**: a departure is final only once the truck has been away 10 min, is beyond 500 m or reached the depot (`StopCandidate.final`); the writer holds it until then (`kept.HELD`), because an observed GPS time is never moved once written: a move between drop points never writes a departure, a real one is written within about 10 minutes. (5) **Leave-and-return**: a later stay of a stop after the truck went beyond 500 m, or stood at another customer's pin, carries the minutes it was away like that (`StaySummary.awayMin`; a one-minute turn beyond 500 m counts one minute, the time standing on the site does not); the visit rebuild sums those inside the shown arrival and departure into `StopVisit.awayMinutes` (migration `20261019120000_gps_site_radius_away`, CHECK > 0) and every unloading time takes them off - the plan screen's Unload (*away N min* under Left), the truck day page (*On site*), the delivery export (*Away from the customer (min, GPS)*), the measured time per customer, the KPI and UNLOAD_OVER in ALERTS (from the window start only what can have been after it). (6) Every GPS event's payload carries its stay's summary (`stay`: `exitRule`, `exitKmh`, `exitDistM`, `standMin`, `maxDistM`, `points`, `frozenRuns`, `merged`, `awayMin`, `radiusM`: distances and minutes only), detector `ivms-v2`; a pending stop's stay shorter than the dwell is kept as a `SHORT_DWELL` fact (never shown, cut first). The dwell stays 3 min (the study found 6 no better). Pins 120-300 m from where trucks stand are an office data fix, not code. `tests/lib/ivms-detector-golden.spec.ts` shows the detector unchanged on 160 seeded truck-days where none of this applies; validated offline on the study's export (numbers in [7.5](#75-open-questions-for-the-owner)). **Review of 19 Oct 2026** (each finding replayed on the study's export first): the site radius takes over only once the stay has a slow point within the stop radius (a truck passing a big customer's pin at 10-26 km/h on its way to the neighbour 235 m away opened a 400 m stay that ran through both visits, so SEVERAL_PINS left both without GPS times), and a site stay ends at its last point before the truck reaches the stop radius of another open stop's pin of the load (exit rule `OTHER_STOP`, so the two stays never overlap); saving a site radius warns (`siteRadiusWarning`, still saved) when another active customer's pin lies within the site radius + the stop radius. A held departure is also final once the pulled history (`IvmsTruckDay.pulledTo` less the next pull's 10-min overlap: `trailCompleteOf`) is 10 min past it with no stay at the pin begun since, and after the truck-day's final pull every departure is final (a tracker that went quiet near the site, ignition never being sent, left it held for good; the clock alone is not enough, the last minutes may not be pulled yet). The later-stay rule of the visit rebuild needs `ivms-v2` events (Precedence above). The alerts replay export keeps each GPS event's `segmentStartAt` and its summary's `awayMin` (`replay-export.ts` `eventOf`), so a replay with the GPS alerts measures UNLOAD_OVER on site as the live alerts do. The live map's "at the stop" (`lib/ivms/vehicles.ts`) reaches the customer's site radius as the GPS alerts' does.
- **Live map** (MAP or TIMES; `GET /api/runs/:id/vehicles`, PLANNER and up): trucks with a load out only (M7), stale after 5 min (`STALE_FIX_SEC`: grey, a clock, no speed, never moving, no ETA), a "Live trucks" switch remembered on the browser, the caption says when the positions are from, how often they come when the allowance stretches the interval (*Positions about every 19 min (Ayun's daily allowance)* at 100 calls a day: most trucks are then grey between two reads) and warns when a read is late by more than two intervals. The truck layer is its own marker set (`PlanMap` `vehicles`), never part of the route drawing or the zoom fit. Live ETA (`lib/ivms/eta.ts`, pure, no outbound call): the plan's own legs (from the planner's road matrix) scaled by what is left, never below the straight-line drive at `avgSpeedKmh` x `distanceMultiplier`; "at stop" only while the fresh fix is within `ivmsStopRadiusM` + 150 m of a stop with an open arrival, and a stop before the latest one the truck has been at is skipped, not "next" (second review M-2). Only trucks with a load of today's plan out, or of yesterday's still DISPATCHED, inside the operating hours; after them only today's DISPATCHED (first review LOW). A parked truck asked about again keeps its fix and its read time moves (no false "late" warning, L-5).
- **A truck's day** (owner request 18 Oct 2026: "if i want to go through a history of a vehicle with one button ... i click on [a truck] it takes me to where the truck is and what it was doing"): the truck code on the plan screen's loads table opens `/t/[slug]/dispatch/truck/[truckId]?date=` for the plan's date (PLANNER and up; another company's truck 404). `lib/ivms/truck-day.ts` (pure) builds it from `GET /api/ivms/trucks/[id]/day` (`truck-day-read.ts`, every query naming the company): the loads on the plans in use, a timeline in the order things happened (the Dispatch press, depot OUT and IN from the driver's taps, the GPS trail, Ayun's webhook or event list, each stop with its plan, its times and their source - driver, dispatcher, GPS -, time on site against the planned unloading, waiting for the window, the result, the photos, GPS stays at a customer that did not become the stop's times as *Earlier GPS visit*, the alerts), the map (stops by result, the trail thinned to 2,000 points for the days the retention keeps whole - today and yesterday by default -, the live position) and the live status (the day screen's rules: `liveVehicleOf`, `liveEta`). OFF: the plan and the results with the visits as the driver and the office made them (`withoutGpsTimes`), a note; MAP: the live position, no trail or GPS time; a suppressed truck-day: no trail, move or GPS visit. Review of 18 Oct 2026: the depot taps are shown as the rest of RouteIQ counts them - one *Left the depot* at the Leaving for next load tap rule R2 counts (`countedLeaveTap` in `lib/delivery/turnaround.ts`: the latest before the first sign at a stop, that sign from the driver's and the office's times and the phone's own photos, never a GPS time), the other taps named on its line (*corrected by tapping again*, *after the truck had reached a stop: not counted*), only late taps one muted line; one *Back at the depot* at the earliest tap (`backAtDepot`) - so the page agrees with the R2 alert it lists; the live position only while the truck has a load of the date out (Locked, Loading, On the road), as `readLiveVehicles` (M7), never a stored row of a truck off duty that the poller has not cleared yet (a backoff); the no-tracker note follows the tracker NOW, so a day that shows GPS recorded while the truck had one says so instead of "from the driver's phone only"; and a date whose read fails (a 429 after clicking quickly through dates) shows its error with **Try again**, never the previous date's loads (`truckDayScreen`). Never an IMEI (only whether there is a tracker), an Ayun object or zone name. **Open Ayun** opens Ayun's own site in a new tab: no link to one vehicle exists there and nothing is passed to it. The trail is the only new place positions are shown; it is never exported and is kept `ivmsTrailDays` as before.
- **Tracker mapping** (company admin, Trucks page **GPS trackers (Ayun)**): by IMEI only; plates only suggest (`lib/ivms/match.ts`: digits, letters as a multiset, Arabic-Indic digits; EXACT / DIGITS / AMBIGUOUS). `Truck.ivmsImei` is hidden from every other read (`PRISMA_GLOBAL_OMIT`). **Suggest from Ayun** makes one object-list call (`lib/ivms/admin-call.ts`, counted in the ADMIN share first, never waiting for the poller's lease) only in MAP or TIMES, only for the company of `AYUN_TENANT_SLUG`; without the server variables it answers `NOT_CONFIGURED` and the admin types the IMEI from the Ayun portal. A tracker set on a truck is read from that moment only (`IvmsTruckDay.trailFrom`, second review M-1); with GPS tracking OFF no truck-day row is created for it (only an existing one is marked), so OFF writes no GPS row.
- **What changes with the link OFF** (second review L-6, the allowed settings exception): `GET /api/tenant/config` and the before/after JSON of a Settings save's audit row carry the ten `ivms*` settings; every other output is byte-for-byte as before (`tests/lib/ivms-off.spec.ts`).
- **Privacy**: never a provider object name, plate, driver name or SIM stored; positions never in exports, sheets or alert texts; the AYUN events' positions are erased with the driver positions (`locationRetentionDays`). Runbook: `docs/admin.md` "GPS tracking (Ayun)"; dispatcher's view: `docs/DISPATCHER_GUIDE.md` "Live trucks and GPS times".
- **With the operations alerts** ([3.20](#320-operations-alerts); main merged in on 16 Oct 2026): both are off by default, and each has its own janitor step in its own try (the in-process janitor, and `/api/cron/janitor`, which runs the IVMS tick and GPS retention before the alert sweep and answers `alerts` and, while the link is in use, `ivms`). The alerts do not use GPS (merge review of 17 Oct 2026, finding 1): `lib/alerts/facts.ts` `alertVisitRow` reads each visit through `withoutGpsTimes` (`lib/delivery/visit.ts`: the visit's times as the driver's and the office's events alone made them, i.e. withGps undone from the stored row; a visit only GPS made counts as none), the load row's *Time at the depot* (`outcome-view.ts` `turnaroundsOf`) reads its first sign the same way, and the replay leaves the AYUN events out; so with GPS tracking *TIMES* on, every alert, the turnaround and the driver page's Leaving for next load offer behave exactly as with it off, and a tap after a GPS-only arrival still counts. GPS feeds the alerts only in GPS tracking ALERTS (next bullet); below it the live positions are never an alert input. A database error in one step no longer turns `/api/cron/janitor` into a 500: the cron route answers 200 with `alerts: { error: <code> }` (or `ivms.tick` / `ivms.retention` `{ error }`) and logs the code, so a monitor of that route's HTTP status should watch `/api/health` `alerts` (`failing`, `stale`) instead. Start fresh removes both features' rows (GPS rows, then the day's alerts: `START_FRESH_DELETE_ORDER`).
- **GPS alerts** (owner request 18 Oct 2026: "build GPS alerts"; the owner believed TIMES already fed the alerts): the fourth mode `ALERTS` (migration `20261018120000_ivms_alerts_mode`; Settings: *Live map, GPS times and GPS alerts* - "Map + GPS times + alerts use GPS times"). Only then, and never with `ROUTEIQ_DISABLE_IVMS=1`, does the sweep read the facts with the GPS (`lib/alerts/gps.ts` `gpsAlertConfigOf`; `facts.ts` six more indexed queries: `IvmsTruckDay`, `TruckPosition`, the trail-confirmed depot moves - `IvmsEvent` DEPOT_IN / DEPOT_OUT with outcome USED, exact only with a trail point at most 5 min before a trail move -, the loads' depot pins, the GPS departures' observed flags). Principles (decided conservatively, `gps.ts` header): GPS fills gaps, never contradicts a driver or office time, never creates a result (the visits are the rebuild's `withGps`; a depot move only stands in for a missing tap); the GPS times the trail gave are facts for every truck-day whose GPS is not suppressed (a suppressed one reads as with the link off), so a row never flips when the live feed pauses; only OBSERVED GPS times measure a duration (an unobserved one is an upper bound: "not measured"); what rests on where the truck is NOW reads the live position only while it is fresh (`GpsTruckDayFact.tracked`, `STALE_FIX_SEC`), and between two reads (a fix at most `GPS_WAIT_MIN` = 30 min old: at 100 calls a day positions come about every 20 min) such a rule waits - an open row stays, nothing new is raised from the phone alone - so a row never closes and reopens with each read; with no fix for longer, the phone-based rule; every text that used GPS says "(GPS)", never a position. Per rule: R1 a GPS arrival starts the unloading (live only while the fresh position shows the truck at the stop; away from it, the row waits for the GPS departure that closes it with the minutes), a GPS departure ends it ("unloading took 1 h 20 min (GPS arrival and departure)"); R2 without Back at depot the observed depot IN after the trip before (every stop of it done), without Leaving for next load the observed depot OUT ahead of the Dispatch press and the first stop (`turnaround.ts` `gpsLeftAt`, LeftHow `GPS`; the planned wait at the depot still counts), live only while the fresh position shows the truck at the depot; R3 with a fresh position the live map's ETA (`lib/ivms/eta.ts`), also while the driver is silent; R4 the depot OUT counts as leaving (the row closes with the time, one history row when late: "Dispatch is not pressed yet"); R5 the silence stays the phone's (results come only from it) and is a warning at most while GPS follows the truck; R6 an observed GPS arrival is an arrival; R10 and the end of R1, R3, R5, R6: the truck is back also by the depot IN after its last stop once every stop has a result or a sign; R7, R8, R9, R11 unchanged.
