A pool that cannot start (an `OSError`: out of memory, the process limit) or whose processes die while starting (Pool starts them again and again, and a task would wait for its deadline - up to the whole THOROUGH cap) is closed again and the solve is **refused within seconds**: `WorkersUnavailable`, which `main.py` answers with **503**, `Retry-After: 60` and `{"detail": "The planner is busy or restarting - try again in a minute.", "code": "WORKERS_UNAVAILABLE"}`. Nothing is searched inside the API process. Before, the whole search ran there with no deadline: OR-Tools holds the GIL, so the planner stopped answering anything else (`/health`, `/ready`, other companies' solves) for the length of the search - 20 minutes and more for THOROUGH - and the only trace was one WARNING line. Now the administrator gets an **ERROR** line whose message starts `WORKERS_UNAVAILABLE run=...` (with the cause; the log line itself starts with the timestamp, level and logger name, so log alerts match the code as a substring), and `/ready` reports `ok: false` with `workers: {status: "failed", failed_at, cause}` so the web's `/api/health` is `degraded` `SOLVER_WORKERS_FAILED` ([5.8](#58-health-endpoint)): for 15 minutes after the last failure (`WORKER_ALERT_SEC`), or until a pool starts `WORKER_ALERT_MIN_SEC` (5 minutes) or more after it (`WORKER_HEALTH`). A pool that starts sooner clears nothing (second review of rule 22: the load re-check's fresh pool, seconds after the pool broke, or another company's solve cleared it at once, so monitoring polling `/api/health` every few minutes never saw the failure; `test_a_pool_that_starts_soon_after_a_failure_does_not_clear_the_alert`; `test_idle_worker_killed_during_recommended_keeps_the_plan_within_seconds` checks `/ready` after its solve). A failed start also closes the queue made before the Pool (an audit finding). The web ends the job FAILED with the plain message and keeps the previous plan ([2.7](#27-background-job-model)). The ERROR line and `WORKER_HEALTH` are written before the failed pool is closed, so the alert exists even if closing misbehaves (`test_the_alert_is_written_before_the_failed_pool_is_closed`).
- **The pool breaks during a solve (rule 22 review, 30 Sep 2026).** Two ways a pool that started can stop running tasks for good: its worker-handler thread dies (a worker process died - the out-of-memory killer - and `Process.start` of the replacement raised: the process limit, out of memory), so nothing is ever replaced again; or a worker process dies while it waits for a task, holding the task queue's read lock, so no process can take a task again although replacements start. `_Workers.broken()` detects the first (the handler thread is not alive; after a worker death `_await_all` gives the handler 0.5 s to try its replacement); `_await_all` detects the second when a task has waited to start for `SOLVER_WORKER_START_SEC` while a worker was free (`busy()`: tasks that reported their start in a live process), never while every worker is busy - a load re-check job queued behind a 30 s THOROUGH one in a 1-worker pool is normal (`test_a_task_queued_behind_a_busy_worker_is_not_a_broken_pool`). Either way every task that has not started, or lost its process, comes back `("broken", cause)` at once, not at its deadline (for THOROUGH the 20-minute cap, answered with a misleading 504); a task still running in a live worker goes on. A pool that had run a task alerts once (`mark_broken`: the ERROR line `WORKERS_UNAVAILABLE run=...: the solver's worker processes stopped working during the search (...)` and `/ready` failed). So the optimization is refused with `WorkersUnavailable` (503, as a failed start; `_await_worker`) only when RECOMMENDED's own task cannot run: its worker stopped and no replacement can start, or its search could not start (every worker killed during the road matrix). When another worker stops while RECOMMENDED's search runs (an idle one killed, with or without a replacement), that search goes on: the recommended plan is kept, the alternatives come back broken and are skipped, and the load re-check gets a fresh pool as after an overrun (or, when that cannot start, `_retime_fallback`).
- **Closing a pool is bounded (rule 22 review).** CPython's `Pool.terminate()` waited forever on both kinds of broken pool (in `task_handler.join()`: a dead worker handler never sends the task handler its stop sentinel; in `_help_stuff_finish`: the read lock held by a dead worker), which held the request - its answer, its slot, its `_RUNNING` entry - for good, with no alert. `_Workers.close()` now first stops the pool's processes itself (`_stop_pool_processes`: the worker handler is told to stop as `terminate` does first - otherwise it replaces each worker as it is killed, a new process at the end of every solve, `test_closing_a_pool_starts_no_replacement_process` - every worker process is killed, a dead handler's sentinel is sent, and a read lock left by a dead worker is released), then runs `terminate()` + `join()` in a daemon thread for at most `POOL_CLOSE_SEC` (10 s). When that is not enough it returns False, logs an ERROR line with `WORKERS_UNAVAILABLE` ("a worker pool did not stop within 10 s ...") with `/ready` failed, and the solve goes on (after an overrun, to the fresh load re-check pool or `_retime_fallback`).
- **In-process, for development and tests only.** `SOLVER_PARALLEL=0` never starts a pool (everything in-process, no deadlines, unchanged). `SOLVER_ALLOW_INPROCESS_FALLBACK=1` keeps the old automatic fallback after a failed pool start (exactly `1`; `main.py` logs a warning at startup when it is set, an error on Railway). Neither may be set on a deployed solver. Both startup lines come from `log_startup_warnings()`, which `main.py` runs when it is imported; `test_startup_warnings_are_logged_an_error_on_railway` checks the level of each (ERROR on Railway, WARNING elsewhere, nothing when unset) and `test_the_solver_logs_its_startup_warnings_when_it_starts` imports `main` in a fresh process and finds the ERROR line in its log.

| Constant / env var | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `SOLVER_BUDGET_SEC` (env override) | 540 s | The whole request, including the matrix, must fit; the web waits 600 s |
| `REC_OVERHEAD_SEC` | 20 s | RECOMMENDED limit = min(auto limit, budget left − 20) |
| `REC_GRACE_SEC` | 60 s | RECOMMENDED deadline = min(now + 2 × limit + 60, budget end) |
| `SOLVER_ALT_GRACE_SEC` (env) | 20 s | Alternatives: limit = max(2, limit // 2) when warm-started, capped at the budget left − grace; deadline = limit + grace; skipped if under 2 s remain |
| `REPACK_CAP_SEC` / `REPACK_MIN_SEC` | 15 / 3 s | Each CP-SAT repack: min(15, max(3, limit / 2)) |
| `STAGE_GRACE_SEC` | 20 s | Grace around the post-solve jobs (worker start-up, CP-SAT's import included: `load_repack.warm_up`) |
| `load_repack.CLOSING_LATE_SEC` | 2 s | The most a job's closing recovery may end past the job's budget when its repacks ended late (strict priorities, [4.11](#411-post-solve-stage)); the stage's wait deadline adds it per round of jobs, still no later than the budget end − 2 s |
| `SOLVER_WORKER_START_SEC` (env) | 30 s | Rule 22: a new pool must run its first task within this, else the solve is refused (503 `WORKERS_UNAVAILABLE`); 1 to 600 s |
| `WORKER_ALERT_SEC` | 900 s | Rule 22: how long `/ready` reports a failed pool start, a pool that broke or one that did not close (cleared earlier only by a pool that starts `WORKER_ALERT_MIN_SEC` or more after the failure) |
| `WORKER_ALERT_MIN_SEC` | 300 s | Rule 22, second review: the shortest time `/ready` reports a failure, whatever pools start meanwhile (so monitoring polling every few minutes sees it) |
| `POOL_CLOSE_SEC` | 10 s | Rule 22 review: the longest a request waits for a pool to close; then an ERROR line and the cleanup goes on in the background |

**THOROUGH (29 Sep 2026, `config.search_mode`).** QUICK is everything above, unchanged (a pytest checks the same limits, budgets and search parameters, and that nothing is attached to its search). THOROUGH uses the same steps inside **one deadline, the cap** (`thorough_cap_sec`: `THOROUGH_MAX_SEC`, default 1,200 s, lowered by the request's `max_search_sec`); nothing runs past it (pytest: a hung load re-check and a hung alternative, each cut at the cap).

| Constant / env var | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `THOROUGH_MAX_SEC` (env) | 1,200 s | The whole request: road matrix (min(90 s, 20%)), every search, the load re-check |
| `rec_limit_sec` | cap − matrix − 20 s − tail | RECOMMENDED's search limit: everything up to the tail (`thorough_tail`: the alternatives' limit + 20 s grace + three repack solves + 25 s), and never less than QUICK's limit (T1). At 20 min with the slowest road matrix (90 s): 835-895 s (835 s above 350 stops, 880 s at 200-350, 895 s on NMWC-sized days); with a quick matrix (about 1 s) 924-984 s |
| `thorough_tail` (cap below 20 min) | at most 30% of the cap | Where the full tail (195 s for days up to 120 stops, 255 s above 350) is more than 30% of the cap, the alternatives' limit and each re-check solve shrink **together**, in proportion, never below QUICK's own (half the limit; min(15, max(3, limit / 2))), and `_run_scenarios` keeps exactly the re-check time the tail kept, so the alternatives get the rest of the tail. Review of the long-search PR: only the total used to be cut while the alternatives were still charged the full 115 s re-check reserve, so under about 7 min they were always skipped ("time budget used up by the recommended plan") and up to a third of the cap went unused. Below a cap of about 2-2.5 min for days up to 120 stops, 4.5-5.5 min at 175, 5.5-7 min from 200 to 350 and 8-9.5 min above 350 (the higher figure with the slowest road matrix; `rec_limit_sec`, `thorough_tail`) THOROUGH searches no longer than QUICK and may skip the alternatives: keep `THOROUGH_MAX_SEC` at 10 min or more (default 20) |
| `THOROUGH_STALL_SEC` / `THOROUGH_STALL_SHARE` (env) | 300 s / 0.5 | The convergence stop: RECOMMENDED's search ends once its best plan has not improved for max(300 s, 0.5 × the time searched so far), never before QUICK's time for the day (`StallRule`). A plan last improved at minute 8 is given until minute 16. Measured on 1,200 s traces: no stop lost anything; a shorter rule (max(90 s, 15%), the first proposal) lost up to 177 OMR of search objective on the real day ([OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md](./OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md) §11) |
| Second search (PyVRP, `_pv_start` / `_pv_submit` / `_pv_collect`) | its own 1-process pool | Started after rule 22's proof and never part of it (a pool that cannot start: SKIPPED / NO_PROCESS, the solve goes on). Submitted right after RECOMMENDED. QUICK: told to stop (`search_over`) once the alternatives are in, answer awaited `SOLVER_PYVRP_STOP_GRACE_SEC` at most; Thorough: searches until the load re-check's reserve (`budget_end − tail.stage_sec − 3 s`), its own stall, a stop or a cancel. Always collected before the engine's pool may close, never later than the engine's stage reserve; a worker that died is LOST at once (`_await_all` sees a task whose process is gone, even from before the wait). Its repack is a separate stage job in its own process, with at most the engine's job budget |
| `THOROUGH_ALT_MIN_SEC` | 60 s | Alternatives: max(QUICK's half limit, 60 s) with the 20-min cap (in proportion below it, `thorough_tail`), capped at what is left after the load re-check's time |
| `THOROUGH_REPACK_CAP_SEC` | 30 s | Each CP-SAT repack: max(QUICK's cap, 30 s) with the 20-min cap (in proportion below it); the repack still stops after a quarter of it without improvement (`_solve_until_stalled`). After a stop request the re-check runs with QUICK's cap. `test_load_recheck_time_per_mode` spies on `_post_solve`: THOROUGH passes the tail's cap (30 s), a stopped THOROUGH QUICK's, QUICK none (skeptic review: neither had a test) |

- **How the stop works.** `_watch_search` (THOROUGH only) adds an at-solution callback to the routing search: OR-Tools calls it for every solution the guided local search accepts (tens a second on NMWC days, 1-2 a second at 300 stops), it records the best objective over time, and once the stall rule (or a stop request) says so it calls `Solver.FinishCurrentSearch()`, which ends the search within milliseconds with its best plan. A `CustomLimit` was measured too and rejected: OR-Tools calls it 35,000-110,000 times a second, which cost 3-12% of the search's solutions. The time limit stays the backstop.
- **The report.** The response's `search` (`SearchReport`): mode, cap, RECOMMENDED's limit and search time, the whole request's time, why it stopped (`TIME_LIMIT` for QUICK, `CONVERGED`, `CAP`, `STOPPED`; in either mode `NOT_SEARCHED` when every stop was left out before the search and `NO_PLAN` when the search ended without any plan - skeptic review: both used to read "stopped when it stopped improving"), when the best plan was last improved, the stall that applied, at most 12 points of the best objective over time and the number of solutions. No gap is given: the search proves no bound. Each point is (seconds, search score, stops not planned yet): the score is not money, it holds a large penalty (1,000 OMR or more on real days) for each stop the plan had not planned yet, so a short day's first points are in the thousands (7,226 at the start for a plan that ends at about 170 OMR with every stop served). The watch counts those stops on each improvement (the stops whose successor is themselves: about 0.3 ms at 200 stops, 0.4 ms at 350, measured - under 0.6% of the search, [OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md](./OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md) §11.2) and the Excel prints them with each point, as a score (skeptic review: the ASSUMPTIONS row called it "in the currency"). Reports saved before the count have two values per point. The report is the recommended plan's search only: an alternative searches after it for its own limit with no stall rule (the web says so when one is applied, [2.7](#27-background-job-model)).
- **Cancel and stop (`main.py`).** The endpoint runs the solve in a worker thread and checks every second that its caller is still connected. A web app that restarts mid-solve closes the connection: `SolveControl.cancel()` makes the next wait (`_await_all`, every 0.5 s) raise `SolveAborted`, the worker pool is terminated and the slot frees at once, instead of searching on for nobody for up to 20 minutes while new solves get 503. `POST /optimize-dispatch/stop {run_id, tenant_id}` (token-checked; 404 when no solve of that plan and company runs here, 409 for a QUICK solve) sets the pool's stop flag: the THOROUGH search ends at its next solution, the alternatives are skipped with a warning, the re-check runs with QUICK's time, and the request answers as usual.

**Failure handling.**

- **Worker death, per task (PR4, review L23).** The pool is wrapped in `_Workers`, which stores its size (no `Pool._processes`) and learns which worker runs which task: every task reports its pid when it starts (`_tracked`, through a queue given to each worker at spawn). `_await_all` waits for several tasks in completion order and reports a task **lost** as soon as its own worker process disappears; a sibling that is still computing is never aborted because another worker died (before, any pid change aborted every pending task, and the lost one was noticed only at its deadline). Worker pids come from Pool's private worker list (`_POOL_ATTR`); if a Python upgrade removes it, `pids()` returns None with one log warning and deaths are noticed at the deadlines instead of failing every solve. Tests: `test_a_dead_worker_loses_only_its_own_task` (with and without the private list), `test_sibling_stage_worker_death_keeps_the_recommended_recheck`.
- **RECOMMENDED.** `_await_worker` (one task through `_await_all`) raises `SolveAborted` on the deadline, or when the worker running it dies (e.g. out of memory) and the pool replaces it. The endpoint turns `SolveAborted` into HTTP **504**. Test: `test_killed_recommended_worker_fails_fast`. When the pool broke (rule 22 review, above) it raises `WorkersUnavailable` instead: **503** `WORKERS_UNAVAILABLE`.
- **Alternatives.** A timeout, a lost worker, a broken pool or an exception only skips that alternative, and RECOMMENDED gets the warning "Alternative plan(s) … were skipped …". If an alternative overran (its worker is still busy) or the pool broke, the pool is terminated and a fresh one is created for the post-solve stage. Test: `test_hung_alternative_does_not_starve_the_load_recheck`. When that fresh pool cannot start (rule 22), the finished plans are kept rather than refused: no CP-SAT solve runs in the API process, each plan is re-timed exactly instead (`_retime_fallback`, one small LP per truck, milliseconds) with the note "Loads were not re-checked for fewer trucks (the planner was short of resources) ..." (`NO_WORKERS_NOTE`: plain words for the dispatcher; the technical cause is only in the ERROR line), and the ERROR line and `/ready` report the failed start. Test: `test_load_recheck_without_workers_keeps_the_recommended_plan`.
- **Worker start (rule 22).** Tests in `test_worker_start.py`: a pool that cannot start refuses a THOROUGH solve in under 5 s, before the road matrix, with no search entry point run in the API process, one ERROR line and `/ready` failed; workers that die while starting refuse after the start wait (3 s in the test), and at once when no replacement can start either (the worker-handler thread dies; `SpawnProcess._Popen` patched to raise EAGAIN from the third start; the start wait is 20 s there and the answer must come within 10 s, so "at once" cannot be the wait running out); the fallback only with exactly `SOLVER_ALLOW_INPROCESS_FALLBACK=1`; `SOLVER_PARALLEL=0` unchanged; the 503 over HTTP (the slot comes back, `/ready` alerts, a retry succeeds once processes start again, and `/ready` stays failed after it until the 5-minute minimum is over). The pool breaking during a solve (rule 22 review): RECOMMENDED's worker killed with no replacement possible is a 503 within seconds over HTTP (the slot and `_RUNNING` freed, `/ready` failed); the idle worker killed during RECOMMENDED keeps the recommended plan, re-checked by a fresh pool, well before the alternatives' deadline; every worker killed during the road matrix refuses a THOROUGH plan within `SOLVER_WORKER_START_SEC`; a `Pool.terminate()` that hangs makes `close()` return after `POOL_CLOSE_SEC` with the ERROR line. Second review: after the idle worker is killed, and after a `close()` that timed out followed by a pool that starts a second later, `/ready` still reports the failure; closing a pool (healthy, or one whose idle worker was killed and replaced) starts no process; a task queued behind a busy worker in a 1-worker pool (a 1 s start wait, a 4 s task) is not a broken pool and alerts nobody; the ERROR line and `/ready` failed exist when a pool that did not start is closed. Each of these checks that every worker process and Pool thread really stopped. The `ROUTEIQ_TEST_WORKER_START_EXIT=1` hook makes every worker exit while starting.
- **"Serves more" note.** When an alternative serves more stops than RECOMMENDED and its feasibility report is VERIFIED (PR4: before, a separate "unverified" set that never reached the response), RECOMMENDED gets a note that the other option serves N more stops. Nothing switches automatically.
- **`SOLVER_PARALLEL=0`** solves in-process with **no deadline and no budget**; tests and local debugging only (startup warning since PR4). The same for `SOLVER_ALLOW_INPROCESS_FALLBACK=1` after a failed pool start (rule 22).
- **Test hooks.** The env vars `ROUTEIQ_TEST_HANG_SCENARIO`, `ROUTEIQ_TEST_FAIL_SCENARIO`, `ROUTEIQ_TEST_KILL_SCENARIO`, `ROUTEIQ_TEST_FAIL_REPACK`, `ROUTEIQ_TEST_HANG_REPACK` and (PR4) `ROUTEIQ_TEST_KILL_REPACK=<goal>` inject failures in `_scenario_worker` / `_stage_worker`; (best-of-N, 16 Oct 2026) `ROUTEIQ_TEST_{HANG,FAIL,KILL}_VARIANT=<index>` and `ROUTEIQ_TEST_NO_STALL_VARIANT=<index>` (a search with no stall rule) do the same in `_variant_worker`, for the other searches only.

### 4.10 Extraction and reported costs

`_timed_from_assignment` walks each used vehicle's route:

- it splits the route into loads at the reload nodes; empty loads are skipped;
- each load departs "just in time" for its first stop: max(truck ready, first start − travel). The truck is ready at the start cumul, or at the reload cumul + approximate gap;
- service starts are recomputed forward.

`_build_scenario` is the **single place** where a timed plan (from the search or from the post-solve stage) becomes a `DispatchScenario`:

- **Per stop:** arrival, start, departure (= start + the `service_min` sent), wait, leg km and minutes, cumulative km, `hard_window_ok` and `pref_window_ok`. Minutes are rounded half-up once (`_min_of`). Since PR4 a service start earlier than the drive from the previous stop allows is **not** moved later any more (that hid a timing error and could push the return past the next load's departure unchecked); it stays as given and the feasibility report flags it (`TRAVEL`).
- **Feasibility (PR4, review F04):** at the end, `feasibility.safe_check` re-checks the scenario independently and sets `DispatchScenario.feasibility`; `timing` is EXACT for plans timed by `load_repack.time_plan` (or when no loading time per case is set), ESTIMATED for the route search's own times. A check that itself fails gives UNVERIFIED (never an error).
- **Costs (PR5, review F17; owner decision: the driver is paid for the WHOLE truck day).** One pure module, `apps/solver/costing.py` (`truck_day_costs`, policy `TRUCK_DAY_SPAN`), prices every truck day; `_build_scenario` reports it and `load_repack.score` compares candidates with it, so what the plan reports is what the optimizer minimized:
  - **driver pay** covers the truck day from its first departure (or first frozen departure) to its last return, depot turnaround and waiting included; loading the first load before the shift is not paid;
  - **overtime** is the paid time after that first departure + `overtime_after_min`, at `overtime_cost_per_hour` on top of the driver rate;
  - **per load** (documented allocation): each load owns the paid interval (previous return of its truck, its own return]; load 1 from its departure; the first new load after frozen loads from the last frozen return. `driver_cost` = that interval × rate, `overtime_cost` = its part after the overtime threshold. `fixed_cost` = the truck's day cost on load 1 only (a truck with frozen loads paid it with them); `trip_cost`, `distance_cost` (km × `cost_per_km`) and `fuel_cost` (km / `km_per_litre` × fuel price) are the load's own. `total_cost` is their sum; `time_cost` = `driver_cost`;
  - earlier loads' shares never change when later loads are added, so a re-plan's carried locked loads keep the cost they were planned with, and **locked + new = the whole truck day**, overtime counted once. Exception, documented: loads locked out of order (a later load locked while an earlier one stays planned, then re-planned after it) - the locked load keeps its original share; the workbook's TRUCK DAYS sheet notes the difference;
  - `operating_cost` = the sum of the loads. Each load's `total_cost` is its exact money rounded once to 0.001 OMR, and its six parts are rounded so that they add up to it exactly (`costing.round_parts`, largest remainder: each part within one baisa of its exact value, a zero part stays zero). The loads therefore add up to the exact truck-day money within 0.0005 OMR per load; a larger gap is logged and shown as a "Cost check" warning, never a failed optimization (PR5 review: the earlier check was tighter than the per-part rounding and failed 1-3 load re-plans with a 500). `truck_days[]` repeats the sum per truck;
  - `utilization_pct` = max(cases share, kg share).
- **Optimizer alignment (PR5).** The routing model's span cost plus, for a truck with frozen loads, a soft upper bound on its start at the last frozen return (so waiting before the first new load is paid, as in the report); the repack prices `last return − last frozen return` for such trucks; the exact timing LP no longer rewards a later first departure after frozen loads. Fresh days (no frozen loads) are priced exactly as before; the search models keep integer per-second coefficients, the score uses the exact rates.
- **Per scenario** also: `window_penalty` = minutes outside the preferred window × `pref_window_penalty_per_min`, and `preference_penalties` (window, early arrival, plan continuity; OMR-equivalent, not money); `unserved_penalty` = the unserved stops' service values in OMR; `margin_served` only when margins are in use.
- **On the web** ([3.7](#37-step-5-reviewing-the-plan)): each load's breakdown is stored in `PlanLoad.costJson` (migration `20260928090000_plan_load_cost_json`); the summary adds it up (`costBasis` TRUCK_DAY_SPAN, or MIXED_LEGACY when a load was costed before PR5), and the options table shows each option's **day** cost (carried locked loads + its new loads), physical trucks and kept + new loads (PR7), and its preference cost = `preference_penalties` window + early + continuity (PR7).
- **`objective_value`:** for a raw search plan, the OR-Tools objective; for a plan chosen in the post-solve stage, the candidate's RECOMMENDED-priced score (`best.score.objective`).

### 4.11 Post-solve stage

This is `load_repack.py`, orchestrated by `_post_solve` in `dispatch_solver.py`.

**Why it exists** (module docstring, `OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md` §8.1). The search moves one stop or a short chain at a time. It cannot move a whole load, with its reload visit, to another truck, so every truck tended to keep one short morning load. On NMWC's real day the result was 13 trucks / 21 loads / about 754 OMR, while the same loads fit on 5 trucks / 14 loads / about 490 OMR.

**Inputs (`_post_solve`).**

- The OPTIMIZED raw scenarios, converted back to `TimedPlan`s (`_timed_from_scenario`).
- `values` (the strict service values).
- A `Day` object: solvable stops, usable trucks, matrices, `shift_max_s`, `reload_s`, `loading_s_per_case`.
- `optional`: the stops at least one raw plan left out, weighted by `_repair_weights`. These are small strict-ladder integers, because the full values would not fit CP-SAT.
- `fit_weights` for every stop.
- One job per goal: RECOMMENDED always; MIN_TRUCKS when that scenario has a plan. Jobs run in the pool (`_stage_worker` → `build_candidates`).
- Job budget = min(cap × number of sources, budget left − 25 s). Under 3 s, the stage is skipped with a warning.
- **Extension (`extra_s`, benchmark of 8 Oct 2026, F07).** Each job (and the PyVRP stage job, in its own process) may also use more of the request's time beyond its budget: the rest of it up to the cap minus the grace, shared by the rounds of jobs, at most `EXTENDED_MAX_SEC` (240 s, its four steps of at most 60 s). It is granted, and the wait deadline grows with it, only when a search plan failed the independent check (VIOLATED: a VERIFIED plan always times exactly, so only then can a repair be needed); a hung worker on any other day is abandoned as before (`test_stuck_repack_worker_is_abandoned_in_time`). A job uses it only on a **repair day** (a source's plan could not be timed exactly) whose best plan still leaves stops out: P1-P3 stops, or any stop when its fit repack proved no bound (FEASIBLE with a gap, UNKNOWN). A day whose plans time cleanly, or whose repair serves every stop, ends as before.

**Load facts (`facts`, `depart_range`).**

- For a fixed load (stops in order), `facts` computes:
  - the no-wait offsets from departure to each service start, and the no-wait duration `d`;
  - `lo` = latest (hard start − offset): the earliest departure with no waiting on the road;
  - `hi` = earliest (hard end − offset): the latest departure that meets every hard window;
  - cases, kg, metres, and `gap` = `reload_s + loading_s_per_case × cases` of **this** load, i.e. the exact per-load loading time.
- If `lo > hi`, the load must wait on the road: it departs at `hi` and occupies the truck until `lo + d`.
- `depart_range(day, f, td)` returns the departure interval on a truck, or None if the load can never go on it. It checks cases and kg; the first departure (`earliest_depart_s`, or `ready_s + gap` after frozen loads or on a plan made on its delivery day, PR8 review; otherwise the first load of the day is assumed to be loaded before the shift starts); the latest return; and the shift length when there is no frozen anchor.

**CP-SAT repack (`repack`).**

- **Variables.** For each load j: a departure `e_j`, a selected flag `sel_j`, and a bool `x[j,t]` for each truck t it can go on, with Σ x = sel. Each x enforces the truck's departure interval.
- **Coverage.** Required stops (the ones the source plan carries) are covered by exactly one selected load. Other stops are covered at most once.
- **Per truck.** A `used` flag, and number of loads ≤ `trips_left`. `AddNoOverlap` over optional intervals [e_j − gap_j, e_j + occ_j), so each load's turnaround happens just before it. Day start `st` and end `en`, with `en − st ≤ shift_max` when there is no frozen anchor. A redundant "busy time" bound tightens the model.
- **Costs** (the goal's `Pricing`): fixed × used, plus (trip + per-metre × metres + continuity changes) × x; driver cost on the span, and overtime (on a truck with frozen loads only the new overtime: `en` minus the later of anchor + overtime-after and the last frozen return, audit E4); preferred-window and early-arrival hinges on e_j + offset. For a load that waits on the road these are constants computed at `hi`.
- **Symmetry breaking.** `_identical_trucks` groups interchangeable trucks (same capacity, hours, trips, frozen state and prices). It is disabled when continuity pricing is on. The hint is relabelled to match (`_relabel`, `_add_hint`).
- **Two phases.** If optional stops exist, phase 1 maximises the covered optional weight with 40 % of the time. That value is then fixed, and phase 2 minimises cost with the rest of the time. Service always comes before cost. Phase 1 ends by the solve's own limit, and so does phase 2, unless phase 1 ran long and left it less than 60 % of the limit (at most 0.5 s) (audit E5: each phase had a fixed 0.5 s floor that could push past the limit). Then phase 2 still gets that 60 %, at most 0.5 s, so it can reproduce the hinted plan, and ends up to that much past the limit.
- **Settings.** 2 CP-SAT workers. `_solve_until_stalled` stops when no better solution came for max(1 s, limit / 4) **after the first solution**; before the first one only the solver's own time limit stops it (audit E5: the stall clock started before the first solution, so a search whose first answer took longer than that was stopped with none, UNKNOWN - on a tight synthetic day in 3 of 12 solves). The source plan is the hint, so the result is never worse than the source on these prices.
- **No answer.** A repack that ends without a plan (UNKNOWN, out of time) logs a WARNING (`repack UNKNOWN after X s (limit Y s) for <source>/<goal>: kept the plan it started from`), and the plan it started from stays a candidate of that goal's job whenever it times exactly (audit E5). A fit repack without an answer is logged the same way; the job still has the incumbent (below), so the option gets a checked plan, partial if need be (benchmark F01).
- **Output.** `RepackResult(plan or None, status, seconds)`.

**Exact timing (`time_truck`, `time_plan`, `timing_ok`).**

- `time_truck` builds one GLOP LP per truck with variables D_j (depart), R_j (return) and t (service starts). Constraints: hard windows; "leave just in time" for the first stop; forward travel between stops; R = last start + service + drive back; D_j − R_{j−1} ≥ gap_j; the first departure ≥ `earliest_depart_s` (or frozen return + gap); the shift span when there is no anchor.
- It minimises the RECOMMENDED time costs (preferred and early hinges, span, overtime) plus tiny tie-breaks that keep the day compact.
- The constraints are difference constraints with integer data, so the LP optimum is rounded and then re-checked in integers by `timing_ok`, which covers every hard rule including the trip count.
- `time_plan` also checks each load's capacity.

**Scoring (`score`).** Every candidate is scored on **RECOMMENDED** prices (`_pricing("RECOMMENDED")`):

- `unserved` = the service value lost;
- `cost` = fixed + trip + km × rate + driver span + overtime + soft costs (preferred window, early arrival, continuity). Overtime here counts from the truck's first actual departure (or its frozen anchor), which differs deliberately from the routing model; see `_pricing`'s docstring. On a truck with frozen loads the new loads pay only the overtime after their last frozen return (`costing.truck_day_costs`), as the routing model and the repack now count it too (audit E4);
- also recorded: trucks, loads (new), metres, and `operating`. **Trucks are physical (PR7, B3):** the trucks with new loads + every truck with frozen loads today (`Day.frozen_trucks`, usable or not). Before, only the trucks with new loads counted, so for MIN_TRUCKS "both new loads on one fresh truck" (1) beat "one new load on each of two trucks already out" (2) although it uses 3 physical trucks and pays the fresh truck's day (`test_score_counts_the_trucks_of_frozen_loads`). A truck with frozen loads never pays the "open a truck" fixed cost again in any scenario: not in the routing model, not in the repack prices (`_pricing`, MIN_TRUCKS' ×20 included).

**Candidates (`build_candidates`).**

1. For the RECOMMENDED job (`time_raw`): each raw scenario plan, re-timed exactly. It is discarded if it is infeasible once timed exactly.
2. For each distinct source plan, fewest loads first (best-of-N's other searches after the options' own): a `"<source>+repack:<goal>"` candidate. The pool is the source's loads plus one-stop loads for its optional stops (drop repair). This runs on every day, including fleet-shortage days.
3. **Incumbent first (benchmark of 8 Oct 2026, F01 / F07).** When a source's raw plan cannot be timed exactly, before its repacks: `trim` keeps the part of it that times (each truck that breaks a rule loses its least valuable stop - strict service value, on a tie the longest detour - one at a time, about one timing per stop) and `recover` puts the stops it lost back (below). The result is a `"<source>+recover:<goal>"` candidate within `INCUMBENT_SHARE` (40 %) of the source's time, so the option always has a plan that keeps every rule. On D5 native the main search's plan broke the driver breaks of 8 trucks: trim kept 168 of 180 stops and recover put back the other 12.
4. **Fit fallback.** If the repack found nothing *and* the raw plan cannot be timed exactly, it is repacked once more with every stop optional, hinted with the incumbent. `fit_pool` (F02), most useful first, up to `FIT_POOL_PER_STOP` (3) × its stops + its loads + `FIT_POOL_MIN` (60) entries so the CP-SAT model stays solvable in seconds: each load as is (the incumbent's loads too); **a one-stop load for every stop** (before, only for the stops the search had left out, so a stop the search carried whose load did not survive the timing could not go alone on an idle truck: P02's C3); each load minus one stop; each load cut in two (every prefix and suffix); each load minus two stops, the pairs of least value first. This gives a `"+fit:<goal>"` candidate. It typically happens when loads are more than 80 % full and a per-case loading time is set, or when the search's plan leaves no room for a driver break.
5. **Recovery of the job's best plan** (`recover`). The job's best candidate for its goal gets the stops it leaves out inserted, in strict priority order (P1 first; then the earliest latest start, then the most cases), each where exact timing still passes: into an existing load (its `RECOVER_POSITIONS` cheapest positions by detour), or as a new one-stop load before, between or after a truck's loads (spare time after its last return), or on an idle truck. The `RECOVER_TRIES` (24) cheapest estimates are timed with `time_truck` (breaks, loading readiness and turnaround, shift, depot hours, frozen reservations) and checked with `fits_truck` (pallets / cases / kg); of up to `RECOVER_KEEP` (3) that time, the best for the goal is kept (`load_repack.GOALS`, the same comparison as `_GOALS`), and never one that does not serve more (`Score.service`: a rented truck is not opened for P4/P5 orders alone). The plan's other trucks are not touched. Frozen (locked, loading, dispatched) loads are never in a plan, only the trucks' reservations, so nothing moves them. On a day whose plans timed cleanly this runs at most `CLEAN_RECOVER_SEC` (2 s); on a repair day for the rest of the job's budget. **Swaps on every day (review solver-pipeline-1, Oct 2026).** A stop that fits nowhere may take the place of stops of a lower priority on one load (`_swaps`: tried one stop off before two, then by the smallest km change, and the first that times and serves more is kept - so a P4 order may come off where a P5 order would also have made room, note (b) of the first review, a known limit (in weighted mode, API only, it can cost more than one stop): choosing among several swaps, by the least value put out or by the stops that go back in, was about even on random days without a deadline and clearly worse when the 2 s run out; more of the load's lower stops off - least valuable first, then the biggest - only when one leaves too little room and only while together they are worth less than the stop), timed with the truck's whole day; the stops taken off wait for their own turn to be inserted again, and a swap is kept only when the plan serves more by strict service value. Stops that fit nowhere get another round once the queue is empty, those that failed before the last placement (a stop that failed after it would fail again on the same plan) (third review of the strict-priority fix: a P1 order failed its turn, a P5 order went in later, and the P1 then fitted in its place, with the reason "the planner found no load that could take it"; fourth review: retrying after every placement instead cost failed stops x placements timings and ran the 2 s out on shortage days, 40,614 timing LPs where one pass needs 404); every step serves strictly more, so the recovery ends. On the reviews' random days this leaves 1-for-1 inversions on 37 of 3,000 days instead of 104 with the swaps alone (recover alone, never serving less on any of them) and on 20 of 2,000 instead of 73 through a stage job (9 of them with a P1-P3 order out, instead of 51); the rounds cost about 8-22 % more timing LPs, nearly 3 times one pass on a shortage day where 20 P1 orders fit nowhere (1,124 timing LPs); the rest come from the 24-try limit and the positions `_swaps` offers, so the reason text is still not a proof. Before, only a repair day's extension swapped, so a clean shortage day delivered P4 orders while a P3 order that fits in their place was left out (all three options, VERIFIED, with "Lower priorities are left out first (this is P3)"). When a source plan leaves a stop out while it carries a stop of a lower priority, the repacks leave the closing recovery min(`CLEAN_RECOVER_SEC`, a third of the job's budget) (`CLOSING_SHARE`): in the reviewer's run they had used all of it and the recovery never ran. The recovery gets that time from when it actually starts: when the repacks end late (CP-SAT's last phase may run up to 0.5 s over, then their plans are timed), it may end up to `CLOSING_LATE_SEC` (2 s) past the job's budget, never later, and `_post_solve` waits for it (the stage's wait deadline adds it per round of jobs, still no later than the budget end − 2 s). CP-SAT is imported when a stage job starts (`load_repack.warm_up`, in `_stage_worker` and the PyVRP stage job), before the job's clock: cold, in a fresh worker, it takes 1.3-2 s, and `repack` counts any import in its own limit and seconds. Before (review of the strict-priority fix), the first repack of every stage job imported it outside its limit, so under load the reserve was gone and the recovery never ran on the reviewer's next-day 150-stop plan (3 of 4 runs). The PyVRP stage job runs the same `build_candidates`, so its plans get it too.
6. **Extension** (only as described under Inputs): a **deep recovery** (every insertion tried, and swaps: a P1-P3 stop that fits nowhere may take the place of a stop of lower priority, which then waits for its own turn to be inserted again; strict service value, so the plan always serves more); then, while P1-P3 stops are still out, the **constructive fallback** (`recover` of an empty plan, farthest from the depot first within a priority, with swaps; a `"FALLBACK:<goal>"` candidate, built by the engine's RECOMMENDED job only, like the report's greedy witness) and a longer fit repack hinted with the best plan, then recovery again. Each step at most `EXTENDED_STEP_MAX_SEC` (60 s).

The time is shared fairly across sources (`share`). Every candidate is fully timed and scored, and the pick below keeps the best by the goal's service-first comparison: a later candidate replaces an earlier one only when it is better (feasibility, then P1..P5 service, then cost with preferences).

**Selection per scenario (`_post_solve`, `_GOALS`).**

- RECOMMENDED: (unserved, cost). MIN_TRUCKS: (unserved, physical trucks, loads, operating, cost). MIN_DISTANCE: (unserved, metres, cost).
- A scenario only considers candidates whose `unserved` value is no worse than its own raw plan's.
- If no candidate qualifies, the raw plan broke the exact loading time. The scenario then takes the best candidate overall, and the stops it loses become `timing_drops`.
- Ties prefer candidates derived from the scenario's own search, then any other engine search, then best-of-N's other searches, then the second search (PyVRP).
- **Best-of-N's other searches (solver search upgrade, 16 Oct 2026; `SOLVER_BEST_OF`, off by default).** Their plans come in as `extra_sources` named `RECOMMENDED~<i>` (`LR.Source.extra`): more sources of the same jobs (their left-out stops become optional; the F07 extension is still granted by the options' own plans only), repacked after the options' own, so a plan both make keeps the option's own name. A candidate built from one (`_from_extra`) is used only when it beats the best candidate built without any by a gain the dispatcher can see - the second search's rule (`_goal_gain`: at least 1 OMR or 1 km, fewer trucks or loads, or more service); otherwise that best candidate is the engine's choice, and the second search is compared with it (and falls back to it when its plan fails the independent check). Then the plan's note says so ("Route search 3 of 4 (started from another order of the stops) found a better plan for this option than the main search: …", `_best_of_note`) and `SearchReport.best_of.chosen_for` lists the option. `best_of.gains` records, per option, the best candidate of the other searches against the best one without them on the re-check's own scores (paired evidence of what they add, whether or not it was used). They are not quite "only more candidates" (critiques of 16 Oct 2026): their left-out stops widen the jobs' optional stops and so the strict weights of the options' own repacks, a job's closing recovery and F07 fit repack start from its best plan whichever source made it (and keep that source's name), and the job budget grows by one repack cap per extra source - which is why the replay of saved real requests, not this rule alone, decides whether to switch them on.
- All candidates are shared across scenarios. So, unless it serves more, MIN_DISTANCE never drives more km and MIN_TRUCKS never uses more trucks than RECOMMENDED.
- **The priority repair (solver search upgrade, 16 Oct 2026; `SOLVER_PRIORITY_REPAIR`, off by default).** After the stage, `_run_scenarios` runs `_repair_inversions` when it is on: each option whose plan passes the independent check but leaves a P1-P3 stop out while a stop it outranks rides (`_inversions`) gets the hire check's repair with no solve (`_repair_lost`: the swap, then every stop it outranks taken off one truck's whole day, then a chain of two moves). The repaired plan replaces the option's only when it passes the independent check and serves the day better by priority (`_service_rank`); it keeps the option's other warnings and adds "N P1-P3 stop(s) left out while lower-priority stops rode were put back in their place after the load re-check …", ending "The notes above about the route search and the load re-check describe the plan before this repair." when it kept such notes (review of 16 Oct 2026: they read as if about the repaired plan). A stop it took off and found no other place for reads "Not planned: a higher-priority stop was put in its place after the load re-check …" (`PRIORITY_DISPLACED_HEAD`). Bounded: one deadline for all options, 10 s from its start and never later than `STAGE_GRACE_SEC` before the budget ends, enforced in every step (the swap's timings too); skipped after a stop request; RECOMMENDED is left to the hire check when the request has trucks to rent; the hire check's own solves never run it. A clean day is not touched. Each option is repaired on its own, so a repaired option may serve the day better by priority than one the deadline left as it was. After a repair, "serves N more stop(s)" is offered only for an alternative that serves the day no worse by priority.
- **Join small trips (24 Oct 2026; `SOLVER_JOIN_TRIPS`, off by default; `join_trips.py`).** Nothing above can join two loads: the repack moves whole loads between trucks and the recovery only inserts stops left out, so a company truck could keep a second or third load of one to three customers that its other loads could carry (pilot study of 24 Oct 2026). In `_post_solve`, once an option's plan is built - after the pick, `_shorter_orders`, the PyVRP gain rule and every fallback of the build loop, so every comparison above stays as without it - `_join_option` runs `join_trips.join_plan` on the chosen candidate (at most 2 s per option and 6 s per solve counted from the first option's step, never past the budget end - 2 s; its seconds are given back to `_shorter_orders`' window, so report mode leaves that step its time; LPs only, in the API process like `_shorter_orders`): for each company truck (`not _hired_km`: never a truck to rent or one whose driver is paid by the day) with two or more new loads, the proposals that make it one load fewer - a small load (at most 3 customer visits, the parts of a split order counted once and kept together, any size: `fits_truck` decides the room, bays x Pallet fill or every bay for one customer) as one run in every gap of another load, its visits spread over the other loads (three loads or more), and the truck's shortest round of all its stops cut into fewer loads - ranked by `_day_estimate`, the best 12 timed exactly with `time_truck` (windows, turnaround, the driver break at its cheapest place, latest return, shift, loads per day), and the best one in up to three other stop orders per load. A change is taken when it is at least 0.5 OMR cheaper on money plus the customer time preferences, costs no more money, drives no more km on MIN_DISTANCE, and keeps at least 20 min to the truck's latest return (or the shift's end) and to the break window's end, or is no tighter there than the plan it replaces (owner decision 24 Oct 2026); then the truck is tried again (3 -> 2 -> 1). Locked, loading and dispatched loads are never in a plan, so they are never touched; they bind only through the truck-day (its ready time, frozen return and loads left). The whole joined plan is checked again (the same stops, strictly better on the option's goal `_GOALS`, the gain, no more money), built with the exact arguments of the build it replaces (`kw`, so an argument added to that build later comes along) and used only when the independent check says VERIFIED (else `NOT_VERIFIED`: the plan without it, and a WARNING line); report mode builds and checks it too, then keeps the plan. The notes about how the plan was chosen ("Loads were re-assigned after the route search ...", the second search's, best-of's) keep the numbers of the plan before the join and are carried over; the join's own note comes last: "Small loads joined after the load re-check: T05 2 -> 1 loads (back 13:40 instead of 15:10); ... In all 12 -> 10 loads, 410 -> 402 OMR operating cost. Each joined day was timed again with every rule, the driver break included, and checked independently." (truck codes only, at most 4 trucks named). Moving a one-visit load onto another company truck already out (MOVE) is worked out and reported (`applied: false`) but not applied (`join_trips.ACROSS`, owner decision pending). `SearchReport.join_trips` has per option the outcome (JOINED, WOULD_JOIN, NOT_VERIFIED, ERROR, or the furthest step reached: NO_SMALL_LOAD, NONE_FITS, NOT_BETTER, SLACK, OUT_OF_TIME), loads and gains, and per change the truck, the small load's stop ids, the truck's loads after it (`stops_after`, stop ids in order: what a dispatcher reviews in report mode), the gains, the last return before and after and the margins; its seconds, timings and LPs are the step's own. Its `status` is `FAILED` whenever an option was `NOT_VERIFIED` or `ERROR`, whatever the others did (else `JOINED`, `WOULD_JOIN` or `NONE`), and the log line `join-trips run=<id> ...` counts each option's changes by kind (a reported `MOVE` can sit under `NO_SMALL_LOAD`, which also means no company truck had two new loads). The priority repair runs on the joined plan and keeps its note. Never at the cost of a plan: an error anywhere in `_join_option` is ERROR and the plan stays; the safety net's plans are never joined (that option has no entry; SKIPPED `NO_STAGE` when no option reached the step). The hire suggestion's what-if is never joined (SKIPPED `HIRE_CHECK`; its trial solves get no join), so with `on` the plan in use may be joined while the what-if it is compared with is not: the suggestion's cost comparison is then against an unjoined baseline (3.19).
- If no candidate exists at all (the jobs ran but none produced a timed plan), the raw plan is trimmed in-process to the part that times (`_trimmed`, below); only when nothing of it can be timed is it kept with a warning, its feasibility report saying what it breaks. Only VERIFIED scenarios are advertised as "serves N more".

**Safety net when the stage does not re-check a plan (PR4, review F04).** When the stage is skipped (out of time), its RECOMMENDED job fails, times out or loses its worker, or `_post_solve` raises, every raw plan it had not replaced yet (`done` / `staged`) gets `_retime_fallback`: with a loading time per case set, the **same loads are re-timed exactly** in-process (`load_repack.time_plan`, one GLOP LP per truck, milliseconds; no CP-SAT) and rebuilt, so their departure times keep the exact turnaround (VERIFIED, EXACT). A plan that cannot be re-timed with these loads is trimmed to the part that can (`_trimmed`, benchmark F01: `load_repack.trim` in the API process, bounded by `TRIM_FALLBACK_SEC` = 1.5 s per option, about one timing per stop it leaves out): a checked partial plan (VERIFIED, EXACT) whose left-out stops carry the timing-drop reason and the warning *"The complete plan could not be timed with every rule, so this option is the part of it that can: ..."*. Only when nothing of it can be timed does it stay as the route search found it, with a warning ("could not be re-timed exactly") and a VIOLATED report: shown for review, never dispatchable (the web's feasibility gate). The internal-error path no longer infers "re-checked" from warning texts, so a scenario the stage already replaced keeps its plan without a false "not re-checked" note. Tests: `test_feasibility.py` (`test_stage_failure_with_loading_time_is_retimed_or_flagged`, the review's reproduction: L2 now leaves ≥ L1 return + 130 min; `test_out_of_time_stage_is_retimed`; `test_stage_internal_error_keeps_what_it_already_rechecked`; `test_verified_implies_plan_rules` over three day shapes).

**Warnings added.**

- Timing drops: "N stop(s) the route search had planned are left out …", ending "so the lowest priorities were left out" only when no lower priority rides; otherwise "so they were left out, K of them although lower-priority stops are planned" (16 Oct 2026). A plan built again from it (`_rebuilt`: the hire check, the priority repair) keeps it word for word only while it is still true, works it out again for the timing drops still out - keeping a trimmed plan's "The complete plan could not be timed with every rule …" and the "N stop(s) the route search had left out are planned instead" count (`_timing_warning_parts`) - and drops it when it serves them all.
- A repack that changed the plan: "Loads were re-assigned after the route search: A -> B trucks, … OMR operating cost", plus added stops.
- "N stop(s) the route search had left out were planned after the search".
- A checked partial plan instead of one that breaks the rules (F01): "The complete plan could not be timed with every rule, so this option is the part of it that can: ..." with the timing-drop warning.
- On the web plan screen (not from the solver; `lib/dispatch/left-out-note.ts`, F02 / F07): "N priority 1-3 orders are left out although M trucks are unused. Run the search again (Thorough) or add them by hand." when the plan leaves out P1-P3 orders (not those brought forward to a later day) and trucks of the plan's saved inputs carry no load. Review of 9 Oct 2026: only orders left out for a reason a longer search or an unused truck could change are counted (`IDLE_TRUCK_REASONS`: the search's drops, late orders without room, no truck, the trip limit, no plan found, unknown). Not orders never sent to the optimizer (no usable location, a deactivated customer, cases heavier than any truck, an unknown customer or product), nor `HARD_WINDOW_INFEASIBLE` / `SHIFT_LIMIT`, which the optimizer proves against every usable truck, the unused ones included (before, a customer without a pin planned "anyway" asked for a Thorough search that could never place it).
- On stage timeout, failure or no budget: "Loads were not re-checked for fewer trucks (…); this is the route search result as found." When a per-case loading time is set, it adds "Departure times were re-timed exactly …" or, when that was impossible, "… could not be re-timed exactly: check the timetable before dispatching, or re-plan."

### 4.12 Unserved reason codes and messages

`UnservedReason` is defined in `dispatch_models.py` and mirrored as `DispatchUnservedReason` in `packages/shared-types/src/dispatch.ts`. The Prisma enum `UnservedReasonCode` in `apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma` has these codes plus older v1 codes.

| Code | Set by | When | Message (from code) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MISSING_COORDINATES` / `INVALID_LOCATION` | web `buildDispatchRequest` (pre-drop) | no or invalid location, or outside the service area and not verified, or (audit PR A5) a LOW reading not verified | the customer issue text |
| `INVALID_CUSTOMER` | web `buildDispatchRequest` (pre-drop) | the customer was deactivated after its orders were confirmed | "Customer deactivated after the order was confirmed - reactivate it in Customers to deliver it, or leave it unserved." |
| `EXCEEDS_ANY_TRUCK_CAPACITY` | web `buildDispatchRequest` (pre-drop, the order's heavy lines only) | one case heavier than every usable truck payload | "One case of X weighs N kg, more than any truck payload (M kg) - check the product weight." |
| `NO_AVAILABLE_TRUCK` | `_prefilter` | request has no trucks | "No active trucks at this depot." |
| `NO_ALLOWED_TRUCK` | `_prefilter` / `_build_scenario` (`_not_placed_on_allowed`) | a stop with `allowed_truck_ids` (a small-truck-only customer, owner request 13 Oct 2026) that none of its trucks can take: none can take a new load today, the order is larger than the largest of them (split deliveries off), or (after the search) they had no room or time; checked before the fleet-wide reasons, so a big truck with room never reads as "re-plan to search again" | "Needs a small truck (at most 6 bays): no such truck had room or time left for this P2 stop (T03, T05); the other trucks may not deliver here. Add or hire such a truck, or re-plan." (with `_no_room_reason` appended when the room check proves it). Web label *Needs a small truck*; in the hire check's `CAPACITY_REASONS`, not in `IDLE_TRUCK_REASONS` |
| `TRIP_LIMIT` | `_prefilter` | no usable truck; every truck used up its trips on frozen loads | "Every truck has already used its maximum number of loads (locked/dispatched)." |
| `SHIFT_LIMIT` | `_prefilter` / `_window_prefilter` | no truck has time left (the start for new loads at or after the depot closing, trucks outside their available hours, or taken up by frozen loads) / the round trip does not fit the shift or depot hours | "Planned on the delivery day from 18:15: the depot closes at 18:00, so no new load can leave today." / "No truck is available for a new load between …" / "No truck has shift time left after its locked/dispatched loads." / "A round trip to this customer does not fit inside the truck shift / depot hours." |
| `EXCEEDS_ANY_TRUCK_CAPACITY` | `_prefilter` | cases or kg above every usable truck | "Order is larger than any available truck (…). Split it or use a bigger truck." |
| `HARD_WINDOW_INFEASIBLE` | `_window_prefilter` | no truck can start service inside the hard window | "No truck can reach this customer inside its receiving window HH:MM-HH:MM (earliest possible arrival HH:MM)." |
| `INFEASIBLE` | `_solve_scenario` | the search returned no assignment (scenario `NO_SOLUTION`) | "The optimizer found no feasible plan: <the status in plain words, e.g. no plan was found in the time allowed>. Re-plan to search again, ..." (`_no_plan_message`, PR6; the raw status name before) |
| `LATE_ORDER_NO_CAPACITY` | `_build_scenario` | unserved stop with `late=true` | "Late order (Pn): no unlocked truck/load had capacity or time left. …" |
| `SOLVER_DROPPED_LOW_PRIORITY` (timing) | `_build_scenario` (`_timing_drop_reason`) | the stop is in `timing_drops` (the search planned it; the exact loading time did not leave room) | "Not planned: once every load was timed with the loading time between loads …, the route search's loads no longer fitted the truck days and this Pn stop was left out …". It ends "(lowest priorities first). Re-plan, add a truck, or check the loading time." whenever no lower-priority stop is planned (the text from before, word for word, also for the day's lowest priority: owner decision 16 Oct 2026, texts change only where they were untrue); when N lower-priority stops are planned (solver search upgrade, 16 Oct 2026: a P2 stop read "lowest priorities first" while P3 and P4 stops rode) "… although N lower-priority stops are planned: no check proves it cannot go in their place. Re-plan, add a truck, or add it by hand in place of a lower-priority stop." With the priority repair on (`SOLVER_PRIORITY_REPAIR`) the middle part says what it did: "the planner then tried to put it in place of lower-priority stops and found no place that keeps every rule (not a proof)" or "no time was left to try it in place of lower-priority stops" |
| `SOLVER_DROPPED_LOW_PRIORITY` (displaced) | `_build_scenario` (`displaced`, `_displaced_reason`) | the priority repair (`SOLVER_PRIORITY_REPAIR`, off by default) took the stop off its load to put a higher-priority stop in its place and found no other place for it; never counted among the "could not be placed" stops | "Not planned: a higher-priority stop was put in its place after the load re-check (higher priorities go first), and no other place was found for this Pn stop. Add a truck or add it by hand." |
| `SOLVER_DROPPED_LOW_PRIORITY` (shortage) | `_build_scenario` | total demanded cases > Σ capacity × trips left, or (PR6) total demanded kg > Σ payload × trips left when every usable truck has a payload | `_shortage_reason`: "Fleet capacity shortage: X cases requested vs Y …" (cases only); "Fleet capacity shortage by weight: X kg requested vs Y kg … (the N cases would fit by count; the weight does not)" (kg only); "… X cases / A kg requested vs Y cases / B kg …; weight is the tighter limit today" (both). It ends "Lower priorities are left out first (this is Pn)." only when the day has stops of a lower priority and none of them is planned (the A6 rule of the "no room" reason; scenario s3-shortage-hire-2, Oct 2026: a P1 order kept out by its receiving hours said so while P3 / P4 orders rode). When N lower-priority stops are planned: "This Pn stop was left out although N lower-priority stops are planned: the planner found no load that could take it in their place (its receiving hours, the trucks' hours or their room). Add a truck, widen its receiving hours, or add it by hand."; on a day with no lower priority: "This Pn stop was left out." |
| `SOLVER_DROPPED_LOW_PRIORITY` (no room) | `_build_scenario` (`_no_room_reason`, audit F08) | no shortage, but no load of the plan and no free trip has room for the stop by cases and kg (in 0.1 kg), counting on each load only its stops of the same or a higher priority (A6 review: strict priorities drop lower ones first, so a stop left out by time while lower-priority stops fill the loads keeps the "open" text and its warning), **and** a check proves that no other packing of those stops could carry it too (A6 second review, `_no_packing_fits`, in cases and in kg: together they are more than all usable trips carry, or more of them are over half the biggest truck than there are usable trips; room the route search left spread over several loads proves nothing, so such a stop keeps the "open" text and its warning) | "Not planned: no load or free trip has room for its 1,600 kg (the most room left on a load that takes its 10 cases is 1,400 kg). This Pn stop was left out. Add a truck or raise the loads-per-truck limit." (or "... room for its N cases ..."; "left out (lowest priorities first)" only when the day has lower-priority stops and none of them rides); when lower-priority stops ride on the plan: "... room for its 1,600 kg, even with every lower-priority stop taken off (then the most room on a load that takes its 10 cases is 1,400 kg). This Pn stop was left out. ..."; before, the "open" text below, which advised a re-plan that cannot help |
| `SOLVER_DROPPED_LOW_PRIORITY` (open) | `_build_scenario` | anything else (some load or free trip has room for it, or no check proves that another packing could not carry it). Never called impossible, because only the prefilters prove impossibility | "Not planned: the optimizer found no truck, trip or time slot for this Pn stop within its time limit. …" plus a scenario warning |
| `UNKNOWN_CUSTOMER`, `UNKNOWN_PRODUCT`, `LOCKED_PLAN_CONFLICT`, `ROUTING_PROVIDER_FAILURE`, `UNKNOWN` | no emitter found | in the contract; UI labels exist in `apps/web/app/t/[slug]/dispatch/client-api.ts` | `ROUTING_PROVIDER_FAILURE` appears only as a warning-text prefix in `resolve_matrix` |

On a shortage day, `_build_scenario` adds another warning when what is unserved is more than the shortage explains, in every unit the trucks are short of (PR6: cases, and kg when the payload is the limit; the unserved cases or kg above the shortage plus the largest unserved order): "The trucks are X cases and Y kg short today, but N cases (M kg) are unserved: more than the shortage alone explains …". Before PR6 it counted cases only, so a weight-bound day (scenario test S03: every load 99.8 % full by kg) got this warning and its "re-plan to search again" advice, which cannot help. Since the PR6 review the warning also needs an unserved stop that still fits, by cases and by kg, the room left on a load of the plan or on a load a truck did not use (`_fits_room_left`). Whole stops leave some room on every load, so on a day with several loads the unserved amount can pass "shortage + one order" although nothing more fits (6 loads each 116 kg short of full, every unserved stop 336 kg): that day gets no warning. When an unserved stop does fit somewhere, time, hours or the search's limit kept it out, and the warning stays. The plan screen heads every `SOLVER_DROPPED_LOW_PRIORITY` with "Not planned by the optimizer - see reason" (`OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md` §8.4).

### 4.13 Reconciliation assertion

`_assert_reconciled(req, sc)` runs at the end of every `_build_scenario`. It checks that:

- every request `stop_id` appears exactly once, in one load or in `unserved` (no duplicates, no missing stops, no unknown stops);
- planned cases + unserved cases = total requested cases.

On failure it raises `ReconciliationError`, a subclass of `AssertionError`:

- in the RECOMMENDED worker the exception is not caught, so the request fails. It is not converted to 504 the way `SolveAborted` is;
- in an alternative's worker, that alternative is skipped;
- in `_post_solve`, `_run_scenarios` catches it and keeps the search plans with the "internal error" warning.

`_empty_scenario` (NOTHING_TO_PLAN / NO_SOLUTION) does not call the assertion.

The web repeats a stricter check after saving: `reconcile` in `apps/web/lib/dispatch/reconcile.ts`, called from `refreshPlanFacts` in `plan-service.ts` ([3.6](#36-step-4-optimize)).

### 4.14 Legacy PyVRP /optimize path

- **Solver side.** `apps/solver/solver.py` (PyVRP, `optimize`), with `models.py` and `distance.py` (Haversine and Mapbox matrix), is still served at `POST /optimize` in `main.py`. The solver README describes it as "kept for comparison only".
- **Git history.** Commit `4c40e12` (11 May 2026) swapped OR-Tools for PyVRP on `/optimize`. The OR-Tools dispatch engine arrived in `b50484e` (24 Sep 2026, PR #25).
- **Limits** (`OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md` §4). The installed PyVRP 0.13.4 `solve()` is iterated local search, not HGS. `solver.py` has no reload depots and no soft windows, and its priority prizes are linear (dropping P1 costs only 5× as much as dropping P5). Since 30 Sep 2026 `requirements.txt` pins `pyvrp==0.14.0` (the dispatch engine's second search, `pyvrp_candidate.py`) and `solver.py` is ported to the 0.14 API (`add_location`, then `add_depot(location)` / `add_client(location)`; edges join locations; a route is a list of activities). No behaviour change is intended; the 27 legacy tests pass unchanged.
- **Web side: removed in PR5.** `scheduleOptimize`, `runOptimizeJob`, `buildSolverPayload` (`lib/jobs/optimize-job.ts`) and `callSolver` (`lib/solver-client.ts`) had no reachable caller and are deleted. `optimize-job.ts` keeps `trackInflight`, `isOptimizing`, `whenIdle` and `reapStuckJobs`. `POST /api/runs/[id]/optimize` calls `startDispatchOptimize`. Re-optimizing a plan made by the old optimizer is refused with 409 `LEGACY_PLAN` (`isLegacyPlan`, `start-optimize.ts`).
- **Tests and scripts.** `apps/solver/tests/test_solver.py` (27 tests) still tests the PyVRP module (its docstring says so since PR5). `scripts/bench_day1.py` targets it too.
- **Recommendation** (`OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md` §6.4): remove the endpoint once nothing in `apps/web` calls it (the owner decided to keep it for now). The `pyvrp` dependency stays: the dispatch engine's second search uses it (`OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md` §12).

### 4.15 Benchmark results

All from `docs/OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md`.

- **Decision (§1, §6).** Keep OR-Tools with a self-hosted OSRM. It is the only candidate covering every NMWC rule without a licence fee. VROOM, Timefold, the Google Route Optimization API and PyVRP were compared (§4) and not adopted; §7 lists when to revisit.
- **First measurements (§5).** Synthetic Muscat days, Haversine matrix, 12 trucks.
  - 60 stops: 12.6 s wall. 150 stops: 30.7 s, all stops served.
  - 300 stops failed: a worker died and a warm start stalled.
  - At the old 45 s limit, 40 feasible P5 stops were dropped.
- **Fixes (§5a).** Per-worker deadlines, `soft_prefs` only in RECOMMENDED, 150 s / 240 s limits for big days, plan continuity. After them, 300 stops were all served in 226 s wall. Continuity cut a demo re-plan from 116 changed assignments to 16.
- **Post-solve validation (§8.3).** Production mode, 2 runs per instance, neutral evaluator. The old engine is the `b22a51a` baseline:

| Instance | Old engine RECOMMENDED (trucks / loads / op. cost OMR) | New engine | Objective change |
|---|---|---|---|
| real80 (NMWC real day) | 12 / 19 / 719.9 | 5 / 14 / 492.4–494.9 | −28 % |
| real80_prod | 12 / 21 / 467.2 | 7 / 21 / 310.9 | −30.7 % |
| syn150_s2 / s3 | 11 / 11 / 560.3; 10 / 10 / 514.7 | 8 / 11 / 490.5; 8 / 10 / 464.7 | −9.6 % / −6.7 % |
| syn60 ×3, syn150_s1, syn300_s1 | — | equal or within 0.3 % | ≈ 0 |
| real80_realism (per-case timing) | 10 / 19 / 678.7 (9 loads leave before the truck is loaded) | 6 / 14 / 574–575 | −15 % |

- Against the original 754 OMR, real80 is **−34 %**. It is within about 1 % of the best plan from hours of offline search and 4 % above the 473.9 OMR lower bound.
- Wall time: at most 57 s for days up to 200 stops, and 253 s at 300 stops. The post-solve stage took 1–2 s on synthetic days and about 15–20 s on the real day.
- The new engine varied at most 0.6 % between runs; the old one varied 5–14 %.
- All 60 returned scenarios had 0 violations and all reconciled.
- **Review fixes (§8.4).** 11 defects fixed. On 20 random stress days with per-case loading time, plans that broke the loading time went from 10 of 20 days to **0 of 20**. Post-fix validation matched §8.3: real80 −24 % to −28 %; wall 46–54 s up to 200 stops and 239–244 s at 300.
- **80 % vs 100 % turnaround estimate** during the search: measured with no clear winner, so 80 % stays until real NMWC days with a loading time exist.
- **Harness.** The real-day harness lives in `.dev/bench` (local only, not in git, contains real customer data). The doc gives aggregate numbers only.
- **Outside benchmark of 8 Oct 2026: the recovery fix (F01, F02, F07).** Replays of the benchmark's synthetic inputs through the production worker path (the bundle's lane scripts, 4 CPUs; P02 on 2), every output checked by the bundle's independent checker (it imports no RouteIQ code). "Before" is `main` at `5b2ee06`: the benchmark's saved runs, and a rerun here where noted.
