### 4.16 Re-timing truck days for a move by hand

(PR M1, 24 Oct 2026: the solver part of moving stops by hand. Its caller is the web's check and save (M2, `lib/dispatch/plan-edit.ts`, `plan-edit-apply.ts`) behind the Move dialog (M3), switched by `PLAN_EDIT`; [3.7](#37-step-5-reviewing-the-plan).) `POST /retime-truck-days` (`apps/solver/retime.py`) re-times a few truck days exactly. It never searches: it uses the engine's own timing and checks, in the API process, as the safety net `_retime` does ([4.11](#411-post-solve-stage)).

- **Input** (`RetimeRequest`): `request` = the plan version's request built fresh by the web (today's customers, trucks, settings, frozen loads and same-day clock; every stop of the day); `truck_days` = 1-6 edited trucks, each with its NEW (planned) loads after the move as lists of stop ids; optional `before` = the same trucks' new loads as they are now; optional `best` = one stop to place on one of those trucks (every position of one load, or alone as a new load at every place). It covers a stop moved to another load (same or other truck) at a chosen position or the best one, to a new load, a reorder within a load, a stop taken off (left out of `truck_days`) and an unserved order put on a load. Plan continuity is never priced (`change_penalty_per_stop` taken as 0). 422 for an unknown truck or stop, a stop twice, an empty load, more than 6 trucks or 120 stops (80 before v2; `check_request`, after the token check).
- **Timing.** The truck days are those of the whole request (`_truck_days`: trips left, frozen loads, break state, bays), so they equal an optimization's; the loads are timed on a day of only the stops the call names, on one road matrix of those points (`resolve_matrix` within `RETIME_MATRIX_SEC`). A truck whose loads fit (`fits_truck`: 98% of the bays for several customers, 100% for one; cases; kg; allowed trucks; trips left) is timed by `time_truck` (every hard rule, the driver break at its cheapest place). The scenario is `_build_scenario(..., exact_timing=True)` with the rule echoes (`_echo_rules`, shared with `optimize_dispatch`): VERIFIED / EXACT by the independent check when `ok`. It covers the edited trucks only: the day-level warnings (the priority ranking, other trucks' break notes, shortages) are dropped and its truck counts are the edited trucks'.
- **Refusals, with codes and how much.** A truck with no time or no trip left: `TRUCK_AVAILABILITY` or `TRIPS` (`BREAK` with its break note). Only the break has no place when the same loads time on a NEW day without the break rule (never the same day: its timing cache is keyed by the truck's index): `BREAK` "No place for the driver's 60-min break (to start 14:00-15:00) on T1 with these stops in this order". Otherwise the earliest timetable (each load leaves as soon as the truck is ready, with the exact turnaround, waiting for opening hours) goes through `feasibility.check_scenario`: `CAPACITY_PALLETS`, `CAPACITY_CASES`, `CAPACITY_KG`, `TRUCK_NOT_ALLOWED`, `HARD_WINDOW`, `SHIFT_LIMIT` (the latest return or the shift maximum), `TRIPS`, each with `short_by_min` (minutes, pallets, cases or kg); `NO_TIMETABLE` when none of them names it. That timetable comes back as the scenario (VIOLATED): for the screen, never to save. Hard rules only: whether more cost or km is acceptable is the web's call.
- **Like-for-like cost.** `before` is timed in the same call (same request, matrix and prices): per truck `money_omr` (the plan's own cost model, `costing.truck_day_costs`), `soft_omr` (time preferences, not money), km and times, and `delta_*` = after - before. Current loads that no longer keep the rules with today's data say so (`before.feasible` false, with violations and no money).
- **Best place** (`best`): every candidate place, prefiltered by room, kg, allowed trucks and trips; at most `RETIME_BEST_TRIES` timed, cheapest estimate first; ranked by money + time preferences (`_order_value`), then the last return; the best 3 come back as `options` (each with the truck's loads to send back on a save), and the scenario is the first.
- **Ids.** Planned stops carry the request's own `stop_id` and `order_ids` (split parts included); the web maps the fresh ids back to its plan's rows and portions.
- **Limits and operations.** `RETIME_BUDGET_SEC` (10 s), `RETIME_MAX_CONCURRENT` (4, then 503), `RETIME_BEST_TRIES` (24) ([2.8](#28-timeouts-budgets-and-limits), [2.9](#29-environment-variables-by-service)); no dispatch slot. One log line per check (`retime run=... trucks=... stops=... ok=... relaxed=ok|no|- best_stops=... alt=... provider=... timings=... seconds=...`, ids only; `relaxed`, `best_stops` and `alt` since v2), the startup line `Re-timing for moves by hand (/retime-truck-days v2): ...` (v1 before 25 Oct 2026) and `/ready`'s `retime` (its version, 2 since v2, so the web can tell an older solver). `timings` counts this call's truck timings itself (`LP_STATS` is process-wide). Tests: `apps/solver/tests/test_retime.py` ([5.3](#53-test-suites)).
- **The web side (M2).** `checkPlanEdit` builds the version's request fresh (`buildDispatchRequest`: today's customers, trucks, settings, frozen loads and same-day clock - owner decision D1), matches the edited trucks' stored stops to its stops (`mapStops`; a stop whose orders or parts changed is 409 `STOP_CHANGED`), sends the trucks' loads after the change and as they are now (`before`) and, for a best place, `best`; a best place found is resolved to a concrete place that a save sends as `truck_days` (never `best`; `resolveBestPlace`: the place the stop already has is 409 `NO_CHANGE`, any other mismatch 503). On a day planned by pallets only the products of the orders the change re-times must have cases per pallet (409 `PALLET_FACTOR_REQUIRED`, "then check the move again"), and none of them may have had its cases per pallet corrected since planning (409 `PALLET_FACTOR_CHANGED`, `palletFactorsChangedSince`: a line's planned factor is its split part's own cut factor, else the option's `inputs.palletFactors`; RE-PLAN first). A save stores the re-timed loads with today's factor while the plan screen, the sheets and the day overview read a row with the factor it was planned with, so without this refusal the edited load's manifest, its "Changed after planning" note and the day's RE-PLAN flag would be wrong (release review F1, reproduced on PostgreSQL); more than 120 stops to re-time (80 before v2) is 409 `TOO_MANY_STOPS` before the solver is called. The cost change shown is the solver's after minus before from the same call (critic M5). A save merges the solver's loads into the option in use (`mergeOption`): fresh split-part refs are mapped back to the option's own ids by their lines, or added under a new id (critic M3); the solver's day-level warnings are already dropped, and the option's "serves N more stop(s) ... Use instead" note is dropped too (critic M7); the report is merged per truck (`mergeSolverReport`). A plan on road distances refuses a save checked on straight lines (409 `ROADS_DOWN`). The web waits 20 s; 404 from an older solver is "The route optimizer is being updated", 503 or a timeout "The route check did not answer" - nothing changed either way.
- **Version 2 (25 Oct 2026, moves by hand part 2: the owner's feedback of 24 Oct 2026 - "switch loads between two trucks", "free one load ... not one by one", "we can convince customer for one time only ... truck capacity or break sometimes we can neglect").** Every new field is optional with a default, so the web deployed before it works unchanged: a v1 request gets the v1 answer plus `retime_version` 2, `loads`, `relaxed` null, `allowed` [] and the violations' figures (checked against the released solver on the v1 test days: nothing else differs; `test_retime_v2.py` S-1). An older solver silently ignores fields it does not know, so the web checks `retime_version` before it trusts a v2 answer. The TypeScript mirror has every new field (`test_retime.py`).
  - **Swaps and whole loads** need no new field: two loads exchanged between trucks, a load moved to another truck before or after a chosen load, or the loads of a truck put in another order are explicit `truck_days`; each load keeps its stop order and is timed again on its truck, and new loads keep numbering after the frozen ones.
  - **The figures of a violation** (every caller, `/optimize-dispatch` too; pure additions, `CHECK_VERSION` stays 5, and the web's `inputHash` reads only code, truck and load): `value` / `limit` / `capacity` - CAPACITY_PALLETS the load's pallets, the planning room (the bays at the fill, or the one-customer room) and the bays; CAPACITY_CASES the cases and the case capacity; CAPACITY_KG the kg and the payload; HARD_WINDOW the clock minute of the service start (FINISH: of the end of unloading, also when it is late by under 30 s and only `hard_window_ok` says it, `value == limit`; early: of the service start, `limit` = the opening) and the end of the hours. `late_s` (re-timing only, every HARD_WINDOW of the edited trucks: strict, relaxed and before): the seconds after the end of the hours from the timetable the scenario was built from, `start - latest_start_s(stop, window_rule)`, only when above 0 and not before the opening - a stop 1 s late is 1 s late although its minutes round to the closing. `loads`: the layout the strict answer is for (`truck_days`; with a best place `options[0].loads` for its truck, else the fallback layout the violations are about).
  - **Several stops at once and a whole load** (`best.more_stop_ids`, `keep_order`, `new_load_at`; `_best_v2`): validated in `check_request` (the more stops distinct, in the request, on no load and not `stop_id`; `keep_order` and `new_load_at` only for a new load; `new_load_at` within the truck's loads; the stop count includes them). A best with none of these runs v1 `_best` exactly. Several stops into a load go in one at a time, the earliest end of hours first (none last), then the farthest from the depot, then the stop id, each at the cheapest estimated position (the detour, as `_best`) that keeps the truck within its room and passes a screen with no LP (the truck's earliest timetable meets the hours of that load); the layout is then timed once and, if it does not time, the repairs (from the last placed stop to the first, each at its next position by estimate) one exact timing each until one times: one option. A new load of several stops gets its order the same way into an empty load and is timed at `new_load_at` (then its repairs) or at every place of the day (after the last load first, ranked as v1, up to 3 options); a whole load (`keep_order`) keeps the order sent. At most `RETIME_BEST_TRIES` exact timings in all; a layout over the room costs no LP. No place: no option, and the scenario and violations are those of the screened layout. An option's `position` is `stop_id`'s index in its load. A v2 best gives exactly the answer of the explicit call of `options[0].loads` (S-6).
  - **"Allow anyway"** (`relax`: `late`, `capacity_factor` above 1 and at most 1.5 - the web sends 1.2 -, `no_break`, `seed_no_break`). With it every strict violation carries `overridable` (otherwise null): HARD_WINDOW when `late` and `late_s` is set (arriving early never); CAPACITY_* when the load is at most `floor(x * 120 / 100)` of the truck's OWN capacity in whole units - bays x 1000 pallet units (never the 98% room), cases, or the payload in 0.1 kg; BREAK only when `_own_reasons` found that only the driver break has no place (marked, never matched by its words) - never the break note of a truck with no time left (F17) nor a BREAK of an earliest timetable; anything else, NO_TIMETABLE included, false. A relaxed answer (`relaxed`, `RetimeRelaxed`) is made only when the strict answer is not ok and every strict violation can be allowed or is NO_TIMETABLE (one that cannot - small truck only, the shift or latest return, loads a day, no time left - means `relaxed` null: the change cannot be saved even with overrides). It is made by one function, `_relaxed_answer`, on an explicit layout: seeds only from the trucks that fail with every rule (a truck that keeps every rule keeps its timetable) - every stop of their loads late-soft, the trucks whose capacity can be allowed, and no break only where the break alone had no place or the user asked (`seed_no_break`); each failing truck is timed once on `_relaxed_side`, a NEW `_StageCtx` / `Day` for every relaxation set (`time_truck` caches by truck index per day, F6), where a late stop has no end of hours but waits for opening and pays `LATE_SOFT_PER_S` (`load_repack.RELAX_LATE_OMR_PER_MIN` = 5 OMR a minute, `Day.late_soft`) for every second after its real latest start, so the timing goes late only where nothing else works and never later than needed; a truck over capacity has 120% of its bays, cases and payload; a no-break truck-day has no break. The scenario is then built on the STRICT side (the real stops, rooms and break rule: a late stop has `hard_window_ok` false, `pallet_room_units` is the real room, a no-break truck has no `driver_break` and `break_status` `SKIPPED_BY_HAND`, costs and preferences are the plan's own) and its check is split by `_partition` into `allowed` (a late stop on a truck timed relaxed, capacity within the cap, the BREAK of a no-break truck) and what remains; on a truck that still cannot be timed BREAK is dropped (its earliest timetable holds none) and NO_TIMETABLE "No timetable keeps the rules that cannot be allowed by hand for T08 ..." is added (F5). `ok` = nothing remains, every truck timed, VERIFIED (with `allowed`). A truck still untimed whose break is due is timed once more without its break on a new day; if that works it is named in `break_alternative` (never made no-break by the solver: the web offers "Skip the driver break instead", which checks again with `seed_no_break`). `relaxations` say what was used (the stops actually late), `strict` is the layout with every rule, `trucks` the relaxed figures and deltas.
  - **A best place with `relax`** (no place keeps every rule): the relaxed best - the same candidates (one stop) or the same placement (v2) timed on a relaxed side of the best truck (its stops and the best stops late-soft, the truck over capacity, no break only for `seed_no_break`), ranked by the loads over the planning room, then the seconds late, then money + time preferences, the last return and the estimate - picks the layout, never the strict fallback (F4). The pipeline then runs on a side rebuilt from that layout's stop order exactly as an explicit request builds it, so Check (a best) and Save (the explicit `relaxed.loads`) get the same relaxed answer and the web's overrides hash agrees (F16, S-11). When that layout keeps every rule (the strict search ran out of its share of the time) it becomes the strict answer's only option and nothing needs allowing. When the strict best found a place but another edited truck fails (a change list), the pipeline runs on that place.
  - **`before_relax`**: the current loads that fail with every rule while carrying allowances (the stops allowed late, the trucks allowed over capacity with the factor, the truck-days allowed without the break - frozen loads included, as the web reads them) are timed with exactly those and partitioned, so `before.feasible` holds when only allowed issues remain and the money and cost change exist for a truck allowed by hand earlier.
  - **Budget**: everything stays within `RETIME_BUDGET_SEC` in the API process (rule 22). With `relax` the strict phase (the strict best place, the strict timing - which always runs -, `before`) uses at most `RELAX_SHARE` (0.5) of the time left after the road matrix; the relaxed phase runs to the deadline. When the deadline passes before the relaxed answer is complete, `relaxed` is null and the warning is "Out of time while checking what can be allowed by hand: try again." An error in the relaxed phase never fails the strict answer ("What can be allowed by hand could not be checked: try again.", logged). Tests: `apps/solver/tests/test_retime_v2.py` ([5.3](#53-test-suites)).

## 5. Running, testing, deploying, operating

> **Sources:** `docs/LOCAL_DEV.md`, `docs/RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT.md`, `docs/OSRM_SETUP.md`, `docs/admin.md`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/osrm.yml`, `apps/web/package.json`, `apps/web/vitest.config.ts`, `apps/web/prisma/migrations/`, `apps/web/lib/jobs/*`, `apps/web/lib/solver-client.ts`, `apps/web/app/api/health/route.ts`, `apps/solver/main.py` and `apps/solver/dispatch_solver.py`.
>
> Some older files disagree with these, including the "Local development" and "Deploying to Railway" parts of `README.md` and section 14 of `CLAUDE.md`. Where they disagree, the `docs/` runbooks and the code are the current truth. (`README.md` says this only about `CLAUDE.md`; it does not mark its own "Local development" or "Deploying to Railway" sections as out of date.)

### 5.1 At a glance

| | Web (Next.js 14 + Prisma) | Solver (FastAPI + OR-Tools) | Database | Road routing (OSRM) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Local** | `pnpm --filter @routeiq/web dev` on :3000 (binds 127.0.0.1, owner decision 4) | `python -m uvicorn main:app --port 8000` from `apps/solver/.venv` | PostgreSQL 16: root `docker-compose.yml` on 5432, any local PG 16, or the maintainer's portable PG on 5433 in `.dev/` | none (estimated km), or `infra/osrm` in Docker on `127.0.0.1:5000`. Never the public demo server, not even for local demos (review F22) |
| **CI** | built and started with `pnpm start` inside the `web` job | uvicorn in the `web` job; pytest in the `solver` job | `postgis/postgis:16-3.4` service container | not used by `ci.yml`; `osrm.yml` builds and smoke-tests the image |
| **Production** | Railway service `web` (Nixpacks) | Railway service `solver` (Dockerfile) | Railway service `Postgres` (`ghcr.io/railwayapp-templates/postgres-ssl:18`) | Railway service `routeiq-osrm` (Dockerfile, private network only) |

### 5.2 Local development

**Prerequisites** (`docs/LOCAL_DEV.md`):

- **Node and pnpm:** Node 22 (the version CI and production use, `.nvmrc`; a newer Node installs with an "Unsupported engine" warning from pnpm) and pnpm 9. `corepack pnpm@9.15.9 …` works without a global install. The root `package.json` pins `packageManager: pnpm@9.0.0`, but the lockfile was made with pnpm 9.15.
- **Python:** 3.11 or 3.12 for the solver. OR-Tools and PyVRP publish wheels for both.
- **Database:** PostgreSQL 16. PostGIS is optional.

**One-time setup:**

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm --filter @routeiq/web exec prisma generate   # REQUIRED on Windows: postinstall may generate into the wrong folder
cp .env.example apps/web/.env.local
cp apps/web/.env.local apps/web/.env              # Prisma CLI, seeds and vitest read .env only
cd apps/solver && python -m venv .venv && .venv/Scripts/pip install -r requirements.txt   # bin/ on Linux/macOS
```

**Environment files** (names only; the template is `.env.example`; all are git-ignored):

| File | Read by | Variables |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/.env.local` | `next dev` / `next start` | `DATABASE_URL`, `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`, `NEXTAUTH_URL`, `SOLVER_URL`, `SOLVER_TOKEN`. Optional: `RATE_LIMITS_DISABLED`, `JANITOR_TOKEN`, `MAPBOX_TOKEN`, `RESEND_API_KEY`, `SUPER_ADMIN_EMAILS`, `SIGNUP_MODE`, `TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS`, `SENTRY_DSN` |
| `apps/web/.env` | Prisma CLI, seed scripts, Vitest | keep it identical to `.env.local` |
| `apps/solver/.env` | only the maintainer's local start scripts in `.dev/` source it. `main.py` reads the process environment and loads no `.env` file | `SOLVER_TOKEN` (must equal the web's). Optional: `OSRM_URL`, `SOLVER_PARALLEL`, `SOLVER_ALLOW_INPROCESS_FALLBACK` (rule 22, development only), `SOLVER_BUDGET_SEC`, `SOLVER_ALT_GRACE_SEC`, `OSRM_MAX_SNAP_M` |

**Database options:**

1. **Root `docker-compose.yml`** ("Local dev only"). The `db` service is `postgis/postgis:16-3.4` on port 5432; its credentials match the `DATABASE_URL` in `.env.example`. The `solver` service is built from `apps/solver/Dockerfile` and runs on port 8000 with a fixed development token. It has no `OSRM_URL`, so distances are estimated.
2. **Any PostgreSQL 16.** The first migration, `00000000000000_init_postgis`, skips PostGIS when it is not available.
3. **The maintainer's Windows machine** (local only; `.dev/` is git-ignored, so none of it is in the repo):
   - a portable PostgreSQL 16.9 in `.dev/pgsql/`, data in `.dev/pgdata/`, log in `.dev/pg.log`, listening on `127.0.0.1:5433` (`apps/web/.env` points at that port);
   - `setup.sh`: copies the portable Postgres binaries, creates the solver venv with `uv` on Python 3.12, and runs `corepack pnpm@9.15.9 install --frozen-lockfile`;
   - `start-solver.sh` and `start-web.sh`, plus `start-solver-at.sh` and `start-web-at.sh`, which take a checkout path as `$1` for worktrees;
   - benchmark harnesses (`.dev/bench/`), logs, and **real NMWC data** (`.dev/realdata/`, order workbooks). Treat `.dev/` as private. Never copy it into the repo or into documents.

**Migrate and seed:**

```bash
pnpm --filter @routeiq/web exec prisma migrate deploy
pnpm --filter @routeiq/web db:seed:dispatch                         # demo tenant "nmwc"; prints generated passwords once
pnpm --filter @routeiq/web db:seed:dispatch -- --orders=2026-09-26  # also writes .dev/orders-2026-09-26.xlsx to upload
```

- The seed script `apps/web/prisma/seed-nmwc-dispatch.ts` is idempotent (upserts by code) and never inserts orders. Its data comes from `prisma/nmwc-dispatch-data.ts` (fictional, seeded PRNG). `SEED_PASSWORD` sets the demo passwords; without it the script prints random passwords once.
- Other seeds: `db:seed:synth` → `seed-synth.ts` (reads `prisma/synth-data/`); `fixtures:dispatch` → `nmwc-dispatch-fixtures.ts`, which regenerates `tests/fixtures/nmwc/`. The legacy `db:seed:nmwc` / `seed-nmwc.ts` (hard-coded password) was deleted in PR1.

**Run:**

```bash
cd apps/solver && SOLVER_TOKEN=... .venv/Scripts/python -m uvicorn main:app --port 8000   # Haversine; or OSRM_URL=http://127.0.0.1:5000 (local infra/osrm)
pnpm --filter @routeiq/web dev
# open http://localhost:3000/t/nmwc/dispatch
```

- Without `OSRM_URL` the solver plans on estimated distances. For road distances run the OSRM image locally (`infra/osrm`, [`docs/OSRM_SETUP.md`](./OSRM_SETUP.md)). **Never use a public OSRM demo server**, especially with `.dev/` data: it would receive real customer coordinates (review F22).
- **Maintainer action:** the local `.dev/start-solver.sh` (git-ignored, so no PR can change it) still defaults `OSRM_URL` to the public demo server when it is unset. Blank that default (its line 5) before using it with real data; until then always start it with `OSRM_URL` set, or empty for estimated km.

**Local gotchas** (`docs/LOCAL_DEV.md`):

- **Stop `next dev` before `prisma generate` on Windows.** The query-engine DLL is locked while the dev server runs.
- **`SOLVER_PARALLEL=0` is for tests and debugging only.** It solves in-process, and `/health` does not answer during a solve. So is `SOLVER_ALLOW_INPROCESS_FALLBACK=1` (rule 22): without it a machine that cannot start worker processes refuses every optimization with "The planner is busy or restarting" instead of solving in-process.
- **Uploads run in a parser process (P5).** `next dev` and the tests fork `scripts/upload-parser-dev.cjs`, which bundles the parser with esbuild into `node_modules/.cache/routeiq-upload-parser` the first time and after a change to one of its sources (about a second), then reads the file. A local `next start` needs `pnpm build` (not `next build` alone, which does not make `.next/upload-parser/parse.cjs`) and must run in `apps/web`. The unit specs read uploads in-process unless they start the real parser (`tests/setup.ts`).
- **Start Next.js through pnpm** (`pnpm --filter @routeiq/web dev`, `build` or `start`, `pnpm dev` in `apps/web`, or `pnpm exec next ...`), never as `node node_modules/next/dist/bin/next`. pnpm's `next` launcher (`apps/web/node_modules/.bin/next`) puts `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules` on `NODE_PATH`, and Next.js's webpack looks for packages there too. That is how Sentry's route wrapper finds `@sentry/core`, which is not a direct dependency of `apps/web` (pnpm does not hoist it). Started without the launcher, `next dev` answers 500 on every API route with "Module not found: Can't resolve '@sentry/core'"; through pnpm it answers 200 (both checked on 29 Sep 2026, P5 review). A `next build` started without the launcher would lack the same path (not checked). Railway and CI start everything through pnpm. Adding `@sentry/core` as a direct dependency of `apps/web` would make a direct start work too; not done.
- **README steps are older.** The "Local development" steps in `README.md` require PostGIS and run `pnpm db:migrate`, which is `prisma migrate dev` (it can create migrations or prompt for a reset). They also copy `.env.example` to `apps/solver/.env`, which the solver never reads. Prefer `docs/LOCAL_DEV.md`.

### 5.3 Test suites

| Suite | Exact command | Needs | In CI |
|---|---|---|---|
| Web unit + tenant isolation | `pnpm --filter @routeiq/web test:unit`, i.e. `vitest run tests/lib tests/tenant-isolation.spec.ts` (`test` is the same) | A migrated Postgres at `DATABASE_URL`. Only `tests/tenant-isolation.spec.ts` and `tests/lib/password-reset.spec.ts` touch the database | yes (`web` job) |
| Web integration (HTTP) | Start the server with `RATE_LIMITS_DISABLED=1 pnpm --filter @routeiq/web dev`, then run `pnpm --filter @routeiq/web test:integration` (`vitest run tests/integration`) | A running web server at `TEST_BASE_URL` (default `http://localhost:3000`) with rate limits off and sign-up open (the default), a running solver, the same DB, and `JANITOR_TOKEN` (or, against a dev server, `SOLVER_TOKEN`) in the test environment (the janitor spec uses it). `SUPER_ADMIN_EMAILS` shared by server and tests enables one extra auth test | yes (`web` job) |
| Migration test (audit PR A5) | From `apps/web`: `MIGRATION_TEST_DB_ADMIN_URL=postgresql://USER:PASSWORD@HOST:PORT/postgres pnpm exec vitest run tests/migrations` | A PostgreSQL user that may create databases. The spec creates the throwaway database `MIGRATION_TEST_DB_NAME` (default `routeiq_a5_migtest`; any other name must start with `routeiq_a5_` and end in `migtest`, `tests/migrations/db-name.ts`, because the spec drops it WITH (FORCE) first if it exists and again at the end), applies the migrations up to `20260930093000` with this repo's `prisma migrate deploy`, inserts orders and files without a depot for every backfill step, applies `20260930120000_orders_always_have_depot` while another connection is still writing an order and an order file without a depot, on a database with a `statement_timeout` and a `lock_timeout` of 1 s (the writer commits only 2.5 s after the migration started: the lock step must wait for it, then fill it in; with the lock step removed the deploy fails with P3018, and with the timeout turned off only inside the lock step it fails with P3018 57014, both checked), checks every result and NOT NULL, runs the SQL again (nothing changes), and drops the database. It applies only the migrations up to `20260930093000`, then the new one (`tests/migrations/folders.ts`), so a migration added later does not make it fail (A5 second review). Since the A5 fifth review it also checks that the database refuses a history-only depot that is active (23514, the CHECK), while anything else about it and any other depot can still be changed. Skipped (8 tests) when `MIGRATION_TEST_DB_ADMIN_URL` is not set. The same command also runs `order-delete-and-audit-indexes.spec.ts` (reviews db-schema-1 and db-schema-2; same database rules, the spec files run one after the other; 6 tests, skipped the same way): it applies the migrations up to `20261007090000`, adds plan history in small (10 versions of 2,000 stops, a manual baseline, 30,000 audit rows) and a wrong order file, applies `20261009090000_order_delete_and_audit_indexes`, and checks the four indexes (valid, with the schema's names: no drift), that every foreign key to `Order` or `UploadBatch` has an index starting with its column (three had none), that deleting the wrong file's orders reads `RouteAssignment` and `ManualBaselineAssignment` by index (before: one full read per order deleted, checked in the transaction's own table statistics), that the Audit log page's per-user counts, as Prisma sends them, are an index-only scan, and that a second run changes nothing | no |
| Type check + lint | `pnpm --filter @routeiq/web exec tsc --noEmit` and `pnpm --filter @routeiq/web exec next lint --max-warnings 0` | nothing | yes |
| Solver | `cd apps/solver && .venv/Scripts/python -m pytest tests -q` (`bin/` on Linux/macOS) | Nothing external: Haversine only, with OSRM calls mocked. Some tests spawn worker processes | yes (`solver` job) |
| OSRM image | `docker build -t routeiq-osrm infra/osrm`, run it, then `OSRM_URL=http://localhost:5000 sh infra/osrm/smoke-test.sh` | Docker, about 4 GB RAM and about 10 minutes to build; `curl` and `jq` | `osrm.yml`, only for PRs touching `infra/osrm/**` |

**Vitest configuration** (`apps/web/vitest.config.ts`): Node environment; includes `tests/**/*.spec.ts` and `lib/**/*.spec.ts` (there are no specs under `lib/` today); `pool: 'forks'` with `singleFork: true`, so tests run serially in one process; `testTimeout` 120 s and `hookTimeout` 60 s. The setup file `tests/setup.ts` makes every spec read uploads in the test process (since audit P5: the `__routeiqUploadParseInProcess` hook, honoured outside production only), so specs that watch or replace SheetJS still see the read; a spec that tests the real parser process calls `useRealUploadParser()` (`tests/lib/upload-parse-helpers.ts`). Since review M3 it also makes every driver pack in the test process (the `__routeiqPdfRenderInProcess` hook, honoured outside production only); `pdf-render-process.spec.ts` and `pdf-render-route.spec.ts` turn it off and use the real renderer process. Since audit PR A2, `esbuild.jsx` is `automatic` (JSX compiled as Next.js does, without `import React`), so the component tests can load the dispatch screen's `.tsx` files. There is no DOM (no jsdom): `tests/lib/hook-host.ts` (adapted from the audit verifiers' harness) calls a component function with its own small hooks runtime (`vi.mock('react', ...)` with `mockReactHooks`), reads the element tree it returns and calls its callbacks like a user; child components are not rendered.

`tests/lib/plan-detail-fixture.ts` is a shared fixture, not a spec. `tests/tenant-isolation.spec.ts` drives tenant-scoped models through `tenantDb()` for two throwaway tenants and asserts that nothing is visible across tenants in either direction.

**Web integration specs** (`apps/web/tests/integration/`). Each suite creates throwaway tenants through `POST /api/auth/signup` (`freshTenant()` in `helpers.ts`, country Oman) and deletes them in `afterAll` (`cleanupTenant()`). Every spec needs the DB. Most also need the web server, and the ones that optimize also need the solver; the specs marked "no web server" below call the code in the test process instead.

**Benchmarks and scripts** (not run in CI):

- `apps/solver/scripts/bench_dispatch.py <stops>` benchmarks the dispatch optimizer. Its docstring says to keep the 300-stop run in the release checklist.
- `apps/solver/scripts/bench_replan.py` compares two solver versions on re-plans around locked loads (PR5; run it for any change to how locked loads are planned).
- `apps/solver/scripts/bench_search.py` (16 Oct 2026) replays saved requests arm against arm, each arm a set of the solver search upgrade's switches (`SOLVER_BEST_OF`, `SOLVER_BEST_OF_QUICK`, `SOLVER_PYVRP_ALLOWED`, `SOLVER_PRIORITY_REPAIR`, `SOLVER_JOIN_TRIPS`, ...), and writes `results.jsonl` and `summary.md` with each arm's verdict under the pre-written rule. No switch goes on before it passes (`RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT.md`). Real requests and its output stay outside the repository, which is public; `test_bench_search.py` keeps the tool working on an invented request.
- `apps/solver/scripts/bench_day1.py` benchmarks the legacy PyVRP solver.
- `apps/web/scripts/rebuild-gps-visits.ts --tenant <code> --from <date> [--to <date>] [--write]` (owner decision 21 Oct 2026, GPS times win): rebuilds the visits with GPS events stored before the release with the new rules. Dry run by default (a READ ONLY transaction; counts per date and rule only, never a name); `--write` is a production write (owner OK), one transaction per depot-date in the driver path's lock order.
- `apps/web/prisma/check-priority-drops.ts --run=<id>` checks the priority drop penalty for one run.
- `apps/web/prisma/check-saved-readings.ts` (audit PR A5 sixth review) counts, per company and read-only, the confirmed customers with a typed or pasted location (`MANUAL_LATLNG`, `GOOGLE_MAPS_URL`, with a saved point) whose saved text (`locationInput`) the parser of the commit it runs on reads as not exact, by reason, and the short links it cannot read again. Since the A5 seventh review a text is judged only when the saved point was read from it: it reads back to the saved point (to 6 decimals), or it holds the saved point as numbers but reads otherwise today (read differently before A5, such as a directions link read at its start). The others are counted apart and not judged by their text: no text kept, a text that reads as another point, the saved numbers as RouteIQ writes them that read as not exact, a text that cannot be read and does not hold the saved point; with how many of them have fewer than 4 decimals as stored. It names no customer. Checked on a throwaway database with writes refused (`default_transaction_read_only`). Unit tests: `check-saved-readings.spec.ts`.
- `apps/web/prisma/smoke-driver-flow.ts` was deleted in PR1 (the driver app is retired). It had written a synthetic driver "SMOKE-DRV" with a live PIN and proof rows into the `nmwc` tenant; the owner clean-up is in [`docs/SECURITY.md`](./SECURITY.md).

### 5.4 CI (GitHub Actions)

**`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** runs on pull requests to `main`, pushes to `main`, and manual dispatch.

| Job | Runs on | Steps |
|---|---|---|
| `web` ("Web (lint + typecheck + unit + integration)") | ubuntu-latest, service `postgis/postgis:16-3.4` on 5432 | 1. checkout, `pnpm/action-setup@v4`, Node from `.nvmrc` (22; pnpm cache), Python 3.11<br>2. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`<br>3. `prisma generate`, then `prisma migrate deploy`<br>4. `tsc --noEmit`, then `next lint --max-warnings 0`<br>5. `vitest run tests/lib tests/tenant-isolation.spec.ts`<br>6. solver venv + `pip install -r requirements.txt`<br>7. start uvicorn on `127.0.0.1:8000`, polling `/health` for up to 30 s<br>8. `pnpm --filter @routeiq/web build` (since P5 `build-upload-parser.mjs` after `next build`; ends with `remove-public-source-maps.mjs` since A1)<br>9. (A1) build output check, `tsx scripts/check-build-output.ts`: no `'use server'` in the app's code, no Server Action in `.next/server/server-reference-manifest.json`, no `.map` file under `.next/static`; (P5) `.next/upload-parser/parse.cjs` is there, holds only the parser, SheetJS's `xlsx.mjs` and Papa Parse, and reads a two-line CSV when forked<br>10. `pnpm start`, polling `/api/health` for up to 60 s<br>11. (A1) on the running app: `/_next/image?...&w=1` answers 404 (400 if the image endpoint were on), a browser chunk answers 200 and its `.map` 404<br>12. `vitest run tests/integration`<br>13. on failure, the last 200 lines of `web.log` and `solver.log` |
| `solver` ("Solver (pytest)") | ubuntu-latest | Python 3.11, `pip install -r requirements.txt`, `pytest tests -v` |

- **Job environment:** names in [2.9](#29-environment-variables-by-service); the values are CI-only placeholders in the workflow.
- **No road routing in CI:** `OSRM_URL` is not set, so the solver plans on estimated distances, and `TEST_EXPECT_OSRM` is not set.

**`.github/workflows/osrm.yml` ("OSRM image")** runs on PRs that touch `infra/osrm/**` or the workflow file, and on manual dispatch. It has a 60-minute timeout. It only validates; nothing is published.

1. Builds `infra/osrm`.
2. Prints the image size and `/data/BUILD_INFO`.
3. Starts the server and waits for `/nearest/v1/driving/58.3920,23.5680`.
4. Runs `infra/osrm/smoke-test.sh`: Ghala → Ruwi/Seeb/Barka/Nizwa within km bounds, Ghala → Khasab through the UAE, and a 100×100 table.
5. Checks an IPv6-bound server (`OSRM_BIND=::`), as used on Railway.

**Other repository automation:**

- `.github/dependabot.yml`: weekly updates for npm (grouped: radix-ui, next-stack, react, prisma, types), pip (`/apps/solver`) and github-actions. **An `ortools` or `pyvrp` bump is an engine change:** its PR fails `test_ortools_version_is_pinned` / `test_pyvrp_version_is_pinned` on purpose. Merge one only after replaying saved real requests on the old and the new version (same requests, same matrix, every option VERIFIED, served-by-priority and cost compared), then update the pin, its test and this handbook; CI passing alone is not enough (the PR #71 incident depended on OR-Tools 9.15's behaviour).
- `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`: asks for the four test commands above and the tenant-isolation checklist: `TENANT_SCOPED_MODELS` in `lib/tenant.ts`, a row in `tests/integration/cross-tenant.spec.ts`, and use of `tenantDb()`.

**State on 25 Sep 2026 (`gh run list`):** every CI run on `main` and on the PR #25–#30 branches passed from `8f744d9` (24 Sep, PR #25's second commit) onward, including `f2f4099` (PR #30), which took 7 min 38 s. Typical duration is 5–8 minutes. The first CI run of PR #25 (`b50484e`) failed. The CI runs of the open Dependabot PRs also failed; they last ran between May and August 2026, before the September fixes, and have not been re-run.

Its very first statement sets its transaction to READ COMMITTED, so a default isolation of REPEATABLE READ or SERIALIZABLE on the database or the role cannot fail it either (A5 fourth review: the first query took the one snapshot before the lock step, and an order without a depot changed by the old app meanwhile failed the backfill with 40001, then P3009). Adds `Depot.historyOnly BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false` (no rewrite) and the CHECK `Depot_historyOnly_not_active` (`NOT ("historyOnly" AND "active")`, A5 fifth review): the previous version keeps serving while the deploy goes live, and its Depots screen, which has no history-only check, could switch the new depot on; the new app then offered it for late orders and new plans and had no screen to switch it off. Fills in every NULL depot, best evidence first, only from the row's own company: (a) an order from its file; (b) an order from the one depot of the plans that held it (stops, unserved rows, the orders an option was made for, a manual baseline, the order it was brought forward to or from; two depots = a conflict, no answer); (c) a file from the one depot of its orders, then (a) again; (d) both from the company's only **active** depot, else its only depot (the depot whose plan already held them, `ordersInScopeWhere` before A5); (e) the rest to a per-company history-only depot `NO-DEPOT` (`NO-DEPOT-2`, ... when the code is taken in any letter case), "No depot (kept for history)", inactive, at one of the company's depots' coordinates (0, 0 without one). Then `SET NOT NULL` on `Order.depotId` and `UploadBatch.depotId`; the foreign keys stay NO ACTION. Safe on existing rows: rows with a depot are never changed, nothing is deleted, each step touches only rows still without a depot, so a second run changes nothing. Tested on a throwaway database with every step, the conflicts, a company with no depot, one with two or more and one with a taken code, while another connection is still writing an order and an order file without a depot and changing another such order, on a database with 1 s timeouts and REPEATABLE READ by default, which the migration waits for and then fills in (`tests/migrations/orders-always-have-depot.spec.ts`, [5.3](#53-test-suites); without the lock step that test fails with P3018, because the backfill cannot see the uncommitted rows and SET NOT NULL then finds them). NMWC has one depot and its orders already carry it: nothing is filled in there. Rollback: `DROP NOT NULL` on both columns; the filled-in depots, the history-only depots, the column and its CHECK can stay (old code ignores the column; its Depots screen gets an error if someone switches a history-only depot on). A local database that applied this migration before the A5 fifth review lacks the CHECK: reset it, or add the constraint by hand |
