### 7.2 Known limitations

| Limitation | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Truck counts are provisional | kg per case was **estimated** in the real-data test. Payloads, windows and per-case times are not yet NMWC's real values | work log; `OPTIMIZER_DESIGN.md` §8 |
| Same-day plans (PR8) | A plan built on its delivery day starts from now + the turnaround setting, and each new load also waits for its loading per case from now; "now" is when the optimization starts (a queued job does not move it), and there is no manual "plan from" time. Loads that left but are still PLANNED in RouteIQ are planned again from now. The route search assumes 80% of a full truck for that first loading (as after a frozen return); the final timetable uses the exact cases | `lib/dispatch/plan-from.ts`, [3.11](#311-step-9-late-orders-and-plan-versions) |
| Optimistic timing defaults | First departure 06:00 (NMWC leaves 07:10-08:00). Fixed 30 min turnaround. Per-case times 0. Fixed stop time. NMWC's real truck cycles on 24 Sep were ~52 % longer | `TenantConfig`, `OPTIMIZER_DESIGN.md` §8 |
| Plans are good, not proven optimal | Searches are time-limited (`auto_time_limit`; since PR7 the time rises steadily from 120 to 200 stops instead of jumping at 200). Results vary between runs (±1-2 % km on the benchmark days; up to 12.6 % on the Sep 2026 scenario days, some of which ran on the old 20 s at 197-200 stops) | `OPTIMIZER_DESIGN.md`, `OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md` §5 |
| Road data | The OSRM map covers Oman + UAE only. There are no time-of-day traffic speeds. Car times are × 1.25 and uncalibrated. Points more than 5 km from a road use Haversine | `providers.py`, `docs/OSRM_SETUP.md` |
| Capacity model | Cases and kg, or (a truck with bays, since 4 Oct 2026) pallets and kg: mixed pallets, each line's cases / its cases per pallet rounded up to 0.001 pallet, at most bays x Pallet fill (a truck with only one customer: every bay, owner rule 13 Oct 2026). No volume, pallet height or stacking rules; loading time stays per case | `OPTIMIZER_DESIGN.md` §1 |
| PDFs | Built-in Helvetica cannot print Arabic, so such text becomes `[?]`. The WhatsApp text keeps full Unicode | `pdf-text.ts` (`pdfSafe`, `UNPRINTABLE`) |
| Driver outputs | Driver sheets (PDF), a WhatsApp link, the Excel workbook and (4 Oct 2026) the driver page per truck-day (QR). The driver PWA is retired (PR1). Since Part 2 the driver page records arrivals, results and photos, but the stop timer works only while the page is open (a locked screen or Maps in front may pause it: such arrivals are "not observed"); positions and times are phone-reported (implausible ones are flagged "unverified timing"). Since Part 3 the results reach the plan screen, the day screen, Bring forward, the KPIs, measured unloading times, the pin check and the actuals Excel; a stop that left with no result still counts as delivered (listed for the dispatcher, owner question Q5). **Undo bring forward only before the copy is planned**: a copy that a plan version refers to cannot be removed in the app (the order-cancel flow is deferred, Q12); the refused result is kept as a conflict that warns on the copy's stop and at Lock. A dispatcher quick-add of a hired truck for one day is not built (Q3) | PR #28, restart audit, [`docs/SECURITY.md`](./SECURITY.md) |
| Legacy SaaS surfaces still reachable | Signup (open by owner decision; always TENANT_ADMIN), onboarding, regions, `runs/*` pages, the sample-order endpoint, the Mapbox option, and the solver's `/optimize` | restart audit "IMPLEMENTED BUT NOT NEEDED" |
| Settings only in the DB (operations) | `timezone`, `osrmUrl`, `priorityWeightsJson`, `orderColumnMapJson`, `serviceAreaJson`, and the `CustomerTypeProfile` rows (shown read-only on Settings since PR5) | `TenantConfig` vs `settings-form.tsx` |
| Deprecated settings columns | `weightObjective*`, `latePenaltyPerMin`, `underutilizationPenalty`, `solverTimeLimitSeconds`, `costPerKmDefault`, `fixedTruckCostPerDayDefault`, `returnToDepot`, `labelEstimatedDistances`: hidden and refused by the API since PR5, read by nothing; dropped in a later expand-then-contract release | `schema.prisma` (`@deprecated`) |
| Costs of loads locked out of order | A locked load keeps the cost share it was planned with. If a later load of a truck is locked while an earlier one stays planned, and a re-plan moves the earlier one after it, the locked load's share still starts at the earlier load's old return; the TRUCK DAYS sheet notes the difference in minutes | `apps/solver/costing.py`, `lib/dispatch/costs.ts` (`paidVsSpanMin`) |
| Order intake rules | Whole cases only. 10 MB / 50k rows on the sheet that is read; a workbook at most 50 MB unpacked and 10 sheets (A1). Since the A1 review also at most 200 columns, 2,500,000 cells (since the P5 second review for a CSV sent as text too), links over 200,000 cells and 10,000 comments, and an Excel upload must be an .xlsx, an old .xls or CSV text; since A1 v3 at most 1,000 metadata entries of each kind and 1,000 comment authors. Since P5 a file is read in its own process (never on the web's event loop), killed after 15 s or at a 512 MB heap and then refused: the widest legal files (50,000 rows of more than about 45 columns, or the same as CSV sent as Excel) need more than 512 MB and are refused "needs too much memory" (before P5 they were read while every user waited 20-40 s); NMWC's real files take well under a second. No HOLD handling. **No amendment or cancel** of a confirmed sales-order line: the same line with another quantity is an error (extra cases go in a late order without a sales-order number, or under a new one). **No batch delete once any of its orders was optimized**, and planned orders cannot be removed in the app at all until the deferred "cancel orders from this file" flow exists (OrderStatus CANCELLED plus a re-plan; owner decision on F20): an administrator has to correct them. A checked file must be confirmed within **24 h** (`VALIDATED_BATCH_MAX_AGE_HOURS`), else uploaded again. A merged SO+SKU line whose rows only partly carry a weight is weighed from the product master as a whole | `order-intake.ts`, `intake-server.ts`, `app/api/orders/[batchId]/route.ts`, `lib/csv.ts`, [3.3](#33-step-1-upload-and-validate-the-order-file) |
| Product codes | One rule for products only (`lib/product-code.ts`): letters, digits, spaces and `. ( ) - _ / + &`, at most 40, tidy, matched ignoring the letter case ([3.3](#33-step-1-upload-and-validate-the-order-file)). A product saved before it (made by an upload, so any code) keeps working: it is found by its tidy code and takes a weight (the Edit dialog never sends the code), but a code with two spaces stays as saved until someone renames it. Customer codes keep their own rule (`codeSchema` on the Customers page; an order file or a late order may bring any text) and since 7 Oct 2026 are matched the same way in the program (`lib/customer-code.ts`): `C_1` is not `CX1` anywhere | `product-code.ts`, `tests/lib/product-code.spec.ts` |
| Order lifecycle stops at DISPATCHED | COMPLETED loads do not mark orders DELIVERED, and a split order whose rest is unserved stays ASSIGNED after its parts are dispatched | `changeStatusTx` in `plan-service.ts` |
| Scaling | One web replica only: the in-flight map, the rate limits and the solve admission live in process memory. Plan correctness does not depend on it since PR3 (database locks); a second replica needs Redis/BullMQ-style shared admission first | `docs/admin.md`, [2.7](#27-background-job-model) |
| Deploys | Web and solver deploy independently; during a rollout the web shows "The route optimizer is being updated". A deploy that has run migrations can only be rolled back by restoring the backup | `solver-client.ts`, `docs/RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT.md` |
| Docs lag code in places | `CLAUDE.md` (the v1.3 build spec from May) and `OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md` are historical. The restart audit's time-budget row (3-45 s, 300 s web timeout) was superseded by `9426307` and PR #29. **Code wins** ([7.4](#74-review-leads-found-while-writing-this-handbook), doc drift) | |

### 7.3 Guide for an AI code reviewer

#### Where to start reading

1. **`docs/OPTIMIZER_DESIGN.md`**: the hard rules and objectives in plain language. This is the behavioural spec to check the code against.
2. **`docs/DISPATCHER_GUIDE.md`**: the user flow (upload → resolve → optimize → review → lock / dispatch → late orders).
3. **`docs/NMWC_DISPATCH_RESTART_AUDIT.md`** and **`docs/OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md` §8**: what was broken, what was fixed, and what was measured.
4. **The contract**: `packages/shared-types/src/dispatch.ts` and its Python mirror `apps/solver/dispatch_models.py`; the data model in `apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma` (`RunPlan`, `PlanLoad`, `RouteAssignment`, `ScenarioResult`, `UnservedOrder`, `Order`, `OrderLine`, `TenantConfig`).
5. **The request path**, in order:
   1. UI: `app/t/[slug]/dispatch/dispatch-client.tsx`, then `plan-view.tsx`;
   2. upload: `api/orders/upload` → `lib/dispatch/intake-server.ts` (`validateIntake`), then `api/orders/[batchId]/confirm` (`confirmIntake`), then `lib/dispatch/order-intake.ts`;
   3. optimize: `api/dispatch/plan` / `api/runs/[id]/optimize` / `api/runs/[id]/replan` → `lib/dispatch/start-optimize.ts`;
   4. building the request: `buildDispatchRequest` in `lib/dispatch/plan-service.ts`, then `lib/jobs/dispatch-job.ts`, then `callDispatchSolver` in `lib/solver-client.ts`;
   5. solver: `apps/solver/main.py` → `dispatch_solver.optimize_dispatch` → `_run_scenarios` → `_post_solve` → `load_repack.py`;
   6. back in the web app: `persistDispatchResult` → `applyScenario` → `refreshPlanFacts` (reconciliation);
   7. load changes: `api/runs/[id]/loads/[loadId]` → `updateLoad` / `changeStatusTx`;
   8. exports: `api/runs/[id]/export/excel` (`lib/dispatch/workbook.ts`) and `export/pdf` (`lib/dispatch/driver-pack.tsx`).
6. **Tenancy and auth**: `apps/web/lib/tenant.ts`, `lib/api.ts` (`withTenantApi`), `middleware.ts`, `lib/auth.ts`, `lib/session-principal.ts`, `lib/auth-credentials.ts`, `lib/rbac.ts`, and [`docs/SECURITY.md`](./SECURITY.md).

#### How to run the tests

Use a local or CI Postgres. **Never** point `DATABASE_URL` at production: the suites create tenants and data. The full recipe is in [5.2](#52-local-development), [5.3](#53-test-suites) and `docs/LOCAL_DEV.md`; CI reproduces it in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

```bash
# Run every line from the repo root. The solver lines use a subshell ( ... ) so the cd does not stick.
pnpm install
pnpm --filter @routeiq/web exec prisma generate          # required on Windows
pnpm --filter @routeiq/web exec prisma migrate deploy    # local DB only
(cd apps/solver && python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt)   # .venv/Scripts on Windows
(cd apps/solver && .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests -q)  # solver: test_dispatch.py, test_repack.py, test_solver.py (legacy)
pnpm --filter @routeiq/web test:unit                     # tests/lib + tests/tenant-isolation.spec.ts (needs DB)
# integration: start solver (SOLVER_TOKEN set) and web with RATE_LIMITS_DISABLED=1, then:
pnpm --filter @routeiq/web test:integration              # tests/integration/*.spec.ts
pnpm --filter @routeiq/web exec tsc --noEmit && pnpm --filter @routeiq/web exec next lint --max-warnings 0
(cd apps/solver && .venv/bin/python scripts/bench_dispatch.py 300)   # release-checklist benchmark (synthetic, ~4 min)
```

Expected counts at `f2f4099`: solver 104, web unit 344, integration 74; after stabilization PR1: solver 117, web unit 522; after PR5 (on PR3 and PR4, with its review fixes): solver 188, web unit 899; after the plan map fix (#36, on PR5): solver 188, web unit 987; after PR6 (on the plan map fix, with its review fixes): solver 194, web unit 1018; after PR7 (on PR6, with its review fixes and the search-time floor): solver 200, web unit 1034; after A1 (audit quick hardening): web unit 1178, with its review fixes 1205, with the A1 v2 fixes 1211; A1 merged with main `22fe298` (PR8, PR9, A2 and A3, which did not update this line): web unit 1340 (75 files); with the A1 v3 fixes: web unit 1350 (75 files); with the A1 v4 fixes: web unit 1363 (75 files); with the A1 v5 fix: web unit 1366 (75 files); solver 213 since PR8 ([5.3](#53-test-suites) has the steps in between; its last count is the latest). The real-data harness (`.dev/bench`) is local only and not in the repo.

#### Critical invariants to check

| Invariant | Where it is enforced | Tests | What a bug looks like |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Exact case reconciliation**: uploaded = planned + unserved, in total, per SKU, per sales order and per **order line** for split parts. Each order appears exactly once | Web: `reconcile()` in `lib/dispatch/reconcile.ts`, run by `refreshPlanFacts`. Solver: `_assert_reconciled` in `dispatch_solver.py` (stops and total cases). Workbook cross-checks in `workbook.ts` (~line 146). Dispatch is refused unless `reconciliationJson.ok` (`changeStatusTx`) | `tests/lib/dispatch-reconcile.spec.ts`, `dispatch-split.spec.ts`, `dispatch-workbook.spec.ts` | Cases lost, duplicated or invented; two customer branches merged; a plan dispatched while reconciliation is not OK |
| **Frozen loads never change** (LOCKED, LOADING, DISPATCHED, COMPLETED) | `FROZEN` / `checkTransition` in `load-state.ts`. `createNextVersion` copies them verbatim. `applyScenario` deletes only PLANNED loads and refuses when the frozen set changed after optimizing. The solver plans around frozen trips. `choose-scenario` refuses when this version's loads are locked. A driver cannot change after dispatch (`checkDriverChange`) | `dispatch-load-state.spec.ts`, `dispatch-mvp.spec.ts`, `test_frozen_*`, `test_loading_time_after_a_frozen_load` | Any write to a frozen `PlanLoad` or its `RouteAssignment`s; an order moved back from DISPATCHED / DELIVERED |
| **Tenant isolation on every query** | `tenantDb()` rewrites reads and writes for models in `TENANT_SCOPED_MODELS` (`lib/tenant.ts`). `withTenantApi` and `getCurrentTenant` return 404 on a slug mismatch. **Many queries use raw `prisma.` with a manual `tenantId`**: `plan-service.ts`, `start-optimize.ts`, `day-overview.ts`, `plan-detail.ts`, `intake-server.ts`, `route-sheet-data.ts`, `dashboard.ts`, `api/users/*`. `OrderLine`, `RouteAssignment`, `ScenarioResult`, `UnservedOrder` and `ManualBaselineAssignment` have **no `tenantId`** and are safe only when reached through a tenant-checked parent. `User` and `PasswordResetToken` are outside the wrapper | `tests/tenant-isolation.spec.ts`, `tests/integration/cross-tenant.spec.ts` | A raw query keyed only by `runId` or `id` where that id was never checked against the tenant |
| **Strict priority**: P1 is highest; one higher-priority order beats any number of lower ones | `_strict_weights` / `_service_values` (int64 guard `PENALTY_LIMIT`). Drop penalties × the scenario's largest cost multiplier (MIN_TRUCKS × 20). `buildDispatchRequest` sends `strict_priorities: true`. The file priority can only raise a customer's priority (`Math.min`) | `test_priority_p1_beats_identical_p5`, `test_strict_priority_one_p2_beats_eleven_p3`, shortage-ladder tests in `test_repack.py` | Inverted P1/P5; a P2 dropped to fit several P3s; weighted mode used by the web |
| **No double planning of split portions** | `buildDispatchRequest` subtracts cases already on frozen loads per line (`frozenLineCases`, `frozenWhole`). `splitIntoParts` / `choosePartCapacity` / `mergePortions` / `readPortionLines` in `lib/dispatch/split.ts`. `resolveOrderRef`. An order is DISPATCHED only when every part is out | `tests/lib/dispatch-split.spec.ts`, `tests/integration/dispatch-split.spec.ts` | The same line's cases on a frozen load and on a new load; part totals ≠ line cases |
| **Superseded plan versions are immutable** | Every mutator locks the `RunPlan` row first (`lockRunForWrite` in `lib/dispatch/plan-locks.ts`, PR3) and refuses a superseded version - status SUPERSEDED **or** `supersededAt` set (`isSupersededRun`): `createNextVersion`, `lockOpenRun`, `applyScenario`, `chooseScenario`, `startDispatchOptimize`, `replan` and the job finalization. `applyScenario` writes its status conditionally; `failJob` and the janitor touch only their own job's OPTIMIZING version. An applied plan is never re-optimized in place (`NEW_VERSION_REQUIRED`) | `tests/lib/plan-lifecycle*.spec.ts`, `tests/integration/plan-lifecycle*.spec.ts`, `dispatch-mvp.spec.ts`, `legacy-data.spec.ts` | Any update to a superseded `RunPlan` or its loads; a status flipped back to READY; a mutator that reads the plan before locking it |
| **A plan is OPTIMIZING only while its current job is QUEUED or RUNNING** (audit PR4, F09) | The start writes the job and OPTIMIZING together; `failJob`, the janitor (`reapStuckJobs`), the job's success and stale paths move job, plan and audit row in one transaction under the plan row lock; `repairStuckPlans` / `repairEndedJobPlan` mend older rows; a 202 always names a QUEUED or RUNNING job; 409 `PLAN_STUCK` is decided on the locked plan row, never on a row read before the job checks | `tests/lib/plan-lifecycle*.spec.ts`, `stuck-plan.spec.ts`, `tests/integration/recovery-races-db.spec.ts`, `janitor.spec.ts` | A plan "optimizing" for ever; OPTIMIZE answering 202 with a FAILED job; a job and its plan written in separate transactions |
| **One live plan per depot and day; a failed re-plan keeps a usable plan** | `createInitialPlan` and `createNextVersion` under the day lock (`lockPlanDay`); `replan` checks every known refusal before creating a version; the child is a copy of the previous plan (copy-forward) | `tests/integration/plan-lifecycle*.spec.ts`, `janitor.spec.ts` | Two v1 plans for one day; a live version without a plan after a refused or failed re-plan |
| **No uploaded file is read in the web process** (P5, audit E2) | `parseUploadIsolated` (`lib/upload-parse`) in the three upload routes: a separate process per file with a heap cap and a time limit that kills it, at most two at once, no secrets in its environment; the rows it sends back at most 128 MB, 200 cells a row and 2,500,000 cells, checked in the web process before a row is built (P5 reviews); `repo-guards.spec.ts` (only `lib/csv.ts` and `lib/workbook-guard.ts` load SheetJS or Papa Parse, only the parser loads `lib/csv`, the routes answer the refusals), `upload-parse-*.spec.ts`, the CI build check of the parser bundle |
| **No driver pack is laid out in the web process** (review M3) | `renderDriverPackIsolated` (`lib/pdf-render`) in the PDF export route: a separate process per pack with a heap cap and a time limit that kills it, at most two at once, no secrets in its environment; the PDF it sends back at most 64 MB; `repo-guards.spec.ts` (only `lib/pdf-render/handler.ts` loads the layout `driver-pack-pdf.tsx`, only it and the legacy route sheet load `@react-pdf/renderer`, the route answers the refusals), `pdf-render-*.spec.ts`, the CI build check of the renderer bundle | `pdf-render-process.spec.ts`, `pdf-render-route.spec.ts`, `build-hardening.spec.ts` | A route or page that calls `renderDriverPackPdf` or `renderToBuffer` for a dispatch plan itself; the web frozen for seconds while drivers' sheets print |
| **Every order and order file has a depot** (owner rule, audit PR A5) | The database: `Order.depotId` and `UploadBatch.depotId` NOT NULL (migration `20260930120000_orders_always_have_depot`), foreign keys NO ACTION (a depot with orders is deactivated, never deleted). The upload: `intakeDepot` (a chosen active depot, or the only active one; else 422 `DEPOT_REQUIRED` / `DEPOT_NOT_ACTIVE`). The history-only depot (`Depot.historyOnly`) never active, never on a truck or region | `orders-have-depot.spec.ts`, `orders-have-depot-db.spec.ts`, `tests/migrations/orders-always-have-depot.spec.ts` | A file of a two-depot company filed under the wrong depot; orders of one depot planned by another depot's plan, or by none |
| **Locations are correct; no item is delivered without one** (owner rule, audit PR A5) | Saving: a reading that needs a pin is saved only as a pin placed by hand (`LocationDialog`, and on the server `PUT /api/customers/:id/location` with `checkManualLocation` and the saved-point check `savedPointProblem`, one test for both, with the company's area); no other route writes a verified point (`PATCH /api/customers/:id` refuses coordinates); `POST /api/customers` and the customer import store only exact readings (of the zeros at the end of a written coordinate one counts, in ADD LOCATION too: `countedText`, owner decision of 28 Sep 2026), and an import whose pair contradicts a saved point nobody confirmed marks that point LOW. Planning: `locationBlocksDelivery` (none, 0,0, outside the area and not verified, LOW and not verified) is blocking on the day and never a stop in `buildDispatchRequest`; stops are created only by `applyScenario` and the re-plan copy, from that request, with the planned pin in the snapshot. Going out: LOCK, LOADING and DISPATCH check the customers of the load as they are now with the same predicate (`locationGate` in `changeStatusTx`, 409 `LOCATION_REQUIRED`; a customer import can mark a planned customer's point LOW), and the day counts such customers on PLANNED loads as out of date (`outdated.locationBlocked`); the same gate refuses a stop still planned at a point that was replaced while it was not usable (409 `STOP_PIN_REPLACED`, from the "before" point of the newest `CUSTOMER_LOCATION_SET` row that moved the customer out of the planned point's place (50 m), written with the change and judged on the customer as it is then; a confirmation where it is, typed or by a hand pin within 50 m, is not such a row, A5 fourth and fifth reviews); the legacy run dispatch checks the same. Parser: a map centre (`/@`, `ll=`, `center=`, `sll=`) needs a pin, and a directions link is read only at its end | `location-rule.spec.ts`, `location-rule-routes.spec.ts`, `dispatch-location-dialog.spec.ts`, `customer-import-locations.spec.ts`, `plan-lifecycle.spec.ts`, `day-overview-weights.spec.ts`, `location-rule-db.spec.ts` | A reading that needs a pin stored as read or as verified; a route storing the client's source or confidence; a stop, a lock or a dispatch for a customer without a usable location, or for a stop still at a point that was flagged and replaced; a location change without its audit row |
| **No truck leaves on a timetable that breaks a rule** (PR4, review F04) | Solver: `feasibility.check_scenario` on every scenario (`_build_scenario`), the exact re-time safety net when the post-solve stage does not run, "serves more" only for VERIFIED options. Web: `checkPlanFeasibility` per truck-day in `lib/dispatch/feasibility.ts`, recomputed under the row lock in `changeStatusTx` (`timingGate`) for LOCK / LOADING / DISPATCH; `FEASIBILITY_GATE=warn` is the only bypass, and it is audited | `tests/test_feasibility.py`, `assert_plan_rules` (requires VERIFIED), `tests/lib/dispatch-feasibility.spec.ts`, `plan-feasibility-gate.spec.ts`, integration `dispatch-timing.spec.ts` | A load that leaves before it can be loaded (turnaround), a missed hard window, kg over payload or a shift overrun that can still be locked or dispatched; a raw search plan returned as if it had been re-checked |
| **A plan shows what it was planned with** (PR4, review F08) | `ScenarioDetails.inputs`, `RouteAssignment.stopSnapshotJson` and `PlanLoad.truckSnapshotJson` written by `applyScenario`, copied by `createNextVersion` (`copyRowData`, NULL-safe); `getPlanDetail`, `load-geometry`, the driver sheets and the workbook read the snapshots and only flag live changes (`masterChanged`); contact details (driver name and phone, customer access notes) stay live | `plan-feasibility-gate.spec.ts`, `plan-snapshots.spec.ts`, integration `dispatch-mvp.spec.ts` (27-29) | A pin, window or truck correction silently changing a locked, dispatched or superseded load's sheet; the ASSUMPTIONS sheet built from today's settings under a "built with" title; a re-plan of pre-snapshot rows throwing on a Json null |

THOROUGH: the cap (`THOROUGH_MAX_SEC`, 1,200 s; the solver's own value is the ceiling) < the cap + `THOROUGH_WAIT_MARGIN_SEC` (120 s) = 1,320 s (`solverWaitMs`, `search-mode.ts`); every stage (road matrix, RECOMMENDED, alternatives, load re-check) runs inside that one deadline. Largest auto limit is 240 s. Alternatives get a hard deadline, and RECOMMENDED is never lost. A job is found lost by its heartbeat (written every 30 s; the plan screen after 2 min, the janitor after `STALE_HEARTBEAT_MS` = 5 min), never by how long it ran, so a wait may be longer than `STUCK_JOB_MS` (15 min, only for jobs from before heartbeats) | `test_alternative_deadline_never_loses_the_recommended_plan`, `test_thorough_cap_is_honoured_*` (`test_search_modes.py`), `search-modes.spec.ts` (the wait `callDispatchSolver` arms), `long-search-jobs.spec.ts` (heartbeat and lost jobs), `janitor.spec.ts` (the janitor's SQL with heartbeats) | A new stage outside the deadline, a web wait at or below the solver's budget or cap (env overrides that differ between web and solver), or a job path that stops writing its heartbeat while it waits or runs; a plan stuck in OPTIMIZING |

| **Timezone and cutoff are Asia/Muscat** | `lib/dispatch/time.ts` (`DEFAULT_TZ`, `isAfterCutoff`, `tomorrowIso`, `dateOnly` = UTC midnight for DATE columns). `TenantConfig.timezone` and `planningCutoffMin` (default 18:00 the day before). Plan times are minutes from local midnight | `tests/lib/dispatch-time.spec.ts` | `new Date()` / `toISOString().slice(0,10)` used for "today" or "tomorrow"; UTC-based cutoffs; clock times shown as minutes since departure |

#### Intentionally out of scope (do not report as bugs)

- **Recording actual deliveries, POD or KPIs.** That is OPERATION-PROJECT Lane A. RouteIQ only plans.
- **Route optimization inside OPERATION-PROJECT**: never.
- **A proven global optimum.** The product promises an "OPTIMIZED PLAN" within a time limit.
- **Profit claims without margin data.** Margin is used only when every order carries one.
- **Designed fallbacks:** OSRM down → labelled Haversine plan; a timed-out alternative is skipped with a note; a failed repack returns the search plans with a warning.
- **Deferred features:** live traffic, in-day real-time re-dispatch, pickups and returnable empties (`OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md` §7); driver PWA / GPS / POD, Mapbox Matrix, manual baseline comparison, the 30-day dashboard.
- **Multi-replica scaling** needs Redis / BullMQ first. It is a v2 item.
- **Legacy surfaces** (PyVRP `/optimize`, `runs/*`, legacy run pages) are kept on purpose until removal. Findings there matter only if they affect security, tenant data or dispatch plans.
- **The unrelated Fleet Management repository** is not part of this system and must not be used.

#### What NOT to do

- **Do not touch production.**
  - No Railway changes, no deploys, no migrations or `prisma migrate resolve` against the production DB.
  - No writes through the production web URL (listed in `docs/RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT.md`), and no load status changes on real tenants.
  - Never give OSRM or the solver a public domain (OSRM has no auth).
- **Do not push or merge to `main` without explicit approval from the owner and a fresh Postgres backup.** Every push to `main` auto-deploys web and solver and runs migrations pre-deploy, which cannot be rolled back without restoring the backup.
- **Never commit or print secrets.** Env var names are fine (`DATABASE_URL`, `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`, `NEXTAUTH_URL`, `AUTH_URL`, `SOLVER_URL`, `SOLVER_TOKEN`, `OSRM_URL`, `JANITOR_TOKEN`, `MAPBOX_TOKEN`, `RESEND_API_KEY`, `SUPER_ADMIN_EMAILS`, `SIGNUP_MODE`, `TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS`, `SENTRY_DSN`); values are not. Never hash a literal password in code (a test fails on it). They live in Railway and in local `.env` files, which are git-ignored.
- **Never copy anything from `.dev/`.** It holds real NMWC orders, the local Postgres data, the benchmark harness and its caches. It is git-ignored and local only. Report aggregate numbers only, and never quote real customer names from any source, including old PR descriptions.
- **Do not "fix" a bug by weakening an invariant**: relaxing reconciliation; letting frozen loads or superseded versions change; dropping a `tenantId` filter; switching the web to weighted priorities; raising a timeout past the next layer's limit.
- **Do not edit historical migrations.** Add a new one; use expand → migrate → contract for destructive changes.
- **Do not bulk-merge Dependabot majors** (zod 4, eslint 10, next-stack, recharts 3, prisma). Each needs its own tested PR.
- **Do not use `railway config migrate` or Railway IaC.**
- **Do not point `OSRM_URL` at the public demo server in production.**
- **Do not add a Server Action (`'use server'`), `next/image`, or `productionBrowserSourceMaps` before the Next.js upgrade** (audit A1, owner decision 4). The unit tests and the CI build check fail on them; the reasons are in [`docs/SECURITY.md`](./SECURITY.md) section 9.
- **Never read an uploaded file in the web process: a route calls `parseUploadIsolated` (`lib/upload-parse`), never `parseUpload` or SheetJS itself** (P5). It checks the size and type, then runs `parseUpload` in a separate process with a heap cap and a time limit, at most two at once; its refusals (`UploadParseRefused`) go through `uploadRefusedResponse`. Keep what the parser process bundles to the parser's own modules, SheetJS's `xlsx.mjs` and Papa Parse (`scripts/upload-parser-build.cjs` refuses anything else: no database client, nothing that reads secrets), and keep the options a route passes as data (`ParseSpec`), since a function cannot cross to the other process. `repo-guards.spec.ts` fails when a file other than `lib/csv.ts` and `lib/workbook-guard.ts` loads SheetJS or Papa Parse, or one other than `lib/upload-parse/handler.ts` loads `lib/csv`.
- **Never lay out the driver sheets in the web process: the PDF export calls `renderDriverPackIsolated` (`lib/pdf-render`), never `renderDriverPackPdf` itself** (review M3). The web builds the model (`driverPackModel`, plain data) and the renderer process lays it out with a heap cap and a time limit, at most two at once; its refusals (`PdfRenderRefused`) go through `pdfRefusedResponse`. Keep what the renderer bundles to its own modules and what React, `@react-pdf/renderer` and `qrcode` bring in (`scripts/pdf-renderer-build.cjs` refuses anything else: no database client, nothing that reads secrets), and keep the model plain data.
- **Do not hand an uploaded file to SheetJS (`XLSX.read`) except through `parseExcelSheets` in `lib/csv.ts`** (audit A1 review). It runs `guardSpreadsheet` first (SheetJS picks its reader from the bytes, and a few KB can make it loop for minutes), reads with `sheetRows`, `cellFormula: false` and `cellText: false` (the customer import's lat / lng cells alone keep a reference to their number format or CSV text, taken off every cell again before `sheet_to_json`, and only `parseUpload` works out their decimals, on the sheet it reads: `readWorkbook`, `shownSources`, A5; never format cells per cell with `XLSX.SSF.format`, which parses the format again each time, A5 fourth review), checks that SheetJS reads the sheet list the guard replayed (A1 v4), and checks every sheet's range before `sheet_to_json`. When SheetJS is upgraded, re-check `sheetReads` and the other copies of its code in `lib/workbook-guard.ts` against the new version (each names the SheetJS function it copies; the SYLK replay also decides, in `idFileFormatsCells`, whether a customer file that begins with "ID" may be read with `cellText`). `upload-limits.spec.ts` has the files that got through before.
- **Do not treat `CLAUDE.md` (the v1.3 build spec) or `OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md` as current behaviour.** Use `docs/OPTIMIZER_DESIGN.md` and the code.

- **F05**: `IntakeLineKey`, per-tenant intake lock and re-check at confirm (duplicate lines or file, master changes, stale late flag, 24 h expiry); an amended quantity is an error; the same SO on another date a warning; content hash with the delivery date.
- **F20** (L17): no batch delete once planned, one transaction, `UnservedOrder` FK NO ACTION, reconciliation fails on a missing scoped order. The "cancel orders from this file" flow is deferred; one order can be cancelled since 13 Oct 2026 (Cancel order, [3.11](#311-step-9-late-orders-and-plan-versions)).

- Case-variant customer / product twins resolve deterministically and cannot be created any more.

**PR2 review fixes** (adversarial verification of the PR2 branch; each has a test):

- **Corrected case weights reach open lines.** New `OrderLine.weightFromMaster`: a line without a file weight follows the product master, so a wrong case weight corrected under Products (1500 typed for 1.5) is applied at the next optimize / re-plan instead of being frozen at the first value. File weights and frozen loads never change. The product PATCH answer says how many open lines will take it; the day screen lists them and offers RE-PLAN.
- **Partial kg of merged rows.** A merged SO+SKU line with some blank weights is weighed from the master as a whole (0 kg = unknown when it has none), no longer stored at a partial kg that counted as known.
- **Refused re-plan no longer changes the live plan.** The re-plan probe applies master weights in memory only; they are saved in the transaction that starts the optimize (`applyWeightChanges`), after the parent was superseded. Set-based updates, guarded by the kg they were built from.
- **Optimize start vs batch delete.** The start transaction takes the intake lock and checks the scoped orders still exist (409 `ORDERS_CHANGED`) before OPTIMIZING is set; explicit 30 s / 10 s timeouts on it and on the late order, and P2028 answers 409 `INTAKE_BUSY`.
- **Late-order duplicates across case twins**: the `IntakeLineKey` lookup covers every twin id.
- **Day screen and plan view agree with the optimizer**: weight notes count the open rest of partly locked orders; a deactivated customer shows only with open, non-frozen orders; RE-PLAN is enabled when the plan in use is out of date (weights corrected, customer deactivated with orders still on planned loads), and the plan view names both.
- **Pre-release file hash**: a batch confirmed before this release (raw-row hash) still blocks the same file for the same dates.
- **Wording**: the batch-delete 409, the guide and 3.3 no longer suggest a late order or re-plan to remove orders; the weight question and notes tell planners and supervisors to ask a company admin; extra cases of a confirmed line go in a late order without a sales-order number (or a new one). The legacy run page asks the location / weight questions.
- **Tests added**: the 480-min service cap in `requestJson` with its warning, frozen load and assignment kg after a re-plan, and a customer deactivated while on a LOCKED load.

**Stabilization release, PR3 "Plan lifecycle and concurrency".** Fixed. Since the fourth review it has one additive migration (`20260926110000_plan_load_driver_set_by`: the hand-set driver marker) and one new optional key in `summaryJson` (`driverChanges`); nothing else changes the schema or a stored JSON shape:

- **F03** (L13, L14, new issue 18): every refusal of a re-plan is checked before a version exists - 409 `NOTHING_TO_PLAN` (every order on a locked, loading or dispatched load), 400 no truck, 409 job running, 429 / 503 admission - and Re-plan / OPTIMIZE are disabled when there is nothing to plan. Copy-forward: a new version copies every load, the chosen option (with its unserved rows) and the plan facts, so a failed optimization shows "Optimization failed - previous plan kept" and the copy can be locked and dispatched. A version without an applied plan never becomes READY from a load change and allows only unlock / back to locked. "Upload orders first" only when there are no orders.
- **F06**: version 1 is created under a per-day advisory lock (`createInitialPlan`, also for the legacy `POST /api/runs`, which answers an existing plan with 200); `createNextVersion` takes the same day lock. No partial unique index (Prisma 5 cannot express it; legacy duplicate v1 rows).
- **F07** (L15, new issues 9-12, 16, 17): every plan mutator locks the `RunPlan` row first and re-checks under it (`lib/dispatch/plan-locks.ts`); superseded = status SUPERSEDED **or** `supersededAt` set, everywhere (plan screen, driver sheets, WhatsApp, versions list, `currentPlan`, legacy dispatch); `applyScenario` writes READY / DISPATCHED conditionally; `startDispatchOptimize` does its checks, the job, OPTIMIZING and `OPTIMIZE_STARTED` in one transaction; a lock wait over 5 s answers 409 "Plan is being saved - retry" instead of a 500; `applyScenario` sets DISPATCHED when every load is out.
- **ADD-JOB-AUDIT**: the job's result and `OPTIMIZE_SUCCEEDED` commit together; `failJob` and the janitor never overwrite READY or SUPERSEDED; a stale result (version superseded, reaped, or taken over) is not applied.
- **NO_SOLUTION options** (solver new issue 24) cannot be used (409 `SCENARIO_NOT_USABLE`; "No plan" on the screen); a RECOMMENDED `NO_SOLUTION` on a version that holds a plan fails the job and keeps the plan.
- **ADD-STALE-DAY-CLIENT**: the day screen drops out-of-date day answers (`request-gate.ts`), disables its actions until the selected day has loaded, shows a load error instead of the old day, builds payloads from the loaded day only and sends `expect`; the server answers 409 `DAY_MISMATCH`. New issue 10: while any action of the plan screen runs, the others are disabled.
- **F16 solve admission**: per-user (15/h) and per-company (30/h) quotas, `SOLVER_MAX_CONCURRENT` concurrent solves in total and one less per company, with a fair queue (at most 2 waiting per company), shared by every solve entry; the solver refuses more than `MAX_CONCURRENT_DISPATCH` with 503.
- **Review of PR3, fixed before merge** (all confirmed findings):
  - *Admission fairness* (medium): the first defaults (2 per company = every slot of the default 2, one shared first-come queue of 10) let one sign-up company run both solves and fill the queue, so NMWC got 503 or waited about 45 minutes. Now one less per company than in total, at most 2 waiting per company (then 429 `SOLVE_QUEUE_TENANT` to that company only), and a freed slot goes to the company with the fewest solves running. Unit cases: one company's 12 starts, then another company runs at once. (Tightened after the second review, below.)
  - *Driver double-booking* (medium): the PLANNED copies a re-plan carries forward were taken as the new plan's drivers without a clash check, so a re-timed trip could put one driver on two trucks at once. Every driver RouteIQ fills in is now checked against the trips already given out, frozen loads included ([3.9](#39-step-7-a-driver-per-load)).
  - *Failed re-plan and weights* (low): master weights were saved when the optimization started, so after a failed re-plan the copied loads showed the old kg and utilisation while the "out of date weights" warning disappeared. Weights are now saved only in the job's finalization, with the plan that uses them ([3.6](#36-step-4-optimize)).
  - *Completed on a version without a plan* (low): DISPATCHED to COMPLETED is allowed again there, "Completed" is offered, and the `NO_PLAN_APPLIED` / `NOTHING_TO_PLAN` texts and the day-screen hint advise unlocking only when a LOCKED or LOADING load exists ([3.8](#38-step-6-load-states)).

- **Simplified driver rules (owner decision after the sixth review), before merge.** Every round of the driver rules found new edge cases; the seventh review confirmed more (among them: a note never ended on the real plan screen after Keep, because `getPlanDetail` passed rows without `driverHandSet`; "Use instead" could still double-book through the previous version's driver; a driver kept in the summary for a dropped trip could come back onto a driver already on the road, or fail an apply once its user was deleted). The rules were replaced by one short rule set ([3.9](#39-step-7-a-driver-per-load)): the evidence is the loads of the version being applied, frozen loads keep their drivers, a hand-set driver stays on its trip, every other trip - the one that moved least first - gets its own driver, the driver of the truck's nearest trip or the truck's default, whichever is active and free first, and a note only when a trip loses or changes its driver. Removed: the separate evidence of the previous version, the drivers kept in the summary for dropped trips (an older summary's list is ignored) and the notes for trips that were only filled in. `getPlanDetail` now feeds the notes its own loads, so a note ends on the screen and in Excel once the dispatcher sets that trip's driver. Tests: `tests/lib/dispatch-load-state.spec.ts` (every pass, the candidate order, moved-least, the notes), `tests/lib/plan-lifecycle.spec.ts` (the re-plan job and "Use instead" give the same drivers and notes for the same evidence, in both truck orders; frozen loads; an inactive and a dropped hand-set driver; Keep ends a note in `getPlanDetail`; an older summary), `tests/lib/choose-scenario-route.spec.ts`, `tests/lib/driver-pack.spec.ts`, `tests/integration/plan-lifecycle-db.spec.ts`; the rules were checked by mutation (the two reviews below found rules no test pinned yet; they are pinned now). `tests/lib/repo-guards.spec.ts` keeps the removed promises (a dropped driver coming back, "Driver added" notes) and helper names out of the docs and `lib/`.

"No driver" is now marked too (who, when; not a hand-set driver), and the notes read that marker (`driverSetByDispatcher`), so a note ends for good once the dispatcher sets that trip's driver ([3.9](#39-step-7-a-driver-per-load)).

The code follows the stable rule; the docs now say so, and `tests/lib/repo-guards.spec.ts` keeps the old wording out.

Each now has a test that fails under that mutation (`tests/lib/dispatch-load-state.spec.ts`, `tests/lib/plan-lifecycle.spec.ts`, `tests/lib/driver-pack.spec.ts`, `tests/integration/plan-lifecycle-db.spec.ts`).

**Stabilization release, PR4 "Frozen snapshots and the dispatch feasibility gate".** Fixed (migration `20260927090000_plan_snapshots_feasibility`, three nullable JSONB columns):

- **F08**: every option keeps what it was computed with (`ScenarioDetails.inputs`: depot, trucks, stops, config, settings, job); loads and stops keep the truck and customer facts they were planned with (`PlanLoad.truckSnapshotJson`, `RouteAssignment.stopSnapshotJson`), copied by re-plans (NULL-safe); plan detail, map, driver sheets, WhatsApp and workbook show the planned facts and flag later corrections as "changed after planning", never switching silently ([3.7](#37-step-5-reviewing-the-plan)).
- **F04 A** (solver): `feasibility.check_scenario` checks every returned scenario (`DispatchScenario.feasibility`: VERIFIED / VIOLATED / UNVERIFIED, EXACT / ESTIMATED); when the post-solve stage does not run (out of time, no candidate, exception) the raw plan is re-timed exactly, else reported VIOLATED; "serves more" only for VERIFIED options ([4.11](#411-post-solve-stage)).
- **F04 B** (web): `checkPlanFeasibility` per truck-day, stored in `RunPlan.feasibilityJson` and enforced on LOCK / LOADING / DISPATCH (409 `TIMES_NOT_VERIFIED`); `FEASIBILITY_GATE=warn` as the audited emergency switch; TIMES NOT VERIFIED on the sheets and the workbook ([3.8](#38-step-6-load-states)).
- **L23** (minimal): a dead stage worker loses only its own task; no healthy RECOMMENDED re-check is aborted because a sibling's pid changed.
- **F01 item 4 / F02 inside the gate**: each load's physical kg against the payload it was planned with; cases planned with no weight reported as `KG_UNKNOWN`.
- **New issues 13 / 60**: the ASSUMPTIONS sheet comes from the settings stored with the plan (both halves since the review below: also the routing-coverage line, never the web's `OSRM_URL`).
- **New issue 22**: each scenario carries its own timing status; no false "not re-checked" note. **23**: a service start before the truck arrives is reported (`TRAVEL`), not silently repaired. **25**: `hard_window_ok = false` is gated. **28**: `SOLVER_PARALLEL=0` logs a warning outside development (an error on Railway) and is documented ([5.11](#511-known-operational-gotchas) #11). **31**: the `OPTIMIZER_DESIGN.md` text on returned timetables matches the behaviour.
- **Review of PR4, fixed before merge** (all confirmed findings; each has a test):
  - *Split part filled to its payload refused forever* (medium): the web rounded each part's line and order kg separately (12.35 kg cases: 12.4 + 9867.7 = 9880.1 kg on a 9880 kg truck the optimizer filled correctly), so the check blocked it on every re-plan. The parts of a split stop now add up exactly to the kg sent to the optimizer (largest-remainder rounding in `splitIntoParts`), and one rounding tolerance, `KG_ROUNDING_TOL` = 0.5 kg, is used by the check, the workbook's Kg check and `applyScenario`'s cross-check (parts stored before the fix pass too). `dispatch-split.spec.ts` runs the 12.35 kg x 800 case example for every 2-line and 2-order split.
  - *No-weight warning read today's product master* (medium): a 0-kg part whose product got a weight after locking lost its warning and passed as 0 kg (about 8000 kg physically on a 3000 kg truck). "Planned with no weight" is now read from the plan's rows (`portionLinesJson[].kgPerCase`; for older parts, a 0-kg line whose part weighs no more than its weighed lines), and a case weight entered since that puts the load over its payload blocks as `CAPACITY_KG_NEW_WEIGHT` ("OVER PAYLOAD at the case weights entered since planning" in the workbook).
  - *WhatsApp message without the change notes or TIMES NOT VERIFIED* (medium, a regression of this PR): it now prints each change made after planning with the corrected pin, and TIMES NOT VERIFIED first, like the PDF sheet.
  - *Re-plan advised for a problem on a locked or loading load* (low): a re-plan copies such a load unchanged. The 409 (`remedy`, `unlockFirst`), the red box, the load badge and the disabled Re-plan button now say to put that load back to Planned first ("Back to locked", then "Unlock"), then re-plan (`timingRemedy`).
  - *Inverted windows as a permanent "changed after planning"* (low): legacy windows that end before they start were planned as "any time"; `stopMasterChanges`, the check and the snapshots of older options apply the same `usableWindow` rule, so the day is no longer out of date after every re-plan.
  - *Truck corrections did not mark the day out of date* (low): the day overview counts trucks with PLANNED loads whose capacity or payload changed (`outdated.trucksChanged`, step 3 then offers RE-PLAN), and the check warns (`CAPACITY_CHANGED`) when a load not yet out no longer fits the corrected truck.
  - *Access notes frozen in the snapshot* (low): they are contact details, carried as they are now by the plan detail and printed so on the driver sheets, like the driver's name and phone (the snapshot keeps the planned notes for the record).
  - *This PR4 block was missing from 7.4* (low): added.

  - *Three integration tests pinned the old two-key `outdated`* (medium, CI only): `dispatch-weights.spec.ts` compared the day's `outdated` with `{ weightCases, inactiveOrders }`, so the two keys this PR added (`masterChanged`, `trucksChanged`) failed three tests. `day-overview.ts` now exports `UP_TO_DATE` (the shape, every count 0), the specs compare against it, and `day-overview-weights.spec.ts` pins that every path returns exactly its keys.

  - *The day screen said "up to date" while the check blocked the open rest of a split order* (low): a case weight entered after planning for an order partly on a frozen load was skipped by the day overview, so RE-PLAN was off while the PLANNED part got `CAPACITY_KG_NEW_WEIGHT`. **Stabilization release, PR5 "Costs, routing provenance and deadlines, effective settings, audit catalog, error contract, legacy cleanup".** Fixed (migration `20260928090000_plan_load_cost_json`, one nullable JSONB column):

- **F17** (L22; owner decision: DRIVER PAY = the WHOLE TRUCK DAY): one cost model, `apps/solver/costing.py` - the driver is paid from the first departure (or first frozen departure) to the last return, turnaround and waiting included, overtime after the configured hours on top. The same function prices the post-solve score's money (`load_repack.score`) and every scenario's loads, truck days and totals (`_build_scenario`, which checks that the loads add up); the routing model, the repack and the exact timing pay a truck with frozen loads from its last frozen return. Documented per-load allocation (each load owns the time since its truck's previous return; fixed cost on load 1). The web stores each load's breakdown (`PlanLoad.costJson`), and the summary / KPI, the options table (whole-day cost of each option), the workbook (label, breakdown, paid time, TRUCK DAYS sheet) and the dashboard (from the plan summary, so re-planned days count their carried loads) all add the same numbers up. Plans saved before are labelled as costed the earlier way (`costBasis` MIXED_LEGACY). The `dispatch_models.py` driver-rate comment is corrected.

**Stabilization release, PR6 "Scenario findings: intake, messages and exports".** Five realistic-volume days (S01-S05, 320-450 invoices each) were run through the real web flow on `main` (PR1-PR3); each finding below was confirmed by two independent checks. - **B2 (S04, medium): a two-sheet workbook was cut to its first sheet without a word.** `S04_Orders.xlsx` (Orders 1,082 rows + LateOrder 116 rows, 6 urgent clinics) was accepted with no warning and the LateOrder sheet dropped. `parseUpload` now reads every sheet; the order upload refuses order rows on more than one sheet with 400 `MULTIPLE_SHEETS` naming each sheet and its rows ("Upload each sheet as its own file"), saves nothing, and reads a single order sheet wherever it is (`isOrderSheet`, the tenant's aliases included). There is no sheet choice in the screen or the API, so none was added. The customer import and baseline upload name the sheets they did not read ([3.3](#33-step-1-upload-and-validate-the-order-file)).
- **S04 (low): `LATE_REASON_REQUIRED` named the wrong reason.** A file for a day with a plan in use was told "These orders arrived after the planning cutoff". The message is now built from the stored reasons (`lateReasonRequiredMessage`), and the plan reason counts the plan's dispatched and locked loads (`planExistsReason`: "A plan (version 1) already exists for 2026-10-07 (2 of its loads are dispatched)."). The late-order dialog's field no longer says "after cutoff" only.
- **S05 (low): re-upload after a deactivation.** Lines already confirmed for a customer deactivated since were "Customer s05-c05 / MAIN is inactive" errors. They are now duplicates ("Already confirmed: ..., skipped. Customer S05-C05 / MAIN is inactive now: its confirmed orders are not planned until it is reactivated."; the same for a product); a new or changed line stays an error. Duplicate, amendment and inactive messages name the master codes, the refused confirm of a file with errors has the code `FILE_HAS_ERRORS`, and the "already confirmed" file error names the file's dates instead of "this date".
- **Excel (low, S01-S05):** the SUMMARY states invoices (distinct sales orders, `invoiceCounts`) next to delivery orders (one per customer branch; was "Total orders") and stops on trucks; the driver sheets' Notes column carries the access notes and order notes the PDF prints; ASSUMPTIONS no longer claims the x1.25 road time factor for a straight-line plan (PR5 had reworded it to "on road travel times (not on estimated legs)", which still listed it for plans with no road leg) and says when the fuel price was not used; the summary warnings are stored once (the workbook and screen already showed "Distances are ESTIMATED" once; the stored summary had it twice).

Re-plan to search again" - kg explained all but 64 kg, so a re-plan could not help. `_build_scenario` now also bounds the fleet by kg when every usable truck has a payload: the per-stop reason names kg ("shortage by weight", or "weight is the tighter limit today"), and the warning fires only when neither the case nor the kg shortage explains what is unserved and an unserved stop still fits the room left on some load (the second part since the review below; [4.12](#412-unserved-reason-codes-and-messages)).

The reviewer's day (6 trucks x 1 load of 600 cases / 6,500 kg, stops of 30 cases / 336 kg; each load 6,384 kg, 116 kg of room, every unserved stop 336 kg) still got the warning and its re-plan advice, which the dispatcher guide says cannot help; the real S03 day escaped it only because its mixed stop sizes left 78 kg of room in all. **Stabilization release, PR7 "Optimizer: truck count, search time, options trade-off"** (stacked on PR6, which is on PR5 and the plan map fix (#36); answers the confirmed findings B3, T1 and N1 of the Sep 2026 scenario re-test, five realistic days of 160-340 solver stops on main and on main + PR4 + PR5). No migration, no stored JSON shape changed (two optional response fields added):

- **B3** (medium): the truck count ignored the trucks of locked, loading and dispatched loads. `_build_scenario` counted `trucks_used = len({ld.truck_id for ld in loads})` over the NEW loads only, and `load_repack.score()` did the same. After a re-plan the options table and the job message understated the day's physical trucks (the targeted probe, T02 limited to one load: RECOMMENDED shown with 6 trucks but using 7, the alternatives 5 using 6, "10 loads on 6 trucks"), and MIN_TRUCKS, which ranks candidates by that count, could prefer "new loads on a fresh truck" over "new loads on trucks already out", using more physical trucks and paying a fresh truck's day. Fixed:
  - solver: `trucks_used` is the physical count (new loads' trucks + every truck with frozen loads, `_frozen_truck_ids`), also for NOTHING_TO_PLAN / NO_SOLUTION options; new optional `frozen_trucks` and `frozen_loads` on `DispatchScenario` (and in `packages/shared-types`); `LR.Day.frozen_trucks` and `score().trucks` count the same way, so MIN_TRUCKS' selection (`_GOALS`) and the "Loads were re-assigned ... A -> B trucks" note use physical trucks. A truck with frozen loads already never paid the "open a truck" fixed cost again (routing model and `_pricing`, MIN_TRUCKS' ×20 included); now documented and tested ([4.11](#411-post-solve-stage));
  - web: the options table counts each option's trucks from its stored loads + the kept loads' trucks (`physicalTruckCount` in `lib/dispatch/plan-options.ts`, so options saved by an older optimizer show the right number too) and its loads as kept + new ("(N new)"); the job message reads "N new loads + K kept (locked or dispatched) on M trucks" (`jobMessage`; the kept loads are read from the version's rows of `scope.frozenLoadIds`, so a truck deactivated after its load went out - not in the request, so not counted by the optimizer either - still counts, as on the plan screen); the Excel SUMMARY gets the same figures under **PLAN OPTIONS** (its "Physical trucks used" KPI already counted every load of the version).
- **T1** (quality): the automatic search time jumped from 20 s (≤ 200 stops) to 150 s (201-350), so a 200-stop day got 20 s and visibly different plans run to run, while 201 stops waited four minutes. Now monotone without the jump (`auto_time_limit`, `TIME_LIMIT_POINTS`): 20 s up to 120 stops (NMWC's usual 80-120-stop days unchanged), then straight lines to 50 s at 150 stops and 150 s at 200 (135 stops 35 s, 175 stops 100 s), 150 s from 200 to 350, 240 s above as before. It never gives a day size less than the pre-PR7 schedule (owner decision, see the review fixes): **121-200 stops get more** search time (150 stops +30 s, 175 stops +80 s, 200 stops +130 s), so their wall time for three options rises by roughly the extra search time × 1.5 plus a few seconds of re-check (about +45 s at 150 stops; about +3 min at 200, about the 4 min a 201-stop day already took); every other size keeps its time. The straight line suggested with the finding (20 s at 100 stops to 150 s at 350) would give a 120-stop day 30 s (+10 s) and every 201-349-stop day less than 150 s, so the line starts at 120 stops and reaches 150 s at 200. Every value fits the 540 s budget with the slowest road matrix (tested), and the web still waits 600 s ([2.8](#28-timeouts-budgets-and-limits), [4.7](#47-the-or-tools-routing-model)).
- **N1** (quality, transparency only): RECOMMENDED is often dominated by MIN_TRUCKS / MIN_DISTANCE on km and money because it also values early delivery of P1/P2 and preferred hours (a preference the table did not show: +1.6 to +37.2 OMR a day over the cheapest option on the re-test). What RECOMMENDED optimizes is **unchanged**. The options table gets a **Preference cost** column (window + early + continuity, OMR-equivalent; it replaces "Preferred-hours miss", which showed the window part only) and a **What it gains** column (`optionTradeoffs`): RECOMMENDED against the cheapest different plan ("vs MIN TRUCKS: P1/P2 delivered on average 40 min earlier, preference cost 19.5 OMR lower; but costs 35.4 OMR more, 87 km more, 1 more truck"), each alternative against RECOMMENDED, "Same plan as ..." for identical plans. The minutes compare service starts over the P1/P2 stops both options serve (the early priorities follow `early_preference_per_min`, default P1/P2). The Excel SUMMARY lists the same under PLAN OPTIONS. **Owner decision** ([7.5](#75-open-questions-for-the-owner)): RECOMMENDED stays as it is (priority-first timing, option (a)); the options table now shows the trade-off.
- **Tests** (each fails without its fix): solver `test_repack.py` (`test_auto_time_limits`, `test_auto_time_limit_schedule`: monotone for 1-600 stops, 80-120 stops at 20 s, 200-350 at 150 s, the budget; `test_auto_time_limit_never_below_the_pre_pr7_schedule`: no size of 1-600 stops gets less than the pre-PR7 schedule (PR7 review, owner decision; fails on PR7's first schedule from 201 stops); `test_score_counts_the_trucks_of_frozen_loads`: score and MIN_TRUCKS' ranking with two trucks already out and one fresh, and no ×20 fixed cost on the trucks already out; `test_min_trucks_uses_the_trucks_already_out`: end to end, MIN_TRUCKS' selection - the trucks already out cost more per km, so RECOMMENDED puts both new loads on the fresh truck and MIN_TRUCKS must still pick the two trucks already out, 2 physical trucks against RECOMMENDED's 3; PR7 review: its first fixture had equal truck costs, so no candidate left the trucks already out idle and it passed on the old code except for the new response fields), `test_dispatch.py` (`test_trucks_used_counts_the_trucks_of_frozen_loads`: the S04 probe shape, and a day with nothing to plan; `test_web_search_time_schedule_is_the_solver_schedule`, PR7 review); web `tests/lib/plan-options.spec.ts` (14 tests, see [5.3](#53-test-suites)), `tenant-settings.spec.ts` (the Settings search-time row and the web copy of the schedule, never below the pre-PR7 schedule, PR7 review) and `plan-lifecycle.spec.ts` (the re-plan job's message counts a kept load whose truck is no longer in the request); integration `dispatch-costs.spec.ts` extended (the late-order re-plan's chosen option counts the locked load's truck and load like the KPI; the job message).
- **PR7 review fixes:**
  - *Settings still stated the old search time* (medium): the "Search time" row of the effective planner values read "20 s up to 200 stops, 150 s up to 350 stops" from a web constant PR7 had not touched, so for every 122-299-stop day it named another time than the optimizer used (a 200-stop day: 20 s stated, 70 s used by PR7's first schedule). The schedule is now in `planner-bounds.json` (`searchTimeSec`: points, small-day and large-day seconds, and examples); the row is built from its web copy (`searchTimeText`, `autoTimeLimitSec`), a pytest checks the JSON against `auto_time_limit` for 1-600 stops and a vitest checks the web copy and the row text.

The points are now (120, 20 s), (150, 50 s), (200, 150 s): 150 s from 200 up to 350 stops. `test_auto_time_limit_never_below_the_pre_pr7_schedule` (solver) and `tenant-settings.spec.ts` (the web copy) fail if any size of 1-600 stops gets less; the former "at most 1 s more per extra stop" guard became monotone + never below the pre-PR7 schedule + the budget.
