**P5 third review fixes** (same branch, `audit-p5-upload-worker`, on `5f608e0`). Three findings, each confirmed by two skeptics, all low: one in the code (older than P5, outside E2) and two in the handbook. No new API route and no role change (the role matrix is unchanged); the order upload has one new answer, 500 `CHECK_FAILED`; no schema or migration change, no solver change, no new setting.

- *An order file with more than 32,767 different sales orders was refused with Prisma's own text* (low, code; the same on main). An order file may have 50,000 rows. `validateIntake` asked for every sales order of the file in one `IntakeLineKey` query, next to the company and `deliveryDate notIn` the file's dates. PostgreSQL takes at most 32,767 bind parameters in one query, and Prisma cannot split that list next to the other conditions (P2035 from 32,766 sales orders, P2029 from 32,767). The route answered every error except the depot rule as 400 with the error's own text, so the dispatcher got "Invalid `prisma.intakeLineKey.findMany()` invocation in C:\...\intake-server.ts:241:45 ... Query parameter limit exceeded ...". **Fixed** (`lib/dispatch/intake-server.ts`, `app/api/orders/upload/route.ts`):
  - *The sales orders are asked for in parts* of 10,000 (`IN_LIST_PART`, `inParts`): each query holds the company and one part. The file's own dates are left out after the query instead of in it, so no query passes the limit, however many sales orders or dates a file has. The warning ("Sales order ... was already confirmed for ...; this file has it again for ...") is the same, for a sales order in any part.
  - *Anything else that fails while an order file is checked* (the database, a bug) is answered 500 `{ code: 'CHECK_FAILED', message }`: "RouteIQ could not check this file. Nothing was saved. Try again in a moment. If it happens again, tell your administrator." (`INTAKE_CHECK_FAILED`). The error goes to the server log as `[orders-upload] checking the file failed`; nothing is saved. The depot rule keeps its 422.
  - *Such a file can then be added* (not asked for). `confirmIntake` put each line into its customer's order by copying the order's list of lines for every line. One customer's 40,000 lines took 40 s before a row was written, and the confirm's transaction has 60 s: the new integration spec, run with the check fixed and the confirm not yet, got `INTAKE_BUSY` ("Another order file or late order is being added ..."). Each line is now added to its order's list in place: the same lines in the same order.
- *Measured* (this PC, busy with other work; own checks, not in CI; `next start` of this build on port 3008; real files: counts and timings only):

  | File | Before (the code of `5f608e0`, the same as main) | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | 33,000 different sales orders, one customer (CSV, 5 columns) | refused 400 with Prisma's text (P2029) | checked 200 in 12.9 s, `/api/health/live` waited up to 2.3 s meanwhile; confirmed 200 in 15.4 s (33,000 lines and keys) |
  | 50,000 different sales orders, the row limit | refused 400 with Prisma's text (P2029) | checked 200 in 17.7 s, `/api/health/live` up to 2.7 s; confirmed 200 in 20.1 s |
  | 40,000, database level (the new spec at 40,000) | refused 400 with Prisma's text | checked in 11.4 s, confirmed in 17.1 s (with the check fixed but not the confirm: the lines took 39.8 s to group, the confirm passed 60 s, `INTAKE_BUSY`) |
  | NMWC's real order files (three CSVs of 373 rows, the .xlsx of 373 rows, late orders of 4 rows) | - | each checked 200 with every row valid, 0.96-1.9 s; the slowest `/api/health/live` answer per file 77-650 ms |

  One run of 50,000 at the database level, while the PC was under load, confirmed in 70 s: past the 60 s, so it was answered `INTAKE_BUSY` and nothing was saved; the next run took 17.6 s. The confirm's time goes to writing the lines and the keys (about 7 s each for 50,000 on this PC).
- *5.3 had no P5 count* (low, docs). Every earlier PR added its web unit total to 5.3's "Expected counts"; P5 did not, so the last total there was A5's 1718. **Corrected:** the P5 line (1838 in 85 files: 1718 + 120, by spec) and this review's line (1844 in 86 files).
- *The status line said that no file can freeze or crash the web process* (low, docs), while the P5 block and `SECURITY.md` 10 list the request body as open. Next.js 14 reads a whole request body into the web process before the route answers, keeping a copy for its middleware, which runs on the upload routes; the route's `req.formData()` then reads the file before the 10 MB check. Measured here on `next start` without a session (each answered 401): a 50 MB request took the web process from 251 to 356 MB, a 300 MB request from 356 to 859 MB, still held 1.5 s later; a 300 MB request to `/api/health/live`, which the middleware skips, was answered 405 in 10 ms and added 3 MB. None of this is under the parser's heap cap, and no parser process is there for the kernel to kill instead. **Corrected:** the status line (reading a file within the 10 MB limit can no longer freeze or crash the web process; the request body and the order check of a very large file are named as open), [3.3](#33-step-1-upload-and-validate-the-order-file) step 1, [5.6](#56-deployment-on-railway), the 7.5 question (a check in the route comes too late), `SECURITY.md` 10, `admin.md` and `RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT.md`.
- **Behaviour changes a dispatcher can see.** An order file of 32,766 or more different sales orders is checked and can be added; it was refused with Prisma's text. When the check fails for a reason that is not the file's, the answer is 500 in plain words ("RouteIQ could not check this file. ...", also in the dispatcher guide); it was 400 with the error's text. Everything else is the same: NMWC's files give the same rows, lines and warnings (their sales orders are one part), and the confirm makes the same orders and lines in the same order.
- **Deviations** (each with its reason): *the file's own dates are left out after the query* (the finding offered parts, or a raw `= ANY` query): with parts alone, a file with many delivery dates could still pass the limit through the `notIn` list; a raw query would bypass Prisma's types and the fake database of the unit tests. *Parts of 10,000*, the finding's example: each query has 10,001 bind parameters. *500, not 400*, for `CHECK_FAILED`: the failure is not the file's, like "the file reader stopped". *The confirm fix* (not asked for): without it the file the finding names could be checked but not added. *The integration spec uses 33,000 sales orders*, just over the limit, so its confirm stays far inside the 60 s on a busy CI runner; the unit spec covers 40,000, 32,766 and 32,767.
- **Tests** (each new one was run before its fix and failed): `intake-many-sales-orders.spec.ts` (6, new, unit, `fake-plan-db.ts` refusing any read of more than 32,767 bind parameters as PostgreSQL and Prisma do): `inParts`; 40,000 sales orders checked 200 with the other-date warning in the first and the last part (before: 400 with the Prisma text); 32,766 and 32,767 (before: 400); one customer's 40,000 lines confirmed in under 3 s (0.14-0.27 s; 7-14 s before, 8.7 s in the failing run); a database error while checking answers 500 `CHECK_FAILED` without Prisma's text, saves nothing and logs it (before: 400 with the text); the depot rule still 422 (a guard: passed before too). `intake-many-sales-orders-db.spec.ts` (2, new, database level): 33,000 sales orders checked with both other-date warnings and confirmed, and the same file again checked with every line a skipped duplicate (before: 400 with Prisma's text at 33,000 and at 40,000; at 40,000 with the check fixed, the confirm answered `INTAKE_BUSY`). Unchanged and passing: the whole web unit suite (1844 in 86 files), the upload and intake integration specs (57 tests in 9 files, the HTTP ones against `next start` of this build), types and lint. `pnpm build` and the build check passed (the parser bundle 838 KB from 10 files; no Server Actions, no public source maps); the startup check logged `[upload-parse] the file reader works (startup check)`. Counts: [5.3](#53-test-suites).
- **Still open:** the request body (owner question, [7.5](#75-open-questions-for-the-owner)); the order check of a very large file still runs in the web process (2.3-2.7 s for 33,000-50,000 lines here; owner question); a confirm of 50,000 lines takes 17-20 s here and once passed 60 s under load, and `INTAKE_BUSY` then says that another file is being added, which is not what happened. Other lists that grow with the orders are still asked for in one query: the file's delivery dates in the check (`confirmedLineMap`), the file's customers and products at confirm, and the sales orders of the orders being brought forward (`laterLinesOf` in `carry-over.ts`). Only a file of 32,766 or more different delivery dates, customers or products, or a bring-forward of that many sales orders, reaches the limit (NMWC: a few hundred); in the check it is now answered `CHECK_FAILED`.

**Audit of 27 Sep 2026, PR A6 "Solver and plan-output accuracy"** (branch `audit-p6-solver-accuracy`, on main `3451f4d`: the stabilization PRs, Bring forward, audit A1-A4 and A5, with main `d5b436f` (audit P5) merged in later; the consolidated assessment's PR 6, `.dev/audit-2026-09-27/VERIFIED-ASSESSMENT.md`). **Fixed: audit F08, E4, E5, E3, F22, F23, E1**, with the owner decisions as approved: 13 (a moved depot pin), 14 (only new cost), 15 (no hidden payload margin) and 26 (compare priority service first, then cost). No migration and no schema change (the depot origin lives in the existing `PlanLoad.truckSnapshotJson`), no new API route and no role change (changed behaviour noted in `api-role-matrix.spec.ts`); the solver changed, and since the A6 review its answer carries two optional fields per option (`weight_unit_kg`, `new_overtime_only`: the rules the plan was made with), which an older web ignores and an older solver does not send.

- **F08, weights in 0.1 kg** ([4.4](#44-how-the-web-shapes-the-request), [4.7](#47-the-or-tools-routing-model)). Every kg check of the engine works in whole units of 0.1 kg: each stop to the nearest unit, the payload rounded down (`kg_units`, `payload_units` in `dispatch_models.py`) - the route search's Kg dimension, the prefilters, the room-left check, the shortage reasons, the repack and the exact timing (`Facts.kg_units`, `fits_truck`) and the independent check (`CAPACITY_KG`, no `KG_TOL`). 999.1 + 999.1 + 1,001.8 = 3,000.0 kg now fits a 3,000 kg truck with one load in all three options, VERIFIED (it was left out as "low priority"); 3,000.1 kg does not, and its reason reads "3,000.1 kg requested vs 3,000 kg" (it read "3,000 vs 3,000"). The web sends every order, or split portion, to the nearest 0.1 kg with the same floating-point steps (`kgTenths`, `roundKg`, `payloadTenths` in `weights.ts`), sizes split parts for the payload rounded down to 0.1 kg (it floored to whole kg), and the stored load kg (`loadKgFromRefs`), the dispatch check's rows and the plan's stops add up the same tenths. The verifiers' misleading reason is fixed too: a stop that no load and no free trip has room for says "Not planned: no load or free trip has room for its 1,600 kg (the most room left on a load that takes its 10 cases is 1,400 kg). ... Add a truck or raise the loads-per-truck limit." (`_no_room_reason`, [4.12](#412-unserved-reason-codes-and-messages)), not "Re-plan to search again"; the code stays `SOLVER_DROPPED_LOW_PRIORITY`. The ASSUMPTIONS sheet has a Weights row: "each order to the nearest 0.1 kg, checked against each truck's payload with no margin (a load may weigh exactly the payload)" (since the A6 review only for a plan whose option reports `weight_unit_kg` 0.1; an older plan's row states the earlier rule). A6 review: the room counts only a load's stops of the same or a higher priority, so a stop left out by time while lower-priority stops fill the loads keeps the search's reason and warning (below).
- **E4, only new overtime** (owner decision 14). A truck with locked or dispatched loads pays overtime for its new loads only after the later of its day start + overtime-after and its last frozen return (`load_repack.overtime_bound_s`) in the route search's soft bound, the CP-SAT repack and the exact timing - as the reported cost (`costing.truck_day_costs`) always counted it. The verifiers' day (truck A out 06:00-18:00, overtime 4 OMR/h after 9 h; idle truck B 6 OMR): the new load now goes on A for about 3 OMR in the raw route search, the repack and the final plan, instead of B for 6 OMR. The ASSUMPTIONS sheet's Overtime row says "overtime already worked by locked or dispatched loads is not counted again for new loads" (since the A6 review only for a plan whose option reports `new_overtime_only`).
- **E5, the repack never gives up before its first answer.** `_solve_until_stalled` starts its stall clock at the first solution; before it, only the solver's time limit stops the search (it stopped a search whose first answer came after 1 s with none, UNKNOWN). A repack without an answer logs a WARNING ("repack UNKNOWN after X s (limit Y s) for <source>/<goal>: kept the plan it started from") and the plan it started from stays a candidate of every goal's job when it times exactly. Phase 1 ends by the solve's own limit, and so does phase 2 unless phase 1 ran long (the fixed 0.5 s floors are gone), so `share()`, the job budget and the pool deadline still bound the stage; only when phase 1 left phase 2 less than 60 % of the limit does phase 2 still get 60 % of the limit, at most 0.5 s (a phase 2 of a few hundredths of a second ended with no plan once in the benchmark), and that bounded overrun comes out of the next source's share.
- **E3, the loading sheet weighs what the load weighs** ([3.10](#310-step-8-exports)). The plan detail gives each row's SKU lines the row's planned kg (`rowLinesKg` in `split.ts`: the portion's kept case weight, per case for an order weighed at order level, else the lines' kg; 0.1 kg shares that add up exactly), so the manifests, the Excel LOADING MANIFEST and the SKU LOADING SUMMARY equal the load's kg: the verifiers' re-weighed partly frozen part shows 300 kg (it showed 200 kg on a 300 kg load) and an order weighed at order level its kg (it showed 0 kg). The load sheet and the SKU summary check kg as well as cases ("MISMATCH: load records N kg (order weights changed since planning)", "MISMATCH (kg)").
- **F22, an option that breaks the timing rules says so** ([3.7](#37-step-5-reviewing-the-plan)). `OptionFacts` carries the option's own check; `optionTradeoffs` gives a VIOLATED or UNVERIFIED option no trade-off but "Breaks the timing rules (N problems): it cannot be dispatched. Re-plan, or use another option." (UNVERIFIED: "Its timing could not be checked ..."), never compares with it, and RECOMMENDED with no other rule-keeping option says "Every different option breaks the timing rules." Options from before the check are compared as before. The Excel PLAN OPTIONS line adds "timing VERIFIED / VIOLATED".
- **F23, cost per case rounded once**: `rollupRows` rounds to the 3 decimals the dashboard shows (0.045 reads 0.045, not 0.050; its change from yesterday uses the same figure).
- **E1, a moved depot pin** (owner decision 13; not A5's customer-pin rule, where the driver gets the new pin). Each load keeps the depot pin it was planned from in its truck snapshot (`TruckSnapshot.origin`: the option's `inputs.depot`, else the live depot for an option without inputs), `createNextVersion` copies it verbatim, and a load planned before origins were kept gets the depot its version was optimized from on its next copy (`plannedOriginOf`: an earlier copy's origin, else the root load's option). `DetailLoad.origin` feeds the map (per-load start and end, the same `pointsKey` as `GET /api/runs/:id/load-geometry`, a grey marker at a moved origin), the route links, the WhatsApp text, the driver sheets (badge "DEPOT MOVED SINCE PLANNING: ROUTE FROM THE PLANNED DEPOT PIN") and the workbook's DEPOT rows. A pin moved more than 50 m gives the load a `DEPOT` change and the plan its own sentence ("Depot moved since planning: T01 L1 starts and ends at the depot pin it was planned from (2.2 km from the depot's pin now). Locked and dispatched loads keep it."; planned loads: "... is still planned from the old depot pin ... Re-plan to plan it from the new pin."; since the A6 review each load gives its own distance when they differ, and one load reads in the singular), never "Truck capacity changed"; a PLANNED load on the old pin makes the day out of date (since the A6 review also one planned before origins were kept: the option's `inputs.depot`, as on the plan screen) (`outdated.depotMoved`, "the depot pin was moved ..."), so RE-PLAN uses the new pin. Loads with no snapshot at all keep today's behaviour.
- **What looks different after the deploy:** weight-bound days can fill a truck to exactly its payload (utilisation up to 100.0 %); a truck already in overtime on its locked loads gets a new load more often than an idle truck (fewer trucks and less money, more overtime for that driver: see [7.5](#75-open-questions-for-the-owner) for the optional penalty); repack solves on hard days run until their first answer (inside the same budget); loading sheets show kg that equal the load's; options that break the timing rules say so; the dashboard's cost per case can change by up to 0.005; loads kept from before a depot pin was moved are drawn from the old pin with a note.
- **Deploy order:** web first, or both together. A new web with the old solver is safe (it sends kg already in 0.1 kg; the old solver rounds them up as before). A new solver with the old web rounds the old web's unrounded order kg per stop, so a many-stop load could weigh up to 0.05 kg per stop more than the old web's exact sum, which its dispatch check allows (0.5 kg).
- **Deviations** (each with its reason): the reason code for "no room" stays `SOLVER_DROPPED_LOW_PRIORITY` (a new code needs a Prisma enum migration; the words are what the dispatcher reads); the dispatch check keeps its 0.5 kg tolerance (it only allows, and tightening it could block loads locked before the deploy); the optional per-truck payload reserve of decision 15 is not built (it needs a Truck column, a migration this PR was planned without, and about ten touch points; recorded in [7.5](#75-open-questions-for-the-owner) with its design); the visible penalty for drivers already in overtime (decision 14) is recorded, not built; a stored planned kg per whole-order row does not exist, so an older version whose orders were re-weighed later still differs from its stored load kg - the sheet now says so instead of hiding it (full frozen exports are policy 23, not this PR).
- **Tests** (each guarantee fails without its change, except E3's `getPlanDetail` path, which only the A6 review's test below guards, and F22's rule that two options with the same plan beside a broken one are not "the same plan as the other options", which only the third review's test below guards: the first ten new solver tests were run against the old solver files and all failed; the eleventh expects phase 2 to get 0.3 s where the old code gave 0.5 s): solver `test_dispatch.py` +5 (86) and `test_repack.py` +9 (48) ([5.3](#53-test-suites)); web unit `dispatch-split.spec.ts` (0.1 kg part sizes and fit, `rowLinesKg`: the verifiers' two shapes and controls), `dispatch-weights.spec.ts` (`kgTenths` / `payloadTenths` equal the solver's rule, `loadKgFromRefs` adds tenths), `dispatch-feasibility.spec.ts` (the gate's rows in tenths), `dispatch-workbook.spec.ts` (manifest kg = load kg and the kg MISMATCH, the planned depot pin, the ASSUMPTIONS rows), `plan-options.spec.ts` (the verifiers' F22 case, UNVERIFIED, older options, RECOMMENDED broken; getPlanDetail and the Excel line), `dashboard-live-plans.spec.ts` (F23), `plan-snapshots.spec.ts` (origin, the depot note, the day out of date), `day-overview-weights.spec.ts` (`outdated.depotMoved` in `UP_TO_DATE`), `dispatch-plan-map-state.spec.ts` (a load drawn from its origin keeps its road shape), `driver-pack.spec.ts` (route links, badge and WhatsApp from the origin), `plan-feasibility-gate.spec.ts` (the origin written at apply, stamped and copied by two re-plans, shown with its note); integration `dispatch-mvp.spec.ts` 28a (lock, move the depot 2.2 km, re-plan: the locked copy keeps its origin and note, new loads use the new pin, the road shapes match the screen, the day is up to date). No new spec file.
- **Benchmark** (required; method and tables in [`OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md`](./OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md) section 10): main `3451f4d` and the branch, one after the other on the same PC, two web-API runs of each version per day (the five synthetic scenario days S01-S05 plus S04b, and the real NMWC day of 28 Sep moved to 15 Oct), then each day's stored request replayed back to back. **Priority service never got worse: every day, every run, the same number of orders served per priority (P1-P5) and the same number unserved per priority and reason** (the orders themselves are the same on every day but S03, where each version leaves out 5 P4 orders the other serves and the branch carries 4 cases more; corrected by the second A6 review); every option of every run VERIFIED. Cost in the replays: lower on six days (S01 -3.1 %, S02 -0.4 %, S03 -0.2 %, S04 re-plan -2.0 %, S04b re-plan -15.7 % with one truck and one load fewer, real day -0.4 %) and +0.5 % on S05 (the search finding another plan; main's own two runs of S05 differed by 10.6 %); -2.1 % over the seven days. The optimizer's time is within 3 s of main's. Other work kept the PC at about 100 % CPU during the runs; the replays separate the code from that. One repack in a branch web run ended UNKNOWN after its phase 1 overran; the follow-up (phase 2 keeps 60 % of the limit, at most 0.5 s) fixed it before the replays.
- **Not in this part:** the payload reserve and the overtime penalty ([7.5](#75-open-questions-for-the-owner)); the legacy `/route-geometries` and route-adjust paths (assessment PR 8); frozen historical exports (policy 23).

**Audit PR A6 review fixes** (same branch, `audit-p6-solver-accuracy`; review of the A6 branch: seven findings, each confirmed by two skeptics, two medium and five low; one is older than A6 and is recorded as a follow-up, not fixed; each code fix has a test that fails without it). No migration, no new or changed API route (the role matrix is unchanged). The solver's answer gains two optional fields per option, `weight_unit_kg` (0.1) and `new_overtime_only` (true): a web from before them ignores them, and a plan from a solver before them has neither.

- **Fixed.** *A stop left out by its receiving window was told it was left out for its weight, while lower-priority stops rode on the trucks* (medium). `_no_room_reason` counted the room on each load after every stop on it, whatever its priority. The verifiers' day: two P1 stops whose 08:00-08:15 windows are about 70 minutes apart, two P5 stops next to the depot, T01 (1 trip) and T02 (1 trip, from 09:00), 6,000 kg on 6,000 kg of loads. One P1 stop cannot go by time, but it read "no load or free trip has room for its 1,000 kg ... (lowest priorities first). Add a truck ...", and the plan lost its "no check proves they are impossible" warning; taking both P5 stops off serves it no better. Now the room on a load counts only its stops of the same or a higher priority (strict priorities drop lower ones first; a free trip counts in full), so that stop keeps the search's reason and the warning. When the weight reason stands although lower-priority stops ride on the plan, it says so: "Not planned: no load or free trip has room for its 1,600 kg, even with every lower-priority stop taken off (then the most room on a load that takes its 10 cases is 1,400 kg). This P1 stop was left out. Add a truck or raise the loads-per-truck limit."; "lowest priorities first" is said only when no lower-priority stop is served. The dispatcher guide no longer says that a re-plan cannot help with this reason.
- **Fixed.** *The plan-wide "Depot moved since planning" warning gave one distance for every load, often another load's* (medium). `masterChangedNotes` kept only the last load's distance and printed it in both sentences. After two depot moves (a locked load kept through both keeps the first pin), a load 5.6 km from the pin read "2.2 km", and a PLANNED load's distance appeared in the locked loads' sentence; the plan screen and the Excel SUMMARY carry the warning. Now a sentence gives one distance only when all its loads agree ("T01 L1, T02 L1 start and end at the depot pin they were planned from (2.2 km from the depot's pin now)"), else each load its own ("T01 L1 (5.6 km), T02 L1 (2.2 km) start and end at the depot pins they were planned from (distance from the depot's pin now). Locked and dispatched loads keep them."). One load reads in the singular: "T01 L1 starts and ends at the depot pin it was planned from ...", "T01 L2 is still planned from the old depot pin ... Re-plan to plan it from the new pin." Each load's own note, the driver sheet and the Excel DEPOT row were right already.
- **Fixed.** *The ASSUMPTIONS sheet stated the new weight and overtime rules for plans made before this release* (low). The Weights row and the Overtime clause were printed for every plan with the whole-day costs, so a plan made by the solver in production today (each stop rounded up to a whole kg, overtime already worked charged again in the search) and exported after the deploy - the plan in use on deploy day, or any older version kept for the record - described rules it was not made with. Now each option reports the rules that made it (stored with the option in `detailsJson`), `solverRules` in `workbook.ts` reads the option in use, and only such a plan gets "each order to the nearest 0.1 kg, checked against each truck's payload with no margin ..." and "; overtime already worked by locked or dispatched loads is not counted again for new loads". An older plan reads "Weights: earlier rule: the route search rounded each stop up to a whole kg and each payload down to a whole kg (a small margin below the payload)" (the rule of every dispatch solver since the MVP), and its Overtime row reads as it did.
- **Fixed.** *The dispatcher guide said the plan screen's Loading manifest shows kg per product, but it showed cases and a whole-kg total* (low). The manifest now has each product's kg, and its TOTAL line gives the load's kg to 0.1 kg (an 896.8 kg load read "TOTAL (897 kg)"). The help page says "cases and kg per product".
- **Fixed.** *A PLANNED load planned before origins were kept, on a depot pin moved since, got the "still planned from the old depot pin. Re-plan" note, but the day was not out of date* (low). The plan screen reads such a load's origin from its option's `inputs.depot`; the day overview (`plannedLoadsMasterChanged`) read only the snapshot's origin, so Step 3 said the plan was ready and RE-PLAN stayed off until the next re-plan. It now falls back to the chosen option's `inputs.depot` too, so Step 3 and the plan notes agree; an option without inputs gives neither a note nor "out of date" (both use the depot's pin now).
- **Fixed (test).** *E3's change in `getPlanDetail` had no test*: reverting its `rowLinesKg` call to the old `rowLines` passed the whole unit suite. `plan-options.spec.ts` now runs `getPlanDetail` on the fake database with an order weighed at order level (lines of 24 and 16 cases at 0 kg, the order 400 kg) and a LOCKED split part planned at 15 kg per case (its line now says 10 kg per case): each load's manifest kg and each stop's SKU kg equal the load's and the row's kg (400, 400, 300 kg). With the old call it fails (0 kg on a 400 kg load), checked by reverting the line. The A6 Tests line above now says which guarantee this test covers.
- **Follow-up, not fixed (older than A6; main `3451f4d` does the same).** *A normal order at a stop that also holds a late order is labelled "Late order" when the stop is left out* (low). The web merges a customer's orders into one stop, the stop is late when any of its orders is, and every order of an unserved stop gets the stop's reason: the normal order reads "Late order (P3): no unlocked truck/load had capacity or time left" while its Excel "Late order" column is empty. Only the words are wrong. Per-order reasons belong to a later PR, together with the verifiers' second point (within one priority a late-order re-plan kept 90 cases over 125, because the optimizer values a stop, not its cases): listed in [7.5](#75-open-questions-for-the-owner).
- **Tests.** Solver `test_dispatch.py` +2 (88): the window day above (the P1 stop keeps the search's reason and warning), and 3 x 1,600 kg P1 with a 100 kg P5 on two 3,000 kg loads (the weight reason gives the 1,400 kg of room without the P5 stop, not the 1,300 kg beside it, and no "lowest priorities first"; end to end the P5 stop rides on one load only, so this test reads 1,400 kg either way: the third review's direct test below is the one that tells them apart); the 0.1 kg test checks that every option, also one with nothing to plan, reports `weight_unit_kg` 0.1 and `new_overtime_only`. Web unit: `plan-snapshots.spec.ts` (two kept loads from different pins and a PLANNED one, in both orders; one load in the singular; the day's fallback to the option's depot), `day-overview-weights.spec.ts` (a PLANNED load without origin on a moved pin makes the day out of date; not when the option's pin is today's, or with no inputs), `dispatch-workbook.spec.ts` and `plan-options.spec.ts` (`solverRules`: an option without the fields gets the earlier Weights row and no clause; `getPlanDetail` maps the fields; E3 through `getPlanDetail`); `plan-feasibility-gate.spec.ts` and integration `dispatch-mvp.spec.ts` 28a read the singular wording. No new spec file.
- **Benchmark.** No fix of this review changes a plan: the solver change is the words of a "no room" stop, the plan's warning and the two reported fields; the rest is the web's outputs and the day overview. None of the benchmark days of [`OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md`](./OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md) section 10 has a "no room" stop (checked in every stored answer of the branch's two web runs: S03's are a window and a fleet shortage, whose reason comes first; the others are the web's own checks), so its tables stand (10.4).
- **Deploy notes.** No migration. Deploy order as above (web first, or both together). With the old solver, new plans read "earlier rule" on the ASSUMPTIONS sheet, which is right for them; after the solver deploys, new plans state the 0.1 kg and new-overtime rules.

**Audit PR A6 second review fixes** (same branch, `audit-p6-solver-accuracy`, on `fb1dc7e`; five findings, each confirmed by two skeptics, one medium and four low; one is older than A6 and is recorded as a follow-up, not fixed; each code fix has a test that was run on `fb1dc7e` first and failed). No migration, no schema change, no new or changed API route (the role matrix is unchanged), no new field in the solver's answer.

- **Fixed.** *The "no room" reason told the dispatcher a P1 stop needs another truck when the trucks can carry every stop, and the plan lost its "no check proves they are impossible" warning* (medium). `_no_room_reason` gave its reason whenever no single load and no free trip had room for the stop; it never asked whether another packing of the same stops would carry it. The verifiers' smallest day: 1,000 + 1,500 + 1,500 + 1,000 + 1,000 kg of P1 on two 3,000 kg trucks with one load each fit as {1,500, 1,500} and {1,000, 1,000, 1,000}, but the route search packs {1,000, 1,500} twice. The fifth stop read "no load or free trip has room for its 1,000 kg ... This P1 stop was left out (lowest priorities first). Add a truck ...", on a day with no lower priority. Now the reason also needs a proof (`_no_packing_fits`, in cases and in kg, 0.1 kg units): the stops of its priority or higher that the plan serves, with this one, are more than all usable trips carry, or more of them are over half the biggest truck than there are usable trips (no two such stops share a load, whatever the packing; the first review's 3 x 1,600 kg day keeps its reason). Otherwise the stop keeps the search's own reason and the plan's warning, as on main. "(lowest priorities first)" is said only when the day has lower-priority stops and none of them rides. Only the words and the warning change, never a plan.
- **Fixed.** *The plan screen showed an older version's manifest kg that did not add up to its TOTAL, with no note* (low). The per-product kg (new in A6) carry each order's kg now; the TOTAL carries the kg the load was planned with. A re-plan after a corrected product weight re-weighs the orders that are not frozen, so a superseded version kept for the record (the owner keeps them for documentation) read, for example, 2,313.8 kg of products under a 2,303.6 kg TOTAL, while its Excel load sheet already said "MISMATCH: load records 2303.6 kg (order weights changed since planning)". Now `manifestKgNote` (`lib/dispatch/weights.ts`, with the workbook's 0.5 kg `KG_ROUNDING_TOL`; the workbook now uses the same `manifestKgOf` and `manifestKgDiffers`) puts one line under the TOTAL: "The load was planned at 2,303.6 kg. Order weights changed since planning, so the products add up to 2,313.8 kg." The dispatcher guide says so.
- **Fixed (test).** *Review fix #4 (kg per product on the plan screen's Loading manifest) had no test*: removing the per-product cell and putting the TOTAL back to whole kg passed the whole unit suite. The manifest's kg now come from `kgText` (unit-tested: an 896.8 kg load reads "896.8"), and `dispatch-screen-guards.spec.ts` checks that the Loading manifest renders `kgText(m.weightKg)` per product and `kgText(l.weightKg)` on the TOTAL, never `Math.round(l.weightKg)`, and renders the note.
- **Fixed (docs).** *[`OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md`](./OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md) section 10 said every day leaves "the same ones" unserved* (low). On S03 both versions leave out 131 orders with the same counts per priority and reason, but 5 of the 61 P4 orders differ, and the branch carries 4 cases more; the replays store counts only. Section 10.3 and the A6 benchmark bullet above now say "the same number ... per priority and reason" and name S03's difference. The method caveat now lists every day whose two runs differ, the branch's real day included (6 trucks and 556.14 OMR, then 5 trucks and 543.03 OMR). Section 10.5 records this review.
- **Follow-up, not fixed (older than A6; main `3451f4d` does the same).** *On a tight day where every trip is used, a P1 stop is left out although the fleet carries every stop* (low). No stage moves single stops between loads: the repack moves whole loads, and the drop repair adds a stop only as a one-stop load on a free trip. Recorded in [7.5](#75-open-questions-for-the-owner) with the repair. Until then such a stop keeps the search's reason and the warning (the first fix above), never "no room". It did not appear on the benchmark days (NMWC's trucks do several trips).
- **Tests.** Solver `test_dispatch.py` +2 (90): `_no_room_reason` on the verifiers' packing (no reason), on 3 x 1,600 kg and on 3 x 60 cases on two trucks (the reason; "lowest priorities first" only with a lower priority on the day), and on 40 + 60 + 40 + 60 cases (no reason); and the verifiers' day end to end in all three options (a left-out stop keeps the search's reason and the warning). The first review's 3 x 1,600 kg test also checks that a day of one priority never reads "lowest priorities first". Web unit: `dispatch-weights.spec.ts` (`kgText`; `manifestKgNote` with the verifiers' figures, and none within 0.5 kg), `plan-options.spec.ts` (a superseded version whose order was re-weighed after it was made: through `getPlanDetail`, the note on that load only, and the Excel flags the same load sheet), `dispatch-screen-guards.spec.ts` (above).
- **Benchmark.** No plan changes: the solver change decides the words of a left-out stop and the plan's warning, and no stored answer of the benchmark days has a "no room" reason ([`OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md`](./OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md) 10.4 and 10.5), so the tables stand.
- **Deploy notes.** No migration. Deploy order as above (web first, or both together); the two changes are independent.

**Audit PR A6 third review fixes** (same branch, `audit-p6-solver-accuracy`, on `b8e6656`; four findings, each confirmed by two skeptics, one medium and three low; two are the same fault, so three problems, all in the tests; each new check was first run against the fault it guards and failed). No product code changed: no migration, no schema change, no new or changed API route (the role matrix is unchanged), and no change to the solver's answer, to a plan or to any words a dispatcher reads.

- **Fixed (test).** *The repack's phase-limit test contradicted the E5 follow-up and failed at random on a busy machine* (medium and low, the same fault). `test_repack_phase_limits_stay_inside_the_solve_limit` checked that both CP-SAT phases end by the solve's limit (0.3 s, plus 0.05 s). The follow-up `0e339b5` gives phase 2 at least 60 % of the limit (here 0.18 s) when phase 1 ran long. So when building the model and CP-SAT's presolve took more than about 0.05 s (a loaded or cold machine), phase 2 started after about 0.17 s, ended past 0.35 s, and the test failed: the skeptics saw it fail in 2 to 4 of 8 to 10 runs of that test alone at 100 % CPU, and once in the full suite. The code and the handbook were right; the test and its docstring described the rule from before the follow-up. Now the test checks each phase's limit against the rule from the moment that phase started: phase 1 gets 40 % of the time left (at least 0.05 s) and ends by the limit; phase 2 gets the rest, at least its floor, and ends by the limit or its floor. It runs twice: as it was, and with phase 1 paused 0.2 s (the skeptics' slow phase 1, made certain). The old check fails the paused case every time ("(0.213, 0.18)": phase 2 started 0.213 s in with its 0.18 s floor); the new one passes both. A scratch probe ran the new check with phase 1 paused from 0 to 0.45 s, on an idle PC and with 14 busy processes on its 12 threads: the rule never failed. The docstring, the 5.3 `test_repack.py` row, the E5 bullet above and [4.11](#411-post-solve-stage) now say it this way: phase 1 ends by the limit, and phase 2 does too unless phase 1 ran long.
- **Fixed (test).** *The first review's priority filter in the "no room" reason had no failing test since `b8e6656`* (low). Taking the filter out of `_no_room_reason` (`rooms = _rooms(usable_tds, loads)`) passed the whole solver suite. `_no_packing_fits` alone now keeps the window day's stop from the weight reason, and the first review's 3 x 1,600 kg test has its P5 stop on one load only, so the most room there is 1,400 kg either way. The new direct test `test_the_weight_reason_takes_the_lower_priority_stop_off_every_load` puts a P5 stop beside a P1 stop on every load: 3 x 1,600 kg P1 and two 100 kg P5 on two 3,000 kg trucks, and the same by cases (3 x 60 cases P2 and two 30-case P5 on two 100-case trucks). The reason must give 1,400 kg and 40 cases of room. Without the filter it gives 1,300 kg, and the test fails (checked by taking the filter out, then putting it back).
- **Fixed (test).** *F22's "Same plan" guard had no test* (low). Taking `!broken.length &&` out of `optionTradeoffs` passed every web unit test. The case it matters for: RECOMMENDED and MIN TRUCKS keep the timing rules and are the same plan, and MIN DISTANCE is a different plan that breaks them. `plan-options.spec.ts` now checks that case with VIOLATED and with UNVERIFIED: RECOMMENDED reads "Every different option breaks the timing rules.", MIN TRUCKS "Same plan as RECOMMENDED", MIN DISTANCE its broken-rules text, and no row reads "Same plan as the other options". Without the guard both rule-keeping rows read "Same plan as the other options", and the test fails (checked by taking the guard out, then putting it back).
- **Tests.** Solver `test_dispatch.py` +1 (91) and `test_repack.py` +1 (49: the phase-limit test now has two cases) ([5.3](#53-test-suites)). Web unit `plan-options.spec.ts` +1. No new spec file. The A6 Tests line and the first review's Tests line above now name the tests that guard those two rules.
- **Benchmark.** No plan changes: only tests and docs changed ([`OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md`](./OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md) 10.6), so the tables stand.
- **Deploy notes.** Nothing new to deploy: no product code changed. Deploy order as above.

**Owner decisions of 5 Oct 2026 on the driver page** (branch `driver-page-followups`, on the delivery outcome branch `delivery-outcome-driver-page` `7387a1d`). The owner answered four questions after the driver page demo: *"1) photos 90 days is enough. 2) ok but needs to be monitored and documented well. 3) one per depot. 4) the dispatcher is the planner he just doesnt have privilages of admin like changing location."* One additive migration (`20261005090000_driver_page_owner_decisions`, [5.5](#55-database-migrations)).

- **(1) Photos 90 days.** `TenantConfig.photoRetentionDays` defaults to 90 (`DEFAULT_PHOTO_RETENTION_DAYS` in `lib/settings-fields.ts`, used by the janitor's and the photo route's fallbacks); the migration moves companies still on 365 to 90 and their positions to at most 90 (the rule "positions never longer than photos" is unchanged: `retentionSaveProblem` and the janitor's clamp), audited. Storage: about 6 GB at NMWC volume instead of 25 GB ([`docs/admin.md`](./admin.md)).
- **(2) "Camera not working", monitored and documented** ([3.18](#318-delivery-outcomes-and-the-driver-page)): the list on the Deliveries card and the plan screen, the 3-a-day driver-link alert and load badge, the dashboard line, the Excel column, link count, **Without photo** sheet and Summary lines; the dispatcher guide's daily check and weekly review, the driver guide (English and Arabic).
- **(3) One Call dispatcher number per depot.** `Depot.dispatcherPhone` (Depots form, company admin; audited with the depot), `dispatcherPhoneFor` in the manifest; the company number in Settings is the fallback.
- **(4) The dispatcher is the PLANNER.** Role checks changed (before -> after): `lib/dispatch/load-state.ts` `checkTransition` (DISPATCHED and COMPLETED: SUPERVISOR -> PLANNER); `app/api/runs/[id]/dispatch/route.ts`, `unlock/route.ts`, `reset-stuck/route.ts`, `stop-search/route.ts` (`role: 'SUPERVISOR'` -> `'PLANNER'`); `app/t/[slug]/dispatch/page.tsx`, `dispatch/plan/[id]/page.tsx`, `runs/[id]/page.tsx` (`canDispatch={canApproveOverride(...)}` -> `canPlan(...)`; the legacy run page's debug download keeps `canApproveOverride` through its own `canDownloadDebug`). Unchanged: VIEWER read-only; TENANT_ADMIN for a saved location, the loading rule, users, depots, trucks, drivers, products, regions, cost / routing / retention settings, the pin check; SUPERVISOR for the solver debug JSON. The screens' words now say "a dispatcher" where they said "a supervisor" (stuck plan, stopped search, `PLAN_RESET` label).
- **Tests.** Web unit: four new spec files (`dispatcher-role`, `depot-dispatcher-phone`, `photo-retention-90`, `camera-exceptions`); updated `api-role-matrix`, `stuck-plan`, `dispatch-load-state`, `plan-lifecycle`, `search-modes`, `long-search-jobs`. Integration: `recovery-races-db.spec.ts` (a PLANNER resets a lost job, a VIEWER is refused).
- **Deploy notes.** The migration runs in the pre-deploy step (one column, one default, and an `UPDATE` of companies on 365 with an audit row each where the driver-page migration already ran with 365; see the review fixes below). The `postgres-volume` is 4.6 GB: raise it before photos reach about 3 GB ([`docs/admin.md`](./admin.md)). Each depot's dispatcher phone is empty until an admin fills it in (the company number is used meanwhile).

**Review of the owner decisions of 5 Oct 2026** (same branch, one commit). Seven findings, all fixed (two were the same defect):
- **Fixed (medium).** *An office **Record** on a result saved with "Camera not working" took the stop off every monitor and out of the audit's "before".* The office's result became the newest OUTCOME and `rebuildVisit` wrote its empty `noPhotoReason`, so the stop left the Deliveries card, the plan list, the dashboard KPI, the Excel column and the **Without photo** sheet, and the truck's count fell (3 became 2: no red alert, no badge); the audit's `beforeJson` had no `noPhotoReason` or source. Now the visit keeps the driver's own last Delivered / Partly apart from the current result (`StopVisit.driverResultAt`, `driverResultOutcome`, `driverNoPhotoReason`, `driverPhotoKeys`; `driverFacts` ignores office events; migration `20261005100000_results_without_photo` adds and fills them), every monitor reads those (a corrected stop is marked *corrected by office*), and the office audit's before / after keep the source, the no-photo reason, the photo count and the driver's mark. The dispatcher guide no longer says "nobody can remove the mark": a correction keeps it; only the driver's own new result with a photo replaces it.
- **Fixed (low).** *A result whose named photo never arrived was not counted.* A driver could skip "Camera not working" by letting an upload fail (or a reissue on another phone dropped the queued photo). **Photo not received** now counts with it: the driver's result named a photo, none arrived, and none can (`photoWaitOver`: the link revoked or reissued after the result, past its upload time, or the trip completed 60 minutes ago); the same list, KPI (`photoNotReceived`, `withoutPhoto`), Excel reason and sheet, and the link's count. The dispatcher guide warns that a reissue drops photos still waiting on the old phone.
- **Fixed (low).** *The retention migration could write a false 365 → 90 audit row for every company and override an admin's explicit 365.* `20261004090000` now creates `photoRetentionDays` at 90 (it is not in production), so a deploy of both changes nothing; where it already ran with 365, `20261005090000` skips a company whose admin saved the field in Settings and writes its audit row like a Settings save (`entityId` = the company, `{ tenant, config }`). - (Decided by the owner on 27 Sep 2026, evening; audit PR A5) **(A2) Should a LOW-confidence location reading require the dispatcher to move the pin before saving?** Owner: "its a standing rule locations should always be correct as part of sop no item will be delivered without location." A standing rule the system enforces, not a report: the location part of PR A5 ([7.4](#74-review-leads-found-while-writing-this-handbook), [3.4](#34-step-2-customer-locations-and-details)). Enforced: a reading that is not exact is saved only as a pin placed by hand (ADD LOCATION and the customer page's Set location, and the server checks it again); no other route stores such a reading as a usable location (the customer import leaves it out and lists it); a LOW location nobody confirmed is not planned; a legacy run is not dispatched while a customer on it has no correct location. Decided by the owner on 28 Sep 2026: **an imported location nobody has confirmed yet (HIGH or MEDIUM, "Location came from an import and was never confirmed by a dispatcher") is still planned, with that note** (owner: "Plan with a warning": NMWC's customer file counts as correct, and a pin a dispatcher corrects becomes confirmed); a MEDIUM one can no longer be confirmed as it is (the dispatcher places the pin). Customers confirmed at a point outside the delivery area before A5 are still planned: the read-only count in [5.12](#512-how-to-verify-a-deploy) check 13 lists them for a look on the map. Decided by the owner on 28 Sep 2026 (asked after the A5 third review): **should a load be refused whenever a customer's pin was corrected by more than 50 m after it was planned, until it is re-planned?** Owner: **"Allow, driver gets new pin"**. A pin corrected after planning does not block the load: it can go, and the driver's text and sheet show the planned stop with "New pin - ask the dispatcher which one to use" and a link to the new pin (the frozen-plan-facts behaviour since PR4, kept as it is; recorded in [7.4](#74-review-leads-found-while-writing-this-handbook), "A5 owner decisions"). Only a stop still planned at a point that was not usable (LOW, outside the area, 0,0) when a new pin more than 50 m away replaced it is refused (`STOP_PIN_REPLACED`, [3.8](#38-step-6-load-states)): that point was never a place to deliver to.

Enforced: migration `20260930120000_orders_always_have_depot` gives every such order and file a depot and makes `depotId` required; an order file is never linked to a depot nobody chose ([7.4](#74-review-leads-found-while-writing-this-handbook), [5.5](#55-database-migrations)). - (Decided by the owner on 28 Sep 2026; asked after the A5 fifth review) The customer import counts one zero at the end of a coordinate, in every file: 23.5800 is 3 decimals and not saved as exact (a file cannot tell a rough 23.58 shown with 4 decimals from a typed one; about 1 in 100 real 4-decimal values per axis ends in 00 and then needs its pin placed by hand). **Should ADD LOCATION and the new-customer form (`POST /api/customers`) count the same way?** Owner: **"Same rule everywhere"**. Done in audit PR A5 ([3.4](#34-step-2-customer-locations-and-details); [7.4](#74-review-leads-found-while-writing-this-handbook), "A5 owner decisions"): a pair a dispatcher types or pastes into ADD LOCATION (the Read, and the server's check on Save) or sends to `POST /api/customers` counts one zero at the end of each coordinate, with the import's own function (`countedText` in `location-input.ts`). "23.5800, 58.4100" needs a pin placed by hand, and the dialog and the server say why: "Fewer than 4 decimals (only one zero at the end counts). Drop the pin on the customer's exact location."; "23.5850, 58.4105" and 6-decimal pairs are exact as before. A pair written as text in a Google Maps link or a `geo:` URI counts the same way, because padding reaches it; Google's own pin (`!3d...!4d...`) keeps its digits, not cut, but needs 4 decimals (A5 sixth review: Google repeats a coordinate searched for as the pin, so a searched "23.58, 58.41" came back exact), and degrees, minutes and seconds of a pair with fewer than 4 decimals need a pin too. Before, a dispatcher who typed or pasted "23.5800, 58.4100" (for example copied from a cell formatted to show 4 decimals) got an exact reading, saved as confirmed.
- (A5 sixth review) **Customers a dispatcher confirmed from a reading that is not exact under today's rules: flag them, or leave them?** ADD LOCATION keeps the text a location was read from, so they can be found: a pair padded with zeros ("23.5800, 58.4100", before the "Same rule everywhere" change), a rough coordinate searched in Google Maps and shared (before the sixth review), and any reading the screen before A5 let through (a map centre, fewer than 4 decimals, a directions link read at its start). Today they stay usable and are planned, because a confirmed point is never judged again. Flagging them would mean their orders are not planned until a dispatcher places the pin by hand. `apps/web/prisma/check-saved-readings.ts` counts them per company, read-only ([5.12](#512-how-to-verify-a-deploy) step 13): the question is about its "confirmed from a pasted reading ... read as not exact today" count only, where the saved point is where the text kept points (A5 seventh review). The customers it lists as "not judged by their text" were not located from that text: a map click or two typed numbers on the customer page before A5 (which set the point, confirmed and HIGH, and left the text as it was), or a saved point confirmed as it is; flagging by the text would stop exact map-clicked customers. The same lines say how many of those have fewer than 4 decimals as stored (typed rough on the customer page, or exact values ending in 0; the stored number cannot say which), for a look on the map, like the unconfirmed HIGH query in step 13. Nothing changes until the owner decides.

(A1 v4, applied as a default on the same terms) A workbook with a chart sheet (a tab that holds only a chart), a dialog sheet or a macro sheet is refused, because SheetJS turns a chart sheet's chart into cells past every cap. Do NMWC's order or customer workbooks ever have a chart sheet? If they do, the alternative is to skip such sheets instead of refusing the file.
- (P5, applied as defaults, to confirm before the merge) **Uploads are read in a separate process, not a worker thread** (the assessment said worker thread): a worker's heap cap can abort the whole web process (reproduced with a legal 0.22 MB file on Node 22 and 24), a child process ends alone. **Heap cap 512 MB and time limit 15 s**: NMWC's real files need about 60-70 MB and well under a second, NMWC's shape at the row limit about 400 MB and 5-20 s on this PC; the widest legal files (50,000 rows of more than about 45 columns, or the same as CSV sent as Excel) need 650-900 MB and are refused, where before P5 they were read while every user waited 20-40 s. Keep 512 MB / 15 s, or 768-1024 MB / 20-30 s (more memory on the web service, see the question above)? **The request body**: `req.formData()` still reads a whole upload request into the web process before the 10 MB check (an older gap, not E2): cap it by `Content-Length` first? (P5 third review) Next.js 14 reads the body even before the route runs, keeping a copy for its middleware, also for a request without a session: a 300 MB request took the web process up by 500-620 MB. So a check in the route comes too late; a cap in front of the web service, or one in the middleware (not tested whether Next.js still reads the body then), would be needed. Where, and at what size? (P5 third review) **The order check of a very large file** still runs in the web process, as before P5: while files of 33,000 and 50,000 lines were checked, `/api/health/live` waited up to 2.3-2.7 s here (on a busy PC). NMWC's files have a few hundred lines (at most 0.65 s there). Move that check off the web process too, or leave it? **The name P5** in the handbook (A5 is the owner-rules PR). (P5 review, applied as a default) **The rows a parser process sends back are at most 128 MB**, each text sent once; a file whose answer would be larger is refused "needs too much memory". No file within the upload caps comes near it (the largest measured sends 44 MB; NMWC's files well under 1 MB). Keep 128 MB? (P5 second review, applied as a default) **A CSV sent as text counts every value, empty ones too**: a CSV saved from Excel with more than 200 columns, most of them empty columns after the data, is refused ("... (also empty columns after your data) ..."). Until the CSV intake review fix (9 Oct 2026) the same file sent as Excel (Chrome or Edge on a PC with Excel installed) was read, because SheetJS read it and dropped those columns. Since that fix every CSV is read as text, so this Windows Excel-MIME path follows the 200-column cap too and such a file is refused whatever type the browser sends. Should RouteIQ drop empty columns after the data in a CSV, as SheetJS did? (The cap itself is unchanged until the owner decides; NMWC's CSV files have 8-15 columns.)

(PR9 review, decided by the owner) Today's leftovers are offered for tomorrow the same evening: today's orders are listed in their own group, unticked, and carried only when ticked on their own ([7.4](#74-review-leads-found-while-writing-this-handbook), "Owner decision: today's orders").

The schedule reaches 150 s at 200 stops, so 201–299-stop days keep 150 s and 121–200-stop days get more, up to about +3 min wall time at 200 stops.) Is 150 s enough for 201–350-stop days? The re-test's S03 (240 stops) varied 317.7–377.3 km between runs on 150 s; re-running it several times, and once with a longer `time_limit_sec` for comparison, would show whether those days need more.
- (Decided by the owner when PR7 was merged: option (a), keep RECOMMENDED as it is - priority-first timing - now that the options table and the Excel show the trade-off; a cheaper option stays one **Use instead** away.) **(PR7, N1) Should RECOMMENDED become cost-first?** Today it minimises money + preferences: minutes outside preferred windows (0.05 OMR/min), P1/P2 delivered later in the day (0.01 / 0.005 OMR per minute after the shift start) and moved orders on late-order re-plans (3 OMR each). On the Sep 2026 re-test that cost +1.6 to +37.2 OMR a day over the cheapest option, for P1/P2 delivered hours earlier (S05 on main: P1 on average 06:54 against about 09:47). Options: (a) keep it, now that the table shows the trade-off (PR7); (b) cost-first: RECOMMENDED = the cheapest plan, the preferences only as a tie-break (P1/P2 then often in the second wave); (c) keep the preferences but lower the early-delivery rates, or make them tenant settings (see the question on `early_preference_per_min` above). A same-day re-plan should measure "early" from the re-plan time, not 06:00 (N2), whichever is chosen.
- (Audit PR A6, owner decision 14: recorded, not built) **Spare drivers already in overtime?** Since A6 the optimizer counts only new cost: overtime a truck's locked or dispatched loads already work is not charged again, so that truck gets a new load when it is cheaper than opening another truck - fewer trucks and less money, but more overtime for that driver. If NMWC wants to spare such drivers, a visible Settings value "extra cost per hour for a driver already in overtime" (off by default, 0) would add that cost for new loads of trucks with locked loads in the route search, the repack and the timing, and the ASSUMPTIONS sheet would name it. Say if you want it.
- (Audit PR A6 review: a follow-up, older than A6) **Late-order reasons per order, and which stop a late-order re-plan keeps.** A customer's orders travel as one stop, and the stop is "late" when any of its orders is: when that stop is left out, its normal order also reads "Late order (P3): no unlocked truck/load had capacity or time left" (its Excel "Late order" column stays empty). Only the words are wrong; the fix is per-order reasons in the web's unserved mapping (or per-order late flags for the solver). The same verifiers saw a late-order re-plan keep two P3 stops of 90 cases over one P3 stop of 125 cases: within one priority the optimizer values a stop, not its cases. Should a re-plan keep the most cases within a priority (owner decision 26 compares priority service first, then cost)?
- (Audit PR A6 second review: a follow-up, older than A6; main `3451f4d` does the same) **A stop left out on a tight day although the trucks could carry every stop.** When every trip of the day is used, the route search can pack the stops so that the room left is spread over several loads. 1,000 + 1,500 + 1,500 + 1,000 + 1,000 kg of P1 on two 3,000 kg trucks with one load each fit as {1,500, 1,500} and {1,000, 1,000, 1,000}, but the search packs {1,000, 1,500} twice and one 1,000 kg P1 stop stays out, also with a 20 s limit. No later stage repairs it: the repack moves whole loads between trucks, and the drop repair adds a left-out stop only as a one-stop load on a free trip. The verifiers saw it on 53 of 126 random exact-fit days of three trucks with one trip each (RECOMMENDED alone) and on 2 of 38 with all three options, on main and the branch alike. It did not appear on the benchmark days ([`OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md`](./OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md) section 10): NMWC's trucks do several trips, so a free trip is usually left. Since the second A6 review such a stop keeps the search's own reason ("Re-plan to search again") and the plan's "no check proves they are impossible" warning, never "no room". The repair, for a later PR: when the served stops and the left-out one still fit the used trips in total, move or swap single stops between loads, with the exact timing check (`load_repack.time_plan`); or give the repack a stop-level model when every trip is used. Owner decision 26 puts priority service first: say if this should come before other work. (Review solver-pipeline-1, Oct 2026: the closing recovery now swaps on every day, but only across priorities - a left-out stop in place of stops of a LOWER priority on one load. A stop left out while only stops of its own priority or higher ride, as here, is still not repaired; nor is a higher priority that needs loads of two trucks reorganised: on scenario s3-shortage-hire-1's saved day A the served P1..P4 went from 9 / 5 / 12 / 3 to 9 / 7 / 13 / 3, still one P1 short of the 10 a P1-only solve serves; its bay-fleet day C2 went from 7 / 7 / 13 / 8 to 8 / 6 / 11 / 9, the 8 P1 of its P1-only solve. A priority-tiered source (the P1 stops solved alone, then extended) would close day A's gap; not done.)
- (Audit PR A6, owner decision 15: recorded, not built) **A per-truck payload reserve in kg?** Weights are now checked to 0.1 kg with no margin, so a load may weigh exactly the payload. A reserve would keep N kg of every load free on a chosen truck. The design: a column `Truck.payloadReserveKg` (default 0, a migration); one `effectivePayloadKg()` (payload minus reserve) used by the dispatch request, split sizing, the too-heavy check, the dispatch check, the exports and the change notes; the truck form refuses a reserve at or above the payload in plain words (a payload of 0 means "no limit" to the optimizer, so it must never reach 0 that way); a reserve of 0 sends exactly today's request. Build it only if NMWC asks for it.

- (Delivery outcome, 4 Oct 2026, spec section 22; Part 3 built with these defaults, to confirm) **Q1** photo storage: **decided 5 Oct 2026: 90 days** (about 6 GB, a quarter of the 25 GB of 365 days; built); 1600 px or 1280 px is still open. **Q4** same-day second attempt: send the missing cases on another truck the same day, or Bring forward only? **Q5** no result at day end: keep "counts as delivered and listed", or require a result for every stop before a load can be Completed? **Q6** a Delivered recorded by the dispatcher without a photo is allowed and shown "no photo (office)": acceptable? **Q8** corrections after a load is Completed: every dispatcher (built; the owner's decision of 5 Oct 2026 "the dispatcher is the planner" keeps it so). **Q12** removing a planned brought-forward copy needs the order-cancel flow (a CANCELLED status and a re-plan): build it next? **Q13** "Camera not working" saves Delivered without a photo: **decided 5 Oct 2026: allowed, monitored and documented** (built: the lists, the 3-a-day alert, the dashboard KPI, the Excel column and sheet, the guides). **Q3** a dispatcher quick-add of a hired truck for one day (not built).

**Records that exist only outside the repo:**

- The go-live time, the test company slug `nmlj`, the real-data counts (373 lines, 46 SKUs, 13 trucks, bays × 95 cases, 3 t / 10 t payloads), NMWC's actual 13 trucks / 19 trips, and the production v4/v5 figures are recorded only in the work log. (PR #30's 4 trucks / 12 loads / 229 OMR and the work log's 4 trucks / 12 loads / 884 km / 228 OMR are two different plans, so they do not conflict: the first is the MIN_TRUCKS option shown on v4, the second the v5 plan after re-optimize, per work log.)
- The deep-test result "engine = proven optimum on 27-28 of 30 small exact instances" exists only in the work log / local `.dev/bench`, not in `docs/OPTIMIZER_BENCHMARK.md`.
- PR #30's description was written when the PR was opened (07:17 UTC on 25 Sep) and says an adversarial review "is running on the branch". Commit `6c525ba` (07:20 UTC, merged in PR #30) is labelled "Review finding" and records one finding and its fix: a Re-plan with a late order waiting stays a LATE_ORDER re-plan. The repo does not record whether the review found anything else, or when it finished.
- PR #27's GitHub description names real NMWC customers. Should it be edited, given that real customer names should not leave `.dev/`?

## Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **NMWC** | National Mineral Water Co., Muscat, Oman: the customer and only production user of RouteIQ |
| **Tenant** | One company in the multi-tenant database (`Tenant` + `TenantConfig`). NMWC's demo tenant slug is `nmwc`; the production real-data test company is `nmlj` |
| **Depot** | The warehouse every load starts from and returns to (`Depot`) |
| **Customer branch** | One delivery location, identified by customer code + branch key (`customerKey(code, branchKey)`) |
| **Order** | All lines for one customer branch on one delivery date (`Order`), made of SKU lines (`OrderLine`) |
| **Stop** | One visit in the solver request: all open orders of one customer branch (`DispatchStop`, `stop_id` = customer id), or one part of a split delivery |
| **Load / trip** | One physical truck departure from the depot and return (`PlanLoad`, solver `PlannedLoad`). A truck can make several loads a day (`maxTripsPerTruck`, `maxTripsPerDay`). "Trip" and "load" mean the same thing |
| **Split delivery / portion / part** | An order too big for any truck, cut into parts (`<customerId>#k` stops, `<orderId>~k` portion ids); `<orderId>~open` is the open rest of a partly frozen order. Portion columns: `portionCases`, `portionWeightKg`, `portionLinesJson` |
| **Frozen load** | A load in LOCKED, LOADING, DISPATCHED or COMPLETED. It is never changed by a re-plan; the solver sees it as `frozen_trips` |
| **Load states** | PLANNED → LOCKED → LOADING → DISPATCHED → COMPLETED (`lib/dispatch/load-state.ts`) |
| **Plan (RunPlan)** | One version of the plan for one depot and one delivery date |
| **Plan version** | Each re-plan creates version N+1 (`createNextVersion`) with a reason (INITIAL, LATE_ORDER, MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT, REOPTIMIZE); the parent becomes SUPERSEDED and read-only |
| **Scenario / plan option** | One of three solver answers: RECOMMENDED (service, then true cost), MIN_TRUCKS (fewest trucks and loads), MIN_DISTANCE (fewest km). `ScenarioResult` rows |
| **Applied / chosen scenario** | The scenario turned into loads (`RunPlan.chosenScenarioId`). RECOMMENDED is applied automatically; "Use instead" applies another |
| **Re-plan vs re-optimize** | A re-plan creates a new version and keeps frozen loads. REOPTIMIZE is a re-plan with no moving charge (every stop may change truck). LATE_ORDER and MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT re-plans keep the moving charge. A REOPTIMIZE while late orders wait becomes LATE_ORDER |
| **Plan continuity / moving charge** | `previous_truck_id` per stop plus `change_penalty_per_stop` (3 OMR): moving a stop to another truck costs extra (`usesPlanContinuity`) |
| **Late order** | An order recorded after the planning cutoff (default 18:00 the day before, Asia/Muscat) or after a plan is applied (`Order.isLate`) |
| **Pending order** | An order of the day that is not in the applied plan's scope, i.e. it arrived after the plan was made |
| **Unserved** | An order or part left out of a scenario, always with a reason code (`UnservedOrder`) |
| **Pre-drop** | An order unserved before the solver runs (missing or invalid location) |
| **Reconciliation** | The exact cases check: uploaded = planned + unserved, in total, per SKU, per sales order and per line (`reconcile()`; solver `_assert_reconciled`). Dispatch is refused unless it is OK |
| **P1-P5** | Priorities: P1 highest, P5 lowest. **Strict priorities** mean one higher-priority stop outweighs any number of lower ones |
| **Hard / preferred window** | Receiving hours. Service must start inside the hard window; the preferred window is a soft cost |
| **Service time** | Minutes at the customer: base minutes plus unloading minutes per case (`stopServiceMin`) |
| **Turnaround / reload** | Time at the depot between loads: `reloadMinutes` plus loading minutes per case |
| **Planned from (same-day plan)** | A plan built on its own delivery day starts from now + `reloadMinutes` (the preparation time) instead of the first departure: no new load leaves earlier (PR8, `lib/dispatch/plan-from.ts`) |
| **Loading from (same-day plan)** | The time a plan built on its own delivery day was made (`loading_from_min`): loading of its new loads starts then, so each leaves no earlier than it + turnaround + loading per case of its cases, on every truck (PR8 review) |
| **Truck-day** | The solver's per-truck availability: earliest departure, latest return, trips left (`TruckDay`) |
| **Reload node** | An optional OR-Tools node at the depot that ends one load and starts the next on the same truck |
| **Repack** | The CP-SAT post-solve stage that re-assigns whole loads to trucks and departure times (`load_repack.py`) |
| **Warm start** | Starting the MIN_TRUCKS and MIN_DISTANCE searches from RECOMMENDED's raw loads |
| **OSRM** | Open Source Routing Machine: the self-hosted road-routing server (`infra/osrm`) that gives real road km and times |
| **Haversine / Estimated** | Straight-line distance × 1.3, used when OSRM is not configured or fails; plans are labelled "Estimated km" |
| **roadTimeFactor** | Multiplier (default 1.25) that turns OSRM car times into truck times |
| **RunJob** | One optimize attempt with its request, response and error JSON |
| **In-flight map** | The in-memory registry of running optimize jobs (`trackInflight`); the reason web must run as one replica |
| **Janitor** | The 60-second sweep that fails jobs with no heartbeat for 5 minutes (jobs from before heartbeats: 15 minutes after they started), repairs plans left optimizing behind an ended job, and closes stale driver shifts |
| **Legacy plan** | A plan made by the old PyVRP optimizer before Sep 2026; read-only (`LEGACY_PLAN`) |
| **Driver sheets / driver pack** | The PDF per load for drivers (`driver-pack.tsx`); no costs or margins |
| **OMR** | Omani rial, the currency of all costs |
| **OPERATION-PROJECT Lane A** | NMWC's separate system that records actual deliveries; RouteIQ only plans ([`docs/OPERATION_PROJECT_HANDOFF.md`](OPERATION_PROJECT_HANDOFF.md)) |
| **Ayun IVMS** | NMWC's vehicle-tracking system, a source of actual trip times for calibrating `roadTimeFactor` |
| **`.dev/`** | The git-ignored local folder on the maintainer's machine with real data, a portable Postgres and the benchmark harness. Never copy it |
